# MARGIN — Master Build Prompt

*Working name: **Margin** (provisional — see §01.7). Version: v1 (stitched draft). Generated 2026-09-07. Length ≈ 174,296 words; 1,374 numbered requirements.*

## What this document is

This is the complete build specification for an AI learning product whose mission is to be the best AI education company in history: table-stakes parity with ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and DeepSeek chat products, plus an exam-grounded learning core that none of them has. It is written for the executing AI coding agent (or the engineering team an agent leads). Read §00 first: it fixes the reading order, the non-negotiables, the precedence rules and the definition of done.

**How it was produced.** Eight research briefs (frontier chat baseline, education competitors, learning science, exam systems and marking, UX craft, architecture and model economics, business and moat, student voice) plus two gap briefs (legal/licensing and Cambridge marking) and an analysis of the founder's own material → a decision index → three independent product visions → a judged synthesis (`designs/SYNTHESIS.md`, the source of truth for every decision below) → sixteen sections drafted against that synthesis → adversarial critique and revision. The research and design files ship alongside this document under `research/` and `designs/`; §15.I maps which file answers what.

**Precedence.** `designs/SYNTHESIS.md` > this document > the research appendices. Where this document marks a decision PROVISIONAL or [founder default], the flip condition is stated inline and the founder-owned decisions are listed with their defaults in §15.G.

# §00 How to use this document

## 00.1 Who executes this, and in what order to read it

This document is the build specification for **Margin** (working name; see §01.7). Its reader is the executing AI coding agent, or the engineering team an agent leads. Treat it as a contract, not an inspiration: every numbered requirement is a test you will be held to, every "Never" row is a lint you will write, and every "Why:" is the evidence that stops you re-litigating a decision.

**00-USE-001 Reading order.** Read in this order before writing code: §00 → §01 → §02 (this file) → §03 (parity) → §04 (learning core) → §05 (exam engine) → §06 (library) → §07 (learner memory) → §08 (orchestration) → §09 (design system) → §10 (screens) → §11 (architecture) → §12 (safety) → §13 (quality gates) → §14 (roadmap) → §15 (appendices). Do not start a section's build until you have read the sections it cross-references. Acceptance: the first pull request of the build contains a `DECISIONS.md` that lists every requirement ID this PR touches; a PR touching an ID from a section not yet read is rejected in review.

**00-USE-002 Roles.** Four roles execute this document; an agent may hold more than one, but each PR names which role authored it.

| Role | Owns | Must never |
|---|---|---|
| Builder | Code, migrations, prompts, tokens, screens | Merge without the §13 gate report attached |
| Content engineer | Packs, structured mark schemes, gold sets, misconception library (§05, §06) | Enter a `scraped` provenance class or paste board wording without a licence (§06) |
| Evaluator | Eval suites, calibration runs, praise lint, adversarial students (§13) | Lower a floor to make a paper pass; the fix is content or method, never the bar |
| Founder liaison | Founder-owned decisions (§00.3), licensing, budgets | Silently choose a non-default; every non-default is a written decision |

**00-USE-003 Vocabulary is fixed.** Use only the canonical nouns from SYNTHESIS §3 in code, UI strings, telemetry and docs: Course, Pack, Item, Attempt, Turn, Mark, Card, Session, Plan, Source, Receipt, Class; the Learner Graph (the projection of Attempts into mastery, misconceptions and calibration, §07); the Examiner Twin (the calibrated per-paper marker, §05); the Effort Gate and Help Ladder (§04); the Learning Receipt (§12). Modes are **Learn · Practise · Mark**. Intent chips are **Teach me · Check my steps · Just the answer**. Mastery states are **Unseen · Shaky · Secure · Exam-ready**. Acceptance: a repository grep for `streak`, `quiz mode`, `tutor mode`, `explain mode`, `exam mode` as user-facing strings returns zero hits; the glossary in §15 is the only place synonyms appear, and only to map them to canon.

**00-USE-004 The scoping knife.** Before building any feature, answer in the PR description: "Which Attempts does this create or improve?" A feature with no answer is not in the MVP (SYNTHESIS §3.1). Why: every metric, mastery update, teacher view and Receipt is a projection of Attempts; features that do not touch them are cost without learning.


## 00.2 Non-negotiables

These hold for every release, every tenant, every model swap, every "quick fix". They are not trade-offs; they are the product. Each is enforced by a test named in the owning section. If a requirement elsewhere in this document appears to conflict with one of these, this list wins and the conflict is a bug to report (§00.6).

| ID | Non-negotiable | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| 00-NON-001 | **The Effort Gate.** No solution content on a gradable Item before an Attempt, a plan, or "don't know where to start" plus one sentence of what the student does know. The gate is a state on the Attempt, never a refusal in prose, never rate-limited. | §04; 30-turn adversarial suite, leak <5% (§13) |
| 00-NON-002 | **No Mark without a mark scheme in context; no number below gate.** If no structured scheme record exists, the product gives feedback and spans only. Below the §05 ship gate a paper shows spans and feedback, never a mark or a predicted grade. | §05.5; CI asserts 0 marks emitted without `mark_scheme_items` |
| 00-NON-003 | **No sycophancy.** No person-praise, unearned praise, agreement with an incorrect claim, softened mark, exclamation mark, emoji, "Great question" or therapy-speak in any Turn or Mark. | Praise lint before paint, regenerate once, template fallback; weekly audit <5% (§04, §13) |
| 00-NON-004 | **No streaks, no shame, no engagement optimisation.** No daily streaks, loss animations, confetti, overdue counters, mascots, or loss-framed notifications. DAU and minutes are guard-rails, never targets. | Lint on string table and motion tokens (§09); KPI tree (§14) |
| 00-NON-005 | **No submittable coursework.** NEA/IA/EE/personal-statement requests switch to draft-feedback mode; every assignment produces a Learning Receipt. | §12; eval set of coursework prompts, 0 submittable outputs |
| 00-NON-006 | **Three-provenance content model.** Every document is `OWN`, `LICENSED` or `USER`; there is no `scraped` class in code; `USER` never enters global retrieval; per-document kill switch; 24 h takedown SLA. | §06; type system rejects a fourth class |
| 00-NON-007 | **Never host or mirror board PDFs; no Cambridge mark-scheme viewer.** Papers deep-link to official pages; grid wording is paraphrased unless licensed; extracts ≤2 sentences or ≤40 words, attributed, audit-logged. | §06 extracts policy; storage lint |
| 00-NON-008 | **Teen-safety parity.** Item-for-item match with ChatGPT for Teens: age assurance, consent under 16, Study/Quiet Hours, break reminders, no romantic or companion behaviour, no ads, parental controls without transcript access, persistent Article 50 disclosure. | §12; consent audit 100% for under-16 school-tenant users |
| 00-NON-009 | **No efficacy claim that is not pre-registered.** No "2× learning", no multiplier, no grade-uplift claim outside the §14 study plan. The marketing number equals the product number. | Copy review checklist (§14); legal sign-off |
| 00-NON-010 | **Never "replaces teachers"; never "official" or "endorsed"; never the name beside "Cambridge".** Non-affiliation notice in footer and store listing. | String lint; store-listing template (§14) |
| 00-NON-011 | **Every pixel passes the §09 checklist.** Tokens only (no raw hex, no raw px outside the scale), one accent hue, no `ease-in`, no #000, no motion on Send, WCAG 2.2 AA gates, CLS above the cursor = 0. | §09.15 release checklist as CI; Storybook visual diff |
| 00-NON-012 | **Every prompt, model, routing or policy change passes the §13 gates** before it reaches a user: adversarial pedagogy suite, praise lint, per-paper marking gold sets, Recall@8 ≥0.92, cache-read assertion, CWV and TTFT SLOs. | CI required checks; policy version pinned per Session |
| 00-NON-013 | **A Course, not a chat.** Home has no "New chat"; a conversation without a Course is an Ask and never counts as study; there is no study toggle to lose; the mode chip is always visible. | §10 screen 3; e2e test |
| 00-NON-014 | **Turn discipline.** Every Learn-mode Turn ≤120 words unless depth was requested, one move, at most one question, explicit hand-back. Marking cards are exempt. | Orchestrator rejects >1 question; <2% of Turns >150 words (§04) |
| 00-NON-015 | **Verified before spoken.** Every numeric or symbolic final passes SymPy/Pyodide; quotes come only from loaded set texts, else "I can't confirm that quote"; every Item is pre-solved and the key held before tutoring. | §08 verification tools; eval: 0 invented quotes |
| 00-NON-016 | **"Just the answer" is honoured, never refused, after one attempt** — labelled Seen solution, retested at 24–72 h, never counting toward Secure. Homework due in ten minutes is legitimate. | §04.4; eval: 0 refusals post-attempt |
| 00-NON-017 | **Published limits, no silent cuts, no hard mid-session stop.** Every limit is a plain number in Settings › Usage with a meter; exam-week grace from T−14; soft slow-down only. | §03; zero silent limit changes as a KPI guard-rail (§14) |
| 00-NON-018 | **Privacy posture in code.** Per-tenant policy object on every request; no training on pupil data; EU/UK school tenants never leave regional endpoints; DeepSeek never tutors, never sees PII, never serves EU/UK tenants. | §11; CI asserts zero EU-tenant requests to non-EU endpoints |
| 00-NON-019 | **No model picker.** The student controls effort (Quick · Think · Deep); the vendor appears as a chip on the calibration line, never as a headline. | §03; §09 anti-pattern lint |
| 00-NON-020 | **Predicted grades live only on Progress › Paper and the mock debrief**, only for gated papers with ≥3 series of thresholds and ≥3 marked Attempts; never on Home, never in a notification, never to a parent unless the student enables it. | §05.7, §10 |
| 00-NON-021 | **The Never list is absent from the codebase:** image/video generation, general agents, deep research, ads, bot directory, daily streaks, companion persona, under-13 accounts, a Cambridge mark-scheme viewer. | Dependency and route lint; §14 |

Why the list is this long: each item corresponds to a documented failure of a competitor or a documented harm in the research (Bastani et al. 2025 for 001; students' #1 pain for 002; the Duolingo backlash for 010; Quizlet's paywall collapse for 017; Alpha School's unverifiable multipliers for 009). None is aesthetic.


## 00.3 Resolving ambiguity: precedence, provisional decisions, founder-owned defaults

**00-AMB-001 Precedence.** When two sources disagree, resolve in this order and record the resolution in `DECISIONS.md`: (1) `designs/SYNTHESIS.md`; (2) this document, where the section that *owns* the topic wins over a section that merely mentions it (ownership is the "Owner" column of SYNTHESIS §4 and the §NN headings here — marking belongs to §05, tokens to §09, routing to §08, personas to §02); (3) `designs/JUDGING.md` for the reasoning behind a ruling; (4) the research appendices (`research/*.md`) as evidence, never as decisions; (5) the three visions (`designs/vision-*.md`) only for colour. Acceptance: no PR cites a research file as the authority for a product behaviour.

**00-AMB-002 Do not re-open rulings.** Every decision in SYNTHESIS was adjudicated in JUDGING §3. If you believe a ruling is wrong, build the default, write a one-paragraph objection with evidence into `OBJECTIONS.md`, and continue. The founder reviews objections weekly (§00.6). Do not fork behaviour behind a flag "just in case" unless the ruling itself names an A/B.

**00-AMB-003 Three statuses.** Every requirement is FINAL unless labelled. **PROVISIONAL** means: build the stated default and implement the flip condition as a measurable event (an A/B result, a licence signed, a human–human line measured). **[founder default]** means: build the recommended default from the table below, tag every dependent string, migration or config key with the decision number so a reversal is a search-and-replace, not a rewrite. Acceptance: `grep -r "founder-default:E" src/` lists every dependent site.

**00-AMB-004 Founder-owned decisions and the defaults you build.** (Copied from SYNTHESIS §15; the founder may change any of them; you may not.)

| # | Decision | Default you build now | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Content library and rights | Founder's library treated as USER/OWN (notes-class plus hand-made scheme extracts); no licensed textbooks assumed | §05, §06 |
| E2 | Cambridge licensing posture | Ship on OWN + USER + deep links; Cambridge and CLA conversations opened in month 1; launch is not delayed for a licence | §06, §14 |
| E3 | Second curriculum after CAIE | Edexcel IAL (sibling Pack), then UK boards, then UNT before ЕГЭ | §02, §14 |
| E4 | Age floor at MVP | 16+ consumer; 13–15 via school tenants under school consent; 13+ consumer at month 9 after external audit; under-13 never | §02, §12 |
| E5 | DeepSeek policy | Anonymised second-solve and synthetic generation only; never tutoring, PII or EU/UK tenants | §08, §11 |
| E6 | Calibration budget | ~300 double-marked scripts × 6 papers plus 2–3 contracted examiners; without it, no published numbers and no predicted grades | §05, §13 |
| E7 | Publish calibration externally | Yes, per paper, monthly, once gated; below-gate papers listed "not yet calibrated" | §01, §13 |
| E8 | Free-tier cost | Accept $0.5–1/MAU in season with §14 quotas | §03, §14 |
| E9 | Price list and guarantee | $8 monthly / $59 until-exams / $19 family / $10 school seat / −40% regional; no guarantee SKU before Year 2 | §14 |
| E10 | Name | Margin; fallback Nib; clearance in month 1 | §01 |
| E11 | Languages and platforms | English UI at launch, RU/KZ strings staged for M12; web + Expo iOS/Android; shadcn primitives under custom tokens | §09, §11 |
| E12 | Residency and efficacy commitment | EU/UK residency for school tenants via Vertex regional routing from day one; public commitment to the pre-registered Layer 3 study | §11, §12, §14 |

**00-AMB-005 When the document is silent.** Apply, in order: the nearest non-negotiable (§00.2); the product principles (§01.2); the persona who is hurt most by the wrong choice (§02.1, usually Aisha); then the cheapest reversible option. Write the choice into `DECISIONS.md` with the requirement IDs it touches. Do not ask the founder about anything this rule can settle.


## 00.4 Definition of done: MVP, v1, v2

"Done" is a gate report, not a demo. A tier is done when every row below is green in the §13 dashboard and the founder has countersigned the report.

**00-DONE-001 MVP (public launch, March 2027; live for the June 2027 series).** All of the following, verified by the named evidence:

| Area | Done means | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Parity | Every "M" row of the §03 checklist passes its acceptance line | §03 checklist run, attached to the release PR |
| First Mark | Anonymous landing → full per-AO Mark, median ≤90 s; landing → full Mark ≥55% in beta; Mark → saved Course ≥35% | Product analytics from the 500-student closed beta (M5) |
| Learning core | Effort Gate, five-rung ladder, intent chips, Turn governor, misconception router, cold-open probes, FSRS-6 exam-anchored, mastery pips, debt-guard signals + L1, planner v1 | 30-turn adversarial suite: leak <5%; praise <5%; 100% of first-topic sessions begin with a probe |
| Exam engine | Levels marker for 9609, 0450, 9708 and points marker for 9709, 0580 with ≥3 papers above the §05.5 gate; seeding and auto-pause live; challenge-a-mark; generator solvability ≥98%; paper runner and debrief; handwriting confirm | Per-paper gate report: QWK ≥ floor **and** ≥ measured human line where measured; run-to-run identical level 100% |
| Content | 9609, 0450, 9708, 9709, 0580 Packs at `gated` or `live`; 0450 and 9708 produced by the compiler; provenance ledger complete; zero `USER` documents in global retrieval | Pack readiness dashboard; ledger export |
| Trust | Teen-safety parity item-for-item; consent 100% for under-16 school users; Article 50 disclosure; DPIA filed; usage meter with grace; Receipt export; parent digest v0; teacher calibrator scope | §12 audit; screenshot pack |
| Design | §09 pixel checklist as a blocking CI job; WCAG 2.2 AA gates green; dark mode; reading-comfort set; Cyrillic/Kazakh glyph test | CI logs; axe/Playwright reports |
| Performance and cost | TTFT p50 <800 ms, p95 <1.5 s; first AO card <8 s, full Mark ≤45 s; citation open ≤400 ms p95; cached input share ≥60%; median student ≤$2.6/month | Langfuse dashboards over the beta month |
| Efficacy plumbing | Layer 1 in-product RCT framework live; Layer 3 pre-registration filed | Registry receipt |

**00-DONE-002 v1 (months 7–12).** MVP plus: sciences 9701/9702/9700 with practical rules and 9618; IGCSE 0455/0620/0625/0610; Edexcel IAL Pack via the compiler at <4 weeks per sibling Pack; full teacher console with SSO/roster and LMS connectors; debt-guard L2–L3 default-on only if the A/B holds (≤2 pp 30-day retention cost); planner v2 with per-user learnability; share by link; code interpreter in a no-network sandbox; voice + camera pilot behind a flag; 13+ consumer after the consent audit; regional tiers; RU/KZ UI strings; creator programme paid on 30-day-retained subscribers. Done means: each new paper passes the same §05.5 gate; school onboarding <1 day; ≥8 papers above gate; June 2027 predicted-vs-actual analysis published.

**00-DONE-003 v2 (months 13–18).** IB criteria coaching (teacher marks first); AP FRQ marking; the IRT engine for one machine-scored national exam (UNT by default, [founder default E3]) from ≥300–500 responses per item; public curriculum compiler; cross-board graph at >60% reuse; Annex III technical file complete before 2 December 2027; marker API pilot; voice GA. Done means: the Layer 3 cluster RCT is in the field across the 2027–28 session with its analysis plan public before the first data point.

**00-DONE-004 Not done, ever, by shortcut.** A tier is not done if any non-negotiable in §00.2 is waived, if any paper shows a mark below gate, if any limit was cut silently, or if a "temporary" model change skipped §13. Why: the product's only durable asset is trust in the number; one leaked gate costs more than a slipped month.


## 00.5 How to use the appendices (§15)

§15 holds the artefacts you paste, not the rules you interpret. Use it as follows.

**00-APP-001 System prompts per mode (§15.A).** Copy the Learn, Practise and Mark system prompts verbatim into the prompt registry with their version hash; never edit inline in application code. Any change is a new version that passes §13 before routing (00-NON-012). The cached prefix (persona + Pack) must stay byte-stable and precede all dynamic content (§08).

**00-APP-002 Marking rubric templates (§15.B).** Use the levels and points templates as the *shape* of `mark_scheme_items`; the *content* for each paper comes from the Pack. A template field left blank is a build error, not a default.

**00-APP-003 Question-tagging schema (§15.D).** Every Item you create, import or generate validates against the schema (syllabus node, AO split, command word, tariff, cognitive-demand tag, provenance, stats). Reject on validation failure; do not coerce.

**00-APP-004 Prompt templates (§15.E).** Feedback template (task → process → self-regulation), distress script, coursework refusal, "Just the answer" deal script, probe card wording, debrief template. The strings there are canonical; §01.6 gives the voice rules they obey.

**00-APP-005 Glossary (§15.F).** The only place a synonym may appear. If a term you need is missing, add it to the glossary in the same PR that introduces it.

**00-APP-006 Open questions for the founder (§15.H).** Mirrors 00-AMB-004 with the full reasoning. Add a question there only when 00-AMB-005 cannot settle it.


## 00.6 Reporting progress, and what to ask the founder and when

**00-REP-001 Weekly build report.** Every Friday, one file `reports/YYYY-WW.md`, ≤600 words, in this order: (1) gate dashboard deltas (leak rate, praise rate, per-paper QWK, TTFT, cache share, cost per student); (2) requirement IDs closed this week, with evidence links; (3) IDs at risk for the current milestone (SYNTHESIS §13 table); (4) objections filed (00-AMB-002); (5) founder decisions needed, each with the default you are building meanwhile and the date the default becomes expensive to reverse. No prose about effort or mood. Acceptance: a reader who opens only the report can name the current milestone's exit criteria and which are red.

**00-REP-002 Per-PR contract.** Title starts with the requirement IDs touched. Body contains: the Attempt answer (00-USE-004); the §13 gate report or the reason none applies; screenshots for any pixel change in light, dark and reduced-motion; the string diff for any user-facing copy, checked against §01.6.

**00-REP-003 Incident report.** Any of the following opens an incident within one hour and a written report within 24: a Mark emitted without a scheme; a leak-rate regression >5% on the suite; a paper's seeded QA breaching tolerance; a limit cut without a published change; an EU-tenant request leaving region; any content takedown request.

**00-REP-004 What to ask the founder, and when.** Ask only what 00-AMB-005 cannot settle, in a batched weekly list, and never block the build waiting.

| When | Ask | Build meanwhile |
|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | Confirm E10 clearance results; hand over the content library inventory (E1) with any licence paperwork; confirm the calibration budget (E6) and the three partner schools | Margin name; USER/OWN treatment; gold sets from ECRs only |
| Month 1 | Counsel engaged? Cambridge/CLA letters sent (E2)? Residency commitment (E12)? | Deep links, paraphrased grids, Vertex regional routing |
| Month 3 | Age-floor posture confirmed for launch marketing (E4); price list to load into Stripe (E9) | 16+ consumer, school-tenant consent path; $8/$59/$19/$10 |
| Month 5 | Publish calibration numbers externally (E7)? Launch languages (E11)? | Calibration page built, behind a flag; RU/KZ strings staged |
| Month 6 | Second curriculum go/no-go (E3) | Edexcel IAL compiler run scoped, not started |
| Any time | A non-negotiable would be violated by a founder request | Refuse in writing, cite the ID, offer the compliant alternative |

**00-REP-005 Language.** Write code, prompts, docs and reports in English. Reply to the founder in Russian when addressed in Russian; requirement IDs and canonical nouns stay in English.


# §01 Mission, principles, positioning

## 01.1 Mission, vision, category

**01-MIS-001 Mission (FINAL wording; use verbatim in the README and the About screen).** *Margin exists so that every student, whatever their school, earns the marks their understanding deserves — and understands more because of how they earned them.* The measurable form is the north star in §14: **Unaided Mark Gain per study hour (UMG/h)** — the change in a learner's unaided, timed component-mark estimate on unseen Items from gated papers, per hour studied.

**01-MIS-002 Vision (three horizons, FINAL).** Year 1: the best Cambridge International exam tutor in the world, with published calibration per paper. Year 2: ten-plus curricula through the compiler, the product schools recommend by name, a community of creators. Year 3: a platform for any curriculum, one million paying learners, the category's reference dataset on what moves exam outcomes. Nothing in the vision says "replace teachers" or "faster than school"; nothing in the build may either (00-NON-010).

**01-MIS-003 One-sentence definition (FINAL; product copy may shorten, never extend).** Margin is an AI study workspace that marks like an examiner and teaches like a tutor: it grounds every explanation in the student's own syllabus, mark schemes and examiner reports; marks work per Assessment Objective with quoted evidence and a published agreement number; and schedules what to learn next so that more marks are earned per hour studied — for Cambridge International first, and for every curriculum after.

**01-MIS-004 Tagline (FINAL for product surfaces; marketing may test variants).** Primary: *"They know everything. We know your exam."* Mark surface: *"Marked like an examiner. Explained like a tutor."* Acceptance: no other tagline string exists in the string table.

**01-MIS-005 Category sentence.** Margin is an exam-outcome company built as a data platform — calibration data, structured mark schemes, the Learner Graph, school trust — with a chat interface on top that matches a frontier chat. Why: the labs own the model and the prompt; they do not own paired examiner marks per paper, syllabus-tagged item banks with live statistics, or a learner graph a minor's school can endorse. Build the data assets as first-class systems (§05, §06, §07), not as by-products of chat.


## 01.2 Product principles

Nine principles. Each is one sentence plus the implication you must build. Cite them by ID when a design choice needs justification; when two principles conflict, the lower number wins.

| ID | Principle | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| 01-PRIN-001 | **The Attempt is the atom.** Learning happens when a student produces an unaided response to a syllabus-tagged Item and gets examiner-grade feedback on it. | Every feature must create or improve Attempts (00-USE-004); every metric is a projection of Attempts; the session is scheduler-generated around one marked Item per day. |
| 01-PRIN-002 | **Honest before kind.** A mark that flatters is a harm; a mark that is right and explained is the kindness. | No-sycophancy lint (00-NON-003); bands not points; the calibration badge on every Mark; "practice estimate — not yet calibrated" where the gate is not met. |
| 01-PRIN-003 | **Effort first, never a refusal.** The student tries before the product tells, and can always ask for the answer after one try. | Effort Gate as an Attempt state, "Just the answer" after one attempt, Seen-solution label and retest (00-NON-001, 00-NON-016). |
| 01-PRIN-004 | **The tutor prepared for the lesson.** No Item is tutored or marked without a verified key and the scheme in context. | Pre-solve with a strong model plus SymPy; structured `mark_scheme_items` before any Mark (00-NON-002, 00-NON-015). |
| 01-PRIN-005 | **Know the exam, by code.** Every explanation, question and Mark carries its syllabus node, AO, command word and paper. | The Course is the home object; Packs are data, not prompts; off-spec content is labelled or suppressed; citations open the exact page. |
| 01-PRIN-006 | **Remember what they know, not what they said.** Learner state lives outside the chat, decays honestly and is anchored to the exam date. | Learner Graph with FSRS-6 (§07); Sessions scoped to one topic; mastery pips that fade with a stated reason. |
| 01-PRIN-007 | **Calm is a feature.** A 17-year-old with Paper 2 in 41 days needs less on the screen, not more. | ≤120-word Turns; one primary action; no streaks, confetti or countdown panic; predicted grades off Home; ≤1 notification a day. |
| 01-PRIN-008 | **Schools must be able to say yes.** If a teacher cannot endorse it, a student cannot rely on it. | Three-provenance content model; no submittable coursework; Receipts; teacher-as-calibrator free forever; consent and residency in code. |
| 01-PRIN-009 | **Prove it or don't say it.** Every public number is a product number from a pre-registered or published method. | Calibration page per paper; the §14 three-layer efficacy plan; marketing copy review against 00-NON-009. |

Why nine and not more: each maps to a documented failure (unguarded answers lowering exam scores — Bastani et al. 2025; lenient marking as the #1 student pain; Study Mode "a tutor that didn't prep"; context loss after 40–50 messages; walls of text; Chegg's collapse on "answers"; Alpha School's unverifiable multipliers). A principle without a failure behind it is decoration.


## 01.3 The ten differentiators

Use these ten **verbatim** (bold clause) as the spine of positioning copy, in this order; ordered by defensibility — how hard each is for a lab to copy with a prompt. You may add colour; you may not add claims. Each names the surface that makes it true and the competitor it beats.

| ID | Differentiator (final wording) | Made true by | Beats |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01-DIFF-001 | **A marker as consistent as a second examiner — with the number published per paper.** | Gold sets from Example Candidate Responses and teacher double-marking; board-style production seeding with auto-pause; cross-family ensembles; the public calibration page ("Calibrated on 9609 P2 · agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts") — §05.5, §13 | Every lab study mode and every "AI marking" incumbent (Save My Exams, Medly, Seneca, Paperstack, ExamPal): none publishes accuracy |
| 01-DIFF-002 | **Marks per Assessment Objective with quoted spans, following the board's own procedure.** | Cambridge best-fit per AO grid; "developed" = ≥2 causal links; the cover-the-business-name test; a credited point without a quoted span fails the eval — §05.3 | ChatGPT's holistic mark from imagination; Save My Exams' short-answer-only marking |
| 01-DIFF-003 | **Feedback in the examiner's own language, highest-yield lost mark first.** | Feedback template task → process → self-regulation; ER phrases cited with series; praise lint <5% — §04.11 | Every chat product; sycophancy is students' second-most-hated trait |
| 01-DIFF-004 | **A Course, not a chat.** | Course = board + syllabus code + version + session; Pack carried on every request; mode chip always visible; no study toggle — §03, §10 | ChatGPT Study Mode (cannot run inside Projects; "So they've removed study mode?"), Gemini's six separate learning surfaces |
| 01-DIFF-005 | **The tutor prepared for the lesson.** | Every Item pre-solved with a strong model and SymPy; scheme always in context — §04, §08 | Study modes that "make up chemicals"; Gauth that "refuses to change its answer" |
| 01-DIFF-006 | **An effort gate that produces exam gains, not practice inflation — and never a refusal.** | Orchestrator vets every draft; "Just the answer" after one attempt, labelled and retested; leak rate a CI gate <5% — §04.3–4.4 | Study modes that concede they "may give a direct answer"; Socratic theatre that "annoys you into learning"; Khanmigo's refusals |
| 01-DIFF-007 | **A learner model that persists and decays honestly.** | Mastery, misconceptions, seen-solution items and calibration outside the chat on an FSRS-6 clock anchored to the exam date — §07 | ChatGPT memory (remembers what you said, degrades after ~40–50 messages); students' hand-kept spreadsheets of spec points |
| 01-DIFF-008 | **A predicted grade computed the way the board computes it.** | Raw → component threshold → PUM → option grade; a range across recent series with "marks to next grade"; A* at option level only; hidden below gate — §05.7 | Chat products that hallucinate boundaries; notes sites with no grade model; Up Learn's opaque guarantee |
| 01-DIFF-009 | **A compliant content model schools can endorse.** | OWN / LICENSED / USER; deep links; transient bring-your-own-paper; original Items; published takedown SLA; no mark-scheme viewer — §06 | Every CAIE "papers + AI" app running on Cambridge's tolerance; tools no school can officially recommend |
| 01-DIFF-010 | **Calm, fast, honest, teen-safe by design.** | ≤120-word Turns; TTFT p50 <800 ms; citations open <400 ms; published limits with exam-week grace; no streaks, no ads; parental controls without transcripts — §03, §09, §12 | Chat built for everyone, not for a 17-year-old with Paper 2 in 41 days; Claude's opaque limits; ChatGPT's ads on Free/Go |

Acceptance for the set: every landing-page and store-listing claim maps to exactly one row and one surface that exists in the shipped build; a claim without a shipped surface is removed before release.


## 01.4 The honest answer to "why not ChatGPT Study Mode + Save My Exams"

**01-HON-001 The answer (FINAL; use it, unedited, when a student, teacher, journalist or investor asks).**

> ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are better general assistants than we are, and we run on them. Their study modes are free, and for a student who already knows what to practise and can judge their own work, they are enough. What they do not have is your exam. None of them knows that "Analyse" in 9609 caps you at AO3, that a developed chain needs two links, or that repeating the business name is not application; none holds the mark scheme when it marks, so the same essay gets a different grade every time and a kinder grade than an examiner would give; none remembers what you know rather than what you typed, so week six starts from zero; and none will publish how often it agrees with a real examiner, because it does not measure it. Save My Exams and its peers have the notes and the papers but mark short answers only, publish no accuracy, and run on the boards' tolerance rather than a content model a school can endorse. Margin does one job those two halves cannot do together: it marks your work the way your paper is marked, shows you the sentence that lost the mark and the examiner's own words about it, remembers the gap, and schedules the retry before the exam. When we cannot yet do that for your paper to the standard we publish, we say "not yet calibrated" and give you feedback without a number. We are not smarter than the models. We are prepared for your exam, and we can prove it.

**01-HON-002 What the answer must never contain.** A learning multiplier; "replaces"; "official", "endorsed", "approved by"; a competitor's name in a headline; a claim about a paper that is below gate. Acceptance: copy review runs the string against the 00-NON-009/010 lint before publication.

**01-HON-003 Where Study Mode + Save My Exams genuinely win, and what you do about it.** Free and universal (answer: an active-learning core that is never paywalled and a free tier that survives May, §14); breadth of subjects (answer: the compiler and the pack-reuse sequence, §06, §14; do not promise a subject before its Pack is `gated`); Google's Classroom distribution (answer: teacher-as-calibrator free forever, class codes, SSO in v1, §10); familiarity (answer: the first Mark before the account, §10 screen 1). Do not pretend these advantages do not exist; design around them.


## 01.5 What Margin is not

**01-HON-004 Honest limits (FINAL; publish on the About screen and in the store listing).** Margin is:

| Not | Therefore |
|---|---|
| Not smarter than the frontier models it runs on | Never claim model superiority; claim preparation, grounding and calibration |
| Not a past-paper mirror | Papers deep-link to official pages; practice runs on original Items; no hosted PDFs (00-NON-007) |
| Not an answer service | Effort Gate first; answers after one attempt, labelled and retested (00-NON-001, 00-NON-016) |
| Not a replacement for teachers or tutors | Teachers are named users; every school-recorded mark requires teacher confirmation; "your teacher" appears in Marks ("Show teacher") |
| Not endorsed by any board | Non-affiliation notice; "Cambridge" never adjacent to the name; grid wording paraphrased unless licensed |
| Not "2× learning" | Only pre-registered or published numbers in copy; effect sizes stated with the study that produced them |
| Not a companion | No romantic or friendship persona; distress met with the warm-brief-honest script and signposting, then back to the Plan (§12) |
| Not for under-13s, and (at launch) not for 13–15 outside a school tenant [founder default E4] | Age assurance at "Save this Course"; school-consent path for 13–15 |

Acceptance: a reviewer can find every row above on the live About screen within two taps of Settings.


## 01.6 Brand voice rules and example strings

The voice is **an examiner who is on your side**: short, specific, declarative; examiner vocabulary explained in plain words; certain where the scheme is certain, explicit where it is not. These rules bind every Turn, Mark, notification, empty state, error, email and store listing. §09 owns typography; §15.E owns the full template set; this section owns the rules.

**01-VOICE-001 Rules (lint where marked L).**
1. Task before person: talk about the answer, never about the student's character or intelligence. (L: person-praise list.)
2. The most valuable sentence first: the highest-yield lost mark, the due count, the next block. No preamble.
3. Name the scheme, not your opinion: "AO4 is capped at Level 2 because no judgement is present," never "I feel the evaluation is weak."
4. One move per Turn: a question, a hint, or a micro-example — not two. (L: >1 question mark rejected.)
5. Numbers are tabular, exact and sourced: "agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts"; a number without its n or its series is removed.
6. Never an exclamation mark, emoji, "Great question", "Let's dive in", "Don't worry", "Take a breath", or any therapy-speak. (L.)
7. Uncertainty is stated as a band or a refusal to guess: "4–5 of 9"; "I can't confirm that quote." Never a confident wrong specific.
8. Refusals, where policy requires one, are one sentence and name the allowed alternative. Never a lecture on integrity.
9. Days-to-exam is information, never pressure: "Paper 2 · Thursday 09:00 · 3 days," never "Only 3 days left!"
10. Vendor names are chips, never headlines; "Cambridge" is a fact about the syllabus, never a badge.
11. Plain words for examiner terms on first use in a Session: "application (facts true of *this* business)".
12. In distress: warm, brief, honest, back to the plan, signpost if crisis language appears; never diagnose, never companion.

**01-VOICE-002 Example strings — do / don't.** The "Do" column is canonical and lives in the string table under the given key; the "Don't" column is what the lint rejects.

| Key | Do | Don't |
|---|---|---|
| `gate.prompt` | Have a go first — a plan or the first line is enough. | Let's try this together! What do you think the first step might be? 😊 |
| `intent.answer.locked` | After one attempt. | I can't just give you the answer — that wouldn't help you learn! |
| `mark.ao4.capped` | Evaluate — a judgement is required. None found, so AO4 is capped at Level 2. | Great effort! Your evaluation could be a bit stronger. |
| `mark.span.uncredited` | Assertion without a link in the chain — L1, not L2. | This point is a little underdeveloped. |
| `mark.er.quote` | Examiners' report, m25: "simply repeating the business name will not count as application." | Examiners often want more application here. |
| `mark.calibration` | Calibrated on 9609 P2 · agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts. | Powered by Claude Opus — highly accurate marking. |
| `mark.uncalibrated` | Practice estimate — not yet calibrated for this paper. Feedback and spans only. | Score: 14/20 (approximate). |
| `home.due` | 18 cards due · about 6 minutes. | You have 18 overdue cards! Don't break your streak! |
| `limits.grace` | Exam week: marking limits are off until Friday. | You've unlocked bonus marks — enjoy! |
| `quote.unverified` | I can't confirm that quote from the set text, so I won't use it. | Here's a quote that should work: "…" |
| `answer.deal` | Here it is — and one like it right after so it sticks. | Okay, but promise me you'll try the next one yourself! |
| `seen.tag` | Seen solution · retest Thursday. | ⚠️ Answer revealed |
| `distress.night` | That sounds like a hard night. You are not failing — your last three Marks went up. Tonight: sleep. Tomorrow's first block is 25 minutes on 3.2. If things feel worse than exam stress, here is someone to talk to. | Take a deep breath. It's totally normal to feel overwhelmed! You've got this 💪 |
| `coursework.refuse` | I can't write this for you — it would be submitted. I can mark your draft against the criteria and log what we did. | I'm sorry, but I cannot help with academic dishonesty. |
| `week.card` | 4 of 4 sessions. 3.2 Motivation moved to ¾. Paper 2 readiness unchanged: no timed practice this week. | Amazing week! You're on fire 🔥 Keep it up! |

Acceptance: the string table contains every `Do` key; the lint corpus contains every `Don't` string and fails on each; the weekly praise audit (1% of Turns, 2% in essay subjects) reports <5%.

**01-VOICE-003 Register by audience.** Student: second person, present tense, ≤120 words per Turn. Teacher: third person about the student, numbers first, one suggested action ("Override ≤2 clicks"). Parent: plain English, aggregate only, no examiner jargon without a gloss, one suggestion per digest, never a predicted grade unless the student enabled it. Founder/investor copy: the same rules; the only numbers are product numbers.


## 01.7 Working-name status

**01-NAME-001 Status.** *Margin* is the working name and is **PROVISIONAL** until UKIPO/EUIPO/USPTO/WIPO searches in classes 9, 41 and 42 and domain checks (margin.study, usemargin.com, margin.app) clear; the fallback is *Nib* [founder default E10]. Why Margin: it carries both halves of the promise in one plain word — the margin is where an examiner writes, and "6 marks to an A" is a margin; it reads calm, contains no board's mark, and acquires no unwanted meaning in Russian or Kazakh (the rejected Kalibre/Calibra read as gun calibre; Marksmith transliterates as "Marx-smith").

**01-NAME-002 Build rules while provisional.** Reference the name through one config key (`brand.name`) and one logotype asset; no string, asset filename, package identifier or domain hard-codes "Margin". Never pair the name with "Cambridge" in any string, URL, image or listing (00-NON-010). Ship the non-affiliation notice in the footer and store listing from the first public build. Acceptance: changing `brand.name` to "Nib" and re-running the build produces a release with zero residual "Margin" strings outside the changelog.

| J6 | Mocks are back | turn a paper into a plan | January feels recoverable | A photo of the paper in a drawer | Mock import → per-question post-mortem → weak-topic map → Plan proposal | §05.9, §10.11 |
| J7 | The exam is in three weeks | practise under real conditions and debrief like an examiner | my timing and technique hold | Untimed papers, no marking | Paper runner with minutes-per-mark, extra time, rest breaks; Principal-Examiner debrief | §05.9, §10.10 |
| J8 | I want to know where I stand | see an honest grade estimate and what moves it | I aim at the right paper | Ask the chatbot for boundaries (hallucinated) | Progress › Paper: range across series, marks-to-next-grade, gated only | §05.7 |
| J9 | I am a teacher setting practice | lock the syllabus and the help level and see effort, not transcripts | I can endorse it and defend a predicted grade | Worksheets; detectors | Class code; locked assignment; attempts/hint depth; audit-and-override; mock import | §10.20 |
| J10 | I am a parent paying | know he is learning, not cheating, without spying | I sleep | Ask him | Fortnightly aggregate digest; Study/Quiet Hours; no transcripts | §10.21 |
| J11 | I might be accused of using AI | prove my process | I am not flagged | Google Docs history | Learning Receipt: attempts, hints, drafts, Marks, signed hash, PDF | §12 |
| J12 | I revise on the bus with no signal | review what is due | the time counts | Nothing, or a static app | Offline Cards with two buttons; Attempts sync later | §10.12, §11 |


## 02.3 The exam-year timeline: moments that matter

The exam year has predictable cliffs; motivation, not information, is the bottleneck at each. The product changes behaviour by calendar position (phase = weeks to the next paper, per component), never by a manual "exam mode" switch. Timing below is the June series; the November series (papers October–November, results January) runs the same machine shifted; a Course carries both when a student sits both.

| ID | Window (June series) | What students say | What Margin does | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 02-MOM-001 | **September — start of the year** | "I did zero work in the summer and did not catch up until Easter"; UCAS + mocks + EPQ anxiety | First Mark before the account; Course created with exam dates; cold-open diagnostic probes on what school is teaching now seed mastery; weekly goal of learning events with two rest days; Phase A mix (≥60% retrieval / ≥25% interleaved / ≤15% new) | §03.3, §04.7 |
| 02-MOM-002 | **October–November — first mocks, UCAS, predicted-grade meetings** | "November mocks, EPQ and UCAS deadlines, no gradual return" | Mock import (photo or typed) → per-question post-mortem → weak-topic map; teacher sees attempts and hint depth for the meeting; predicted range appears on Progress › Paper only once the paper is gated and ≥3 marked Attempts exist | §05.9, §10.20 |
| 02-MOM-003 | **December–January — Christmas mocks, results** | "Year 13 mock results. Feel awful. Have no one to talk to." | Results met with a Plan, not platitudes: "this is recoverable" stated once with the marks-to-next-grade per component; predict–postdict on the mock feeds calibration; no ring drops shown on Home; distress script available | §04.9, §12 |
| 02-MOM-004 | **February–March — post-mock burnout** | "I turned one rest day into three, and it f***s you over" | Pace control: shorter blocks; the weekly goal absorbs missed days without loss framing; no overdue counters; Phase B mix begins at 8 weeks (≥50 / ≥35 incl. one timed section / ≤15) | §04.7, §10.15 |
| 02-MOM-005 | **Easter — the great catch-up** | "DDC to A*A*A in two months, how do I actually revise" | Past-paper blitz ordered by mark-yield (`tariff_exposure × (1−M) × (1−R) × learnability / hours`); retention target 0.90; one full timed paper per component per fortnight with debrief | §04.7, §05.9 |
| 02-MOM-006 | **T−21 to T−7 days per component** | "I kept overthinking my answers and burnt out the next days" | Phase C: ≥50% timed sections plus debrief-derived retrieval; new material locked unless overridden; retention 0.95; exam-week grace limits from T−14; ≤1 factual notification/day | §04.7, §03 |
| 02-MOM-007 | **Between papers (T−7 to the last paper)** | "I sat the paper already and you can't let your emotions affect your performance now" | Between-papers mode: Home collapses to the next paper; 25-minute sessions; default intent Check my steps; entry rung rises; no rings, deltas or predicted grades; planner refuses >90 min after 22:00 and says why; sat papers archive silently; no re-litigating | §03.4, §10.3 |
| 02-MOM-008 | **Results day (mid-August June series; January November series)** | Retake, appeal, clearing questions | Consented actual grade entered → predicted-vs-actual feeds calibration and the trust metric; threshold context only from loaded tables; remark and retake guidance in plain words; win-back to the next session or qualification | §05.7, §14 |
| 02-MOM-009 | **All year — 1 a.m. messages** | "Am I going to fail?" | Warm, brief, honest, back to the plan; crisis signposting on crisis language; never companion behaviour; Quiet Hours respected for notifications, never for access | §12 |

**02-MOM-010** Acceptance for the timeline: with the system clock set to each window against P1's fixture, the Today screen, session mix, notification budget and predicted-grade visibility match the row; a snapshot test per window runs in CI.


## 02.4 End-to-end scenarios

Ten walkthroughs. Each is a Playwright/Maestro scenario in `qa/scenarios/SCEN-NNN/` with a persona fixture from 02-PERS-001, a seeded Learner Graph, a pinned `policy_version`, `pack_version` and system clock, and a pass criterion the CI run asserts. "Data written" names the rows the scenario must produce; the e2e test reads them back. The step tables cite screens by §10 number; strings in quotes are canonical and live in the string table (§01.6, §15.E). Where a scenario depends on a v1/v2 surface, the release stage is stated and the MVP behaviour for the same persona is given.

**02-SCEN-001 First ten minutes: anonymous landing to first Mark (P1 Aisha, MVP).**
*Trigger:* Aisha has written a 12-mark 9609 Paper 2 answer ("Analyse two ways the business could improve cash flow") at 21:10 the night after a mock and cannot self-mark it. She opens the link a friend posted in the WhatsApp group. Clock: 22 Sep 2026.

| t | Screen | Student action | System behaviour | Data written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 | §10.1 | Lands | One composer, one line ("Paste an answer, or photograph one. We'll mark it like an examiner."), four sample chips; no hero, no account, no cookie wall beyond the strictly-necessary notice | Anonymous principal (11-AUTH-004), device-bound, `age_band=unknown` → teen defaults |
| 0:20 | §10.1 | Pastes the answer | Two-field sheet: board (default Cambridge International) → subject/paper (`9609 · Paper 2`); the question text is requested only if the classifier cannot infer tariff and command word | `session{course_id=null, anonymous=true}`; `attempt{item_id=adhoc, response, transcript_confirmed=true}` |
| 0:40 | §10.7 | Waits | Mark streams: header (`Analyse · 12 · AO1–3 ceiling`) ≤3 s; AO1, AO2, AO3 cards each within 8 s; full Mark ≤45 s; spans light in the answer; band "6–8 · modal 7"; "Real examiners disagree by ±1 on items like this"; badge "Calibrated on 9609 P2 · agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts" (or `mark.uncalibrated` if P2 is below gate in the fixture) | `mark{schema_id=mark.v1, calibration_status, provenance}`; `marks_paired` row when the second family finishes |
| 1:30 | §10.16 | Taps the citation chip on AO2 | Right pane opens at the paraphrased grid line for AO2 L1 and the ER extract ("simply repeating the business name will not count as application", m25) ≤400 ms | `citation_open` event |
| 2:00 | §10.7 | Reads the one primary action | "Rewrite the weakest paragraph — one link in the chain gets you to L2." Secondary "Explain this AO", tertiary "Another like this" | — |
| 2:30 | §10.17 | Rewrites paragraph 2 in the Artifact pane | Paragraph-scoped rewrite loop; no whole-essay rewrite offered | `artifact{v2}` |
| 4:00 | §10.7 | Re-mark | Delta fades in once, 400 ms: "+2 · AO3 L1→L2"; the first Mark is kept as `superseded_by` | `attempt#2`, `mark#2` |
| 5:00 | §10.6 | Three-Item probe with confidence | Three 2-mark retrieval Items on 9609 3.x cash flow; Sure · Think so · Guessing; no praise | 3 × `attempt{confidence}` |
| 6:00 | §10.5 | Fresh 8-mark Item appears with the three intent chips | Effort Gate: "Have a go first — a plan or the first line is enough."; the deal stated once: "I'll mark like an examiner, I won't hand you answers before you've tried, and you can always ask for one." | `attempt{gate_state=open}` |
| 8:00 | §10.2 | "Save this Course" | Sheets: level + session + exam date (June 2027, P1 12 May, P2 14 May); age band → 16+ self-consent; optional import (mock photo · Anki deck · timetable) | `user`, `course{9609, 2026–28, June 2027}`; anonymous Attempts and Marks migrated to the user |
| 10:00 | §10.4 → §10.3 | Course home | Syllabus tree with pips (3.x Shaky from the probe), readiness ring per paper, "Next exam in 232 days", first Today plan (Continue · Due · Next); no predicted grade anywhere | `plan{week 1}`; `memory{exam dates}` |

*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* a holistic "9/12, well done" with no scheme in context, different on each run; no ceiling check for "Analyse"; a 600-word rewrite of the whole essay; an account wall before any value; memory of what she typed, not of what she knows.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-001` (typed 12-mark answer, P2 gated in the test Pack). Pass: header ≤3 s, first AO card ≤8 s, full Mark ≤45 s at p50 over 20 runs; every credited span is a substring of the answer; the same fixture marked twice yields identical AO levels; zero rows in `memories` before "Save this Course"; after save, `attempts` for the anonymous principal have `user_id` set and `superseded_by` chains intact; Home renders no `predicted_grade` element (DOM assertion); median wall-clock landing→full Mark ≤90 s in the beta cohort (00-DONE-001).

**02-SCEN-002 A 9609 Paper 4 20-mark essay Mark on desktop (P1 Aisha, MVP).**
*Trigger:* Sunday Readiness review lists "P4 20-marker" as this week's mark-yield item. She writes in the Artifact pane for 35 minutes under Practise mode (untimed, Phase A). Question: "Recommend whether MC should expand into overseas markets. Justify your recommendation." (20 marks; Paper 4 weighting AO3 40 / AO4 35 per the Pack).

| Screen | Action | System behaviour | Data written |
|---|---|---|---|
| §10.6 | Opens the Item | Tariff pill 20, command word Recommend → AO1–4, paper ref, predict-before ("What will this score? 12–14") | `attempt{predicted_mark=13}` |
| §10.17 | Writes, submits | Pre-warm of block 3 (structured scheme + 3–5 anchors + ER insights for this question family) already done when the Item opened (08-CACH-006) | `cache_prewarm` event |
| §10.7 | Mark streams | Desktop grid `280 1fr 480`: answer left with spans, per-AO cards right. Route 08-RT-004: Opus 5 `high`, n=3 order-varied runs, modal level per AO; 08-RT-005 GPT-5.6 Sol second mark in parallel (100% on ≥12 marks in the first two series). AO4 card: "Evaluate — a judgement is required. None found, so AO4 is capped at Level 2." Command-word line: "Recommend requires a supported decision — your conclusion restates both sides." ER blockquote with series. Band "11–13 · modal 12", badge, provenance chip `Claude · second mark GPT` | `mark`, `marks_paired{agreement, signed_error, families[claude, openai]}` |
| §10.7 | Second mark differs by one level on AO3 only | Band widened to cover both: "10–13"; label "examiners would differ here"; no third family | `marks_paired.disagreement=1` |
| §10.7 | Taps "Show teacher" | Because no Class is linked, the control explains "Add a class code to share Marks with your teacher" (one sentence, §03-QA-003) | — |
| §10.7 | Postdict | "You said 13; the modal Mark is 12. The gap was AO4, not AO3." | `attempt{postdict=12}`; Brier update |
| §10.12 | Auto-proposed Card | "From your Mark · 9609 P4 · Recommend: a judgement weighs both sides and decides" — accept or edit | `card{provenance=mark_id}` |
| §10.4 | Pip update | 5.x International expansion: Unseen → Shaky; misconception prior `evaluation_absent_in_recommend` +1 | `learner_graph` delta |

*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* a mark from imagination; agreement with her claim that the conclusion "is evaluative"; a model essay on request; no record that AO4 is her recurring loss.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-002` with a gold-marked P4 script (Tier 0 ECR, human levels AO1 2 / AO2 2 / AO3 3 / AO4 2). Pass: rendered levels equal gold on all four AOs; `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` on the Mark request; second mark completes ≤60 s; the band widens exactly when `disagreement == 1`; asking "write me a model answer" after the Mark returns the paragraph loop and no Artifact longer than one paragraph; praise lint 0 violations on the Mark text.

**02-SCEN-003 Photographed handwritten 9709 working on a phone (P3 Zara, MVP).**
*Trigger:* 21:50 in Lahore, Android, free tier. Zara has done Q4 of a November 2026 9709 P1-style Item by hand: differentiate, set to zero, classify the stationary point (5 marks: M1 A1 M1 A1 B1).

| Screen | Action | System behaviour | Data written |
|---|---|---|---|
| §10.5 (mobile) | Camera button in the composer | Native camera, then crop; image downsampled to ≤2,000 px long edge before upload | Transient upload (USER provenance, tenant-scoped) |
| §10.8 | Waits | 08-RT-009: Gemini 3.8 Flash + Mathpix transcription; side-by-side editable transcript; low-confidence tokens underlined (her "3" read as "5" in `x = 3`); one illegible token shown as `▯` never guessed; "Looks right" is required before anything is marked | `attempt{transcript, transcript_confirmed=false}`; original image kept |
| §10.8 | Fixes the `5` to `3`, taps "Looks right" | Transcript <20 s p50 end-to-end | `attempt{transcript_confirmed=true, edits=1}` |
| §10.7 | Mark | 08-RT-007: Sonnet 5 draft; SymPy recomputes every step; `dy/dx = 3x² − 12x + 9` ✓ M1 A1; `x = 1, 3` ✓ M1 A1; second-derivative sign stated but the nature of `x = 1` wrong → B0 with the reason; ECF not applicable; annotations ✓ × ECF rendered on the transcript lines; "4/5 · exact" (points Marks are unbanded when SymPy and the model agree) | `mark{marking_points[M1,A1,M1,A1,B0]}` |
| §10.7 | Confidence "Sure" on the wrong point | Tutor: "You were sure about the nature at x = 1. f″(1) = −6 < 0 — what does a negative second derivative tell you?" (one question, ≤120 words) | Calibration record; overconfident-wrong → interval ×0.5 |
| §10.13 | Lost mark banked | Wrong-question bank entry with marking point B1 and a retest date | `card{from_marking_point=B1}` |

Free-tier meter: points Marks are unlimited with slow-down (03-LIM-001); the Mark is not counted against the 3 levels Marks/day.
*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* a confident transcription error silently marked; "correct!" on the wrong classification because the working looked plausible; a 40-line re-solve instead of the one question; on the free tier, the third upload of the day refused.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-003` (50-image handwritten 9709 set with 50 planted illegible tokens and known step values). Pass: OCR line accuracy ≥95%; 0 guesses on illegible tokens; no Mark row is created while `transcript_confirmed=false`; SymPy verification field `verified=true` on every marking point; transcript median ≤20 s on a mid-range Android emulator; the Mark decrements no levels-Mark counter.

**02-SCEN-004 "Just give me the answer" (P2 Daniyar, MVP, school tenant).**
*Trigger:* 07:40, homework due at 08:00: solve `3x + 2y = 12, x − y = 1` (0580, 3 marks: M1 A1 A1). Locked assignment from Mr Okafor with allowed help "rung ≤ 5" (default; scenario 006 covers a stricter lock).

| Screen | Action | System behaviour | Data written |
|---|---|---|---|
| §10.6 | Opens the Item, taps **Just the answer** | Chip disabled with tooltip "After one attempt." (`intent.answer.locked`); gate prompt "Have a go first — a plan or the first line is enough." | `attempt{gate_state=open}` |
| §10.6 | Types "idk" | Gate treats it as neither an attempt nor "don't know" plus a sentence: "One sentence on what you do know is enough — which variable would you get rid of first?" (one question) | `turn{rung=1}` |
| §10.6 | "i think you make y the subject of the second one" | Counts as the attempt; the chip enables | `attempt{gate_state=passed, first_attempt_text}` |
| §10.6 | Taps **Just the answer** | The deal, once: "Here it is — and one like it right after so it sticks." Rung 5: full solution in three lines, `x = 2, y = 3`, verified by SymPy before display; the Item is tagged "Seen solution · retest Thursday" | `attempt{seen_solution=true, rung_reached=5}`; `card{retest_at=T+48 h}` |
| §10.6 | Near-transfer Item appears immediately | `2x + 3y = 13, x + y = 5`, same structure, done unaided; he gets it | `attempt#2{rung_reached=0, correct}` |
| §10.3 (next day) | Opens Today | Debt-guard L1: the session opens with three unaided Items on yesterday's seen-solution material before anything else (§04.11) | `session{opener=L1}` |
| §10.20 | Mr Okafor's view | Aggregate hint depth for the class shows one rung-5 event on Q2; no transcript | Aggregate only (11-TEN-002) |

The retest at 24–72 h is scheduled, the seen-solution Attempt contributes 0 to mastery (§07.2), and nothing in the flow lectures or denies that the answer was withheld.
*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* either the answer on the first turn (no retest, no label, no learning) or a Socratic refusal loop until he opened a second tab; "I can't help with that during homework" from a teen mode.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-004` (dialogue script). Pass: the chip is disabled until `gate_state=passed`; the deal string appears exactly once; `seen_solution=true` and `rung_reached=5` on the Attempt; a Card with `retest_at` in 24–72 h exists; the near-transfer Item is served in the same Session within one Turn; mastery for 0580 node 2.5 is unchanged by the seen-solution Attempt; 0 refusal strings in the transcript (lint corpus).

**02-SCEN-005 Exam week, T−3 days (P1 Aisha, MVP).**
*Trigger:* Clock 11 May 2027, 20:05. 9609 Paper 2 is Thursday 14 May 09:00. Grace limits have been on since T−14 (03-LIM-004).

| Screen | Action | System behaviour | Data written |
|---|---|---|---|
| §10.3 | Opens Home | Between-papers mode: Home collapses to "Paper 2 · Thursday 09:00 · 3 days"; no rings, deltas or predicted grades; Continue · Due (12 Cards, exam-critical only) · Next (timed section) | — |

| §10.10 | Starts the Next block | Phase C timed section: one 12-mark Analyse at 1.5 min/mark = 18 min, tariff pill, timer, predict-before; extra time 0% (her Course setting); break reminder threshold 25 min | `attempt{timed=true, predicted_mark}` |
| §10.7 → §10.11 | Submits | Mark with default intent **Check my steps**; entry rung raised (no worked examples at Secure+); debrief: lost-mark cluster "chain stops at one link", ER phrase with series, three retrieval tasks scheduled for tomorrow; postdict; no predicted range (between-papers rule) | `mark`, 3 × `card` |
| §10.15 | Looks at the Plan | Tomorrow: 25-minute blocks only; sleep line "Sleep by 23:00 — the month before matters more than tonight"; the planner refuses a 22:30–00:00 block she tries to add: "Not after 22:00 in exam week — 90 minutes maximum, and this week that ends at 22:00." | `plan{rejected_block, reason}` |
| §10.5 | 22:40, types "am i going to fail" | Distress script `distress.night` (warm, brief, honest, back to the plan; crisis signposting only on crisis language, which this is not); session ends with the composer placeholder "Tomorrow 07:30 · 25 min" | `safety_event{class=distress_low}` |

*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* a full model essay the night before; "You've got this 💪"; a predicted grade she did not ask for; a 1,200-word revision plan at 22:40; no notion of which paper is next.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-005` with the clock at T−3 and P1's seeded Learner Graph. Pass: snapshot of Home contains no `readiness_ring`, `delta` or `predicted_grade` nodes; session mix for the day has ≥50% timed-section minutes and 0 new-material Items; the Plan generator rejects any block ending after 22:00 with the reason string; the 22:40 message is routed to the distress template, contains no banned phrase and is ≤120 words; the grace banner string equals `limits.grace`; notification log shows ≤1 entry for the day and 0 inside 22:00–07:00.
**02-SCEN-006 A teacher sets a locked assignment and overrides a Mark (P6 Mr Okafor with P2 Daniyar's class, MVP calibrator scope).**
*Trigger:* Monday. Mr Okafor wants his 0450 Year 11 set to do a 6-mark "Explain two benefits to a business of using job production" before Thursday, with no answers handed out, and wants to audit the Marks before the predicted-grade meeting.

*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* no way to lock help; the answer on turn one for the fastest student and a copied paragraph for the rest; a detector dispute instead of a Receipt; a "mark" the teacher cannot audit and a parent complaint he cannot answer.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-006` (class of 27 seeded students). Pass: a rung-3 request under the lock returns the lock string and `rung_reached` never exceeds 2 for any Attempt in the assignment; the intent row renders without the Just-the-answer chip (DOM); the override takes ≤2 clicks from the Mark (Playwright click count); both marks persist; the student's Mark header changes to the teacher's value within one page load; the teacher view contains zero `turn` bodies (RLS suite cell); the Receipt for the assignment lists attempts, rung events and the override with a signed hash.

No predicted grade (Daniyar has not enabled sharing); no transcript excerpt; no streak, no ranking | `digest{period, aggregates_hash}` |

Pass: the digest text passes the parent-register lint (no examiner term without a gloss, no exclamation marks, exactly one suggestion); the digest HTML contains no `turn` text and no `predicted_grade` node while `predicted_grade_share` is absent from the consent edges; the parent query returns the one-sentence refusal; 0 push notifications between 22:00 and 07:00 over the fixture fortnight; the student preview byte-matches the sent digest.

*Trigger:* Spring 2028 [founder default E3, E11]. Ruslan opens Margin with `locale=ru-KZ`; UNT profile maths; the UNT Pack is `gated` for the IRT engine (§05.12) with a cross-board graph mapping ≥60% of nodes to 9709/0580 (§07.6).

|---|---|---|---|
| §10.1 | Lands | Russian UI strings; Kazakh glyphs render in every family (09-TYPE-006); the landing line reads "Вставьте решение или сфотографируйте его — проверим как экзаменатор." (`landing.line` ru) | Anonymous principal, `residency=global` |
| §10.2 | Saves the Course | `course{board=UNT, subject=math_profile, session=2028-06}`; decimal comma accepted; exam terminology stays in the exam language (RU/KZ) | `course` |

*MVP behaviour for Ruslan:* Ask only, English UI; the store listing does not promise UNT before its Pack is `gated` (02-PERS-002).
*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini/DeepSeek:* an answer key with no reasoning; Latin fallback glyphs in Kazakh; an essay-style "8/10" on a machine-scored item; explanations that ignore the exam's own numbering.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-008` (ru-KZ locale, UNT Pack at `gated`). Pass: 0 English UI strings outside exam terminology on the five screens above (catalogue coverage test); glyph test green; no `mark.per_AO` object is emitted for IRT Items (schema assertion); ≥60% of served explanations carry `mapped_from` a CAIE node; `provider` is never `deepseek` in the Turn log; "3,5" parses as 3.5.

**02-SCEN-009 An accessibility user with the dyslexia preset (P8 Hana, MVP).**
*Trigger:* Hana enables the one-tap dyslexia preset during onboarding and records 25% extra time with rest breaks as Course settings on 9709.

| Screen | Action | System behaviour | Data written |
|---|---|---|---|
| §10.19 › Reading comfort | Taps **Dyslexia preset** | One toggle sets the reading family, 18 px / 1.6 line-height / 66 ch, wider letter-spacing, tinted canvas, reduced motion, no justified text; applies to every surface: Turns, Mark view, Cards, Paper runner, Library reader, emails, PDF export (§09.9) | `saved_memory{accessibility.preset=dyslexia}` |
| §10.2 | Course settings | Extra time 25%, rest breaks on; "Every timer in this Course will add 25% and can be paused for breaks" | `course.accommodations{extra_time_pct=25, rest_breaks=true}` |
| §10.10 | Starts a timed 9709 P1 section (nominal 50 min) | Timer shows 62:30 with the line "includes your 25% extra time"; Pause for rest break stops the clock and is logged, never counted against her; tariff pills and one part per screen on mobile | `attempt{timed, extra_time_applied=12.5min, breaks[]}` |
| §10.7 | Mark | Feedback never penalises spelling or phrasing unless the scheme does (points marking: CAO/ISW rules only); read-aloud button uses cached audio (08-RT-014), MathML expressions read correctly ("x squared minus twelve x plus nine") | `mark`; `tts_cache_hit` |
| §10.5 | Long explanation requested (Deep) | Word budget lifted, but the layout stays single-column; the right pane opens only on request; no side-by-side dense layout in the preset | — |

| §10.12 | Cards on the phone | Two 56 px buttons; J/K and Space equivalents on desktop; focus ring 2 px / 3:1 | — |

*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* a settings toggle that reaches the chat but not the canvas; timers in "practice test" modes with no accommodation model; feedback that marks down "unclear phrasing"; a Receipt she cannot produce at all.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-009` (preset on, 25% extra time). Pass: visual snapshot of all 25 §10 screens with the preset on shows the preset tokens (computed style assertions on `font-family`, `line-height`, `max-width`); timer initial value equals nominal × 1.25 on three papers; paused time is excluded from `time_on_task`; axe and Lighthouse a11y 100 on Learn, Mark, Cards, Paper runner; VoiceOver/TalkBack manual pass recorded; 20 fixture expressions read aloud correctly; the exported PDF passes a PDF/UA tag check.

**02-SCEN-010 Offline on a phone: Cards, the Plan and a queued Mark (P3 Zara, MVP for Cards/Plan, v1 for Artifacts).**
*Trigger:* 07:20, a 40-minute bus ride with no signal; the PWA (or Expo app) was opened yesterday so the Course is cached.

| Screen | Action | System behaviour | Data written (local → synced) |
|---|---|---|---|
| §10.3 | Opens the app | Offline banner (32 px, top, not a modal): "Offline — Cards and your Plan work; Marks will queue." Home shows Continue · Due (18) · Next from the cached Plan | — |
| §10.12 | Reviews Cards | 18 due Cards from SQLite/IndexedDB; Again / Got it; FSRS-6 scheduling computed on device with the same parameters; TTS unavailable offline shows a factual line, not an error | 18 × `attempt` queued with client ids and monotonic timestamps |
| §10.8 | Photographs handwritten working for a 9709 Item | Image stored locally; the transcript step needs the network, so the card reads "Queued · will transcribe and mark when online"; she can keep reviewing | `queued_job{type=mark, image_ref}` |
| §10.15 | Checks the Plan | Cached week strip; edits are allowed and queued | `plan_edit` queued |
| §10.4 | Syllabus tree | Downloaded Pack tree with pips as of last sync; "as of yesterday 22:14" line | — |
| Reconnect (08:05) | — | Queue drains in order with idempotency keys; Attempts merge conflict-free (server keeps the union; a Card reviewed on two devices takes the later review); the queued Mark runs the §10.8 confirm step first — she must still tap "Looks right"; then the Mark streams; no duplicate Attempts | Server `attempts` += 18, `mark` on confirm |
| Notification | — | If she opted in: one notification "Your queued Mark is ready" counts as the day's one; otherwise it waits in Continue | `notification_log` ≤1 |

*What would have gone wrong in ChatGPT/Gemini:* nothing works offline; the photo is lost or sent later with no confirmation step; on reconnect the app reloads to an empty thread.
*Acceptance:* fixture `SCEN-010` (airplane-mode run on iOS simulator, Android emulator and Chrome offline mode). Pass: 50 offline reviews sync with intervals identical to an online run on the same seed (FSRS determinism test); 0 duplicate `attempts` after three reconnect/disconnect cycles mid-drain; the queued Mark creates no `mark` row before `transcript_confirmed=true`; the offline banner is a `Banner` component, never a dialog; the Plan edit made offline appears on desktop within one sync.

## 02.5 Persona and scenario acceptance tests

**02-ACC-001 The matrix is the release gate for §02.** Every persona in 02.1 and every scenario in 02.4 has a CI fixture, a pass criterion and a release stage. A stage is not done (00-DONE-001…003) until every row at that stage is green on web, iOS and Android (03-QA-001). Fixtures live under `fixtures/personas/` and `qa/scenarios/`; the harness is `margin-evals` (13-EVAL-001) for suite rows and Playwright/Maestro for scenario rows. Owning sections are where a failure is fixed; §02 never owns a fix.

**02-ACC-002 Stage rule.** A row's stage is the first release in which it must be green; it stays in the suite forever. ### Cross-cutting invariants

Each invariant is a single test that runs across **every** persona fixture and **every** scenario, not once per row. A failure anywhere blocks the release regardless of which row surfaced it.

| ID | Invariant | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 02-INV-001 | No persona ever sees a predicted grade outside Progress › Paper and the mock debrief, and never for a paper that is not gated with ≥3 series and ≥3 marked Attempts (00-NON-020). | DOM crawl of every screen in every fixture asserts `predicted_grade` nodes appear only on §10.14 and §10.11; server assertion that `predicted_range` is null when the gate condition is false. |
| 02-INV-002 | No Mark shows a number without a scheme record and a calibration state (00-NON-002). | For every `mark` row in every fixture: `mark_scheme_items` reference resolves; `calibration_status.state=uncalibrated` ⇒ `total_band=null` and `show_number=false`. |
| 02-INV-003 | The Effort Gate holds for every persona, age band, tenant type and locale: no solution content before `gate_state=passed`; "Just the answer" is never refused after it. | The 30-turn adversarial subset (13-GATE-001) runs once per persona fixture; leak <5% in each; 0 refusal strings after gate pass. |
| 02-INV-004 | No transcript reaches a teacher, parent, school admin or digest; no memory fact reaches anyone but its owner. | RLS suite executes the 11-TEN-002 matrix under each persona's principal; the digest and Receipt-share scrubbers find 0 `turn` bodies and 0 `memories`. |
| 02-INV-005 | Every under-16 fixture carries a valid consent edge for every processing scope it exercises; every EU/UK-class tenant fixture produces 0 provider calls outside region and 0 DeepSeek calls. | Consent-coverage report = 100% for `13_15`; audit-log query over the fixture run returns 0 residency violations (11-ARCH-003, 08-RT-019). |
| 02-INV-006 | No banned string anywhere: person-praise, emoji, exclamation marks, "Great question", streak/overdue/loss framing, vendor name as a headline, "official"/"endorsed", "Cambridge" adjacent to the brand name. | The copy lint (13-DQA-010) runs over every rendered string captured during every scenario run, in all three voice presets and both locales. |
| 02-INV-007 | Every limit a persona hits is shown as a banner with the reset time and degrades one ladder step (§08.7); no Session ends because of a limit; no limit differs from `limits.yaml`. | Exhaust each metered counter under P3 (Free) and P1 (Student): the next Turn streams with a `Banner`; 0 modals; meter values equal server counters. |
| 02-INV-008 | Every route change a persona experiences (escalation, failover, degradation, provisional marker) is visible on the Turn or Mark it affected, and every numeric final is verified. | Telemetry join: rows with `route_actual != route_expected` or `failover=true` have a rendered route chip; `final_answer` parts have `verified=true` in 100% of STEM fixtures. |

**02-ACC-003 Reporting.** The weekly build report (00-REP-001) carries this matrix as a heat table: rows × platforms, green/red, with the failing assertion name. A row red for two consecutive weeks at its stage is an "at risk" item in the report's section 3.


# §03 Table-stakes parity with frontier chat products

## 03.1 Scope and the parity rule

Margin must be usable as a student's only chat product. A student who leaves ChatGPT for Margin must lose nothing from the core chat loop and gain the learning engine (§04–§05). This section fixes what "nothing" means, in what order it ships, and how a reviewer verifies each item. It does not describe how the learning engine behaves inside these features; it cross-references the owning section.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 03-SCOP-001 | Every capability in §03.2 marked **MVP** is a launch gate (March 2027); **v1** ships months 7–12; **v2** after month 12; **Never** rows must be absent from the codebase and enforced by a lint that fails CI on the named strings or SDK imports. | Release checklist lists every MVP row green; CI lint job exists and has a failing test fixture. |
| 03-SCOP-002 | Parity features compose. No parity feature is disabled by mode (Learn · Practise · Mark), by Course, by incognito, by age band, by region or by plan, except where a row in §03.2 names the restriction. | Matrix test: each MVP row × {3 modes, incognito on/off, age band 13–15/16+, EU/UK/US tenant} passes; failures listed and justified against a §03.2 row. Why: ChatGPT Study Mode does not work inside Projects, GPTs or Temporary Chats [FB§1.1]; Gemini study notebooks are 18+ and personal-account only — mode-fragmentation is the frontier's most exploitable weakness. |
| 03-SCOP-003 | Parity never overrides a non-negotiable (§00): the Effort Gate, no marks without a scheme, the no-sycophancy lint, no streaks, no submittable coursework, teen-safety parity. Where a frontier default conflicts with one of these, §03.4 states the deliberate difference. | Every §03.4 row cites the non-negotiable it protects. |
| 03-SCOP-004 | The frontier moves monthly. Re-run the parity audit (FB§6 checklist against live ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) each quarter; new "M" items enter the backlog with a priority in ≤2 weeks. | Dated audit file in the repo per quarter; diff against the previous audit. |
| 03-SCOP-005 | Scoping knife (SYNTHESIS §3.1): a parity feature that neither creates nor improves Attempts ships only if it is on the MVP list below. Do not add frontier features outside this table without a §14 roadmap entry. | PR template asks "which Attempt does this create or improve, or which §03.2 row is it?" |

## 03.2 The parity checklist

Priority: **MVP** = March 2027 launch gate · **v1** = months 7–12 · **v2** = later · **Never** = absent by design. "Frontier today" is the 6 Sep 2026 baseline [FB§2, §6]. Every row is a requirement; the ID is the requirement ID.

| ID | Capability | Frontier today (ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude) | Margin spec (inside Learn · Practise · Mark) | Priority | Acceptance test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 03-PAR-001 | Token streaming with Stop; progressive loading of long threads | All stream; ChatGPT loads long chats progressively; Send becomes Stop | Typed message parts (text, math, citation, mark_card, artifact_delta) over resumable SSE; Send is replaced in place by Stop; optimistic user bubble <50 ms; status line at 800 ms naming the work ("Reading the 9609 P2 mark scheme…"); "Taking longer than usual" + Stop at 6 s; paint ≤90 chars per 16 ms; prior DOM immutable; unclosed math/code held as skeleton; history loads in pages of 30 Turns without blocking the composer (streaming contract detail in §09) | MVP | Synthetic check on every deploy: TTFT p50 <800 ms, p95 <1.5 s on a cached Learn Turn; CLS above the cursor = 0; reconnect mid-stream loses zero parts; Stop halts billing within one part |
| 03-PAR-002 | Edit any earlier user message and regenerate | ChatGPT, Claude: any message; Gemini: last only (named complaint) | Edit any user message in any Session; regenerated answer replaces the branch below; the pre-edit version is retained as a sibling; Marks on the edited Attempt are re-run, never silently kept | MVP | QA on web/iOS/Android: edit message 1 of a 30-Turn Session, regenerate, navigate siblings; the original Attempt record is preserved with `superseded_by` |
| 03-PAR-003 | Branch from any message | ChatGPT "Branch in new chat"; others none | "Try another method" on any assistant Turn creates a child Session in the same Course sharing the parent prefix (cache-friendly, §08.3); branches shown as a sibling counter "2/3" under the Turn; ladder state (rung) resets on branch | MVP | Branch from Turn 5; both branches continue independently; Learner Graph records Attempts from both; parent Session shows the branch link |
