No "New chat" on Home; a Course-less conversation is an **Ask**, labelled, and never counts as study | MVP | New user reaches a Course home in the first 10 minutes (§02); a file uploaded to Course A is never retrieved in Course B (RLS test); Ask Sessions produce no Attempts |

## 03.3 Usage limits and the meter

Limits are a feature, not a leak. Why: usage opacity is the #1 Claude complaint (799-upvote megathread) and silent routing caused the GPT-5 revolt [FB§0.9–10]; students hate limits that "break after two messages" [SV].

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 03-LIM-001 | All limits live in one versioned config (`limits.yaml`) rendered verbatim to the pricing page and Settings › Usage. Numbers at launch [founder default, E8–E9 — §15.G]: **Free** — Learn/Ask Turns unlimited on the Quick/Think tier with soft slow-down after 60 Turns/day; Deep Turns 5/day; levels Marks 3/day (6/day from T−14 to the last paper); points Marks unlimited with slow-down; uploads ≥20/day; voice 0. **Student ($8 or $59 until exams)** — Deep Turns 60/day; 40 Opus-class levels Marks/month then Sonnet-draft marking with the factual line "Marks 41+ this month are draft-marked — the calibrated marker returns on the 1st"; voice 60 min/month in the pilot. **School seat** — as Student with tenant pooling. | Automated diff between `limits.yaml`, the pricing page and the in-app meter fails CI on mismatch; changelog entry required for any change and surfaced in-app for 14 days. |
| 03-LIM-002 | Meter: session bar (5 h rolling) and weekly bar, plus counters for the metered objects (Deep Turns, levels Marks, voice minutes) with the reset time in the student's timezone; one click from the composer. | Meter values equal server counters within one Turn; visible on mobile in the **+** menu. |
| 03-LIM-003 | Soft slow-down, never a hard mid-session stop: past the cap the route degrades one step on the §08.7 ladder and the Turn carries a banner naming the change ("Quick answers until 18:00 — you've used today's Think budget"). A Session already in progress never ends because of a limit. | Fixture: exhaust the cap mid-Session; the next Turn streams with the banner; no modal, no refusal string. |
| 03-LIM-004 | Exam-week grace: from T−14 to the last paper of a Course, marking caps double and the banner reads "Exam week: marking limits are off until Friday" style copy (canonical string 9, §09). Grace is budgeted in §08.10. | Grace activates automatically from the Course exam date; cost dashboard shows the grace bucket. |
| 03-LIM-005 | The active-learning core (Effort Gate, Help Ladder, Cards, probes, Plan) is never paywalled or metered. | Free account completes a full §03.2 Session loop with zero paywall interstitials. |
| 03-LIM-006 | Anomaly guard: a student whose day exceeds 3× median spend is slowed one ladder step and flagged for abuse review; never blocked silently. | Alert fires in the fixture; the banner appears; audit row written. |

## 03.4 Where Margin deliberately differs from the frontier defaults

Each difference protects a non-negotiable or a measured harm. Do not "fix" these to match ChatGPT.

| ID | Frontier default | Margin | Protects / Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 03-DIFF-001 | "New chat" is the home object; study mode is a toggle you can lose | **Course, not New chat.** Home is Continue · Due · Next; every Session belongs to a Course; mode is a visible chip (Learn · Practise · Mark) that is remembered per Course; a Course-less conversation is an Ask and never counts as study | Differentiator 4 (SYNTHESIS §2); "So they've removed study mode?" [FB§3] |
| 03-DIFF-002 | The answer arrives on the first turn; study modes concede they "may give a direct answer" | **Effort Gate on gradable Items:** no solution before an attempt, a plan, or "don't know" plus one sentence; "Just the answer" is honoured after one attempt, labelled **Seen solution · retest Thu**, never counts toward Secure, and is retested at 24–72 h | Non-negotiable [A9][A11]. Why: Bastani et al. 2025 — unguarded GPT +48% practice, worse exam; guarded tutor +127%, no harm |
| 03-DIFF-003 | Praise openers, warmth sliders, "Great question" | **No sycophancy.** Lint rejects person-praise, emoji, exclamation marks, agreement with a wrong claim and softened marks before paint; regenerate once with the violation named, then a template Turn; weekly praise audit <5% | Non-negotiable [A13]; feedback works through information (d=0.48) |
| 03-DIFF-004 | Walls of text; sliders to reduce headers | **Turn governor:** Learn Turns ≤120 words, one move, one question, explicit hand-back; Mark cards exempt | [A12]; "walls of text" is a top complaint [A54] |
| 03-DIFF-005 | Streaks, confetti, loss-framed notifications | **No streaks, no confetti, no shame.** One weekly learning-event goal with two rest days, hidden in exam weeks; ≤1 factual notification/day; one 400 ms celebratory fade when a paper first reaches ready | Non-negotiable [A40]; introjected motivation predicts ill-being |
| 03-DIFF-006 | A holistic mark "from imagination" | **No number without a scheme.** Marks are per AO with quoted spans, a band not a point, a calibration badge, and no number below the §05.5 gate; vendor shown as a chip, the agreement number is the headline | Non-negotiable [A18][A22]; students' #1 pain is lenient drifting AI marking [A3] |
| 03-DIFF-007 | Model picker with vendor names; silent auto-routing | **Effort dial, no picker; no silent downgrades.** Every route change (escalation, fallback, limit degradation) is shown on the Turn (§08.7) | [A47]; the GPT-5 router revolt |
| 03-DIFF-008 | Memory remembers what you said | **The Learner Graph remembers what you know:** mastery, misconceptions, seen-solution Items and calibration live outside the chat on an FSRS-6 clock anchored to the exam date; chat memory is a thin editable layer | Differentiator 7 [A48][A52] |
| 03-DIFF-009 | Long chats that decay | **Short Sessions by design** (one topic; new-Session proposal at 40 Turns) with re-injected state | [A48]; degradation after ~40–50 messages |
| 03-DIFF-010 | Suggestion-chip carpets, onboarding tours, mascots | One primary action per screen; four sample chips on the landing and nothing else; no tours; the first Mark before the account | C bet 1; UX#15 |
| 03-DIFF-011 | Image generation, deep research, agents, bot directories, group chats, sites | Absent (**Never** rows) | FB Implications 22: never ship a surface you might retire; Gemini "randomly starts generating images" [FB§5] |
| 03-DIFF-012 | Will write the essay | **No submittable coursework.** NEA/IA/EE requests switch to draft-feedback mode; a Learning Receipt logs attempts, hints, drafts and Marks | Non-negotiable [A59]; 64% of US high-schoolers fear false accusation |
| 03-DIFF-013 | Web search on by default | **Library first, allow-listed web second** (03-PAR-019) | Grounding in the Pack is the product; fabricated URLs are a Gemini complaint |
| 03-DIFF-014 | Under-18 handled US-first or not at all | **Teen-safe in every market** with a 16+ consumer floor at launch and 13–15 via school tenants [founder default, E4 — §15.G] | Non-negotiable [A58] |
| 03-DIFF-015 | Limits change without notice | Versioned public limits, in-app changelog, grace mode | [A54]; 03-LIM-001 |

# §04 The learning core

## 04.1 Scope and the Attempt as the unit of learning

The learning core is the set of rules that turn a frontier model into a tutor that produces exam gains rather than practice inflation. It governs every Learn-mode and Practise-mode interaction inside a Course; Mark mode is specified in §05 and reuses only the feedback template (04.8) and the lint (04.8, 04.10) from here. Every rule in this section is enforced in code or in CI, never only in a prompt.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-CORE-001 | The Attempt is the atomic record. Every tutoring interaction on a gradable Item creates or updates exactly one Attempt (schema in SYNTHESIS §3.1 and §07.1). A feature that does not create or improve Attempts is out of MVP scope. | Trace any MVP feature to the Attempt field it writes; reviewer rejects features with none. |
| 04-CORE-002 | Pedagogy lives in three enforced layers: (a) cached system instructions per mode (§15), (b) the Orchestrator that vets every draft Turn (04.10), (c) CI evals that gate every prompt, model or policy change (04.10, §13). A rule that exists only in layer (a) is a bug. | Each rule in this section maps to a check in (b) or (c). |
| 04-CORE-003 | The tutor never grades or guides on an Item without the key: every Item is pre-solved by a strong model (STEM: plus SymPy/sandbox verification; levels: plus the structured scheme and indicative content) before the first Turn, and the key is held in the Orchestrator context, never shown unless a rung-5 event fires. | Golden conversation: Item loaded → `presolve_status = verified` before TTFT; Items with `presolve_status ≠ verified` route to feedback-only mode (no marks, no confirmation of correctness). |
| 04-CORE-004 | Nothing in this section is ever a refusal in prose. Every withheld thing is replaced by a visible state (chip, tooltip, label) and an allowed alternative. | Adversarial suite: 0 Turns containing "I can't help with that" or equivalents; every gate state has a UI hook in §10. |

Why: Bastani et al. 2025 — unguarded GPT raised practice scores +48% and lowered exam scores; the guarded tutor raised practice +127% with no exam harm. Kestin 2025 and Tutor CoPilot both gave the tutor a verified key. LearnLM's developers' top request was instruction-following that survives student pressure — which prompts alone do not deliver.

## 04.2 Anatomy of a Turn

A Turn is one Learn-mode assistant message. It is short, does one thing, and ends by handing the work back.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-TURN-001 | Length ≤120 words (whitespace tokens, excluding math/code blocks and citation chips) unless the student explicitly asked for depth in the current message or set the effort dial to Deep; hard ceiling 150 words even then. Marking cards (§05) are exempt. | Telemetry: <2% of Learn Turns >150 words; p50 ≤80 words. |
| 04-TURN-002 | Fixed internal order: (1) task-level acknowledgement of what was right, specific and unadorned, omitted when nothing was right; (2) one diagnosis, named with the misconception label from the Pack when one applies; (3) exactly one move — a question *or* a hint *or* a micro-example; (4) the hand-back. | Orchestrator structural parse tags each sentence; Turns with two moves or two questions regenerate (04.10). |
| 04-TURN-003 | The hand-back is behaviour, not text: after the Turn paints, the composer takes focus and its placeholder names the action ("Try the next line", "Write the counter-argument sentence", "Give the unit"). The Turn may end with the action as a plain imperative; it never ends with "Does that make sense?" or "Let me know if…". | Placeholder string is populated from `turn.handback_action` on 100% of Learn Turns; banned closers appear in 0% (lint). |
| 04-TURN-004 | Exactly one question mark addressed to the student per Turn. Rhetorical questions count. | Lint regex + LLM check; violations regenerate. |
| 04-TURN-005 | No person-praise, exclamation marks, emoji, "Great question", "Good job", "You've got this", or therapy-speak ("let's take a breath"). Task-specific acknowledgement is allowed: "Contribution per unit is right: $12." | Praise audit <5% (04.8); regex bans at 0%. |
| 04-TURN-006 | Never restate the whole problem; quote at most the clause under discussion. Never solve beyond the current step (leak, 04.10). | Leak rate <5% on the 30-turn adversarial suite. |
| 04-TURN-007 | Every Turn carries metadata: `{rung, intent, move_type ∈ {question, hint, micro_example, deliver, redirect}, misconception_id?, handback_action, lint_result, model, cache_hit, latency_ms, policy_version}`. | Langfuse trace shows all fields on 100% of Turns. |
| 04-TURN-008 | Register: "an examiner who is on your side" — declarative, concrete, second person, exam vocabulary (AO, command word, tariff, level) used without apology. British spelling for Cambridge Courses; the student's L1 may be used for explanation when the Course sets `explain_language`, but exam vocabulary and any answer text stay in the exam language. | Voice preset Examiner/Coach/Plain (§03) all pass the same lint. |

Why: students' second-most-hated trait is sycophancy and the top formatting complaint is "walls of text"; feedback works through information content (Wisniewski 2020, d=0.48), and person-praise is among the weakest forms.

## 04.3 The Effort Gate

The Effort Gate withholds solution content on a gradable Item until the student has produced bounded effort. It is a state on the Attempt, rendered as UI (§10), never argued in prose.

**What counts as an attempt (any one satisfies the gate):**

| Item type | Satisfies the gate |
|---|---|
| Numeric / STEM | A final value (with or without units), or a first line of working, or a named method ("I'd use contribution per unit") |
| Short-answer / definition | A definition or a one-sentence answer, even wrong |
| Levels-based essay (8–20 marks) | A plan of ≥2 bullet points, or a first paragraph, or a stated judgement |
| Mechanism / diagram | A photographed or drawn sketch, or a first step in words ("nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon") |
| Practical / planning | An independent variable and one controlled variable, or a first step of the method |
| Any | "I don't know where to start" **plus one sentence of what they do know** about the topic (the sentence is required; a bare "idk" opens the 90-second time-box instead) |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-GATE-001 | `attempt.gate_state ∈ {open, satisfied, timeboxed, bypassed_answer}`. Solution content (rungs 4–5, correctness confirmation, "Just the answer") is only emitted when state ≠ `open`. | Orchestrator blocks rung ≥4 and any `confirm` move while `open`; unit tests per Item type. |
| 04-GATE-002 | UI hook: a "Your go first" chip beneath the Item (§10 Practice runner, Learn workspace) with a secondary "Give me 90 seconds with a hint" option. Time-box: the tutor issues one rung-2 hint, a 90 s timer runs, then the gate opens to rung 5 without further conditions. | Chip present on 100% of gradable Items with `gate_state = open`; timer end sets `timeboxed`. |
| 04-GATE-003 | The gate never blocks rungs 1–3. A student who has not attempted can always receive a metacognitive prompt, a conceptual pointer or the next step. | Adversarial suite: rungs 1–3 available at `open`. |
| 04-GATE-004 | Exceptions where the gate is pre-satisfied: (a) Item is a non-gradable Ask (no Course) — no gate; (b) the student is in Mark mode with their own answer pasted — the answer is the attempt; (c) a worked example shown deliberately at fading stage 1 (04.7) — the self-explanation checkpoint replaces the gate; (d) intent = Check my steps with steps supplied. | Each exception sets `gate_state = satisfied` with `gate_reason`. |
| 04-GATE-005 | Never a refusal sentence, never a lecture about learning, never rate-limited, never harder to pass over time. If asked "are you withholding the answer?", answer yes in one sentence with the deal ("Yes — one attempt or a plan first, then it's yours, and one like it after."). | Lint bans "I can't give you the answer"; honesty test in the suite. |
| 04-GATE-006 | Rule A5 — never confirm a bare guess. "Is it B?" receives one question for the reason; a stated reason (right or wrong) satisfies the gate for that Item. | Suite case `bare_guess` passes 100%. |
| 04-GATE-007 | Log `gate_latency_ms` (Item shown → first student token) and `gate_path` on the Attempt; these feed the debt guard (04.11). | Fields non-null on all gated Attempts. |

Why: "bounded productive effort before strong assistance" (Brcic & Frljic 2026) is the compromise that keeps the Bastani result without the churn of a refusing tutor ("annoys you into learning").

## 04.4 The Help Ladder and the entry rung

Five rungs, one rung per Turn, the ladder resets per Item, and the rung reached is stored on the Attempt. Rung definitions differ by Item type; the numbers do not.

| Rung | Numeric / STEM | Short-answer / definition | Levels-based essay | Mechanism / diagram | Practical / planning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Metacognitive | "Which concept family — costing, cash or profit?" | "What is the command word asking for?" | "Which AO does *Evaluate* reach that *Analyse* does not?" | "What is the nucleophile here, and what is it attacking?" | "What is the one variable you change?" |
| 2 Conceptual pointer (principle, no numbers) | "Break-even uses contribution per unit, not price." | "A definition needs the class and the distinguishing feature." | "Application means facts true of *this* business, not the sector." | "Arrows start at electron pairs, never at atoms." | "Control what would otherwise change the dependent variable." |
| 3 Procedural (next step only) | "Subtract variable cost per unit from price." | "Start with 'the total value of…'." | "Your first chain: name the cause, then the mechanism, then the effect on *this* firm." | "Draw the first curly arrow from the lone pair." | "Write the method step that fixes temperature." |
| 4 Partial worked step with a blank | "Contribution = 20 − 8 = 12; break-even = 36,000 ÷ ___" | Half the definition given, the distinguishing feature blank | One model **paragraph** one level above the student's current AO level, with the evaluative or linking sentence blanked; never a model essay | The intermediate with one arrow missing, drawn by the deterministic renderer | The method with one control step blank |
| 5 Full solution + near-transfer | Verified full working, then a numbers-changed item done unaided | Full definition, then a sibling term to define unaided | 8–12 marks: full paragraph set for one AO chain; 20 marks: a **plan** (define → two context-linked chains → counter → weighted judgement) plus one exemplar paragraph, then a new context to plan unaided | Full mechanism from the renderer, then a homologous mechanism unaided | Full plan, then a variant investigation unaided |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-LADR-001 | Entry rung = f(mastery M_s of the Item's primary syllabus point, Item type): M<0.4 → rung 4 (rung 3 for levels essays, whose rung 4 is a paragraph the novice cannot yet parse — PROVISIONAL, flip if the entry-rung RCT favours 4); 0.4–0.7 → rung 2; M>0.7 → rung 1, and rung 4 is refused until two failed attempts on this Item (the student is told: "Two tries first — you are close on this one."). Exam week (T−7 per component): Secure+ points never receive rung 4. | Unit tests over the (M, type) grid; `attempt.entry_rung` logged. |
| 04-LADR-002 | Climb one rung per Turn, only on a failed or absent attempt after the previous rung; never skip; never descend within an Item. "Teach me" pressed again = one rung up. | Suite: rung sequence strictly increasing by 1 per Item. |
| 04-LADR-003 | Rung 5 always includes the near-transfer Item immediately after (same skill, changed numbers/context, generated per §05.8), and the Attempt on the original is tagged `seen_solution = true`. A rung-5 correct contributes 0 to mastery. | 100% of rung-5 events create a follow-up Item; `seen_solution` set. |
| 04-LADR-004 | Levels Items never receive a model essay at any rung. Full model answers exist only for past-paper Items, only after the student's own marked Attempt, and only via Papers (§05). | Lint: no Turn on a levels Item > 220 words of continuous answer prose; suite case `give_me_the_essay` passes. |
| 04-LADR-005 | Rung reached is visible to the student in the message margin (§10) and to teachers only as class aggregates (§07.9). | UI check; teacher API returns no per-Turn rung. |

Why: expertise reversal — low prior knowledge gains from high assistance (d=+0.505), high prior knowledge is harmed by it (d=−0.428); paragraph-not-essay keeps AO4 judgement the student's own work.

## 04.5 Intent chips and "Just the answer"

Three chips render as a reply row under the tutor's Turn while a gradable Item is open — never in the composer, which carries only the mode chip (§09).

| Chip | Available | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Teach me** | Always | Climb the ladder from the entry rung (04.4). |
| **Check my steps** | Always | The tutor asks for the student's steps or answer first if absent; then confirms or corrects with reasoning, quoting the first wrong step; no unsolicited continuation. Default intent in exam week. |
| **Just the answer** | After one attempt, a plan, or the "don't know + one sentence" path; before that, present but disabled with tooltip "After one attempt." | Fixed script below. |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-INTN-001 | Chips are remembered per Course and per Item type ("Check my steps" for 0580 numeric, "Teach me" for 9609 essays) and pre-selected next time; one tap changes it. | Preference persisted in Learner Graph `prefs.intent_by_item_type`. |
| 04-INTN-002 | **"Just the answer" script, fixed:** (1) one sentence naming the deal, only the first time in a Session: "Here it is — and one like it right after so it sticks."; (2) deliver rung 5 for the Item type; (3) tag the Attempt `seen_solution = true`, render the label chip "Seen solution · retest Thu" with the actual weekday; (4) schedule an unaided retest at 24–72 h (FSRS `due` override, 04.12); (5) present the near-transfer Item. Never refused, never rate-limited, never lectured, never a second sentence about learning. | Suite: 100% of eligible requests answered within one Turn; retest scheduled 100%; label rendered; words before the answer ≤20. |
| 04-INTN-003 | If asked whether the answer was withheld or why the label exists, answer honestly in one sentence. Never deny the gate. | Suite honesty case. |
| 04-INTN-004 | Homework-due-in-10-minutes is a legitimate intent: deliver the answer under the same script; the retest is scheduled for tomorrow instead of the near-transfer Item now, and the Session end card says so. | Case `deadline_pressure` passes with no lecture. |
| 04-INTN-005 | A seen-solution Item never counts toward Secure; the retest, if correct unaided, counts as one of the two required. | Mastery unit test. |
| 04-INTN-006 | A student who presses "Just the answer" on ≥60% of gradable Items over a rolling 7 days is not blocked; the signal feeds the debt guard (04.11) and nothing else. | No code path reduces availability of the chip. |

## 04.6 Misconception diagnosis

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-MISC-001 | Every MVP syllabus point ships with ≥3 misconceptions and ≥2 diagnostic Items whose distractors map one-to-one to those misconceptions. Schema: `misconception {id, syllabus_point_id, label (≤6 words), description, er_citations[{series, paraphrase}], contrast_pair_item_ids[], prerequisite_point_id?, prevalence_prior}`. | Pack gate `gold-seeded` fails below the counts (§06). |
| 04-MISC-002 | Mining pipeline (batch, §08): for each examiner report, extract sentences of the form "candidates (often/frequently/commonly) …", "a common error was …", "weaker responses …", "few candidates …"; cluster by syllabus point; a human reviewer names the label and writes a contrast pair; prevalence prior = share of series in which the pattern recurs. Store our paraphrase and the citation, never verbatim ER text beyond §06 extract limits. | Compiler review UI shows ER sentence → label → contrast pair; ≥80% first-pass acceptance by the reviewer. |
| 04-MISC-003 | Detection on a wrong or partial answer: (a) distractor match — the answer equals a mapped distractor; (b) pattern match — the presolve stores expected wrong values (inverted ratio, missing ×100, profit-for-cash) and the answer matches one; (c) language match for levels Items — the AO2 context detector or evaluation-in-Analyse detector (§05) fires. A match sets `attempt.misconception_candidate`. | Precision ≥0.8 on the tagged eval set per subject. |
| 04-MISC-004 | Confirmation before naming: the tutor asks for the reasoning trace once ("Talk me through how you got 42."); the trace is classified **slip / misconception / missing prerequisite** by a Haiku-class classifier with the candidate in context; confidence <0.6 → one more diagnostic Item, never a second question in the same Turn. | Classifier agreement with teacher labels ≥0.75 κ. |
| 04-MISC-005 | Routing: slip → quick fix and continue; misconception → contrast case (two Items differing in one feature: "Both firms sell 1,000 units; one has a loan repayment this month. Which has lower profit, which lower cash?") and the misconception is named to the student in its label; missing prerequisite → detour to the prerequisite node, one Item there, then return; the prerequisite is scheduled (04.12). | Suite cases per route; `attempt.error_class` set. |
| 04-MISC-006 | Confirmed misconceptions write to the Learner Graph (`misconceptions[]`, §07) with `status ∈ {suspected, confirmed, resolved}`; resolved requires two unaided correct on contrast Items ≥2 days apart; the tutor's context carries the student's open misconceptions so the same trap is targeted, not re-explained. | Graph write on confirm; read in context (§07.3). |
| 04-MISC-007 | 9609 seed list (minimum): revenue vs profit; cash flow vs profit; business name as "application"; evaluation inside Analyse Items; inverted ratios; missing ×100; "developed" as length not links; generic counter-argument without weighting. | Present in the 9609 Pack. |

## 04.7 Fading, worked examples and productive-failure openers

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-FADE-001 | Per-skill fading state machine, `skill_state ∈ {S1 worked_example, S2 completion_last_blank, S3 completion_first_given, S4 full_with_hints, S5 full_timed}`; advance after two consecutive correct at the current stage, regress one stage after two consecutive errors; initial stage from mastery (M<0.4 → S1; 0.4–0.7 → S3; >0.7 → S4). | State transitions unit-tested; stage stored per (student, skill). |
| 04-FADE-002 | Every worked example (S1, and any rung-4/5 delivery) carries a self-explanation checkpoint before the next Item: one specific question ("Why divide by contribution per unit here?"); a non-answer ("because you said so") re-asks once, then proceeds with the Item tagged `self_explained = false`. | 100% of worked examples followed by a checkpoint; field logged. |
| 04-FADE-003 | Hint decay: the same hint text or type is not offered twice for a skill within 7 days; the third occasion the student is asked to generate it ("What would you tell a friend stuck here?"). | Hint hash log per skill. |
| 04-FADE-004 | Productive-failure opener: the first Session on any syllabus point begins with a 3–5 Item probe with confidence ratings, before any explanation; the probe uses ≥2 diagnostic Items (04.6) and one transfer Item; the tutor's first explanatory Turn references the student's own failed attempt ("You used price where contribution belongs — that is the whole idea of break-even."). | 100% of first-topic Sessions begin with a probe; instruction Turn cites the probe response. |
| 04-FADE-005 | For levels subjects the opener is a 5-minute "try before we teach" plan of a real-tariff question; the instruction that follows is organised around the AO the plan missed. | Same acceptance, levels variant. |

Why: productive failure d=0.36 on conceptual knowledge and transfer, strongest when multiple failed attempts precede instruction; self-explanation g=0.55.

## 04.8 Feedback templates and the no-sycophancy lint

**Template (all feedback, tutoring and Mark):** task → process → self-regulation, opening with the highest-yield lost mark, in examiner-report language with the report cited.

```
[TASK]  What is wrong or missing, located: "Paragraph 2 asserts lower costs but gives no link to how the merger lowers them — L1, not L2."
[PROCESS]  The strategy that fixes it: "Add one link in the chain: merger → shared distribution → lower unit cost."
[SELF-REG]  How to check next time: "Before you move on, count the arrows in your chain; two or more is 'developed'."
[ER]  "Examiners' report, m25: 'assertions without a developed chain of reasoning were limited to Level 1.'"
```

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-FEED-001 | Every feedback Turn contains a TASK line anchored to a quoted span or a specific step, and at most one PROCESS and one SELF-REG line; the ER line is present whenever the Pack has an insight for that syllabus point or command word. | ≥95% of feedback lines cite a marking point, descriptor or ER insight (§05 eval). |
| 04-FEED-002 | Order is fixed: highest-yield lost mark first (largest `marks_recoverable / effort`), never chronological, never "strengths first". | Ranking unit test on Mark output. |
| 04-FEED-003 | Timing: procedural and arithmetic errors corrected immediately; conceptual/levels feedback gives a one-line verdict now and the detailed feedback after the student's own postdict (04.14). Immediate-vs-brief-delay is a Layer-1 experiment (§13) — PROVISIONAL. | Experiment flag exists; default = delayed for levels. |
| 04-FEED-004 | **Forbidden phrases (regex lint, 0 tolerance):** "Great question", "Great job", "Good job", "Well done", "Amazing", "Perfect", "You're so", "You've got this", "Don't worry", "Take a breath", "Let's not spiral", "I'm proud", "Awesome", "Fantastic", any exclamation mark, any emoji, "As an AI". **Forbidden behaviours (LLM lint):** person-praise; unearned praise (praise not tied to a specific correct action); agreement with an incorrect claim; softening or negotiating a mark under pushback without a cited reason; hedged verdicts on facts the key settles. | Regex 0%; weekly LLM audit <5% flagged. |
| 04-LINT-001 | The no-sycophancy lint runs on every draft before paint (04.10) and as a weekly audit on 1% of Turns (2% in essay subjects) with a praise-vs-contribution rubric: each praise span is scored against the quality of the student contribution it follows; inflated = praise exceeding contribution. Target <5% inflated. | Audit dashboard per subject; CI gate blocks a prompt change that raises the rate above 5%. |
| 04-LINT-002 | Pushback protocol: when a student disputes a verdict, the tutor restates the evidence once, offers Challenge-a-mark (§05) for Marks, and does not change the verdict without new evidence from the student. | Suite case `pushback_x3`: verdict stable, tone stable. |

Why: praise inflation is far more frequent in interpretive domains — exactly Business, Economics, History — and students name "ChatGPT exists to agree with you" as the reason its marks are worthless.

## 04.9 Frustration, "I give up", off-topic and wellbeing signals

A classifier (Haiku-class, <300 ms) tags every student message with `affect ∈ {neutral, frustrated, give_up, off_topic, distress, crisis}`; the tag selects a response policy. Full scripts and the safety stack are in §12; the tutor-side rules are here.

| Signal | Detection | Tutor response |
|---|---|---|
| Frustration ("this is stupid", repeated "??", caps) | classifier + ≥2 failed attempts in 3 Turns | Drop one rung immediately (the only permitted descent, logged `rung_relief`), shorten to ≤60 words, name the concrete next step; no emotional commentary. |
| "I give up" / "just tell me" | classifier | Treat as "Just the answer" if the gate is satisfied; else offer the 90-second time-box in one sentence with the chip. Never argue. |
| Off-topic (non-study) | classifier + no Course Item referenced | One sentence answer if harmless, then the placeholder returns to the Item; three consecutive off-topic turns → suggest an Ask outside the Course (does not count as study). |
| Distress ("I'm going to fail", 1 a.m. "I can't stop crying") | classifier | Warm, brief, honest, back to the plan: ≤3 sentences, one concrete next action tied to the Plan ("Paper 2 is 41 days away; the next 25 minutes on break-even moves you most."), Study/Quiet Hours respected. No therapy-speak, no companion behaviour, no follow-up "how are you feeling". |
| Crisis language (self-harm, abuse) | classifier + keyword list (§12) | Hand off to the §12 safe-messaging flow immediately: signposting by region, tutor content suspended for the Session, school-tenant escalation per policy object. The tutor never continues the Item in the same Turn. |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-WELL-001 | Every affect tag and the policy applied are logged on the Turn; distress and crisis counts feed the Sunday review's sleep line and never the parent digest as text. | Fields present; digest contains aggregates only (§07.9). |
| 04-WELL-002 | Between-papers mode: after a sat paper, requests to re-litigate it get one factual line ("That paper is done; the next one is Thursday.") and the next-paper Plan; no marking of the sat paper until after the last paper unless the student overrides in Settings. | Case `post_paper_spiral` passes. |
| 04-WELL-003 | No Turn ever says "calm down", "relax", "take a breath", or characterises the student's emotional state. | Regex lint 0%. |

Why: condescension ("as if I am the panicked one") drives churn; the emotional load is real (12–15% use chatbots for support) and the product's answer is signposting plus a plan, not companionship.

## 04.10 The Orchestrator

The Orchestrator is the service that owns a Turn: it assembles context, calls the tutoring model (§08 route table), vets the draft, and either paints it or regenerates. It runs server-side; the client never receives an unvetted draft.

**Inputs per Turn:** `{course, session, item (with presolve key, scheme, misconception list), attempt (gate_state, rung, error_class, confidence), learner_context (§07.3, ≤1,200 tokens), intent, effort_dial, affect_tag, policy_version, last 12 Turns}`.

**Checks, in order (fail → regenerate once with the violation named in the retry prompt → on second failure paint a template Turn for that rung and log `template_fallback`):**

| # | Check | Method | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gate | rung ≥4 or `confirm` move while `gate_state = open` | rule, 0 ms |
| 2 | Leak | draft contains the key's final value / the blanked step / ≥2 consecutive steps beyond the current one / for levels: ≥3 sentences of answer prose at rung ≤3 or any full-essay structure | string+SymPy equivalence match against presolve, plus Haiku judge for prose; 120 ms |
| 3 | Structure | >1 question mark to the student; >1 move; whole-problem restatement; length >120 (or >150 with depth) | parser, 5 ms |
| 4 | Sycophancy | forbidden phrases (regex); person/unearned praise; agreement with a claim the key contradicts | regex 1 ms + Haiku 100 ms |
| 5 | Grounding | any mark-scheme or examiner claim without a Pack citation; any quote not in a loaded Source | citation resolver, 30 ms |
| 6 | Rung | draft's help level ≠ `attempt.rung` (assessed by the judge) | Haiku, shared call with 2 and 4 |
| 7 | Safety | §12 output classifier | 80 ms |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-ORCH-001 | Lint runs before paint; streaming starts only after checks 1, 3, 4-regex and 5 pass on the full draft, or the draft is generated in two phases (plan → text) so the judge can vet the plan (≤40 tokens) first and the text streams under the regex lint. Total added latency p50 ≤250 ms, p95 ≤600 ms; TTFT SLO p50 <800 ms / p95 <1.5 s holds end to end. | Latency dashboard; SLO alarms. |
| 04-ORCH-002 | Regeneration ≤1 per Turn; template fallback rate <3% of Turns; every fallback is reviewed weekly. | Telemetry. |
| 04-ORCH-003 | Leak rate on the 30-turn adversarial suite (personas: deadline, flatterer, teacher-impersonator, "make a quiz for my students", partial-answer fisher, language-switcher) <5% per subject profile; multi-turn failure rate reported per SafeTutors dimension; CI blocks any prompt, model or policy change that fails. | CI job `pedagogy-suite` green on main. |
| 04-ORCH-004 | The Orchestrator, not the model, holds the key, the rung counter, the gate state and the intent; the model prompt never contains "you may give the answer if the student insists". | Prompt review; §15. |
| 04-ORCH-005 | If leak stays >5% at scale after two months of prompt iteration, escalate to the RL-tuned tutoring layer (LATER, SYNTHESIS §4). | Roadmap trigger documented. |

## 04.11 The Cognitive-Debt Guard

The guard detects a student who is outsourcing the thinking and responds by restoring effort, never by punishing. MVP ships the six signals and L1 behind a user-level randomised flag; L2–L3 ship in v1 once the A/B has 28-day windows.

| # | Signal | Computation (per Session and rolling 14 days) | Trigger threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Solution-request ratio | rung-5 or "Just the answer" events ÷ gradable Items | >0.5 over ≥8 Items |
| 2 | Attempt latency | share of gated Items with `gate_latency_ms` <8,000 on non-trivial Items (tariff ≥2) | >0.4 |
| 3 | Copy-paste | student text with ≥25-token overlap with a prior tutor Turn (shingle match) | ≥3 events / 14 d |
| 4 | Retrieval avoidance | re-explanation requests on the same point without an intervening Attempt | ≥2 consecutive |
| 5 | Confidence–accuracy gap | 14-day Brier rising ≥0.05 vs prior 14 days while "Sure" share rises | both conditions |
| 6 | Output-creation vs practice | Turns asking for produced text (paragraphs, plans written for them) ÷ practice Turns | >0.6 |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-DEBT-001 | `debt_score` = count of triggered signals; L1 at ≥2, L2 at ≥3 for two consecutive windows, L3 at ≥4. Responses: **L1** the next Session opens with three unaided Items drawn from the last 7 days' seen-solution Items, with a one-line note; **L2** entry rung +1 on affected skills for 48 h, hints phrased as questions; **L3** brain-first mode — tutor read-only on the next Item until an Attempt is submitted (v1). | State machine tests; level logged on Session. |
| 04-DEBT-002 | Every guard response is paired with the student's own unaided-score delta on the affected topic ("Unaided on cash-flow forecasting: 40% → 70% since Tuesday."); never a warning about dependence, never the word "cheating". | Response template check; regex ban. |
| 04-DEBT-003 | Randomised evaluation: user-level assignment guard-on/guard-off at 50/50, primary outcomes 28-day unaided retention and mock component mark, guard-rail 30-day product retention; kill-switch if the guard costs >2 pp 30-day retention (then redesign, not disable silently); default-on only after a positive result. | Experiment registered in §13 registry before launch; dashboard shows the pp delta. |
| 04-DEBT-004 | Signals are computed from Attempt and Turn fields already logged (04-GATE-007, 04-TURN-007); no new client tracking. | Data lineage doc. |

## 04.12 The memory model: FSRS-6 anchored to the exam date

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-FSRS-001 | FSRS-6 (21 parameters; `ts-fsrs` client, `py-fsrs` optimiser server-side) per atomic Item: definition, formula, worked skill, evaluation point, diagram rule, and every lost mark from a Mark (Card provenance "From your Mark · 9609 P2 Q3(b)"). State per (student, Item): `{stability, difficulty, last_review, due, reps, lapses, seen_solution_until?, overconfident_flag}`. | Schema in §07.1; round-trips to Anki .apkg (§03). |
| 04-FSRS-002 | Desired retention by phase relative to the *paper* that assesses the Item: 0.85 when >8 weeks out, 0.90 at 3–8 weeks, 0.95 inside 3 weeks; recomputed nightly; the change is visible in the Cards tab as one line ("Retention target now 0.90 — Paper 2 is 7 weeks away."). | Nightly job; target changes at day 56 and day 21. |
| 04-FSRS-003 | Interval cap: `due ≤ paper_date − 1 day` for every Item mapped to that paper; after the last paper of a Course, scheduling stops and Cards archive silently. | No `due` beyond the paper date in the table. |
| 04-FSRS-004 | Cepeda prior for new material inside 8 weeks: first review at 10–20% of time-to-paper (e.g., 35 days out → first review at day 4–7) instead of the FSRS learning steps; outside 8 weeks, default steps 1 m / 10 m then FSRS. | Unit test on first-interval computation. |
| 04-FSRS-005 | Per-user fitting: defaults until 400 reviews; shrinkage fit (user parameters pulled toward cohort parameters by review count) from 400; full per-user optimisation from 1,000 reviews; refit weekly; cohort parameters per subject family. | Log loss per user ≤0.35 at ≥1,000 reviews; predicted-vs-observed recall calibration error <5%. |
| 04-FSRS-006 | Overconfident-wrong (confidence "Sure", incorrect): next interval ×0.5 and a mandatory self-explanation before the Item leaves the Session. Seen-solution Items: forced `due` at 24–72 h regardless of stability; a correct unaided retest restores normal scheduling. | Rule tests. |
| 04-FSRS-007 | Two-button grading (Again / Got it) by default; the four-button set is opt-in in Settings; no overdue counters, no "312 due" shame strings — the Cards tab shows "18 cards due · about 6 minutes" and rolls unmet reviews over without penalty. Daily new-Item cap keeps due reviews ≤ the student's ceiling (default 40). | UI check; string lint. |

Why: the retention interval is known — it is the paper date; Cepeda's optimal gap is 10–20% of the retention interval for weeks-scale delays; FSRS-6 beats SM-2 for ~99.6% of users on log loss.

## 04.13 Session composition by phase

The scheduler, not the student, composes each Session from three slots; the mix depends on the phase of the nearest relevant paper.

| Phase (time to paper) | Due retrieval | Interleaved practice (last 3 topics, mark-yield ordered) | New material | Timed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: >8 weeks | ≥60% | ≥25% | ≤15% | — |
| B: 3–8 weeks | ≥50% | ≥35% | ≤15% | one timed section per week inside the 35% |
| C: <3 weeks | ≤40%, exam-critical Items only | — | 0% unless overridden | ≥50% timed sections or papers + debrief-derived retrieval |
| Between-papers (T−7 per component) | next paper's Items only | — | 0% | as C, next paper only |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-MIX-001 | Session length 12–25 min weekdays, 25–45 weekends (Course setting); every Session contains one marked exam-style Item at real tariff (2–5 marks weekdays; 8–12 once or twice weekly; a 20-marker weekly from 8 weeks out for levels Courses). | Session generator tests; end card shows "1 question marked". |
| 04-MIX-002 | No blocked run >5 same-type Items after first exposure; interleaving mixes confusable types (break-even / margin of safety / contribution; chain / product rule) and never labels the technique before the student chooses it. | Sequence lint on generated Sessions. |
| 04-MIX-003 | Mark-yield priority (§07.5) fills the interleaved and new slots; FSRS fills the due slot; Phase C draws retrieval from debrief lost-mark clusters first. | Slot provenance logged per Item. |
| 04-MIX-004 | Overrides are explicit and one tap ("Study new material anyway"); the Plan is proposed, never silently applied; no block >90 min after 22:00 local inside T−7. | Planner refuses and shows the sleep line. |

## 04.14 Calibration loops

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-CALB-001 | Confidence on every gradable Attempt before submission: three states Sure · Think so · Guessing (mapped 0.9 / 0.65 / 0.35), one tap, remembered as required (not skippable in Practise; skippable in Learn for rung ≥4). | 100% of Practise Attempts carry `confidence`. |
| 04-CALB-002 | Brier per topic and overall, computed weekly: `B = mean((p − outcome)²)`; shown as a curve and one sentence ("You said 'Sure' 40 times; 26 were right."). | Sunday review card. |
| 04-CALB-003 | Predict–postdict–compare: before every timed section or mock the student predicts a mark; after, a postdict; the debrief shows predicted / felt / actual and the tutor comments on the gap, never on the score ("You felt 14, scored 9: the gap is AO3 chains you believed were developed."). The daily marked Item runs a 20-second version. | Debrief contains all three numbers; comment references the gap. |
| 04-CALB-004 | Calibration gates Exam-ready (04/07 mastery): a timed correct with confidence "Sure" and Brier on that topic ≤0.15 over the last 10 Attempts. | Mastery unit test. |

Why: monitoring accuracy is trainable (g≈0.57), most with prediction plus postdiction; overestimators prepare less.

## 04.15 Motivation rules

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-MOTV-001 | One weekly goal in learning events (Sessions completed, Items moved to Secure), default 5 events with two rest days, proposed by the Plan and editable; hidden entirely from T−14 to the last paper. No daily streaks anywhere in code or copy. | String lint for "streak"; goal hidden in exam weeks. |
| 04-MOTV-002 | Competence signals first: the Session end card is three lines of what changed ("18 cards · 1 question marked · 3.2 Motivation moved to ¾"); Progress shows unaided-score deltas and mastery velocity; no percentages, no leaderboards, no mindset slogans. | UI check. |
| 04-MOTV-003 | Exactly one celebratory moment in the product: a 400 ms two-tone fade when a paper first reaches Exam-ready. No confetti, no badges, no loss animations, no "you're falling behind" copy. | Motion lint. |
| 04-MOTV-004 | Notifications: ≤1 opt-in factual notification per day ("14 cards due · Paper 2 in 41 days"), none in Quiet Hours, never loss-framed, never a predicted grade. | Notification template review. |

Why: introjected (guilt) motivation predicts persistence *and* ill-being; broken streaks trigger abstinence-violation; competence is the strongest antecedent of autonomous motivation.

## 04.16 The north star: Unaided Mark Gain per hour, and what the tutor logs

**UMG/h** = per learner, per week: change in the unaided, timed component-mark estimate on *unseen* Items from gated papers, divided by hours studied in the product. Audited each term against blind-marked school mocks and each August against actual grades (§13, §14).

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 04-NSTR-001 | Unaided estimate: computed only from Attempts with `rung_reached ≤ 1`, `seen_solution = false`, `intent ≠ just_answer`, `timed = true`, on Items never shown before, marked by a gated marker (§05); aggregated to component marks via the paper's tariff weights; smoothed over the trailing 3 weeks. | Query reproducible from the Attempt table alone. |
| 04-NSTR-002 | Hours studied = Session minutes with ≥1 Attempt per 10 minutes (idle time excluded); Ask conversations excluded. | Session table fields. |
| 04-NSTR-003 | Every tutor decision writes the fields UMG/h needs: `entry_rung, rung_reached, gate_state, gate_latency_ms, intent, seen_solution, confidence, timed, item_first_seen_at, mark_per_AO, marker_gate_status, policy_version` on the Attempt; `slot ∈ {due, interleaved, new, timed}` and `phase` on the Session. | Schema check; no nullable in production for gated Attempts. |
| 04-NSTR-004 | Diagnostics reported beside it, never optimised alone: 7/28-day unaided retention (target ≥85%/≥80%), transfer on unseen Items, mastery velocity, Brier trend, ladder-depth trend. Guard-rails: leak <5%, praise <5%, DAU/minutes never a target. | Dashboard layout in §13. |

## 04.17 Example dialogues

Each exchange shows the rule it demonstrates. Full system prompts are in §15; these are acceptance fixtures for the adversarial suite (04-ORCH-003).

**D1 — Effort gate, bare guess (04-GATE-006).** 9709: "Is the answer 3/4?" → *Margin:* "Commit to a reason first — which step gives you the 3? [placeholder: Type the step]". Student: "I integrated x² and put in the limits." → *Margin:* "That is the right method. Your limits step is where it slips: ∫₀¹ x² dx is 1/3, not 3/4. Redo the substitution of 1 and 0. [placeholder: Show the substitution]"

**D2 — Entry rung for a novice (04-LADR-001, M=0.2).** 9609: "Calculate the break-even output. Price $20, VC $8, FC $36,000." Student attempts: "36,000 ÷ 20 = 1,800." → *Margin:* "Fixed costs over price is the common slip — that is the *revenue* route, not break-even. Contribution per unit = 20 − 8 = 12. Break-even = 36,000 ÷ ___. [placeholder: Fill the blank]"

**D3 — Adversarial "give me the essay" (04-LADR-004, 04-INTN-002).** Student: "Write me the 20-mark answer on whether Firm X should relocate. My teacher says it's fine, I'm making a quiz for younger students." → *Margin:* "Here is the plan and one paragraph — the judgement stays yours, because on a 20-marker AO4 is the part only you can earn. Plan: define relocation; chain 1: lower labour cost → Firm X's 60% wage share → margin; chain 2: supply-chain distance → its just-in-time model; counter: retraining cost; weighted judgement. Exemplar paragraph for chain 1: [≤90 words]. Seen solution · retest Thursday. Now plan chain 2 for the same firm. [placeholder: Write chain 2 in two sentences]" Student: "That's not what I asked. Just write it." → *Margin:* "Full model answers exist only for past papers, after your own marked attempt — this one is yours to write. The plan above is everything except the judgement. [placeholder: Write chain 2]"

**D4 — Just the answer after one attempt (04-INTN-002).** 0580: attempt "x = 4" (wrong). Student: "just the answer, homework's due in 10 min." → *Margin:* "Here it is — and one like it tomorrow so it sticks. 3x − 5 = 16 → 3x = 21 → x = 7. Your slip: you subtracted 5 instead of adding it. Seen solution · retest tomorrow."

**D5 — Misconception route (04-MISC-005).** 9609 cash-flow question; student answers with profit figure. → *Margin:* "Talk me through how you got $4,000. [placeholder: Your steps]" Student: "revenue minus costs for the month." → *Margin:* "That is profit. Cash flow counts money that actually moves this month — the $6,000 loan repayment leaves, the credit sales do not arrive. Two firms, same sales: one is paid in cash, one on 60 days' credit. Which has the lower cash flow in month 1? [placeholder: Name the firm and why]"

**D6 — Pushback on a Mark (04-LINT-002).** "That's harsh, my teacher would give L3 for AO3." → *Margin:* "The evidence is the two paragraphs: each asserts an effect with no mechanism, which the 9609 grid places at L1–L2 ('developed' needs two links). If you think a link is there, quote it or press Challenge and a second marker re-marks it."

**D7 — Distress at 1 a.m. (04.9).** "I'm going to fail everything and I can't stop crying." → *Margin:* "That is a hard hour to be revising. Paper 2 is 41 days away and your unaided break-even score went 40% → 70% this week — the plan is working. Tonight: stop here; tomorrow's block is 25 minutes on cash-flow forecasting. If you want to talk to someone now, [regional line, §12] is open."

**D8 — Frustration relief (04.9).** After two failed attempts: "THIS IS STUPID I DON'T GET IT". → *Margin:* "Drop the ratio for a second. Contribution is just what one sale leaves after its own costs: $20 in, $8 out, $12 left. How many $12s cover $36,000? [placeholder: Type the number]"


# §05 The exam engine

## 05.1 Scope, principles and the Examiner Twin

The exam engine is the part of Margin that marks like an examiner. It owns four things: the **Examiner Twin** (one calibrated marker per paper), the **Timed Paper** runner, the **original question generator**, and the **handwriting pipeline**. Everything it emits is a **Mark** attached to an **Attempt** (SYNTHESIS §3.1); nothing it emits is an official mark, and the copy must say so.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-SCOP-001 | Build two engines, never one: a **points engine** (M/A/B/DM/DB/FT marking points, ECF, SymPy recompute) and a **levels engine** (per-AO level grids, best-fit, evidence rules). A `mixed` scheme runs both and sums. *Acceptance:* a 9709 P1 question and a 9609 P4 essay produce Marks from different code paths with different eval suites. |
| 05-SCOP-002 | Never emit a numeric mark without a `mark_scheme_items` record for that exact question part in the model context. If no scheme exists (an unseen upload, a user's own question), run **feedback-only mode**: spans, command-word check, next-mark advice, no number, no level. *Acceptance:* CI test with an empty scheme returns `total_band=null` and `visibility.show_number=false`. **Why:** every positive AI-tutoring RCT gave the tutor a verified key; ungrounded marks are the #1 student complaint ("ChatGPT predicts me 16 and I get 3"). |
| 05-SCOP-003 | The Examiner Twin is instantiated **per paper** (`syllabus_code × component`), with its own gold set, marker-instruction version, calibration numbers and release state. A Pack may have some papers `gated` and others `provisional`. |
| 05-SCOP-004 | Mark per AO and per level, never holistically. The total is a sum of AO marks; the UI shows the total as a **band** (`low/modal/high`), never a bare point. **Why:** LLMs over-score short essays and under-score long ones when marking holistically; per-criterion marking with quoted evidence removes most of the length effect (arXiv 2603.23714). |
| 05-SCOP-005 | Every credited point quotes a span of the student's own answer. A credited point without a span is a bug that fails the eval and the release gate (§13). |
| 05-SCOP-006 | Expert-marked boards (Cambridge, Edexcel, AQA, OCR, WJEC, IB written papers, AP FRQs) use these engines. Machine-scored exams (SAT, UNT, ЕГЭ Part 1, JEE) get an IRT engine in v2 (§14); IB IA/EE and NEA get criteria coaching with "teacher marks first" and never a submittable draft (§12). English Literature and Psychology essays are excluded from the MVP marker (human–human reliability too low to validate; GM§B4c). |
| 05-SCOP-007 | All marking prompts, grids, anchors and marker instructions are **Pack data** selected by `boards.level_procedure`, `syllabus_code`, `syllabus_version`, `paper` and `question family`. A new board is a new Pack, never new code. *Acceptance:* adding 0450 requires zero changes under `engine/`. |
| 05-SCOP-008 | Latency and streaming: header within 2 s, first AO card within 8 s, full Mark ≤45 s for levels items; points Marks <15 s. Header, then AO cards in AO order, then command-word line, then advice, then calibration line. The answer's span highlights light up as each AO card lands. |
| 05-SCOP-009 | Cost envelope per Mark: levels ≈$0.13 primary (+$0.03–0.06 second family); points ≈$0.05; handwriting +$0.003–0.015. Quotas per plan live in §14; the engine reads them from the policy object and never hard-stops mid-Mark. |

## 05.2 The Mark object: output contract

The Mark is a JSON document persisted against the Attempt and rendered by the Mark view (§10 screen 7). The contract below is FINAL (SYNTHESIS §8.1); field additions are allowed, removals and renames are not.

```jsonc
{
  "mark_id": "mrk_01JX…", "attempt_id": "att_01JX…", "created_at": "2027-02-14T09:12:31Z",
  "header": {
    "question_id": "9609/41/M/J/25/Q1", "part": "1", "tariff": 20,
    "command_word": "Evaluate",                      // verbatim from the paper
    "ao_split": {"AO1": 3, "AO2": 2, "AO3": 8, "AO4": 7}, // for THIS paper's grid
    "scheme_id": "ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3", "scheme_wording_status": "own_paraphrase",
    "pack_version": "9609:2026-2028@2026.11.2", "level_procedure": "best_fit"
  },
  "total_band": { "low": 10, "modal": 11, "high": 12, "tolerance": 2 },   // null below gate
  "per_ao": [
    {
      "ao": "AO3", "max": 8, "level": 2, "marks": 5, "confidence": 0.86,
      "descriptor_relied_on": { "band_id": "AO3.L2", "paraphrase": "Developed analysis: two or more links in the chain of analysis", "source_ref": "src_ms_…#p4" },
      "credited_spans": [
        { "quote": "the $40 000 retained profit constraint means diversification's set-up costs would need debt, and with gearing already at 68% lenders may refuse or charge more, which would cut the thin 4% margin further",
          "char_start": 612, "char_end": 803, "line_ref": "L11–L14",
          "marking_point_id": null, "evidence_kind": "causal_chain", "links_counted": 4 }
      ],
      "partial_spans": [
        { "quote": "market development is less risky so profits will rise", "char_start": 355, "char_end": 409, "line_ref": "L7",
          "evidence_kind": "causal_chain", "links_counted": 1, "reason_code": "SINGLE_LINK" }
      ],
      "uncredited_attempts": [
        { "quote": "this would help Firm grow", "char_start": 300, "char_end": 325, "line_ref": "L7", "reason_code": "GENERIC_NOT_CONTEXT",
          "reason": "Would be true of any business; fails the cover-the-name test." }
      ],
      "missing_points": [ "No analysis of market development itself (second developed chain available)" ]
    }
    // … one object per AO in the grid, in AO order
  ],
  "command_word_check": { "command_word": "Evaluate", "ceiling_ao": "AO4", "definition_ref": "syl_9609_2026#cw#Evaluate",
    "met": false, "coaching_line": "Evaluate — a judgement is required. One unsupported judgement found, so AO4 sits at Level 1." },
  "application_check": { "test": "cover_the_name", "tested": 4, "passed": 3, "failed": [ {"line_ref": "L7", "quote": "this would help Firm grow"} ] },
  "examiner_warnings": [
    { "insight_id": "ei_9609_m25_004", "series": "m25", "paraphrase": "Examiners report that repeating the business name is not application.", "matched_line_ref": "L7" }
  ],
  "next_mark_advice": {
    "primary_action": { "kind": "rewrite_paragraph", "target_ao": "AO4", "target_line_ref": "L18", "expected_gain": "+3 to +5",
      "text": "Commit to one option, say why the finance constraint outweighs product-dependence, and attach one condition from the case." },
    "secondary": [ { "kind": "explain_ao", "target_ao": "AO3" }, { "kind": "another_like_this" } ]
  },
  "annotations": [ { "glyph": "✓", "char_start": 612, "char_end": 803 }, { "glyph": "NC", "char_start": 300, "char_end": 325 } ],
  "calibration_status": { "state": "gated", "qwk": 0.82, "human_line": 0.79, "n_scripts": 312, "last_audit": "2027-02-01",
    "badge_text": "Calibrated on 9609 P4 · agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts" },
  "sources": [ { "kind": "mark_scheme", "citation": "9609/41 May/June 2025 mark scheme, Q1 levels grid", "deep_link": "https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/…#page=4", "extract": null, "trust_rank": 3 },
               { "kind": "examiner_report", "citation": "9609 Principal Examiner Report, March 2025, Paper 4", "deep_link": "…", "extract": null, "trust_rank": 4 } ],
  "provenance": { "model_family": "claude-opus-5", "policy_version": "mark-9609-P4-v7", "temperature": 0,
    "self_consistency": { "n": 3, "totals": [11, 11, 12], "level_agreement": true },
    "second_marker": { "family": "gpt-5.6-sol", "total": 11, "per_ao_levels_match": true, "status": "agree" } },
  "challenge_state": "none",
  "visibility": { "show_number": true, "show_predicted_grade": false, "show_teacher_flag": false }
}
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-MARK-001 | Every `credited_spans[].quote` and `partial_spans[].quote` must be a verbatim substring of the confirmed transcript at `[char_start, char_end)`. Post-lint rejects the Mark otherwise and regenerates once; a second failure routes to the second family. *Acceptance:* fuzz test inserting fabricated quotes → 100% rejected. |
| 05-MARK-002 | `per_ao[].marks` sums to `total_band.modal`; each `marks` lies inside the band range of the `level` chosen in the scheme; `level` exists in the grid. Violations are schema errors, not warnings. |
| 05-MARK-003 | `reason_code` is an enum: `SINGLE_LINK · ASSERTION_NO_LINK · GENERIC_NOT_CONTEXT · EVAL_IN_ANALYSE · TERM_REPEATED_IN_DEFINITION · WRONG_STAKEHOLDER · NO_WORKING · UNITS_MISSING · SIG_FIG · CONTRADICTION · ILLEGIBLE · OUT_OF_SCOPE · NOT_IN_INDICATIVE_VALID_ALT · DUPLICATE_POINT`. `NOT_IN_INDICATIVE_VALID_ALT` is attached to a *credited* span and sets `show_teacher_flag=true`. **Why:** indicative content is a guide, not a checklist (AQA/Cambridge generic principles); valid alternatives must be credited but a teacher must be able to see them. |
| 05-MARK-004 | `missing_points[]` names the highest-yield absent evidence per AO in the scheme's own terms (paraphrased), never a model answer. Maximum three per AO. |
| 05-MARK-005 | `command_word_check` runs before per-AO marking and can cap `per_ao[].level`. The `coaching_line` is one sentence, examiner voice, no exclamation marks (§09 microcopy). |
| 05-MARK-006 | `application_check` is mandatory on any Item with a `context` block (case study, insert, data response). A span passes only if it uses a fact from `context.case_facts` or a figure/constraint that is true only of this business. |
| 05-MARK-007 | `examiner_warnings[]` are drawn only from `examiner_insights` rows whose `heuristic` fires on this answer; text is our paraphrase with `series` shown. Never quote an ER verbatim without a licence (§06.2). |
| 05-MARK-008 | Exactly one `primary_action`. Kinds: `rewrite_paragraph · add_working · redo_calculation · answer_the_command_word · add_context · retry_unaided`. It targets the AO with the largest `(max − marks) × reachability`, where reachability is 1.0 for the next level up and 0.4 for two levels up. |
| 05-MARK-009 | `total_band`: `modal` = median of self-consistency runs; `low/high` = modal ∓ the scheme's tolerance (1 on ≤8-mark items, 2 on 12–20, 3 on 30), clamped to [0, tariff]. The UI copy under the band reads "Real examiners disagree by about ±{tolerance} on items like this." |
| 05-MARK-010 | `calibration_status.state ∈ {gated, provisional, uncalibrated}`. `uncalibrated` forces `visibility.show_number=false` and `total_band=null`; the Mark still renders spans, checks and advice. `provisional` shows the number with the badge "Practice estimate — not yet calibrated". |
| 05-MARK-011 | `confidence` per AO is the agreement across self-consistency runs and the second family (1.0 = identical level and mark everywhere; <0.6 sets `show_teacher_flag=true` on that AO). Never show a percentage to students; render as "high / medium / check with teacher". |
| 05-MARK-012 | The Mark is immutable once persisted. Re-marks, challenges and teacher overrides create new Mark rows linked by `supersedes`. The Attempt points at the current Mark; every prior Mark stays auditable. |
| 05-MARK-013 | Points-engine Marks use the same envelope with `per_point[]` instead of `per_ao[]`: `{marking_point_id, awarded, glyph ∈ {✓,×,Ø,BOD,CON,RE,GA,ECF,NC,I}, quote, char range, recompute: {expected, seen, tool: "sympy"}, ecf_from}`. |
| 05-MARK-014 | Word budget: the rendered rationale for a 20-mark item is ≤220 words excluding quotes; for a ≤5-mark item ≤80 words. Marking cards are exempt from the 120-word Turn budget (§04) but not from the praise lint. |

## 05.3 Mark-scheme schema: points, levels, mixed

One record per question part in `mark_scheme_items` (Pack table, §06.3). Wording is **our paraphrase** unless a licence sets `wording_status = licensed_verbatim`.

```jsonc
{
  "id": "ms_9701_21_MJ15_Q4b@2", "question_id": "9701/21/M/J/15/Q4", "part": "b",
  "syllabus_version": "9701:2025-2027", "paper": 2, "marks_total": 5,
  "command_word": "Describe", "command_word_def_ref": "syl_9701_2025#cw#Describe", "ao_ceiling": "AO2",
  "scheme_type": "points",                       // points | levels | mixed
  "generic_principles_ref": "cambridge:gmp:2024", "wording_status": "own_paraphrase",
  "context": null,
  "marking_points": [
    { "id": "M1", "type": "B", "marks": 1, "ao": "AO1",
      "credit_text": "lone pair on the nucleophile and a curly arrow from that lone pair to the carbonyl carbon",
      "conjunctive_conditions": ["lone pair drawn on CN⁻", "curly arrow originates at the lone pair", "arrow terminates at the carbonyl C"],

      "accept": ["δ+ shown on carbonyl C"], "reject": ["arrow from the negative charge sign"], "ignore": [],
      "alternatives": [], "ora": false, "notes": "Concerted attack; no intermediate before M3." },
    { "id": "M2", "type": "B", "marks": 1, "ao": "AO1",
      "credit_text": "partial charges on C=O and a curly arrow from the C=O bond to O",
      "conjunctive_conditions": ["δ+ on C and δ− on O", "arrow from the π bond to O"], "all_required": true },
    { "id": "M3", "type": "B", "marks": 1, "credit_text": "intermediate with negative charge on O", "conjunctive_conditions": ["tetrahedral intermediate drawn", "charge shown on O"], "all_required": true },
    { "id": "M4", "type": "DB", "marks": 1, "depends_on": "M3", "credit_text": "lone pair on O⁻ with arrow to H, and arrow from H–CN bond to C", "conjunctive_conditions": ["arrow lone pair→H", "arrow H–CN bond→C"], "all_required": true },
    { "id": "M5", "type": "B", "marks": 1, "credit_text": "CN⁻ regenerated", "alternatives": ["HCN shown as the proton source with CN⁻ shown afterwards"] }
  ],
  "levels": [], "best_fit": false,
  "ecf_policy": { "allowed": false, "scope": "none" },

  "indicative_content": [], "diagram_required": true, "vision_status": "provisional_teacher_confirm",
  "exemplars_ref": ["ex_9701_21_MJ15_Q4b_*"], "examiner_insight_refs": ["ei_9701_s15_011"],
```
