
A levels record differs in `levels[]` and `best_fit`:

```jsonc
{ "id": "ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3", "scheme_type": "levels", "marks_total": 20, "command_word": "Evaluate", "ao_ceiling": "AO4",
  "context": { "case_study_id": "9609/41/M/J/25/insert", "business_name": "Firm", "case_facts": ["retained profit $40 000", "gearing 68%", "net margin 4%", "family-owned", "owner plans sale in 3 years"] },
  "levels": [
    { "ao": "AO1", "max": 3, "bands": [ { "level": 2, "range": [2,3], "descriptor": "Developed knowledge of relevant concepts", "evidence_rule": "≥2 accurate concepts or one concept with its mechanism" },
                                       { "level": 1, "range": [1,1], "descriptor": "Limited knowledge", "evidence_rule": "1 accurate concept" } ] },
    { "ao": "AO2", "max": 2, "bands": [ { "level": 2, "range": [2,2], "descriptor": "Developed application to the business", "evidence_rule": "≥2 spans pass cover-the-name" },
                                       { "level": 1, "range": [1,1], "descriptor": "Limited application", "evidence_rule": "1 span passes cover-the-name" } ] },
    { "ao": "AO3", "max": 8, "bands": [ { "level": 2, "range": [4,8], "descriptor": "Developed analysis: two or more links in the chain", "evidence_rule": "≥1 chain with ≥2 counted causal links; 7–8 needs ≥2 developed chains on both sides of the question" },
                                       { "level": 1, "range": [1,3], "descriptor": "Limited analysis: one link in the chain", "evidence_rule": "≥1 chain with exactly 1 link" } ] },
    { "ao": "AO4", "max": 7, "bands": [ { "level": 3, "range": [6,7], "descriptor": "Effective evaluation: a developed, contextual judgement drawing together developed evaluative comments that balance key arguments", "evidence_rule": "committed judgement + weighing statement + case condition" },
                                       { "level": 2, "range": [3,5], "descriptor": "Developed evaluation: judgement supported by some evaluative comment", "evidence_rule": "judgement + ≥1 supported evaluative comment" },
                                       { "level": 1, "range": [1,2], "descriptor": "Limited evaluation: unsupported judgement or weak evaluative comment", "evidence_rule": "judgement asserted without support" } ] } ],
  "best_fit": true, "ecf_policy": { "allowed": false }, "indicative_content": [ { "id": "IC1", "text": "Ansoff: market development carries lower risk than diversification", "ao_hint": "AO3" } ] }
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-SCHM-001 | `type ∈ {M, A, B, DM, DB, FT}`; `A` and `DM/DB` require `depends_on`; awarding a dependent point without its dependency is a schema-level error. |
| 05-SCHM-002 | Conjunctive points ("lone pair AND curly arrow") are stored as `conjunctive_conditions[]` atoms with `all_required=true`; the engine credits the point only if every atom is evidenced, and reports which atom failed. |
| 05-SCHM-003 | Scheme "//" alternatives are stored in `alternatives[]` and credited **once**; "ORA" (or reverse argument) sets `ora=true` so the mirrored statement is creditable; `accept/reject/ignore` map the scheme's own lists. |
| 05-SCHM-004 | Every levels band carries an `evidence_rule` in machine-checkable terms (counted links, passed context spans, presence of judgement + weighing + condition). **All levels are always present**, including Level 0 semantics via `range [0,0]` when the grid defines it. **Why:** accuracy fell progressively as 6→3→1→0 rubric levels were omitted from context (medRxiv 2026). |
| 05-SCHM-005 | `best_fit=true` for Cambridge levels grids; strict-hierarchical grids set it false so the engine requires every lower band before the next. |
| 05-SCHM-006 | `ecf_policy.scope ∈ {none, within-part, across-parts, whole-question}`; `penalties.sig_fig_once_per_paper` and `units_missing ∈ {lose_A_mark, lose_B_mark, none}` follow the scheme's stated rules. |
| 05-SCHM-007 | Schemes are versioned (`@n`) and never overwritten; a Mark pins `scheme_id@n`. Series re-wording (e.g. Pearson IAL 2025) is a new version. |
| 05-SCHM-008 | `context.case_facts[]` is populated by the compiler from the insert (OWN summary of facts, not the insert text) and is the only ground truth for the cover-the-name test. |

## 05.4 Marking procedure per board; ECF/OFR; method and accuracy marks

The procedure prompt is selected from `boards.level_procedure`; the engine never uses a generic rubric-reasoning prompt.

| Board | `level_procedure` | What the levels engine does |
|---|---|---|
| Cambridge International | `best_fit` | Level each AO **independently** from its own grid. Read the whole response for that AO, pick the band whose descriptor is the best fit (a response need not meet every clause), then place within the band: bottom if the evidence rule is just met, top if met with margin. Never let AO3 evidence lift AO4. |
| AQA | `ladder_up` | Start at the lowest level; climb while the response meets the descriptor of the next level; the descriptor describes the *average* performance for the level; weight AOs per the question's stated split and do not over-reward one skill. |
| OCR | `top_down` | Start at the highest level and descend to the first level the response matches; within-level placement per OCR's borderline/bottom/consistent wording; use OCR annotations. |
| Pearson Edexcel | `bullet_evidence` | Bullets inside a level are AO-tagged; place holistically in the level, then top/bottom by how many bullets are evidenced. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-PROC-001 | The rationale names the procedure used ("Best fit within AO3: …"); the eval checks the named procedure matches `boards.level_procedure`. |
| 05-PROC-002 | **Developed analysis** = a chain with ≥2 counted causal links (`links_counted` from cause → mechanism → effect → consequence). Count links, never words. A paragraph with no connective (which means · so · therefore · as a result · leads to · consequently) and no causal structure is `ASSERTION_NO_LINK`. |
| 05-PROC-003 | **Application** is credited only for facts true of this business (cover-the-name test, 05-MARK-006). Repeating the business name is `GENERIC_NOT_CONTEXT`. |
| 05-PROC-004 | **Evaluation inside an Analyse item** earns 0 and produces the fixed line "Analyse — no evaluation marks are available on this question; the {n} sentences of judgement earned nothing." **Why:** the highest-frequency avoidable error in 9609 examiner reports. |
| 05-PROC-005 | A committed judgement is required for AO4 Level 3 in any Evaluate/Assess/Discuss/Recommend/Justify item: "both have merits; it depends" without a named decisive factor is Level 1. |
| 05-PROC-006 | **ECF / own-figure rule.** When a later step uses the candidate's own earlier wrong value with a correct method, award the method/FT marks and annotate `ECF`; ECF scope follows `ecf_policy.scope`; never award `cao` points by ECF. Rationale states "own figure carried forward from (a)". *Acceptance:* wrong (a) used correctly in (b) earns full method marks in (b). |
| 05-PROC-007 | **M/A/B rules.** M marks are independent unless `depends_on` says otherwise; A marks require their M; B marks are independent; DM/DB require the asterisked earlier mark; FT allowed only where `ecf_allowed` or `type=FT`; `isw` ignores subsequent working after a correct answer; `cao` demands the exact answer; `AG` (answer given) requires complete working. `SOI` (seen or implied), `AEF/OE` and `AWRT` are honoured via `accept[]`. |
| 05-PROC-008 | Every numeric or symbolic final is recomputed with SymPy from the candidate's own working before an A mark is awarded; a recompute mismatch on a correct-looking final is annotated `BOD` and flagged, never silently credited. |
| 05-PROC-009 | Sig-fig/rounding penalties (`RE`, `GA`) apply once per paper per the scheme; units missing lose exactly the mark the scheme names. |
| 05-PROC-010 | Annotation glyphs are the fixed set `✓ × Ø BOD CON RE GA ECF NC I` rendered in the answer margin (§09); each maps to a documented meaning shown on hover. |
| 05-PROC-011 | **Working required.** Calculation items award method marks only when working is visible; a bare wrong answer is 0 with the fixed warning "No working shown — a wrong final answer with no method scores zero." |
| 05-PROC-012 | Command word → AO ceiling from the Pack's verbatim table (Define/State/Identify → AO1; Explain/Calculate → AO1–2; Analyse → AO1–3; Discuss/Evaluate/Assess/Recommend/Advise/Justify → AO1–4). Definitions come from the syllabus version, never from model memory. |

## 05.5 The marking pipeline

```
Attempt(answer, item) ──► 0 Preconditions ──► 1 Assemble context (cached) ──► 2 Pre-checks
  ──► 3 Level-first-then-mark (levels) | 4 Point match + SymPy (points) ──► 5 Self-consistency
  ──► 6 Second family ──► 7 Disagreement policy ──► 8 Post-lint ──► 9 Persist ──► 10 Stream
```

| Step | Requirement (ID) |
|---|---|
| 0 Preconditions | **05-PIPE-001** Require: confirmed transcript (`transcript_confirmed=true`, §05.11), a `mark_scheme_items@n` for the part, and the policy object (tenant, age band, allowed providers). Missing scheme → feedback-only mode (05-SCOP-002). Effort Gate state is irrelevant in Mark mode: the student is submitting work, not asking for a solution. |
| 1 Context | **05-PIPE-002** The static prefix, byte-stable and ≥1,024 tokens for prompt caching (§08): examiner persona for this board · generic marking principles (paraphrase or licensed text) · the verbatim command-word definition · the full grid or marking points · indicative content · `context.case_facts` · **3–5 scored anchors** for this question family (Tier 0 ECR/specimen first, then Tier 1) with commentary · negative exemplars of lenient marking · the versioned marker instructions. Dynamic suffix: the transcript with line numbers. CI asserts `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` on golden Marks. **Why:** anchors in context are what make prompting-only AES accurate ("Anchor is the key", 2026). |
| 2 Pre-checks | **05-PIPE-003** Deterministic code, not a model: command-word → ceiling; word/line count and length bucket (for bias telemetry, never for marks); language detection; leak check that the answer is not a copy of the tutor's own prior Turn (sets `seen_solution` context); handwriting `[illegible]` token count (>10% → warn before marking). |
| 3 Levels | **05-PIPE-004** One structured call per Mark, but the schema forces **per-AO sequential reasoning: evidence spans → evidence-rule evaluation → level → mark within level**, in AO order, before any total. The total is computed by code from the per-AO marks, never emitted by the model. |
| 4 Points | **05-PIPE-005** Sonnet 5 draft matches every marking point to spans and runs SymPy on numeric steps; Opus 5 confirms only the points where the draft's confidence <0.8 or the recompute disagrees; ECF is resolved by code from `depends_on`/`ecf_policy`. |
| 5 Determinism | **05-PIPE-006** Temperature 0, structured JSON output, `seed` pinned. For levels items ≥12 marks run **n=3** and take the median mark per AO; if any AO level differs across runs, mark `confidence<0.6` for that AO and set `show_teacher_flag`. For 8-mark items n=1 unless the tenant is a school with two-marker mode on. Target: identical total ≥95%, identical level 100% across reruns. |
| 6 Second family | **05-PIPE-007** GPT-5.6 Sol marks independently from the same context on **100% of levels items ≥12 marks for the first two exam series per paper**, then 20% + all disputes and all challenges once the paper is `gated`. Points items: second family only on disagreement between draft and confirm. Both Marks are stored; the student sees one. **Why:** paired cross-family marks per paper are the most durable calibration asset (JUDGING 15). |
| 7 Disagreement | **05-PIPE-008** Agreement = every AO level identical and total within tolerance. Disagreement >1 level on any AO **or** total beyond tolerance → third family (Fable 5.1) breaks the tie by AO; if the three do not converge on a level, the Mark ships `provisional` for that AO with `show_teacher_flag=true` and enters the **human audit queue** (teacher of record if a Class exists, else the contracted-examiner queue, SLA 72 h). The student sees the modal Mark with "An examiner is checking AO4". |
| 8 Post-lint | **05-PIPE-009** Code checks: quotes are substrings (05-MARK-001); sums and ranges (05-MARK-002); reason codes valid; command-word cap applied; no praise, exclamation marks or emoji in any free-text field (§04 lint); rationale word budget (05-MARK-014); no verbatim grid sentence longer than the extract cap unless licensed (§06.2). Failure → one regeneration with the violation named → second family → error card, never a silent Mark. |
| 9 Persist | **05-PIPE-010** Write Mark, update Attempt (`mark_per_AO`, `confidence`, `policy_version`), enqueue Cards for lost marks (§04), emit Langfuse trace with model, cache hit, n, agreement, latency. |
| 10 Stream | **05-PIPE-011** Typed message parts: `mark.header` → `mark.ao` × k → `mark.command_word` → `mark.advice` → `mark.calibration` → `mark.done`. The client paints spans as each `mark.ao` arrives; earlier parts never reflow. |

**05-PIPE-012 Marker instructions vs grid.** Reflect-and-Revise refinement (≈200 held-out human-marked scripts per question family) rewrites only the **marker instructions** (interpretation notes, common-error rules, anchor commentary); the official grid and marking points are never edited by a model. Each refinement produces `policy_version+1`, which must re-pass the gate before it marks live traffic. **Why:** +0.19 to +0.47 QWK from rubric refinement against ~200 human-scored samples (arXiv 2510.09030).

**05-PIPE-013 Route and failover.** Primary Opus 5 (levels) / Sonnet 5→Opus 5 (points); failover on 529/503, 429 without retry-after <2 s, or TTFT >4 s to the second family, tagged in telemetry; EU/UK school tenants route via regional endpoints and never to DeepSeek; DeepSeek is never a marker (§08, §11).

## 05.6 Calibration and release gates

This subsection restates the FINAL rule in SYNTHESIS §8.5 as testable gates. The unit of gating is the **paper** (Examiner Twin instance); readiness `gold-seeded → gated → live` is computed, never set by hand.

**Gold sets (05-GATE-001).** Tier 0: Example Candidate Responses and specimen answers (seeds, never sole truth; enter via teacher upload where SSH-only). Tier 1: partner-school scripts double-marked by two teachers with the official scheme, **both marks kept** — this yields the human–human line per question family. Tier 2: teacher overrides confirmed by a second teacher or contracted examiner. Target ≈300 scripts per paper, stratified by tariff, command word, handwritten/typed, length quartile, region/L1. Synthetic answers are used only for robustness suites, never for headline metrics. Budget and staffing are FOUNDER-OWNED [E6] — [founder default]: ≈300 scripts × 6 papers with ex-examiner rates; without it, no published numbers and no predicted grades.

**Ship gate per paper (05-GATE-002, FINAL).** Marking becomes visible (numbers shown) when the paper meets **both**:

| Item class | Absolute floor (a) | Human-line rule (b) |
|---|---|---|
| Points (9709, 0580, 9609 calculations) | exact ≥97% · within ±1 ≥99.5% · per-marking-point F1 ≥0.90 | QWK ≥ measured human–human QWK on the same Tier-1 items |
| Levels 8–12 marks | QWK ≥0.75 · within ±1 ≥85% · AO-level agreement ≥80% | same |
| Levels 20–30 marks | QWK ≥0.70 · within ±2 ≥85% · AO4-level agreement ≥80% | same |
| All | rationale validity ≥95% (human audit: every credited span real and correctly read) · signed error within ±0.3 per 10 marks · run-to-run identical total ≥95% and identical level 100% · no fairness bucket (region, L1, handwritten, length) lagging overall QWK by >0.05 | |

Where the human line is not yet measured, (a) applies alone and every Mark carries the **provisional** badge. Ofqual's 0.52–0.96 figures are grade probabilities, not QWK; they justify measuring our own line, never lowering the floor.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-GATE-003 | **Badge-drop.** The provisional badge drops when the paper reaches the published stretch: QWK ≥0.80 (8–12) / ≥0.78 (20-mark) **and** the human line is measured and met. Below stretch but above gate the badge reads "Calibrated · agreement {qwk} · {n} scripts"; at stretch the same line without "provisional" anywhere in the Mark. |
| 05-GATE-004 | **Below gate:** feedback, spans, checks and advice show; `total_band=null`, no level numbers, no predicted grade. The header reads "Feedback only — this paper is not yet calibrated". |
| 05-GATE-005 | **Seeding with auto-pause.** 2–5% of production Marks per paper re-inject gold scripts (indistinguishable to the pipeline). Tolerance per question family = the scheme tolerance (05-MARK-009). A family whose rolling 20-seed window breaches tolerance on >15% of seeds, or whose signed error exceeds ±0.5 marks on 20-mark items, **pauses within one batch**: new Marks in that family route to the second family with the provisional badge, and the content lead is paged. Resume requires re-standardisation on the seed set. *Acceptance:* inject a deliberately lenient policy version in staging → pause fires before the 21st seed. |
| 05-GATE-006 | **Standardisation before live.** No `policy_version` or model change marks live traffic until it marks the seed set (ECRs + 20 teacher-marked scripts per family) within tolerance. Runs in CI as the marking gold-set gate (§13). |
| 05-GATE-007 | **Monthly bias audit** per model and paper: signed error and QWK by length quartile, handwritten/typed, region, L1, model family; results on the internal gate dashboard and, for gated papers, on the public page. |
| 05-GATE-008 | **Published per-paper calibration page** (in-product FINAL; external publication PROVISIONAL on [E7], [founder default] = yes, monthly). Fields per paper: state (gated / provisional / not yet calibrated), QWK, level agreement, within-tolerance %, signed error, n scripts, gold tiers used, human–human line, fairness buckets, series covered, policy version, last audit date, challenge rate and upheld rate. The marketing number must equal this page's number. |
| 05-GATE-009 | Teacher overrides (≤2 clicks, reason code, both marks stored) enter Tier 2 gold after second confirmation; a per-paper disagreement trend is reported quarterly; nothing enters a school-recorded grade without teacher confirmation (§10, §12). |

## 05.7 Challenge this Mark

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-CHAL-001 | One tap on any Mark: "Challenge this Mark". Optional one-line reason; optional AO selection. Never rate-limited per Mark; a student may challenge each Mark once per stage. |
| 05-CHAL-002 | Stage 1 (automatic, <60 s): re-mark by a **different family** from both the primary and the second marker of the original Mark, same context, same policy version. Render side-by-side: original vs re-mark per AO, with both rationales and the spans each credited. Outcome: `upheld` (within tolerance, same levels), `revised` (new modal Mark supersedes), or `split` (levels differ). |
| 05-CHAL-003 | Stage 2 (on `split`, or when the student taps "Still disagree"): escalate to the teacher of record if a Class exists (console queue, §10) else the contracted-examiner queue; SLA 72 h; the human sees transcript, image, all machine Marks and the scheme; the human Mark supersedes and, once confirmed by a second human, enters Tier 2 gold. |
| 05-CHAL-004 | Copy is examiner-voice and neutral: "Second look by another marker: AO3 unchanged (L2, 5/8); AO4 revised L1→L2 (+2). Reason: the sentence at L18 weighs the finance constraint against product dependence." Never apologise, never praise. |
| 05-CHAL-005 | Every challenge logs `{mark_id, stage, families, outcome, delta_per_ao, human_id?}`; targets: challenge rate <3% of Marks, upheld ≥70% of challenges (i.e. overturned <30%); a paper whose overturn rate exceeds 30% in a month is flagged on the gate dashboard and re-standardised. |
| 05-CHAL-006 | During between-papers mode (§04) challenges still work but Stage 2 SLA messaging says "after your paper" if the exam is within 72 h; no predicted-grade recomputation is triggered by a challenge in exam week. |

## 05.8 Predicted grades

The method is the board's: component raw → component threshold → Percentage Uniform Mark → option grade. Nothing is invented.

```python
def predicted_grade(course, attempts_by_paper, thresholds):          # thresholds: last ≥3 series per component
    per_paper = {}
    for paper in course.papers:
        raw = component_estimate(attempts_by_paper[paper])            # timed, unaided, gated Marks only; recency-weighted
        pums = []
        for series in thresholds[paper][-3:]:
            grade_floor = series.grade_at(raw)                        # A–E (no A* at component level)
            pums.append(series.pum_interpolate(raw))                  # linear between thresholds; A*=90 A=80 B=70 C=60 D=50 E=40 [verify per syllabus guide]
        per_paper[paper] = dict(raw=raw, pum_low=min(pums), pum_high=max(pums), marks_to_next=series.next_threshold(raw) - raw)
    option_pum = weighted_mean(per_paper, course.option_weights)      # e.g. A Level 9609: each paper raw/2 of 200
    return dict(grade_range=option_grade_band(option_pum_low, option_pum_high), per_paper=per_paper, series_used=[...])
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-PRED-001 | Inputs are only Marks from **gated** papers, produced under timed conditions or from full Timed Papers, unaided (no seen-solution Items), recency-weighted (half-life 6 weeks). Practice Marks in Learn mode never feed the estimate. |
| 05-PRED-002 | Output is a **range** across the last three series' thresholds, with the series named, the spread shown, and "marks to next grade" per component. A* is computed only at option (syllabus) level, never for a component. Label everywhere: "Practice estimate, not a board mark". |
| 05-PRED-003 | Unlock conditions, all required: paper `gated`; ≥3 series of thresholds loaded for that component; ≥3 marked Attempts on that paper meeting 05-PRED-001; the student is not in between-papers mode. Otherwise the panel shows what is missing ("2 of 3 timed attempts on Paper 2"). |
| 05-PRED-004 | Surfaces: **Progress › Paper** and the **mock debrief** only. Never Home, never notifications, never the parent digest unless the student enables "share predicted grade" (default off); teachers see it in the console for gated papers. |
| 05-PRED-005 | Threshold tables are ingested per series as facts (public PDFs, deep-linked); the PUM mapping is stored per syllabus from the official PUM guide and flagged "verify" until the compiler has read the guide for that syllabus. |
| 05-PRED-006 | Nothing from this engine flows into a school-recorded grade without teacher confirmation (Annex III human-oversight posture, §12). |
| 05-PRED-007 | Results day: with consent, the actual grade is stored against the last estimate; predicted-vs-actual error per paper is the trust metric (§14) and is published with the calibration page. |

## 05.9 The Timed Paper runner and the Principal-Examiner debrief

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-TIME-001 | A Timed Paper is built from Pack metadata (`papers.duration_min, marks, question_types, allowed_materials`) and either an original item set (default) or the student's own uploaded past paper (USER, transient, anchored by question numbers). The runner never displays Cambridge paper text it does not hold as OWN/LICENSED. |
| 05-TIME-002 | Layout: question-by-question navigation with **tariff pills** ("[8]", "[20]") and command word visible; a pacing bar per question at `minutes_per_mark = duration / marks` (9609 P4 1.9 · P2 1.5 · 9709 P1 1.47 · 9702 P5 2.5); an over-run turns the bar amber, never red, and never auto-advances. Mobile: one part per screen. |
| 05-TIME-003 | Timer inherits Course settings: extra-time % (0/25/50) and rest breaks that stop the clock; both set once in Settings and applied to every timer. Reading time is a separate pre-phase when the paper has an insert. |
| 05-TIME-004 | Answer input modes per part: text editor; math keypad with MathML output; table editor; camera (handwriting pipeline, §05.11, confirmation deferred to the end of the paper so the clock is not spent on OCR); structured diagram description. Autosave every 5 s; a dropped connection never loses work. |
| 05-TIME-005 | Predict-before-start ("What mark do you expect? Sure / Think so / Guessing") and postdict-after-submit are mandatory and feed Brier (§04). |
| 05-TIME-006 | On submit, all parts mark as one batch (points first, levels in tariff order); the debrief opens when ≥80% of marks are in; the rest stream. |
| 05-TIME-007 | **Principal-Examiner debrief** is generated only from the marked Attempts and the `examiner_insights` corpus, in the structure of a real report: *Key messages* (≤3) · *General comments* · *Comments on specific questions* (per lost-mark cluster). Each lost-mark cluster cites ≥1 ER insight with its series ("m25"); the historical-threshold line reads "Your 27/40 would have been a B in June 2025 and March 2025, an A in June 2024 (thresholds are historical)". |
| 05-TIME-008 | The debrief ends with exactly three scheduled retrieval tasks and one tap "Turn lost marks into Cards" (one Card per lost marking point/level gap, provenance "From your mock · 9609 P2 Q3(b)"). |
| 05-TIME-009 | Exam week: sat papers archive silently; the debrief hides predicted grades and rings; the tone rule is warm-brief-honest (§12). |
| 05-TIME-010 | Teacher mock import: a teacher uploads a class's scripts (tenant-scoped) → each becomes an Attempt + Mark for the student → the same debrief; teacher overrides feed gold (05-GATE-009). |

## 05.10 The original question generator

Under the three-provenance model the original item bank is the default practice corpus, so the generator is load-bearing at MVP (JUDGING 20).

```yaml
generate_item:
  inputs: {syllabus_node: "9609 5.3", paper: 2, tariff: 8, command_word: "Analyse", ao_split: {AO1: 2, AO2: 2, AO3: 4},
           cognitive_demand: "apply-analyse", stimulus: "case", misconception_target: "revenue_vs_profit", seed_family: null}
  outputs: {item_text, stimulus (fictional business, own currency, ≤180 words, 2–4 numeric facts), scheme: mark_scheme_items (own wording),
            pre_solve: model answer at each level + SymPy-verified numerics, tags: [node, ao_split, command_word, tariff, demand], provenance: OWN}
  checks: [command_word_verbatim, tariff_ao_valid_for_paper, style_similarity ≥ 0.8, solvability ≥ 0.98, near_duplicate_pass, stimulus_original, no_real_entities]
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-GEN-001 | Command words come only from the Pack's verbatim table for that syllabus version; tariff and AO split must be a legal combination for the paper type (`papers.question_types`), e.g. 9609 P1 Section A = (a) 2 + (b) 3; P1 Section B = 8 + 12; P4 = 20. |
| 05-GEN-002 | The scheme is emitted **with** the item, in our wording, through the same `mark_scheme_items` schema, including `context.case_facts` for stimulus items, then passes the schema lint (05-SCHM-*). |
| 05-GEN-003 | **Solvability**: an independent family (not the generator's) answers the item blind; numeric items must reproduce the key within the scheme's accept list; levels items must reach the top level under the emitted scheme. Batch pass rate ≥98%; failures are discarded, never repaired by hand. |
| 05-GEN-004 | **Style similarity**: a cross-family judge scores register, stimulus conventions and command-word usage against the paper's real-item *metadata profile* (length, numeric density, insert conventions), threshold 0.8. |
| 05-GEN-005 | **Near-duplicate check** against the reference index of real paper text (embeddings + 8-gram shingle hashes built from official public PDFs and tenant uploads; the index stores hashes and vectors, never displayable text). Reject if cosine ≥0.85 to any real question or any 8-gram shingle overlap ≥3 with a real stimulus. *Acceptance:* feeding a real 9609 question through the generator as a "variant" is rejected 100%. |
| 05-GEN-006 | Stimulus rules: fictional business names checked against a blocklist of real companies and prior stimuli; no third-party text; numbers internally consistent (SymPy check on ratios stated in the case). |
| 05-GEN-007 | **"5 more like this"** holds `tariff`, `command_word`, `ao_split` and `cognitive_demand` fixed and varies surface (industry, numbers, stakeholder); interleaving rules from §04 apply after first exposure. |
| 05-GEN-008 | QA sampling: 5% of new items per paper per week to a teacher/ex-examiner review queue; teacher rejection <10% is a release metric; rejected items and reasons feed the generator instructions (never the schema). Items carry `item_stats` from day one so facility and discrimination accumulate toward IRT (v2). |
| 05-GEN-009 | Every generated item renders with the label "Original item · in the style of 9609 Paper 2"; never "past paper", never a board logo. |

## 05.11 The handwriting pipeline

```
photo(s) ──► capture & normalise ──► VLM transcription (layout-preserving) ──► confidence per token
      ──► student confirms / corrects ("Looks right" required) ──► Mark from transcript AND image ──► original kept
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 05-HAND-001 | Capture: auto-crop and deskew, ≤2,000 px longest side, multi-page ordering, QR hand-off from desktop to phone camera. Reject blur (Laplacian variance below threshold) with a one-line retake prompt, never a modal. |
| 05-HAND-002 | Transcription route: Gemini 3.1 Pro for dense/cursive pages, Gemini 3.8 Flash for routine; **Mathpix** for exact maths when the Course subject ∈ {9709, 0580, 9702, 9701, 9700} and the page contains formulae; fallback Claude high-res tier. Budget $0.003–0.015 per page; transcript visible <20 s p95. |
| 05-HAND-003 | The OCR prompt preserves layout and working: line breaks, crossings-out as `~~text~~` (never silently dropped — a crossed-out correct answer is not credited, a crossed-out wrong one is not penalised), insertions, arrows, table structure, units and superscripts; maths as LaTeX. Per-token confidence is returned. |
| 05-HAND-004 | **Illegible tokens are flagged `[illegible]`, never guessed.** Tokens with confidence <0.7 are underlined in the confirm view; the student taps to correct. Pages with >10% flagged tokens show "Retake for a better Mark" before proceeding. |
| 05-HAND-005 | Confirmation is mandatory: side-by-side image and editable transcript; "Looks right" sets `transcript_confirmed=true`; edits are diffed and stored (`transcript_edits`) for OCR evaluation. Marking never proceeds on an unconfirmed transcript. **Why:** ≈88% of raw transcriptions are usable for rubric grading (arXiv 2603.00895); confirmation removes most of the remaining errors for free. |
| 05-HAND-006 | The marker receives the confirmed transcript **and** the image; it quotes only the transcript; it may use the image to resolve a flagged token only if the student left it flagged, and then credits nothing that depends on it. |
| 05-HAND-007 | **Diagrams and mechanisms** (Ansoff/BCG grids, break-even and supply–demand charts, curly-arrow mechanisms, P5 graphs): the VLM emits a structured description (`{axes[], labels[], curves[], shifts[], arrows[{from,to}], charges[], intersections[]}`) against the item's diagram checklist; the Mark for those points ships **"Provisional — teacher confirm"** until a ≥300-item human-marked diagram gold set exists per diagram family and passes 05-GATE-002. |
| 05-HAND-008 | Original images are kept encrypted per tenant retention policy (default 12 months, deletable by the student), available to the teacher of record for override review, never used for training. |
| 05-HAND-009 | Evaluation: character error rate on a held-out set of real student pages per subject (target CER ≤3% typed-equivalent after confirmation; ≤8% before); OCR failures never count against marking QWK — they are a separate dashboard line. |

## 05.12 Worked examples: a 20-mark Paper 4 Mark and a 5-mark Paper 1 Mark

Two end-to-end Marks. Both are OWN Items (05-GEN-009) so nothing on this page reproduces board text; both instantiate the schemas in 05.2 and 05.3 unchanged. Use them as the fixtures behind 15-RUBR-003 (renderer snapshot), 13-MARK-*, and the acceptance test in 06-PSTE-006. Character offsets below are real offsets into the transcripts printed here — a builder can run 05-MARK-001 against them.

### (a) 20-mark Paper 4 essay, levels engine

**Item** `it_9609_p4_0117` · rendered as "Original item · in the style of 9609 Paper 4" · scheme `ms_own_9609_p4_0117@1`, which instantiates the levels grid printed in 05.3 (`AO1` 3, `AO2` 2, `AO3` 8, `AO4` 7; `best_fit: true`) with the same `context.case_facts`.

```
Firm is a family-owned manufacturer of specialist kitchen equipment. 82% of its
revenue comes from one product line. Net profit margin is 4%, gearing is 68% and
retained profit for the year was $40 000. The owner intends to sell the business
in three years.

Evaluate whether Firm should pursue diversification rather than market
development in order to increase the value of the business before its sale. [20]
```

**Student answer** (typed, 332 words, transcript `att_01JXB2…`, line refs are transcript lines):

```
L1  Diversification means selling new products in new markets. Market development
L2  means selling existing products in new markets. Both are growth strategies in
L3  Ansoff's matrix and both carry risk, although the risk is not the same kind of
L4  risk in each case.
L6  One argument for market development is that the product already exists, so the
L7  firm does not pay product development costs and can use the factory it already
L8  has. This would help Firm grow. Market development is less risky so profits will
L9  rise.
L11 However, diversification would reduce Firm's dependence on one product line,
L12 which currently provides 82% of revenue. If demand for kitchen equipment falls,
L13 almost all of Firm's revenue falls with it, so a second unrelated line would
L14 spread that risk. The problem is finance: the $40 000 retained profit constraint
L15 means diversification's set-up costs would need debt, and with gearing already at
L16 68% lenders may refuse or charge more, which would cut the thin 4% margin
L17 further. So the option that lowers risk in the long run raises financial risk
L18 now, and the owner only has three years before the sale.
L20 Diversification also takes a long time to establish. New products often fail and
L21 managers can be spread too thinly across two unrelated markets. Market
L22 development into export markets would use the same factory, so capacity would
L23 not need extra capital, and the workforce would already know the product.
L25 There is also the marketing side of the decision. Selling an existing kitchen
L26 product in a new country still needs research, distribution and promotion, and
L27 the business has never sold abroad before, so it would be paying to learn as it
L28 goes. Some businesses find this cheaper than starting a new product line and
L29 some do not.
L31 In conclusion, both strategies have advantages and disadvantages and it really
L32 depends on the situation of the business. Firm should choose whichever one is
L33 best for it, as long as the strategy is managed carefully and the owner keeps an
L34 eye on the finances.
```

**Mark** (compact; fields omitted here are exactly as in 05.2):

```jsonc
{ "mark_id": "mrk_01JXB2Q9…", "attempt_id": "att_01JXB2…",
```

# §06 The library: content, curriculum packs, licensing

## 06.1 The three-provenance content model

Every byte of content Margin retrieves, displays, marks against or exports belongs to exactly one of three provenance classes. The class is a column, not a convention: it is set at ingest, carried on every `documents`, `chunks`, `items`, `mark_schemes` and `examiner_insights` row (§11.2), checked by the retrieval prefilter (11-RAG-003) and by the render layer, and audited in the `provenance_ledger`. There is no fourth class. A document that cannot be assigned one of the three is not ingested.

### Definitions

| Class | Definition (exact) | Examples | May be pooled into global retrieval | May display text | May be exported (Receipts, Cards, print) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OWN` | Content authored by Margin staff, contractors or generators under our own copyright: original Items and stimuli (05-GEN), our paraphrased scheme wording (`wording_status=own_paraphrase`), `examiner_insights.text`, syllabus-graph nodes we wrote, facts extracted from public documents (syllabus statements, paper structures, AO weights, thresholds), page/question anchors that point at official PDFs. | `it_9609_5.3_0412`, `ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3` (paraphrase), `ei_9609_m25_004`, `syl_9609_2026#2.2.1` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `LICENSED` | Third-party text or images held under a written agreement recorded as a `licences` row with `licence_id, licensor, scope, territories[], display_rights ∈ {grounding_only, extracts, full_text}, expiry, max_quote_words`. Nothing is `LICENSED` until counsel has filed the signed instrument and its `licence_id` exists. | Endorsed coursebook chapters under a Cambridge University Press & Assessment or CLA agreement; verbatim grid wording if Cambridge grants it (`wording_status=licensed_verbatim`). | Yes, only within `scope.syllabus_codes[]` and `territories[]` | Per `display_rights` | Only if `scope.export=true` |
| `USER` | Files a student, teacher or school uploads: past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports, School Support Hub material, textbook photos, notes (including the founder-supplied ZNotes text until a ZNotes agreement exists, SYNTHESIS §9). Processed for the uploading principal only; the `partition_key` is the uploader's tenant (or the user id for individuals); retention per `uploads.retention_until`. | `upl_01JX…` (9609 s24 P4 mark scheme photographed by a teacher), the founder's mechanisms file (`licence_basis="user"` in 05.3) | **Never** | Yes, to the owning principal only | Only to the owning principal, never in a shared artefact |

`licence_basis` on the ledger refines the class: `own`, `licensed:<licence_id>`, `user`, `public_with_permission:<permission_ref>`. `public_with_permission` is a sub-case of `LICENSED` (a written permission is a licence); a public URL alone is never a basis. **Why:** UK law offers no commercial TDM exception (March 2026 report) and Cambridge refuses electronic republication of questions, schemes and ERs; a "we found it online" class would be the exact thing a takedown targets (GL §A1, §A4).

### Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-PROV-001 | `provenance ∈ {OWN, LICENSED, USER}` is a `NOT NULL` enum on `documents`, `chunks`, `items`, `mark_schemes`, `examiner_insights`, `textbook_sections`, `figures`, `exemplars`. A migration adding a fourth value fails CI (schema lint asserts the enum has exactly three members). *Acceptance:* `INSERT … provenance='scraped'` raises; the enum test is in the migration suite. |
| 06-PROV-002 | **Retrieval never mixes tenants' USER content.** Every retrieval call names its partitions explicitly: `['global']` plus at most one tenant partition, equal to the caller's `org_id` (or `user:<id>` for individuals). Two tenant partitions in one query is a request-validation error, not a filtered result. *Acceptance:* the isolation suite (11-DATA-004) runs 10,000 randomised queries across 50 synthetic tenants and returns 0 cross-tenant chunks; a query naming two tenant partitions returns HTTP 400. |
| 06-PROV-003 | **USER content is never embedded into the global partition** and never used to build OWN artefacts that quote it. Generators (05-GEN), Card builders (§04) and the compiler may *read* a tenant's USER chunk only inside that tenant's job; any OWN row they emit must pass 05-GEN-005's near-duplicate check against USER text as well as official text. *Acceptance:* a fixture uploads a unique 40-word paragraph as USER; no OWN row created in the following 24 h contains an 8-gram of it. |
| 06-PROV-004 | **LICENSED served only where scope allows.** The prefilter joins `licences` and drops chunks where `now() > expiry`, `caller.residency ∉ territories`, `course.syllabus_code ∉ scope.syllabus_codes`, or the requested rendering exceeds `display_rights`. A chunk allowed for grounding but not display reaches the model with `render=false` and can be cited but never quoted (06.6). *Acceptance:* flipping a licence's `expiry` to yesterday removes its chunks from the next query with no deploy; a `grounding_only` chunk quoted verbatim fails the post-lint (05-PIPE-009 extends to Learn Turns). |
| 06-PROV-005 | Every OWN paraphrase records what it paraphrases: `source_ref {document_id, page, bbox?}` pointing at the official PDF's location, so the citation chip can deep-link (06.6) without holding the text. A paraphrase row without `source_ref` is a lint error unless `kind=original_item`. |
| 06-PROV-006 | Class is immutable per document version. Re-classifying (e.g. USER → LICENSED when the ZNotes agreement lands) is a **new** `doc_id` ingested from the licensed copy, with the old USER copies untouched. **Why:** a licence covers a specific file the licensor supplied, not whatever a user photographed. |
| 06-PROV-007 | The kill switch (06.10) applies to all three classes identically: `provenance_ledger.kill_switch=true` removes the document's chunks from the prefilter, its `items` from practice selection, its rows from any Pack build and its extracts from caches within the SLA. |

### Provenance ledger entry

Append-only; one row per document version; every row signed into the daily audit hash chain (§12).

```yaml
provenance_ledger:
  ledger_id: pl_01JXQ7…                 # ULID
  doc_id: doc_9609_syl_2026             # stable across versions; version below
  doc_version: 3
  provenance: OWN | LICENSED | USER
  licence_basis: own | licensed:lic_cupa_2027_01 | user | public_with_permission:perm_cb_2026_11
  licence_id: lic_cupa_2027_01 | null
  source_url: https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/697371-2026-2028-syllabus.pdf | null   # official page for facts/anchors; null for USER
  sha256: "9f1c…e2"                     # of the ingested bytes
  bytes: 2481773
  ingested_at: 2026-10-03T14:02:11Z
  ingested_by: user_id | job_id
  uploader_org_id: org_… | null         # USER only; equals partition_key
  partition_key: global | org_01… | user_01…
  expiry: 2028-08-31 | null             # licence end; AQA 3-year public window; Pearson 5-year; USER retention_until
  display_rights: full_text | extracts | grounding_only | anchors_only
  text_status: own | licensed | ref_only
  trust_rank: 1..6
  kill_switch: false
  takedown: {requested_at: null, requester: null, notice_id: null, removed_at: null, reinstated_at: null}
  derived_from: [doc_id@version, …]     # OWN paraphrases list their official sources
  checksum_prev: "…"                    # hash chain
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-PROV-008 | `source_url` is mandatory for `OWN` rows with `derived_from ≠ []` and for `LICENSED`; `sha256` mandatory for all; `uploader_org_id` mandatory for USER. Rows are never updated except `kill_switch`, `takedown.*` and `expiry` (extension by a new licence version). *Acceptance:* trigger rejects any other `UPDATE`; hash chain verifies nightly. |
| 06-PROV-009 | The ledger is queryable by the takedown desk in ≤1 s by `sha256`, `source_url`, `doc_id` or free text over titles; the answer lists every chunk, item, scheme, insight and cache key derived from the document (via `derived_from` closure). |

### Tests the class model must pass before any Pack is `live`

1. **Class purity:** a SQL assertion that no chunk in `partition_key='global'` has `provenance='USER'` (run on every ingest batch and nightly).
2. **Scope fence:** for each `licence_id`, sample 200 queries from a tenant outside `territories` — 0 chunks returned.
3. **Ref-only fence:** for every `documents.text_status='ref_only'` row, `chunks.text` is empty and only `{page, bbox, question_ref}` anchors exist (11-RAG-004).
4. **Derivation closure:** killing a random official document removes 100% of the insights and paraphrases whose `derived_from` includes it (06.10).
5. **Founder library check:** the twelve ZNotes-derived files and the mechanisms file from the corpus sample are classified USER under the founder's org, `trust_rank=5` (revision notes) or `6` (hand-compiled scheme extracts, rising to `3` per record once a human confirms the transcription against the official scheme in 06.7 — the 05.3 example shows the confirmed state), and none of their text appears in `global`.

## 06.2 What is stored, what is displayed, what is deep-linked

This subsection is the storage-and-display matrix the render layer, the cache and the compiler all read from. Three verbs are distinct in code: **store** (bytes in our object storage or text in `chunks.text`), **display** (text or image painted in a Margin surface), **deep-link** (a chip or button that opens the rights-holder's own page in a new tab or the in-app browser). A document may be stored for grounding and not displayed; a document may be deep-linked and never stored.

### The matrix

| Content | Store | Display | Deep-link | Class / basis | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Syllabus **facts**: codes, paper structure, durations, marks, AO weights, topic numbering, learning-objective statements restated, command-word list | Yes (OWN facts, `derived_from` the syllabus PDF) | Yes | Yes, to the official syllabus PDF `#page=` | OWN | Facts are not copyright; keep wording ours except the command-word *definitions*, which are stored verbatim as short quotations under the extract rule (needed for 05-PROC-012). |
| Command-word definitions (verbatim) | Yes, ≤40 words each | Yes, as an attributed quotation with chip | Yes | OWN-quotation (extract rule) | 18 definitions × ≤40 words; logged as extracts once per Pack build, not per view. |
| Official board PDFs: past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports, specimen papers, ECRs | **Never re-hosted.** Store only: `sha256`, page count, per-question page anchors `{question_ref, page, bbox}`, our OWN paraphrases and insights. `chunks.text` empty (`text_status=ref_only`). | Never (no viewer) | Yes, to the exact official URL when public; "Open on School Support Hub" when SSH-only | OWN anchors; the PDF itself is not held | Cambridge refuses electronic publication of questions, schemes and ERs (GL §A1). The Paper Companion anchors feedback to question numbers on the student's own copy. |
| Grade-threshold tables | Yes, as numbers (`thresholds`, `option_thresholds`) | Yes | Yes, to the thresholds PDF | OWN facts | 05-PRED-005. |
| Short attributed extracts from any board or publisher document | Yes, the extract text only, inside the OWN row that cites it (`extract_text`, `extract_words`) | Yes, quoted, with chip | Mandatory alongside | OWN-quotation | Limits below. |
| Endorsed textbook pages | Only under a `licence_id` with `display_rights ≥ extracts`; stored as `textbook_sections` + chunks in `global` | Per `display_rights` | Yes, to the publisher's product page or licensed reader URL | LICENSED | Without a licence: not stored, not displayed; a student may upload their own copy (USER). |
| Revision notes (ZNotes and similar) | Global only under a licence; otherwise USER | USER: to owner only | Yes, to the publisher's page | LICENSED or USER | SYNTHESIS §9: ZNotes is USER until an agreement exists. |
| User uploads (papers, schemes, ERs, SSH material, notes, photos of textbook pages) | Yes, tenant partition, encrypted at rest, `retention_until` | Owner only; teacher-of-record sees a student's upload only when attached to an Attempt in a `receipt_required` assignment | n/a | USER | Transient: default retention 12 months, deletable any time, deletion propagates to chunks and caches ≤24 h. |
| Handwritten answer images | Yes, per 05-HAND-008 | Owner + teacher of record | n/a | USER | Never training data. |
| Our original items, stimuli, schemes, insights, model answers | Yes | Yes | Chip to the *source* they were derived from where applicable | OWN | Rendered with "Original item · in the style of …" (05-GEN-009). |

### Extract limits (enforced, not advisory)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-STOR-001 | An **extract** is verbatim text from a non-OWN, non-`full_text` source. Hard caps per extract: **≤40 words and ≤2 sentences**; per Turn or Mark: **≤3 extracts, ≤100 words total**; per Session: **≤12 extracts**; per document per user per day: **≤10% of the document's pages may be touched by extracts** (page count from the ledger). A licence with `max_quote_words` overrides the per-extract cap in either direction. *Acceptance:* the post-lint counts words of every quoted span against the source chunk; a 41-word quotation fails the Turn and regenerates with the cap named. |
| 06-STOR-002 | **Grid and marking-point wording is never displayed verbatim** without `wording_status=licensed_verbatim`, regardless of length. The Mark shows `descriptor_relied_on.paraphrase` and a chip to the page (05-MARK, 05-PIPE-009). *Acceptance:* the 300 gold Marks contain 0 sentences with ≥8-gram overlap with the ingested official scheme text. |
| 06-STOR-003 | Every displayed extract is **attributed inline** in the fixed form `"…quoted text…" — {Board}, {syllabus code}/{component} {series}, {document type}, p.{page}` with a chip that deep-links (06.6). An extract without a resolvable chip is not rendered; the sentence falls back to paraphrase. |
| 06-STOR-004 | Extracts are **audit-logged**: `{user_id, org_id, doc_id, page, chunk_id, words, surface, turn_id | mark_id, at}` to `extract_log`, retained 3 years, exportable per document for a licensor or a takedown response. |
| 06-STOR-005 | **User uploads are transient and private.** Default `retention_until = uploaded_at + 12 months` (school tenants may set 1–36 months); a student's "Delete this file" removes the object, chunks, figure crops, derived Cards' source text (Cards keep the student's own wording), and cache entries within 24 h and writes the ledger `takedown.removed_at`. Uploads never enter `global`, never train anything, never appear in another user's citations. *Acceptance:* delete → query → 0 chunks within 24 h; nightly job proves no `USER` row in `global`. |
| 06-STOR-006 | The **Papers surface** and the Paper Companion open official PDFs by deep link in the in-app browser; Margin never proxies, caches or screenshots the PDF bytes server-side. For SSH-only material the surface shows the teacher-upload path and the string "Your school can download this from the School Support Hub." |

### Caching rules

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-STOR-007 | Prompt caches (§08) may contain LICENSED text only for tenants inside the licence's territory, keyed with `licence_id` and `residency`; they may contain USER text only in a cache key that includes `org_id` (or `user_id`), TTL ≤1 h. OWN text caches freely. A kill switch or licence expiry invalidates every cache key that lists the `doc_id` in its manifest (06.10). |
| 06-STOR-008 | Client-side and CDN caches never receive extract text or LICENSED text as static assets; they are rendered inside authenticated Turn/Mark payloads only. Offline (11-OFF-001) may store OWN documents and LICENSED documents whose licence has `offline=true`; never USER documents belonging to another principal. |
| 06-STOR-009 | Reference index for the near-duplicate check (05-GEN-005) stores **hashes and vectors, never displayable text**, for official and USER text alike; that index is exempt from extract caps because nothing in it can be rendered. |

### Per-region variations

| Region (tenant `residency`) | Variation |
|---|---|
| UK | Quotation exception (CDPA s.30) is the legal basis for extracts; caps above apply; no commercial TDM exception, so no crawling. Board public windows honoured as `expiry`: AQA 3 years, Pearson 5 years — after expiry, anchors only. |
| EU | Same caps; DSM Art. 4 opt-outs mean no crawling of board sites; LICENSED chunks served only if `territories` includes EU; residency routing per §11 keeps LICENSED and USER text on EU endpoints. |
| US | College Board FRQs and scoring guidelines are publicly posted; still `ref_only` until a permission is filed; extracts allowed under the same caps (fair-use posture); *Thomson Reuters v. Ross* argues against systematic display of editorial scheme text, so the caps are not loosened. |
| Kazakhstan / Russia / rest of world | Same product rules; regional pricing does not change content rights; DeepSeek never sees USER or LICENSED text (SYNTHESIS §15 E5). |

**Why:** the four-pattern analysis (GL §A4) rates transient user processing strongest, short attributed extracts weak-but-defensible, and server-side hosting of board PDFs indefensible without a licence; the matrix encodes exactly that ordering.

## 06.3 The curriculum Pack schema

A Pack is the complete curriculum dataset for one syllabus version, serialised as one versioned document tree in Postgres (Pack plane, `org_id NULL`, §11.2) and exportable as a single YAML bundle for review, diff and CI. Every Mark pins `pack_version` (05.2 header); every Course pins it (11-DATA-005). Below is the canonical bundle. Tables named in F§7.1 and §11.2 are the storage form; this is the logical form the compiler emits and the eval harness consumes.

```yaml
pack:
  id: pack_9609_2026_2028
  version: "2026.11.2"                       # calendar.minor; bumped on every publish
  board: {id: caie, name: "Cambridge International", country: GB,
          marking_paradigm: expert_marked, level_procedure: best_fit,
          annotation_vocab: ["✓","×","Ø","BOD","CON","RE","GA","ECF","NC","I"]}
  syllabus:
    code: "9609"
    subject: Business
    level: "A Level"                          # IGCSE | O Level | AS | A Level | IB HL | AP …
    version_window: {first_exam: 2026, last_exam: 2028}
    source: {doc_id: doc_9609_syl_2026, source_url: "https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/697371-2026-2028-syllabus.pdf", sha256: "…", text_status: own_facts}
    grade_scale: ["A*","A","B","C","D","E","U"]
    pum_map: {"A*": 90, A: 80, B: 70, C: 60, D: 50, E: 40}   # verify_status: pending until the PUM guide is read (05-PRED-005)
    command_words:                             # verbatim, ≤40 words each; the only verbatim board text in the Pack
      - {word: Evaluate, definition: "judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something", ao_ceiling: AO4, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p46"}
      - {word: Analyse, definition: "examine in detail to show meaning, identify elements and the relationship between them", ao_ceiling: AO3, source_ref: "doc_9609_syl_2026#p46"}
      # … all 18
    assessment_objectives:
      - {ao: AO1, name: "Knowledge and understanding", weight_pct: 25}
      - {ao: AO2, name: "Application", weight_pct: 25}
      - {ao: AO3, name: "Analysis", weight_pct: 25}
      - {ao: AO4, name: "Evaluation", weight_pct: 25}
  papers:
    - {number: 1, name: "Business Concepts 1", duration_min: 75, marks: 40, ao_weights: {AO1: 35, AO2: 30, AO3: 20, AO4: 15},
       question_types: [{section: A, count: 4, parts: [{marks: 2},{marks: 3}]}, {section: B, choose: 1, of: 2, parts: [{marks: 8},{marks: 12}]}],
       allowed_materials: [], minutes_per_mark: 1.875, level: AS}
    - {number: 2, name: "Business Concepts 2", duration_min: 90, marks: 60, ao_weights: {AO1: 30, AO2: 30, AO3: 20, AO4: 20}, question_types: [{data_response: 2}], minutes_per_mark: 1.5, level: AS}
    - {number: 3, name: "Business Decision-Making", duration_min: 105, marks: 60, ao_weights: {AO1: 20, AO2: 27, AO3: 23, AO4: 30}, question_types: [{case_study: 1, questions: 4}], minutes_per_mark: 1.75, level: A2}
    - {number: 4, name: "Business Strategy", duration_min: 75, marks: 40, ao_weights: {AO1: 15, AO2: 10, AO3: 40, AO4: 35}, question_types: [{essays: 2, marks_each: 20, on_case: true}], minutes_per_mark: 1.875, level: A2}
  thresholds:                                  # facts, deep-linked; ≥3 series required for predicted grades
    - {paper: 4, variant: 41, series: "M/J/2025", grades: {A: 27, B: 23, C: 19, D: 15, E: 11}, source_url: "…thresholds pdf", doc_id: doc_9609_thr_s25}
  syllabus_graph:                              # §07.6 nodes/edges; official numbering only
    nodes:
      - {id: "syl_9609_2026#5.3", path: "5.3", title: "Costs", objective_text: "…our restatement…", level: AS,
         misconceptions: ["revenue_vs_profit", "fixed_costs_never_change"], diagnostic_distractors: ["Profit = revenue − variable costs"],
         command_words_seen: [Calculate, Explain, Analyse], tariff_histogram: {2: 14, 3: 9, 8: 6, 12: 4}}
    edges:
      - {src: "syl_9609_2026#5.3", dst: "q_9609_22_MJ24_Q1b", kind: assesses, confidence: 0.97, provenance: compiler_v3+human}
      - {src: "syl_9609_2026#5.3", dst: "syl_9609_2026#5.4", kind: prerequisite_of, confidence: 0.85, provenance: editor}
      - {src: "syl_9609_2026#5.3", dst: "syl_0450_2026#4.2", kind: equivalent_to, confidence: 0.9, provenance: compiler_v3}
      - {src: "syl_9609_2026#5.3", dst: "tb_cupa_9609_cb3#ch22", kind: explained_in, confidence: 0.95, provenance: licence:lic_cupa_2027_01}
  questions:                                   # metadata always; text only where OWN/LICENSED
    - id: "9609/41/M/J/25/Q1"
      paper: 4, variant: 41, series: "M/J", year: 2025, number: 1, part: null
      marks: 20, command_word: Evaluate, ao_ceiling: AO4, ao_split: {AO1: 3, AO2: 2, AO3: 8, AO4: 7}
      tags:                                    # §15.D tagging schema
        syllabus_nodes: ["syl_9609_2026#6.2", "syl_9609_2026#6.4"]
        cognitive_demand: evaluate
        stimulus: case_study
        skills: [ansoff, finance_constraint, risk]
        difficulty_prior: 0.62
        diagram_required: false
      text_status: ref_only                    # Cambridge default: canonical ID + anchors, no text
      anchors: {qp: {doc_id: doc_9609_41_s25_qp, page: 2, bbox: [72, 140, 540, 420]}, ms: {doc_id: doc_9609_41_s25_ms, page: 4}, insert: {doc_id: doc_9609_41_s25_in, pages: [2, 3]}}
      official_links: {qp: "https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/…", ms: null, ssh_only: [ms, er]}
      scheme_ref: "ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3"
      exemplar_refs: ["ex_9609_41_MJ25_Q1_ecr_a", "ex_9609_41_MJ25_Q1_t1_017"]
      item_stats: {n: 412, p_correct_modal: 0.48, discrimination: 0.41, mean_latency_s: 1410}
  mark_scheme_items:                           # 05.3 schema, one per part; wording_status per record
    - {ref: "ms_9609_41_MJ25_Q1@3", inline: true}   # full 05.3 record embedded in the bundle
  examiner_insights:                           # OWN paraphrase; never ER text
    - id: ei_9609_m25_004
      scope: {syllabus_node: "syl_9609_2026#*", paper: 4}
      series: m25
      pattern: common_error                    # scored_well | weaker_responses | common_error
      text: "Examiners report that repeating the business name is not application; credit needs a fact that is true only of this business."
      student_tip: "Use a number or constraint from the case, not its name."
      heuristic: {kind: regex_or_classifier, spec: "business_name_mention AND NOT case_fact_within_25_words", fires_on: AO2}
      source_pointer: {doc_id: doc_9609_m25_er, page: 7, paragraph: 3, official_url: null, ssh_only: true}
      provenance: OWN
      wording_check: {max_8gram_overlap_with_source: 0}
  textbook_sections:                           # only under licence
    - {id: tb_cupa_9609_cb3#ch22, document_id: doc_cupa_9609_cb3, title: "Costs and break-even", path: "22", page_start: 318, page_end: 331,
       licence_id: lic_cupa_2027_01, display_rights: extracts, trust_rank: 2, provenance: LICENSED, expiry: 2028-08-31}
  exemplars:
    - {id: ex_9609_41_MJ25_Q1_t1_017, question_id: "9609/41/M/J/25/Q1", source: teacher_double_marked, marks: {AO1: 3, AO2: 1, AO3: 5, AO4: 3}, marks_second: {AO1: 3, AO2: 2, AO3: 5, AO4: 2},
       commentary: "…", handwritten: true, blob_key: "…", provenance: USER→gold_consented, org_id: org_partner_01, consent_id: cst_…}
  trust_ranks: {syllabus: 1, endorsed_textbook: 2, mark_scheme: 3, examiner_report: 4, revision_notes: 5, user_upload: 6}
  provenance_ledger: [ {ledger_id: pl_…, doc_id: doc_9609_syl_2026, provenance: OWN, licence_basis: own, expiry: null, …},
                       {ledger_id: pl_…, doc_id: doc_cupa_9609_cb3, provenance: LICENSED, licence_basis: "licensed:lic_cupa_2027_01", expiry: 2028-08-31, …} ]
  readiness:
    state: gated                               # draft → ingested → mapped → gold_seeded → gated → live
    per_paper: {1: gated, 2: gated, 3: provisional, 4: gated}
    mapped_pct: 0.985                          # questions linked to scheme items (≥0.95 for `mapped`)
    gold_per_family_min: 4                     # ≥3 for `gold_seeded`
    gate_report_ref: gate_9609_2026.11.2
  changelog:
    - {version: "2026.11.2", at: 2026-11-19, by: editor_07, summary: "Renumbered 5.3.2→5.3.3 after syllabus update; 14 new insights from m25 ER; scheme ms_9609_22_MJ24_Q2b@2 conjunctive split", migration_note: "Pack updated to 2026–28 v2 — 2 syllabus points renumbered", diff_ref: "s3://…/diff.json"}
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-PACK-001 | The bundle validates against `schemas/pack.v1.json` in CI; a Pack that fails validation cannot advance past `draft`. Required top-level keys: `board, syllabus, papers, syllabus_graph, questions, mark_scheme_items, examiner_insights, trust_ranks, provenance_ledger, readiness, changelog`; `thresholds, textbook_sections, exemplars` may be empty arrays. |
| 06-PACK-002 | `questions[].id` follows the canonical form `{syllabus}/{component}/{session}/{year}/Q{n}[{part}]` with `session ∈ {F/M, M/J, O/N}` and two-digit year (`9609/41/M/J/25/Q1`, `9701/21/M/J/15/Q4b`); the normaliser in 06.4 is the only writer. *Acceptance:* regex `^\d{4}/\d{2}/(F/M|M/J|O/N)/\d{2}/Q\d+[a-z]?(\([ivx]+\))?$` matches 100% of ids. |
| 06-PACK-003 | For `board.id=caie`, `questions[].text_status` defaults to `ref_only`; a compiler run that sets `own` or `licensed` on a Cambridge question without a matching `licence_id` fails the build. |
| 06-PACK-004 | `syllabus.command_words` is the **only** place verbatim board text lives in a Pack; each entry ≤40 words with `source_ref`. `examiner_insights[].text` and every `mark_scheme_items[].credit_text`/`descriptor` with `wording_status=own_paraphrase` must show 8-gram overlap 0 with the source document's ingested text (checked against the hash index, 06-STOR-009). |
| 06-PACK-005 | `syllabus_graph.nodes[].path` uses the **official** syllabus numbering; note-derived numbering lives only in the per-source mapping table (06.4 stage 8). Every question carries ≥1 `assesses` edge with `confidence ≥0.8` or is excluded from practice selection. |
| 06-PACK-006 | `edges[].provenance ∈ {compiler_v<n>, compiler_v<n>+human, editor, licence:<id>}`; `equivalent_to` edges across syllabuses require `confidence ≥0.85` and are the cross-board reuse mechanism (§07.6). |
| 06-PACK-007 | `readiness.state` is computed from the sub-fields on every publish (`mapped` ⇐ `mapped_pct ≥0.95`; `gold_seeded` ⇐ `gold_per_family_min ≥3`; `gated` ⇐ ≥1 paper passes 05-GATE-002; `live` ⇐ published and at least one paper `gated`). Hand-setting the state is not possible; the column has no writer except the publisher job. |
| 06-PACK-008 | A syllabus revision (9608→9618; 9609 2023–25→2026–28) is a **new Pack id**, never a new version of the old one; versions within a Pack are additive (renumbering recorded as `node_aliases`, so old Attempts still resolve). *Acceptance:* every `syllabus_node_id` in a 12-month-old Attempt resolves through `node_aliases` to a live node. |
| 06-PACK-009 | `changelog[].migration_note` is the exact string shown in the Course banner (11-DATA-005); ≤120 characters; present on every version ≥ the second. |
| 06-PACK-010 | Bundle size budget: ≤25 MB YAML per Pack excluding exemplar blobs; questions ≤6,000; insights ≤3,000; the diff between two versions is stored and viewable in the compiler UI. |

## 06.4 The Curriculum Compiler pipeline

The Curriculum Compiler is the internal DAG (worker service `ingest`, §11.1) that turns a pile of messy PDFs into a versioned Pack. It is internal from month 1 (SYNTHESIS §9: v0 produces 0450 and 9708 from the 9609 grid engine; the public "any syllabus PDF" compiler is LATER). It runs on **PDFs, never text dumps** — the founder's text extracts (corpus-sample §2) are evidence of what goes wrong, not input.

```
 0 Intake ─► 1 Classify ─► 2 Parse (Docling) ─► 3 VLM page audit ─► 4 Figures & tables ─► 5 Maths OCR
   ─► 6 Per-source cleaning ─► 7 Dedupe ─► 8 Section→syllabus mapping [review UI] ─► 9 Paper-ID normaliser
   ─► 10 Question↔scheme alignment [review UI] ─► 11 Scheme structuring (06.7) [human confirm]
   ─► 12 Examiner-report mining [review UI] ─► 13 Graph build ─► 14 QA sampling ─► 15 Gold seed & gate (05.6) ─► 16 Publish
```

### Stages

| # | Stage | What it does | Output / metric |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Intake** | Accept files from three channels only: official public URLs (fetched once, `sha256`, robots/TDM reservation honoured — a reserved page is deep-linked, never fetched), teacher/school upload (tenant-scoped), licensed deliveries (licensor SFTP with `licence_id`). Write the ledger row (06.1) before any byte is parsed. | 100% of documents have a ledger row before stage 1 (assertion). |
| 1 | **Classify** | Document type `∈ {syllabus, qp, ms, er, specimen, ecr, thresholds, insert, textbook, notes, teacher_material, unknown}`, board, syllabus code, series, component, variant, edition/version window; Haiku 4.5 structured output over the first 3 pages + filename, confirmed by regex on the page footer ("© UCLES 2025", "9609/41/M/J/25"). `unknown` or confidence <0.9 → human queue. Stale editions (9608 notes, 9609 2023–25 notes) get `edition_status=superseded` and map only via aliases. | Type accuracy ≥99% on the labelled set (n=500); superseded editions tagged 100%. |
| 2 | **Structural parse** | Docling (MIT, v2.126+) → DoclingDocument JSON: reading order, heading tree, tables with cell structure, formula regions, figure crops with captions, page/bbox provenance. Marker/MinerU as configurable alternates (MinerU for scanned/multilingual national papers later). | Pages/hour ≥2,000 per worker; every block carries `page, bbox`. |
| 3 | **VLM page audit** | Gemini 3.8 Flash batch re-reads every page image against the Docling output; escalates to Gemini 3.1 Pro or Opus 5 for pages flagged (formula density, table, diagram, scan). Emits per-page `parse_confidence`; disagreement between passes on any text span → human QA. **Every equation page and every old-scan page takes the VLM pass** (old-scan maths is the weakest parser category, 29–84 on olmOCR-bench). | `parse_confidence` p50 ≥0.95; disagreement rate <4% of pages after tuning. |
| 4 | **Figures & tables** | Crop each figure at ≥300 dpi; VLM caption (`alt_text`, `figure_kind ∈ {diagram, graph, mechanism, photo, flowchart, table_image}`, structured description per 05-HAND-007 schema for graphs/mechanisms); embed with `voyage-multimodal-3.5`. Tables re-extracted from layout, never from text; merged headers split by column geometry. Defect addressed: **(1) figures lost as `[Image: …]` placeholders** and **(5) tables with merged headers / misaligned rows**. | 0 `[Image:` strings in any chunk; table cell-count consistency check passes (rows × cols equal across the table). |
| 5 | **Maths OCR** | Every formula region → Mathpix (or the VLM pass when Mathpix is unavailable) → LaTeX + MathML; SymPy parses the LaTeX; unparseable → human queue. Unit strings normalised (`mol dm^-3` → `\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}`), Greek preserved. Defect addressed: **(4) broken maths and units** ("C6H12O6", "cm-3", "10^23", linearised fractions). | ≥99% of formula regions parse with SymPy; a rendered-formula diff UI shows source crop vs KaTeX render for human spot-check (5% sample). |
| 6 | **Per-source cleaning rules** | A rules file per publisher/source family (`cleaning/znotes.yaml`, `cleaning/caie_ms.yaml`, …), versioned, unit-tested against fixture pages. Defects addressed: **(2) bullet glyph artefacts** (`^(Game|o|O|○|•)\s` at line start → list item; never applied inside prose because "Game" can be a word — the rule fires only when Docling's layout marks the block as a list or the line starts a new block); **(7) cross-references** ("ref 4.1", "See TABLE 4", "More about … in 11.2") → resolved `links` where the target exists in the same document, else left as text with `unresolved_ref=true`; footer/header strip ("© UCLES 2025", page numbers, "[Turn over"). | Fixture suite: 100% of 60 known-defect pages cleaned; 0 false list conversions on the 200-page prose sample. |
| 7 | **Dedupe** | Within a document: MinHash over 5-gram shingles, Jaccard ≥0.9 → duplicate block dropped, first occurrence kept, `dedupe_dropped` count logged. Across documents: `sha256` and near-duplicate detection so the same past paper from two uploaders is linked to one canonical `doc_id` (per tenant; never across tenants for USER). Defect addressed: **(3) duplicated blocks** ("Economies of scale" ×2, Pepperberg results ×3, "On-demand streaming" ×6). | 0 duplicate blocks with Jaccard ≥0.9 remain; dedupe never removes a block that appears in a different section path. |
| 8 | **Section → syllabus mapping** | For each section (or question part), propose `syllabus_node_ids[]` with confidence: exact match on official numbering when the source uses it; otherwise embedding + heading similarity + Sonnet 5 classification against `objective_text`. **Note numbering is the note's numbering** — a per-source `mapping_table {source_doc_id, source_section_no, source_title → syllabus_node_id, confidence, status ∈ {auto, confirmed, rejected}}`. Defect addressed: **(8) note numbering ≠ official numbering** ("13.14 Geometric isomers" is ZNotes' number). Review UI: left pane source section with its heading path; right pane the proposed node with siblings; keyboard `y/n/j/k`; batch-confirm for confidence ≥0.95. | Auto-confidence ≥0.9 on ≥85% of sections; human acceptance of auto proposals ≥95%; every section either mapped or explicitly `unmapped`. |
| 9 | **Paper-ID normaliser** | Deterministic grammar → canonical `{syllabus}/{component}/{session}/{yy}` per 06-PACK-002. Handles: `S15 v21`, `S 10 variant 21`, `W 09 variant 21`, `10 variant 23` (year without season → ambiguous, queue), `9609_s25_ms_41`, `9609/41/M/J/25`, `June 2025 Paper 41`, `M/J 2025 P4 V1`, `m25` (F/M), `w24` (O/N), `s24` (M/J). Component = paper × 10 + variant when written separately ("Paper 2 variant 1" → 21). Defect addressed: **(10) informal paper/series identifiers**. | 100% of the 300-string fixture normalises or queues; 0 silent misassignments (any ambiguity queues). |
| 10 | **Question ↔ scheme alignment** | Join QP parts to MS parts by canonical id + part label; verify `marks` agree; detect scheme parts with no question and vice versa; align inserts/case studies to their paper; produce `context.case_facts[]` (OWN summary, 05-SCHM-008). Review UI shows QP anchor crop beside MS anchor crop with the proposed link. | `mapped_pct` ≥0.95 for `mapped`; marks-total mismatch 0 after review. |
| 11 | **Scheme structuring** | The paste-to-structured tool (06.7) run in batch: LLM proposes the 05.3 record in our wording; **a human confirms every record** (<2 min per part). Defect addressed: **(9) mark-scheme micro-format** (conjunctive M1–M5, all-or-nothing, drawing conventions). | 100% human-confirmed before `mapped`; 8-gram overlap with source 0 (06-PACK-004). |
| 12 | **Examiner-report mining** | Sonnet 5 extracts "candidates who scored well… / weaker responses… / common error" triples per question and per syllabus node, rewrites them as OWN insights with `student_tip` and a machine-checkable `heuristic`; `source_pointer` recorded, never the ER sentence. Review UI: paraphrase on the left, source crop on the right, overlap meter, heuristic test-run against 20 gold scripts showing hit count. | ≥90% of insights accepted at first review; heuristic precision ≥0.8 on gold scripts; overlap 0. |
| 13 | **Graph build** | Emit `links` (`assesses, answered_by, commented_on, explained_in, prerequisite_of, equivalent_to`) with confidence and provenance; propose `equivalent_to` edges against existing Packs (0450 ↔ 9609, 0455 ↔ 9708) for the §07.6 cross-board graph; compute per-node `tariff_histogram` and `command_words_seen`. | Every question ≥1 `assesses` edge ≥0.8; `equivalent_to` proposals ≥0.85 reviewed by an editor. |
| 14 | **QA sampling** | Human QA on: 100% of scheme records and insights (stages 11–12); 10% of mapped sections (stage 8), rising to 30% for a source whose acceptance drops below 90%; 5% of formula renders; 5% of figure captions; 100% of pages with `parse_confidence <0.85` or pass disagreement. Each QA action is logged with reviewer id for inter-rater checks (two reviewers on 2% of items; agreement ≥0.9). | QA queue age p95 <3 working days. |
| 15 | **Gold seed & gate** | ECRs and specimen answers → Tier 0 exemplars; partner-school double-marked scripts → Tier 1; standardise the Examiner Twin per paper (05.6). | Per 05-GATE-002. |
| 16 | **Publish** | Validate against `pack.v1.json`, write changelog and migration note, bump `pack.version`, run the retrieval gold set (Recall@8 ≥0.92, 11-RAG-003), snapshot the bundle, notify Courses (11-DATA-005). Old versions stay resolvable forever. | Publish is atomic; a failed validation publishes nothing. |

### Founder library defects, cross-referenced

corpus-sample §2 lists ten defects; stages above cover (1) figures → stage 4; (2) bullet glyphs → 6; (3) duplicates → 7; (4) maths/units → 5; (5) tables → 4; (6) **typos and factual slips in third-party notes** ("273 °C", "Pilivan", "adenine, uracil and cytosine" as pyrimidines) → not fixed by the compiler at all: notes are ingested as-is at `trust_rank 5`, and the tutor handles disagreement through 06.5 conflict behaviour — the compiler only flags a note chunk `canon_conflict=true` when a fact-check pass (Sonnet 5, batch) finds a contradiction with a rank 1–3 chunk on the same node, which raises it in the QA sample; (7) cross-references → 6; (8) numbering → 8; (9) scheme micro-format → 11 and 06.7; (10) paper IDs → 9.

### Throughput, cost, failure modes

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-COMP-001 | **Throughput target:** a sibling Pack (same board, same AO grammar — 0450, 9708, 0455) from intake to `mapped` in **<4 weeks** with one content editor + one ex-examiner, by month 12 (SYNTHESIS §9); a new paradigm (first Edexcel IAL Pack, a national exam) <8 weeks. Machine stages (0–7, 9, 13, 16) for a 1,500-page corpus complete in <48 h wall-clock. |
| 06-COMP-002 | **Cost per Pack (compute, excluding gold scripts):** ≈1,500 pages × (Docling self-hosted ≈$0.00 marginal + VLM audit ≈$0.004/page on Flash batch + escalation 15% at ≈$0.03 + Mathpix ≈$0.01 per formula page) ≈ **$60–120**; scheme structuring and ER mining ≈2,000 LLM calls on Sonnet batch ≈ $40–80; embeddings ≈$5. Total machine cost **<$250 per Pack**. Human cost: ≈120–200 editor-hours + 40–80 ex-examiner hours per sibling Pack (paid per structured record where possible, F§7.2). |
| 06-COMP-003 | **Failure modes and handling:** (a) *silent misparse of a scheme table* → caught by marks-total reconciliation (stage 10) and 100% human confirm (11); (b) *wrong series assignment* → normaliser queues any ambiguity, never guesses; (c) *stale edition mapped to the live syllabus* → `edition_status=superseded` blocks direct mapping, aliases only; (d) *licence expiry mid-build* → prefilter drops the chunks, build fails validation with the `licence_id` named; (e) *injected instructions in uploaded PDFs* → stage 6 strips imperatives addressed to an assistant and logs (11-RAG-007); (f) *VLM hallucinated a caption* → captions are `parse_confidence`-scored and the 5% sample plus any caption with a number in it is human-checked; (g) *duplicate canonical question from two uploaders in one tenant* → linked to one `doc_id`, both uploads retained for retention accounting. |
| 06-COMP-004 | **Metrics dashboard (per Pack, per run):** pages/hour, `parse_confidence` distribution, pass-disagreement %, dedupe dropped %, mapping auto-confidence and human acceptance, normaliser queue %, `mapped_pct`, scheme records confirmed/day, insights accepted %, heuristic precision, QA queue age, cost to date, days since intake. A run that regresses any acceptance metric by >5 points against the previous run blocks publish until an editor acknowledges. |
| 06-COMP-005 | **Idempotence and replay:** every stage is keyed by `(doc_id, doc_version, stage, rules_version)`; re-running with new cleaning rules re-processes only affected documents; the output of any stage for any document is reproducible from object storage + the rules version. *Acceptance:* deleting all derived rows for one document and replaying regenerates byte-identical chunks. |
| 06-COMP-006 | **Review UIs** (stages 8, 10, 11, 12, 14) are internal web screens built from the same design tokens as the product (§09), keyboard-first, with the source crop always visible beside the proposal; each shows the reviewer's acceptance rate and the item's `provenance` badge; nothing in a review UI can edit official text — only our paraphrase, mappings and flags. |

## 06.5 Trust ranks and notes-vs-canon behaviour

Trust rank orders sources when they disagree or tie in retrieval; it never overrides the hard rule that marking uses only a `mark_scheme_items` record (05-SCOP-002). The ranks are FINAL in SYNTHESIS §3.1/§9 and are already used by the 05.2 `sources[]` array (`trust_rank: 3` for a scheme, `4` for an ER). Do not reorder them per subject or per tenant.

### Rank table

| Rank | Source kind | Typical class | What it is authoritative for | What it is not authoritative for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Syllabus (current version window) | OWN facts + verbatim command words | What is examinable, official numbering, command-word meaning, AO weights, paper structure, units and conventions the syllabus states | How a specific question was marked |
| 2 | Endorsed textbook (board-endorsed coursebook) | LICENSED (or USER when the student uploads a page) | Explanations, definitions, worked examples, diagrams | Marking of a specific question; anything post-dating its edition |
| 3 | Mark scheme (official) | OWN paraphrase + anchors; USER when uploaded | The creditable points and level descriptors for that question part; accept/reject lists | General theory beyond that question; other series' wording |
| 4 | Examiner report | OWN insights + anchors; USER when uploaded | What scored and what did not in that series; recurring errors; examiner phrasing of advice | Definitions; the current syllabus content if the series predates it |
| 5 | Revision notes (licensed notes, ZNotes-class community notes) | LICENSED or USER | Compact restatements, lists, mnemonics | Facts when they conflict with 1–4; numbering |
| 6 | User upload of unknown type; the student's own notes; hand-compiled extracts before confirmation | USER | The student's own record of what they were taught | Anything, when it conflicts with 1–5 |

Within rank 5, `sub_rank` separates `licensed_notes (5.0)` from `community_notes (5.5)`; within rank 6, a hand-compiled scheme extract rises to rank 3 per record once a human confirms it against the official scheme (06.7).
