A brief elsewhere proposes syllabus > mark scheme > examiner report > textbook; reject it here — for **explaining**, an endorsed textbook is more reliable than a scheme written for one question; for **marking**, rank is irrelevant because only the scheme record counts.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-TRUST-001 | Retrieval (11-RAG-003) filters by `syllabus_code` and `syllabus_version` **before** similarity; `trust_rank` breaks ties after reranking and boosts by `+0.02 × (6 − trust_rank)` on the fused score, never more. **Why:** a rank-5 chunk that answers the question beats a rank-1 chunk that does not; trust is a tie-breaker, not a filter. |
| 06-TRUST-002 | A **stale-version penalty** applies before trust: a chunk from a superseded syllabus version or a pre-version ER is retrievable only when no current-version chunk covers the node, and is then labelled "from the 2023–25 syllabus — check it is still examinable". |
| 06-TRUST-003 | **Conflict detection** runs on the assembled top-8 (11-RAG-006): when two chunks on the same node state different values for the same quantity, unit, definition, date, name or list membership, and their ranks differ, the orchestrator emits a `conflict` part before the answer. Detection is a Haiku 4.5 structured call over the 8 chunks (`{conflicts:[{fact, a:{chunk_id, value, rank}, b:{…}}]}`), ≤150 ms, cached per (query, chunk set). |
| 06-TRUST-004 | **Canon wins by default.** The answer states the higher-ranked value; the lower-ranked value is shown in the conflict card with its chip; the tutor never silently picks. If both are rank ≥5 and no canon chunk exists, the tutor says neither is canon and offers to check the syllabus. |
| 06-TRUST-005 | ZNotes-style revision notes are **notes, not canon**: `trust_rank=5`, never cited as "the syllabus says", never used to populate `syllabus_graph.nodes[].objective_text`, never used as the sole ground for a definition Item; they may seed Cards for the uploading student with provenance "From your notes". |
| 06-TRUST-006 | Student-facing rank labels are words, never numbers: `Syllabus · Textbook · Mark scheme · Examiner report · Notes · Your upload`. Teachers see the same words; the integer exists only in data and the calibration page. |

### How the tutor speaks when notes disagree with canon (exact strings)

The `conflict` part renders as a card above the Turn (§09 conflict card). Strings below are fixed; `{…}` fields are filled; no other phrasing is permitted (microcopy lint, §15.E).

```
CONFLICT CARD — title:      "Your notes and the syllabus disagree"
line 1 (lower rank):        "Your notes: {value_low}  · {source_low_label}, p.{page}"
line 2 (higher rank):       "{source_high_label}: {value_high}  · {citation_high}"
footer:                     "I'll use the {source_high_label} version. Tap either source to see the page."
```

Worked instances:

```
Your notes and the syllabus disagree
Your notes: standard temperature 273 °C  · ZNotes 9701 theory, p.12
Syllabus: standard temperature 273 K  · Cambridge 9701 syllabus 2025–27, §3.1
I'll use the Syllabus version. Tap either source to see the page.
```

```
Your notes and the examiner report disagree
Your notes: "repeat the business name to show application"  · your upload, p.3
Examiner report: application needs a fact true only of this business  · 9609 Principal Examiner Report, March 2025, Paper 4
I'll use the Examiner report version. Tap either source to see the page.
```

In-Turn sentence (when the conflict is minor enough not to warrant a card, e.g. spelling of a researcher's name): `"Your notes spell it 'Pilivan'; the textbook and the syllabus use 'Piliavin' — I'll use that."` The pattern is fixed: `"Your notes {say|spell|list} {X}; the {source_high_label} {says|spells|lists} {Y} — I'll use that."`

When two canon sources disagree (rank 1 vs 3, e.g. a scheme accepts a definition the syllabus words differently): `"The mark scheme for {question_ref} accepted {Y}; the syllabus wording is {X}. Either earns the mark on that question; learn the syllabus wording."`

When a user asks the tutor to prefer their notes: `"I can explain your notes' version, but I mark against the syllabus and the scheme, so I'll flag where they differ."` The tutor never adopts a rank-5/6 fact as ground truth in a Mark or a Card back.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-TRUST-007 | *Acceptance for the strings:* the 50-item conflict fixture (11-RAG-006) yields a conflict card in 100% of cases with the exact title and footer strings; the praise lint and 120-word budget (§04) still apply to the Turn below the card; a card never appears without both chips resolving (06.6). |
| 06-TRUST-008 | Conflicts are logged `{user_id, node_id, chunk_low, chunk_high, fact, at}`; a note source whose conflict rate exceeds 2% of its chunks over 30 days is flagged in the compiler dashboard and, if LICENSED, reported to the licensor at renewal. |

## 06.6 Citation chips and deep-link rules

A citation chip is the only way a source appears in a Turn, Mark, Card back, debrief or export. It is a typed `citation` message part (11-API-003) rendered as an inline pill; it must resolve (11-RAG-004) or it is not rendered.

### Chip anatomy

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▣ Mark scheme · 9609/41 M/J 2025 · Q1 · p.4 │   ← kind glyph · short citation · locator
└───────────────────────────────────────────┘
  hover/long-press → preview card:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Cambridge International · 9609/41 mark scheme · May/June 2025   │
  │ Q1 · page 4 · Levels grid, AO3                                   │
  │ "…≤40-word extract…"  (only if display rights allow)            │
  │ [Open official PDF ↗]   [Open in Reader]   [Report a problem]    │
  │ Trust: Mark scheme · Provenance: anchors only                    │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```jsonc
{ "part": "citation", "chip_id": "c_01JX…", "kind": "mark_scheme",           // syllabus | textbook | mark_scheme | examiner_report | notes | your_upload | original_item
  "label": "Mark scheme · 9609/41 M/J 2025 · Q1 · p.4",
  "resolve": { "doc_id": "doc_9609_41_s25_ms", "page": 4, "bbox": [70, 210, 540, 470], "char_span": null, "chunk_id": "ch_…" },
  "deep_link": { "url": "https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/…-mark-scheme-paper-41.pdf#page=4", "status": "ok", "checked_at": "2027-02-13T02:10:00Z", "ssh_only": false },
  "trust_rank": 3, "provenance": "OWN", "display_rights": "anchors_only",
  "extract": null,                                                          // ≤40 words when allowed (06-STOR-001)
  "reader_available": false }
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-CITE-001 | A chip resolves to **page + span**: `{doc_id, page, bbox | char_span}`. For `ref_only` documents the span is the question anchor from the Pack (`questions[].anchors`); the Reader is unavailable and the chip's primary action is the deep link. For OWN/LICENSED/own-USER documents the Reader opens the page with the span highlighted ≤400 ms p95. *Acceptance:* ≥98% of chips resolve in the click-through test; 0 chips open hosted text for `ref_only` docs. |
| 06-CITE-002 | Label grammar, fixed: `{Kind} · {syllabus}/{component} {session} {year} · Q{n}{part} · p.{page}` for board documents; `Textbook · {short title} · §{path} · p.{page}` for textbooks; `Syllabus · {code} {window} · §{path}`; `Notes · {source} · p.{page}`; `Your upload · {filename ≤24 chars} · p.{page}`; `Original item · in the style of {syllabus} P{paper}`. Never a bare URL, never a board logo. |
| 06-CITE-003 | **Hover/long-press preview** shows: full citation line, locator, the extract only when `display_rights ∈ {extracts, full_text}` and the Turn's extract budget allows (06-STOR-001), the trust word, and the actions `Open official PDF`, `Open in Reader` (when available), `Report a problem` (routes to 06.10 intake). Preview opens ≤150 ms from cached chip data; no network call on hover. |
| 06-CITE-004 | **Deep-link formats per board** (config, not code): Cambridge public PDFs `https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/{id}-{slug}.pdf#page={n}`; Cambridge subject page fallback `…/programmes-and-qualifications/{slug}-{code}/past-papers/`; SSH-only documents → `https://schoolsupporthub.cambridge.org/` with the chip flagged `ssh_only=true` and label suffix "(School Support Hub)"; AQA `https://www.aqa.org.uk/find-past-papers-and-mark-schemes` with query params, PDF `#page=`; Pearson `https://qualifications.pearson.com/…/{pdf}#page=`; OCR `https://www.ocr.org.uk/…#page=`; College Board `https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/…#page=`; IB: no deep link to papers (Follett store item page only for the citation, no `#page`). PDF fragment `#page=` is mandatory whenever the target is a PDF. |
| 06-CITE-005 | **Link checker**: every distinct `deep_link.url` is HEAD-checked weekly, and daily for the 30 days after a series' publication window (boards move files); status `∈ {ok, moved, dead, blocked}`; `moved` follows one redirect and rewrites the Pack link on the next version; `dead` after 2 consecutive failures. |
| 06-CITE-006 | **When a link dies**: the chip still renders (the citation is true whether or not the board's URL survives); its primary action becomes `Find on {board} site` (the subject page), the preview shows "The official file has moved; the page reference is still correct", and the Paper Companion offers the upload path. A dead link never removes a citation or an insight; it never becomes a link to a mirror site. *Acceptance:* the mirror-domain blocklist (PapaCambridge, XtremePapers, GCE Guide, etc.) is asserted against every `deep_link.url` in CI; 0 matches. |
| 06-CITE-007 | **Density limits per Turn**: Learn-mode Turns carry 1–3 chips (0 only when the grounding gate labelled the Turn "not in your syllabus materials"); a Mark carries ≤2 chips per AO card plus ≤2 in `sources[]`; a debrief ≤1 chip per lost-mark cluster; a Card back ≤1. Beyond the limit the orchestrator keeps the highest trust, then highest rerank score. **Why:** chips are for verification, not decoration; more than three per 120 words halves tap-through in the design review (§09). |
| 06-CITE-008 | Chips are **accessible** (§09): role `link`, accessible name = full citation line, focusable, preview reachable by keyboard; on mobile the preview is a bottom sheet. |
| 06-CITE-009 | Chip taps are logged `{chip_id, action ∈ {preview, official, reader, report}}`; per-Pack "official link tap-through" is a trust metric on the calibration page (§13) and per-source tap-through feeds licensing conversations (06.9). |

## 06.7 The paste-to-structured marking-point tool

The founder's mechanisms file (corpus-sample §4.3) is the highest-value asset in the sample: question → official marking points. This tool makes producing such records faster than typing prose. It is an internal/teacher screen (compiler stage 11 in batch; teacher console at calibrator scope for their own uploads, §10) that turns pasted or OCR'd scheme text into a 05.3 `mark_scheme_items` record in our wording, with a mandatory human confirm.

### Flow

```
paste / select text on an uploaded page ─► 1 detect scheme_type & part ─► 2 LLM proposal (05.3 JSON, own wording)
  ─► 3 deterministic validation ─► 4 confirm UI (source crop | proposed record; atoms editable) ─► 5 save @version, provenance
```

Input example (pasted from the founder's file):

```
S15 variant 21 — nucleophilic addition of CN− to a carbonyl
M1 = lone pair AND curly arrow from lone pair to carbonyl C
M2 = partial charges on C=O AND curly arrow from bond (=) to O−
M3 = structure of intermediate including charge
M4 = lone pair AND two correct curly arrows (from lone pair to H AND from H-C to C)
M5 = CN−
```

Output: the 05.3 record `ms_9701_21_MJ15_Q4b@1` already shown in 05.3 — `M1…M3` as type `B`, `M4` as `DB` depending on `M3`, `M5` with an `alternatives[]` entry, `diagram_required=true`, `vision_status=provisional_teacher_confirm`, `source.licence_basis=user`, `trust_rank` 6 → 3 on confirm.

### Prompt outline (Sonnet 5, structured output against `mark_scheme_item.v1.json`)

```
SYSTEM: You convert examiner mark-scheme text into a structured record. Rules:
 1. Output only the JSON schema provided. No prose.
 2. Rewrite every credit_text in your own words; never copy a sentence of ≥8 consecutive source words.
 3. Split every "AND" / "and" that joins two checkable features into separate conjunctive_conditions; set all_required=true.
 4. "//" or "or" between alternatives → alternatives[] (credited once). "ORA" → ora=true. "cao" → cao=true. "ecf"/"ft"/"own value" → ecf_allowed=true and the point type FT or A with depends_on.
 5. "dep"/"*" markers → type DM or DB with depends_on set to the referenced point.
 6. Tag each point with an AO using the syllabus AO table supplied in context; if uncertain, ao=null and add a note.
 7. If the text is a levels grid, emit levels[] with every band, including a range [0,0] band when the grid defines it, and an evidence_rule per band in countable terms.
 8. Keep accept / reject / ignore lists as atoms. Preserve chemistry/maths notation as LaTeX.
 9. Anything you cannot classify goes in notes, never silently dropped.
CONTEXT: {syllabus AO table (OWN)}, {command-word table}, {question_id, part, marks_total from the normaliser}, {any existing record @n for diff}
USER: {pasted text}
```

### Validation (deterministic, before a human sees it)

| Check | Rule | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Marks sum | Σ `marking_points[].marks` (or Σ `levels[].max`) = `marks_total` from the QP/normaliser | Block; show the delta |
| Dependencies | every `A`, `DM`, `DB`, `FT` has `depends_on` pointing at an existing point (05-SCHM-001) | Block |
| Conjunctive atoms | any `credit_text` still containing " and " / " AND " with `conjunctive_conditions` empty | Warn, highlight |
| Wording | 8-gram overlap with the pasted source = 0 for `own_paraphrase`; if the record is `licensed_verbatim` (licence present) skip | Block; auto-rewrite once, then human |
| AO tags | every point has `ao` or a `notes` entry explaining why not | Warn |
| Command word | `command_word` ∈ the Pack's verbatim table; `ao_ceiling` consistent | Block |
| Schema | validates against `mark_scheme_item.v1.json` | Block |
| Duplicate | no existing record for this `question_id/part` unless creating `@n+1` | Block with diff view |

### Confirm UI

Left: the source crop or pasted text with each detected point colour-coded. Right: the proposed record as a form — one row per point: `id · type · marks · AO · credit_text (editable) · atoms (chips, add/remove) · flags (ECF, CAO, ISW, ORA, dep→)`. Keyboard: `Tab` between points, `Enter` confirms a point, `A` adds an atom, `Ctrl+Enter` saves. The confirm button reads **"Confirm — matches the official scheme"** and is disabled until every point is individually ticked; the confirmer's id, role (`editor | ex_examiner | teacher`) and timestamp are saved on the record. A teacher confirm produces `vision_status`/`trust_rank` changes only inside that teacher's tenant until an editor re-confirms for the global Pack.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-PSTE-001 | Proposal latency ≤8 s p95 for a 5-point scheme; ≤20 s for a 4-AO levels grid. |
| 06-PSTE-002 | **Throughput target:** <2 min human time per points part, <5 min per levels part (F§7.2 stage 4); first-pass acceptance (no edits to atoms) ≥80% on points, ≥65% on levels after month 3; measured per confirmer and shown on the compiler dashboard. |
| 06-PSTE-003 | Every saved record carries `source {document_id, page, bbox, licence_basis}`, `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`, `proposal_model`, `overlap_score`; records are `@versioned` and never overwritten (05-SCHM-007). |
| 06-PSTE-004 | The tool never displays or stores the pasted official text beyond the confirm session for `ref_only` documents: the source pane reads from the user's upload (USER partition) or the clipboard buffer, and the buffer is discarded on save. Only the OWN record and the page anchor persist. |
| 06-PSTE-005 | A teacher-confirmed record for a question the global Pack already covers is diffed against the global record; disagreements >1 mark or any flag difference open a review item for an editor (calibration signal, 05-GATE-009). |
| 06-PSTE-006 | *Acceptance:* the founder's mechanisms file (≈20 mechanisms across S10–W15 variants) is converted end-to-end in under one working day by one confirmer, every record passes validation, and the resulting records mark the 05.12 Paper 1 example correctly in the points engine. |

## 06.8 The first ten syllabuses and why

§14.3 schedules these ten and states when each state is expected; this subsection states **why these ten and in this order**, and what each Pack needs before it can enter `gold-seeded`. The selection rule is one sentence: *maximise engine reuse per Pack, and buy the calibration data for the hardest paradigm first.* Demand is a tie-breaker, never the driver — a Pack we cannot calibrate is a Pack we cannot show numbers for (05-GATE-004), and a Pack with no parent costs 3–4× the editor hours (06-COMP-001).

### Marking difficulty tiers

| Tier | What it is | Engine | Gate cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | MCQ and exact-answer recall | Points, exact match | Trivial; no gold scripts needed |
| **T2** | Structured calculation and short recall with M/A/B, ECF, sig-fig rules | Points + SymPy (05-PROC-006/008) | ≈300 scripts, ≈6 min/script to double-mark |
| **T3** | Short levels items 5–12 marks (data response, short essay, "Analyse") | Levels, 2–3 AO grid | ≈300 scripts, ≈8 min/script |
| **T4** | 20–30-mark essays with an AO4 judgement band | Levels, best-fit, 4 AO grid | ≈300 scripts, ≈12 min/script; second family on 100% for two series (05-PIPE-007) |
| **T5** | Diagram, mechanism, practical-planning and code items | Levels/points + structured VLM description (05-HAND-007) or sandbox (§11.5) | ≥300-item diagram/code gold set **per family**; ships provisional until then |

### The first ten

| # | Code | Subject · level | Series used for gold | Why chosen | Pack readiness needs beyond the standard `mapped` set | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **9609** | Business · A Level (AS + A2) | M/J 25, M/J 24, O/N 24, F/M 25 | The founder's library, examiner network and the whole grid engine start here; P4 is the densest AO3+AO4 paper in the qualification (75% of its marks), so calibrating it first buys the hardest case in the catalogue | `context.case_facts` per insert (05-SCHM-008); ≥40 examiner-report insights with firing heuristics; the AO4 evidence rule (judgement + weighing + condition) validated against ≥60 Tier-1 scripts | T4 (P2 §B, P3, P4), T3 (P1, P2 §A) |
| 2 | **0450** | Business · IGCSE | M/J 25, O/N 24 | First proof that the compiler, not people, produces Packs: same command words, same Ansoff/stakeholder content, different AO weights and tariffs | AO re-weighting must be re-derived, never inherited from 9609; 6-mark "Analyse" and 12-mark evaluation families need their own evidence rules | T3 |
| 3 | **9708** | Economics · A Level | M/J 25, M/J 24 | Second sibling from the same grid engine; adds numeric-in-levels items (diagram + calculation inside an essay) which the 9609 engine does not exercise | Diagram items (supply–demand shifts) enter as T5 and ship provisional; MCQ components gate trivially and give the first "gated" badge cheaply | T4 (P4), T3 (P2), T1 (P1/P3) |
| 4 | **9709** | Mathematics · A Level | M/J 25, M/J 24, O/N 24 | Root of the **points** paradigm: M/A/B/DM/DB/FT, ECF scope, sig-fig penalties, SymPy recompute. Highest-volume CAIE subject and the cheapest paper to reach gate, so it carries the "we mark accurately" proof while 9609 P4 is still provisional | Per-component `ecf_policy.scope`; the accept-list grammar (AWRT, OE, SOI); Mathpix on every handwritten page (05-HAND-002) | T2 |
| 5 | **0580** | Mathematics · IGCSE | M/J 25, O/N 24 | Compiled from 9709 at the lowest marginal cost of any Pack; extends the market down a year group and into the IGCSE cohort that becomes next year's A Level cohort | Core vs Extended tiering; the "no working shown" rule (05-PROC-011) is the dominant error family and needs its own eval slice | T2 |
| 6 | **9701** | Chemistry · A Level | S10–W15 variants (founder's mechanism file) + M/J 25 | The founder's marking-point file is already question→official-points structured, so it converts through 06.7 in one working day and seeds the mechanisms bank; it is the cheapest entry into the sciences | Mechanism items are T5: `diagram_required=true`, `vision_status=provisional_teacher_confirm` until a ≥300-item diagram gold set exists; ships **feedback-only** at launch | T2 + T5 |
| 7 | **0455** | Economics · IGCSE | M/J 25 | Near-zero marginal cost from 9708 if the compiler yields it before M5; opportunistic only — it never displaces work on 1–6 | AO weights differ from 9708 (40/40/20) and must be re-read from the syllabus PDF; the compiler must fail rather than inherit | T3 |
| 8 | **9702** | Physics · A Level | M/J 25, M/J 24 | Reuses the 9709 points engine plus 9701's practical rules; P5 planning-and-analysis is the first paper that is 100% AO3 and forces the levels engine onto a non-essay skill | Practical-paper rule set (planning, uncertainty, graph work); graph items are T5 | T2 + T5 |
| 9 | **9700** | Biology · A Level | M/J 25 | Extended-response families with long accept/reject lists exercise `alternatives[]`, `ora` and `ignore` harder than any other Pack; from 9702 | Very large accept lists per point; `ORA` handling; the `NOT_IN_INDICATIVE_VALID_ALT` teacher flag will fire most often here | T2/T3 |
| 10 | **9618** | Computer Science · A Level | M/J 25 | Code and pseudocode items are verifiable by execution, so the marker gets a ground truth no other subject has; from 9709 | Sandbox execution per item (§11.5); pseudocode dialect rules per syllabus version; code items ship provisional | T2 + T5 |

### Sequencing rules

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 06-TEN-001 | A Pack enters the queue only with a **named parent Pack** whose engine it reuses, or an explicit decision that it founds a new paradigm (9609 levels, 9709 points). No third paradigm before M12. | `pack.parent_pack_id` non-null or a signed paradigm decision in `DECISIONS.md`. |
| 06-TEN-002 | Within a Pack, papers are gated in ascending tier order (T1 → T2 → T3 → T4); a T4 paper never blocks the Pack going `live` — it ships feedback-only (05-GATE-004) while lower tiers show numbers. | The launch state table in §14.3 matches the tier order for every Pack. |
| 06-TEN-003 | T5 families (diagram, mechanism, practical, code) are **always provisional at first ship** regardless of the paper's tier, and are excluded from predicted grades (05-PRED-001) until their own gold set passes 05-GATE-002. | Predicted-grade input query filters `vision_status != 'provisional_teacher_confirm'`. |
| 06-TEN-004 | Subjects whose schemes rest mainly on holistic textual judgement — English Literature, Psychology, History essays — are excluded from the first ten and from v1 (14-PACK-013). The rule to re-open them: measure the human–human line for one paper first, then decide. | No `pack` row for those codes before a measured-line plan exists. |
| 06-TEN-005 | Gold-script capacity is booked per paper **before** the Pack enters `gold-seeded`, using the tier table's minutes-per-script (14-PACK-011). A Pack whose capacity is unbooked stays at `mapped`. | Gold-set manager blocks the state transition. |

**Why not demand-first:** the highest-search-volume CAIE subjects are Maths and Business, which this order already covers at positions 1 and 4; the next tranche by demand (English, Psychology) is precisely the tranche whose marking we cannot yet defend, and shipping a lenient marker on them would spend the calibration moat (SYNTHESIS §12) to win a month of traffic.

## 06.9 Licensing strategy

The product ships without a single licence (06.1 Tier 0 + Tier 1) and treats every licence as an **upgrade that flips a flag**, never as a dependency. Open the conversations in month 1 anyway: the asymmetry is that a refusal costs a letter and a licence converts the main legal risk into a moat. Licensing counterparties, terms and any fee are FOUNDER-OWNED [E2]; the sequence, the asks and the in-product effects below are not.

### The five month-1 conversations, in order

| # | Counterparty | Send in | What we ask for | What we offer | If they say yes | If they say no |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cambridge University Press & Assessment** (permissions, then the AI-licensing team on the Press side) | Week 1 of M1 | (a) mark schemes and examiner reports as **retrieval grounding, not display**; (b) endorsed-coursebook text for RAG with extracts; (c) written confirmation that descriptive use of "Cambridge International A Level 9609" outside the product name is acceptable | Per-document usage reporting from the `extract_log` (06-STOR-004); a per-document kill switch they can trigger (06.10); published calibration numbers per paper; no hosting of any PDF, ever; a named contact and a 24 h SLA | `LIC_MS_GROUNDING` and `LIC_ER_QUOTE` on; `wording_status` may become `licensed_verbatim` per document | Nothing changes: paraphrase + anchors + deep links (already the default) |
| 2 | **CLA Generative AI licence** (UK collective) | Week 1 of M1 | Which school-textbook publishers are in the repertoire; whether **RAG display by a commercial SaaS** is covered as well as training; territory and per-seat or per-title pricing | Volume reporting; a repertoire-scoped ingest that refuses out-of-repertoire titles at stage 0 (06.4) | `LIC_TEXTBOOK_RAG` on for in-repertoire titles only, `scope.syllabus_codes[]` enumerated per title | Endorsed textbooks stay LICENSED-or-nothing; students may still upload their own copy (USER) |
| 3 | **Hodder Education, OUP, Collins** (direct, in parallel with the CLA answer) | Week 2 of M1 | Endorsed CAIE coursebook text for RAG and extracts, per syllabus code, 3-year term | Attribution chip with a buy link on every retrieved section (06.6); referral share on the buy link; no offline copies unless `licence.offline=true` | Same flags as (2), per `licence_id` | Deep-link to the product page only |
| 4 | **Pearson Edexcel** (with AQA queued behind it) | Week 3 of M1 | Past papers, schemes and ERs for IAL Business (WBS) and Economics (WEC) as grounding; confirmation of the 5-year public window we already honour as `expiry` | Same reporting and kill switch; the first non-CAIE Pack is theirs [founder default E3] | `LIC_MS_GROUNDING` scoped to Pearson codes; IAL Packs can quote descriptors | IAL Packs ship on OWN + USER exactly like CAIE |
| 5 | **ZNotes** (and equivalent notes publishers) | Week 4 of M1 | Written permission for the founder-supplied notes corpus to move from USER to LICENSED with `display_rights: extracts` | Attribution on every chunk; traffic to their site; a share of the note-derived Card usage if they want one | The corpus is re-ingested as a **new** `doc_id` (06-PROV-006), `trust_rank` stays 5 | Corpus stays USER under the founder's org, invisible to every other tenant (06.1 test 5) |

**06-LIC-001** Counsel drafts and sends all five; no engineer, founder message or agent-written email opens a licensing conversation. Every reply is filed as a `licences` row or a `permission_denied` note with the date, and both are linked from the ledger.

### The three rights tiers, and what each unlocks

| Tier | `display_rights` | What Margin may do | Default at launch |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Facts only** | `anchors_only` | Store `sha256`, page/question anchors, our OWN paraphrase and insights; deep-link the official PDF; never store or display source text | **This is the launch state for every board document.** |
| **Extracts** | `extracts` | Everything above, plus verbatim quotation inside the 06-STOR-001 caps (≤40 words, ≤2 sentences, ≤3 per Turn/Mark, ≤12 per Session), always with a chip | Endorsed textbooks only, and only under a signed `licence_id` |
| **Full text** | `full_text` | Store and display the document inside Margin surfaces within `scope.syllabus_codes[]` and `territories[]`; grid wording may be shown verbatim (`wording_status: licensed_verbatim`) | Never assumed; requires an explicit `scope.export` decision for Receipts and print |

**06-LIC-002** `max_quote_words` on a licence overrides the extract cap in either direction; the post-lint reads the licence, not a constant. *Acceptance:* set `max_quote_words: 15` on a fixture licence → a 20-word quotation from that document fails the Turn.

### What changes in-product when a licence lands

Nothing is rebuilt. Each flag is derived from the `licences` row at request time and read by the prefilter (06-PROV-004), the renderer and the compiler.

| Flag (derived) | Off (launch) | On | Surfaces affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LIC_MS_GROUNDING` | Scheme text is never in the model context; only our structured `mark_scheme_items` record is | Official scheme text joins the static prefix for that paper; the record stays the source of truth for marks | 05.5 step 1; expect a re-standardisation run (05-GATE-006) because the context changed |
| `LIC_MS_VERBATIM` | `descriptor_relied_on.paraphrase` shown | `descriptor_relied_on.verbatim` shown with a chip and the licensor's attribution | Mark view (§10.7), Receipts |
| `LIC_ER_QUOTE` | Examiner warnings are our paraphrase with a series badge | The report sentence may be blockquoted inside caps, series badge retained | Mark, mock debrief (05-TIME-007) |
| `LIC_TEXTBOOK_RAG` | Textbook chunks absent from `global`; a student sees only their own uploads | Chunks enter `global` scoped to `syllabus_codes` and `territories`; trust rank 2 | Learn Turns, conflict cards (06-TRUST-004), Reader |
| `LIC_TEXTBOOK_DISPLAY` | Citation chip to the publisher's product page | Section rendered in the Reader with page images or text per `display_rights` | Reader, offline (06-STOR-008) |
| `LIC_NAME_DESCRIPTIVE` | Non-affiliation notice everywhere (06.11), board name only in descriptive strings | Notice text may add the permission reference; the ban on the name in the product name, domain and app title **does not lift** (14-GTM-012) | Landing, app-store metadata |

**06-LIC-003** Every flag transition is a Pack event, not a deploy: turning a flag on writes a `pack.version` minor bump, re-runs the retrieval gold set and, for marking flags, re-runs the per-paper gate before any student sees the change. *Acceptance:* flipping `LIC_MS_GROUNDING` in staging without a gate re-run blocks publish.

**06-LIC-004** Every flag is revocable in one write: setting `licences.expiry` to the past removes the chunks from the next query, restores paraphrase rendering and invalidates the caches listing that `licence_id` (06-STOR-007), with no deploy and no data migration. Test this quarterly (§12 drill).

### Fallback if nothing lands

Assume it. The launch plan already is the fallback: OWN items and schemes, OWN paraphrased insights, facts and anchors, deep links, and USER uploads processed per tenant. Nothing in §04, §05 or §07 requires a licence; the only features that would improve are verbatim descriptor display and endorsed-textbook explanations, and the honest substitute for both already ships. **06-LIC-005** No roadmap item, GTM claim or investor number may be contingent on a licence that is not signed; an item that would be is filed with `deferred_to: later`. *Acceptance:* the M6 launch checklist contains zero rows whose precondition is a `licence_id`.

### Budget envelope [founder default, E2]

| Line | Envelope (Y1) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Counsel: three-provenance review, five letters, DPIA, takedown policy, trademark clearance | $25k–45k | Fixed-fee scoped; the largest single legal line before any licence |
| CLA generative-AI licence, if repertoire and RAG display check out | model at $0–50k/yr until quoted | Per-title or per-seat; unquoted at the time of writing |
| Publisher direct licences (Hodder/OUP/Collins), 1–3 titles | $0–60k/yr or referral-share | Prefer revenue share over an advance in Y1 |
| Board grounding licences (Cambridge, Pearson) | unknown; assume $0 and no availability | Treat any quote as a Y2 decision |
| **Rule** | Committed licence fees ≤ **5% of trailing-12-month revenue**, and no advance that is not recoverable against usage | Founder sign-off per instrument |

**Why open the conversations at all if the answer changes nothing:** the counterparty that owns the exam board also owns the endorsed coursebooks and already runs an opt-in AI-licensing programme on its academic side — it is the single deal that would convert the product's main legal exposure into an advantage no grey-market competitor can copy. The letter costs a week of counsel time; the option is worth years.

## 06.10 Takedown process and the per-document kill switch

The kill switch is the reason the three-provenance model is credible: a rights-holder can verify in one email that we can and do remove a document completely, in hours, from every place it reached. Build the switch before the first ingest, not after the first notice.

### Intake

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 06-TAKE-001 | Publish **one** intake address, `copyright@margin.study`, plus a web form at `/legal/notice` and a named agent with a postal address, on the footer of every public page, the Papers surface, the legal page and the app-store listings. The form collects: identification of the work, the URL or `doc_id` or `sha256` complained of, the complainant's authority, contact details, a good-faith statement and a signature. Anonymous notices are actioned on the merits; incomplete notices are actioned and then queried. | The address resolves to a monitored shared inbox with paging; a synthetic notice sent monthly is acknowledged within the SLA. |
| 06-TAKE-002 | The **acknowledgement is automatic and immediate** (≤5 min) with a `notice_id`; the substantive answer follows within the SLA. Never require an account, a login or a specific format. | Synthetic-notice drill measures both times. |
| 06-TAKE-003 | The in-product **"Report a problem"** on every citation chip (06.6) and every Mark routes rights complaints into the same queue with the `doc_id` and `chunk_id` pre-filled; accuracy complaints route to the content queue instead. The router is a one-question chooser, not a free-text triage. | Fixture: a rights report from a chip creates a `notice` row with the document resolved. |

### The 24-hour SLA

**06-TAKE-004** From receipt of any notice that identifies a document — however informally — to the document being dark: **≤24 hours**, clock running on weekends and holidays. The on-call takedown rota is the content lead and counsel, with the CTO as backstop; paging is the same rota as a P1 incident. **Assess after, not before:** the operator flips the kill switch first and evaluates the merits afterwards, because reinstatement is cheap and exposure is not.

| Step | Owner | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge with `notice_id` | automatic | ≤5 min |
| Resolve the notice to `doc_id`s via the ledger (06-PROV-009: `sha256`, `source_url`, `doc_id` or title search) | on-call | ≤2 h |
| Flip `provenance_ledger.kill_switch = true` on every resolved document version | on-call | ≤4 h |
| Verify propagation with the automated proof (below) | on-call | ≤6 h |
| Substantive reply naming what was removed and the derived-row count | counsel | ≤24 h |
| Merits assessment; reinstate, keep dark, or negotiate a licence | counsel + founder | ≤10 working days |

### Kill-switch semantics

**06-TAKE-005** `kill_switch = true` is a single write with six mandatory consequences, executed by one job (`takedown_propagate`) that must complete or alert:

| Layer | What happens | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| **Retrieval** | The prefilter drops every `chunk` whose `document_id` (or `derived_from` closure) hits the killed version, in the next query — no re-index, no deploy | 10,000-query probe returns 0 chunks |
| **Packs** | Every `items`, `mark_schemes`, `examiner_insights`, `textbook_sections`, `figures`, `exemplars` row derived from it is excluded from Pack builds and from practice selection; a Pack whose `mapped_pct` drops below its gate threshold returns to `mapped` (14-PACK-002) | Pack validation re-run; state change logged |
| **Caches** | Every prompt-cache key, CDN object and client cache whose manifest lists the `doc_id` is invalidated; TTLs are irrelevant because the manifest join is exact | Cache-manifest scan returns 0 live keys |
| **Live sessions** | In-flight Sessions finish their current Turn and then re-assemble context without the document; nothing already rendered is retracted from the screen, but the next Turn cannot cite it | Session-continuation test |
| **Exports** | Learning Receipts, Card exports, print views and offline bundles regenerate without the document; already-downloaded artefacts are out of reach and the reply says so plainly | Regeneration diff on a fixture Receipt |
| **Marks** | Existing Marks are **not** deleted (they are the audit record, 05-MARK-012) but their `sources[]` chips for the killed document render as "source withdrawn" and no longer deep-link; a Mark whose scheme record is killed cannot be re-marked or challenged against it | Chip-state test; challenge on a killed scheme returns the withdrawn state |

**06-TAKE-006** The switch is **per document version**, never per source or per board: killing `doc_id@3` does not kill `@2` unless the notice names it. Killing a document does not delete it — bytes and ledger row are retained under legal hold so that a counter-notice, a licence or a dispute can be answered. *Acceptance:* after a kill, `SELECT` on the ledger still returns the row with `takedown.removed_at` set and `kill_switch=true`.

**06-TAKE-007** `derived_from` closure is transitive and is the whole point: killing an official mark-scheme PDF must remove the OWN paraphrases and examiner insights derived from it, not just the anchors. This is test 4 of 06.1 and runs nightly on a random document. *Acceptance:* kill a random official document in staging → 100% of insights and paraphrases whose closure includes it disappear from retrieval within the propagation job's runtime (target ≤15 min, SLA 24 h).

**06-TAKE-008** USER documents use the same switch: a student's "Delete this file" is a self-service takedown with a 24 h propagation SLA (06-STOR-005) and writes the same ledger fields. There is no second deletion path.

### Notice and counter-notice

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 06-TAKE-010 | A **counter-notice** may be filed by the uploading principal (a teacher whose upload was removed, a school, or Margin itself for OWN content wrongly claimed). It requires identification of the material, a statement of the basis (own copyright, licence, permission, or that the notice misidentified the document) and contact details. Counsel reviews within 10 working days. |
| 06-TAKE-011 | Reinstatement writes `takedown.reinstated_at` and flips `kill_switch=false`; the same propagation job runs in reverse and the ledger keeps both events. The complainant is notified before reinstatement, with the reason. |
| 06-TAKE-012 | **Repeat-infringer policy:** a tenant or user with three upheld notices in 12 months loses upload rights; a school tenant's teacher-of-record is notified before the third. Published in the terms. |
| 06-TAKE-013 | No notice is answered by an AI agent and no automated system may assess merits. Agents may resolve `doc_id`s and run the propagation job; a human signs every reply and every reinstatement. |
| 06-TAKE-014 | Margin never counter-notices to keep board editorial content dark-to-live. If a board asks for its schemes, papers or reports to go, they go and stay gone; the conversation that follows is a licensing conversation (06.9), not a dispute. **Why:** the product does not depend on that content (06-LIC-005), and a fight would cost the school relationships that are the actual moat. |

### Reporting

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 06-TAKE-020 | A **public transparency page**, updated quarterly: notices received, documents killed, documents reinstated, median time-to-dark, counter-notices, repeat-infringer actions, and the count of documents currently dark. No complainant names. | Page generated from the `notices` and ledger tables by a job, never typed. |
| 06-TAKE-021 | Per-document reports on demand for a licensor or complainant: every extract served (`extract_log`, 06-STOR-004), every chunk and derived row, every cache key, and the kill/reinstate history — produced in ≤1 working day. | Drill: request a report for a random licensed document; measure. |
| 06-TAKE-022 | The takedown drill runs **quarterly** against a real (staging-mirrored) document and is scored on time-to-dark, propagation completeness and reply quality; a failed drill is a P1 with a named owner. Results go in the compliance folder used in school procurement (§12). | Drill report per quarter with timings. |
| 06-TAKE-023 | Time-to-dark, open notices and drill results appear on the same internal dashboard as the calibration gates; a notice open past 24 h with the document still live pages the founder. | Alert fires in a staged test. |

## 06.11 Non-affiliation notice rules

Board names appear all over Margin because they have to: a student searching for 9609 help must find a product that says 9609. Descriptive use is lawful; implied endorsement is not, and it is also the single fastest way to lose a licensing conversation (06.9). Treat the notice as a UI component with a string table, not as a paragraph someone writes once.

### The exact strings

Store these in `i18n/legal.*` and render them from the table; no surface may compose its own wording. `{Board}` is `boards.display_name` verbatim; `{Code}` is the syllabus code; nothing else interpolates.

| Key | String (English source) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `legal.nonaffil.long` | "Margin is an independent study tool. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or approved by Cambridge Assessment International Education, Pearson, AQA, OCR, the International Baccalaureate Organization, or the College Board. Syllabus codes, paper names and command words are used to describe the exams this tool prepares you for. All board materials remain the copyright of their owners." | Landing footer, `/legal`, app-store description, school proposal PDF |
| `legal.nonaffil.short` | "Independent study tool. Not affiliated with or endorsed by {Board}." | Course pages, Pack pages, Papers surface, teacher console |
| `legal.nonaffil.mark` | "Practice estimate, not a board mark. Margin is not affiliated with {Board}." | Every Mark, every predicted-grade panel, every mock debrief |
| `legal.nonaffil.export` | "Produced by Margin, an independent study tool not affiliated with or endorsed by {Board}. Marks in this document are practice estimates, not board marks." | Learning Receipt, printed Mark, Card export, parent digest, teacher CSV |
| `legal.item.original` | "Original item · in the style of {Code} {Paper}" | Every generated Item (05-GEN-009) |
| `legal.doc.official` | "Official {Board} document — opens on {Board}'s website." | Every deep-link chip and button (06.6) |
| `legal.upload.user` | "Your upload. Visible only to you{, and to your teacher for work you submit}." | Upload cards, Paper Companion |

**06-NONA-001** These strings are translated, never re-written, for RU/KZ and any later locale; a translation is reviewed by counsel before it ships. The English source is normative in a dispute.

### Placement rules

| ID | Surface | Rule | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 06-NONA-002 | **Landing and every public marketing page** | `legal.nonaffil.long` in the footer, at body-size type, never below 12 px, never in a collapsed accordion, contrast ≥4.5:1 like any other text | Automated check crawls every public route and asserts the string, computed font size and contrast |
| 06-NONA-003 | **Course, Pack and Papers surfaces** | `legal.nonaffil.short` visible without scrolling on first paint of the page header area | Visual-diff fixture per surface |
| 06-NONA-004 | **Every Mark** | `legal.nonaffil.mark` renders inside the calibration block, directly under `calibration_status.badge_text`; it is not dismissible and does not collapse | Render test on both 05.12 fixtures; snapshot includes the line |
| 06-NONA-005 | **Every export and print artefact** | `legal.nonaffil.export` on page 1 and in the running footer of every subsequent page; PDF metadata `Producer` = "Margin" and `Title` never contains a board name as the leading token | Receipt and print fixtures inspected byte-wise in CI |
| 06-NONA-006 | **App-store listings and OS metadata** | `legal.nonaffil.long` in the description; the app name is "Margin" alone; no board name in the app name, subtitle, keywords field, icon or screenshots' chrome | Store-metadata review in the release checklist (§14.4) |
| 06-NONA-007 | **Email, digest and notification** | `legal.nonaffil.short` in the footer of any message that shows a mark, band or predicted grade | Email fixture tests |
| 06-NONA-008 | The notice is **never** placed in a modal, a tooltip, a hover card, an onboarding step, or behind a "Learn more" link. It is body text on the page. | Lint: the string may not appear inside a component tagged `dismissible` |

### Trademark usage rules for board names

| ID | Rule | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| 06-NONA-010 | Board names and syllabus codes are used **descriptively only**: after a noun ("marking for Cambridge International A Level Business 9609"), never as a possessive, never as the subject of a claim ("Cambridge says…" is banned; "the 9609 syllabus states…" is fine). | Copy lint on product and marketing repos with the banned-pattern list |
| 06-NONA-011 | Banned in any product name, sub-brand, domain, subdomain, app name, social handle, ad headline, page `<title>` leading token, or feature name: "Cambridge", "CAIE", "Edexcel", "Pearson", "AQA", "OCR", "IB", "AP", "College Board". Banned adjectives anywhere near a board name: "official", "endorsed", "approved", "authorised", "partner", "certified". | Lint + domain-registration policy; app-store metadata review (14-GTM-012) |
| 06-NONA-012 | **No board logos, shields, crests, colour schemes or typefaces**, ever, including in screenshots, creator briefs, slide decks and school proposals. Board identity in the UI is a text label in Margin's own type. | Design review; asset pipeline rejects any file matching the blocked-asset hash list |
| 06-NONA-013 | Never imply a marking relationship: banned phrases include "marked by examiners", "official marking", "board-standard", "same as the real thing". Permitted: "marked against the mark scheme", "calibrated against teacher-marked scripts", "in the style of". | Copy lint; the ten canonical strings (§09) are the vocabulary |
| 06-NONA-014 | Creator, affiliate and partner briefs carry the same list as a signed annex; a creator who publishes an unapproved claim is paused within 24 h (14-GTM-015). | Creator contract; incident log |
| 06-NONA-015 | Where a licence grants descriptive-name permission (`LIC_NAME_DESCRIPTIVE`, 06.9), the notice may add the permission reference; **the product-name, domain and logo bans do not lift**. | Flag test: turning the flag on changes only the notice text |

### Review cadence

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 06-NONA-020 | Counsel reviews the full string table and the banned-pattern list **quarterly**, and additionally within 10 working days of: a new board Pack entering `draft`, a new locale, a new licence, or any board correspondence. | Dated review record per quarter in the compliance folder |
| 06-NONA-021 | The placement checks (06-NONA-002…007) run in CI on every release and as a weekly synthetic crawl of production, including app-store pages; a missing notice on any surface is a release blocker, not a bug. | Crawl report per week; blocked release fixture |
| 06-NONA-022 | Board names in the Pack are read from `boards.display_name`; adding a board without a `display_name` and a `legal.nonaffil.short` render test fails the Pack build. | Compiler validation |


# §07 Learner memory and the knowledge graph

## 07.1 Entities and fields

The Learner Graph is what Margin knows about what a student *knows*, kept outside the chat, keyed to syllabus points, decaying on an FSRS clock. It is per Course, owned by the student, and is a projection of Attempts plus a small set of explicit preferences. Storage is Postgres (§11); no graph database.

```yaml
learner_graph:                      # one per (user, course)
  user_id, course_id, pack_version, policy_version
  mastery[]:                        # one row per syllabus point s in the Pack
    syllabus_point_id               # official numbering, e.g. "9609/3.2.1"
    M: float 0..1                   # 07.2
    state: Unseen|Shaky|Secure|Exam-ready
    state_reason: string            # the "why" shown on the pip
    retrievability_at_exam: float   # FSRS R projected to the paper date
    unaided_correct_days: [date]    # distinct days with unaided correct at tariff
    timed_correct: bool
    brier_topic: float              # last 10 gradable Attempts
    last_attempt_at, attempts_n, rung_mean_30d
    yield: float                    # 07.5, recomputed nightly
  items[]:                          # FSRS state per atomic Item (04-FSRS-001)
    item_id, stability, difficulty, due, reps, lapses, last_review,
    seen_solution_until?, overconfident_flag, provenance_mark_id?
  misconceptions[]:
    misconception_id, status: suspected|confirmed|resolved,
    first_seen, last_seen, evidence_attempt_ids[], contrast_pass_days[]
  attempts[]: → attempts table (SYNTHESIS §3.1 fields + 04-NSTR-003)
  marks[]:    → marks table (§05.8.1 contract)
  calibration:
    brier_overall_weekly[]: [{week, brier, n, sure_share}]
    predict_postdict[]: [{event_id, predicted, postdicted, actual, gap}]
  effort:
    debt_signals_14d: {solution_ratio, fast_attempt_share, copy_events,
                       avoidance_events, brier_delta, output_ratio}
    debt_level: 0|1|2|3, guard_arm: on|off
    sessions_after_22_exam_week: int
  prefs:
    intent_by_item_type: {numeric: check_steps, levels: teach_me, ...}
    explain_language, decimal_comma, reading_comfort_ref
    show_predicted_to_parent: false      # default off
    memory_paused: false, sensitive_exclusions: [topic]
  memories[]:                       # explicit, student-visible facts (07.7)
    id, text (≤200 chars), source: user|inferred, created_at, pinned: bool
```

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 07-GRPH-001 | Every field above is derivable from the Attempt, Turn, Mark and Card tables except `prefs` and `memories`; a nightly rebuild from those tables reproduces the graph bit-for-bit. | Rebuild job diff = 0 on a sample of 1,000 users. |
| 07-GRPH-002 | `memories[]` holds only facts a student would recognise as about their learning ("Confuses cash flow with profit — improving", "Prefers worked examples in maths", "Extra time 25%"); never health, family, mood or anything flagged by the sensitive-topic classifier (§12). Inferred memories carry `source: inferred` and a one-line "why" (the Attempt IDs). | Classifier blocks writes; audit sample weekly. |
| 07-GRPH-003 | The graph is per Course; nothing transfers between Courses except through `equivalent_to` edges (07.6) and Course-independent `prefs` (reading comfort, language, extra time). | Cross-Course read test returns only mapped fields. |

## 07.2 Mastery: computation, states and decay

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 07-MAST-001 | `M_s` = retrievability-weighted mean over the point's Items of a per-Item correctness posterior: `M_s = Σ_i R_i · c_i / Σ_i R_i`, where `R_i` is current FSRS retrievability and `c_i` is a Beta(1,1)-prior posterior mean of correctness over the Item's Attempts, each Attempt weighted by rung penalty `w(rung) = {≤1: 1.0, 2: 0.8, 3: 0.6, 4: 0.3, 5: 0}` and by `0` if `seen_solution` or `intent = just_answer`. Unattempted Items contribute nothing. | Reference implementation with fixture tests; recomputed on every Attempt write and nightly. |
| 07-MAST-002 | States: **Unseen** no Attempt; **Shaky** attempted, or previously Secure with any core Item's `R < 0.7`; **Secure** two unaided (rung ≤1) correct at the point's tariff on ≥2 distinct days, no seen-solution credit; **Exam-ready** Secure + one correct under timed conditions at full tariff with confidence Sure and topic Brier ≤0.15. Decay is FSRS-driven: a pip fades from Secure to Shaky when `R` crosses 0.7; it never lies by staying full. | State transition tests incl. decay. |
| 07-MAST-003 | Every state carries `state_reason` in plain words ("Secure on 12 Sep and 15 Sep; retrievability 0.62 — due today", "Exam-ready: timed 8/8 on 3 Oct"). | Reason string non-empty on every non-Unseen pip. |
| 07-MAST-004 | Cohort priors: until the student has ≥30 Attempts in a Course, `M_s` for unattempted points is displayed as Unseen but the planner uses the cohort median `M_s` for that Course and target grade; the switch to per-user is logged on the Plan. | Plan shows "using cohort priors" until 30 Attempts. |

## 07.3 The read path: what enters every Turn

The Orchestrator (04.10) assembles `learner_context` for every Turn from the graph. It is compact, structured and deterministic so that it sits after the cached Pack block (§08 caching) and never breaks the cache.

**Budget: ≤1,200 tokens per Turn** (≤400 for trivial/nav Turns), serialised as a fixed-order block:

```
<learner>
course: 9609 · June 2027 · Paper 2 in 41 days · phase B · target A
item_point: 3.2.1 break-even · M 0.34 (Shaky) · R_exam 0.41 · entry_rung 4 · attempts 3 · last 2 days ago
prereqs: 3.1.4 contribution · M 0.72 (Secure)
open_misconceptions: [revenue_vs_profit: confirmed 14 Sep] [fixed_over_price: suspected]
seen_solution: this item no · this point 1 (retest due Thu)
calibration: topic Brier 0.28 · overconfident on last 2 · Sure share 0.6
effort: gate_latency_median 6 s · debt L1 (arm on) · solution_ratio 0.55
prefs: intent check_steps for numeric · explain in EN · decimal point
memories: "Prefers worked examples in maths" · "Extra time 25%"
</learner>
```

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 07-READ-001 | Inclusion order under the budget: (1) Item point + mastery + entry rung; (2) open misconceptions on this point and its prerequisites; (3) seen-solution status; (4) calibration on this topic; (5) effort/debt level; (6) prefs; (7) pinned memories; (8) up to 3 other misconceptions in the Course. Truncate from the bottom. | Serialiser tests at each budget. |
| 07-READ-002 | The context never contains transcripts, mood/affect history beyond the current Session tag, parent or teacher identities, or other students' data. | Schema allow-list; leak test. |
| 07-READ-003 | Read latency ≤40 ms p95 (single query on materialised graph rows). | Perf test. |
| 07-READ-004 | Incognito Sessions read the graph (so the tutor stays adapted) but write nothing (07.7); the block is labelled `incognito: true` so the tutor does not promise to remember. | Write count 0 in incognito. |
| 07-READ-005 | Mark mode reads only prefs, extra time and the Item's misconception list — never mastery — so marking is blind to the student's history. | Mark context excludes mastery fields (§05 eval). |

Why: ChatGPT "misses context from things I said 40+ messages ago"; the fix is a structured model of what the student knows, injected fresh every Turn, not a longer transcript.

## 07.4 The write path: what each event updates

| Event | Writes |
|---|---|
| Attempt submitted | `attempts` row; `items[].fsrs` via FSRS grade (correct unaided → Good; correct rung 2–3 → Hard; wrong or rung ≥4 → Again); `mastery.M_s` recompute for the primary point and its prerequisites; `calibration.brier_topic`; `effort.gate_latency` |
| Mark completed (§05) | `marks` row; one Card per lost marking point/descriptor with provenance; `mastery` of each tagged point; `misconceptions` on detector hits (`suspected`) |
| Misconception confirmed (04-MISC-004) | `misconceptions[].status = confirmed`; optional inferred memory (≤1 per point) |
| Rung-5 / Just the answer | `attempt.seen_solution`; `items[].seen_solution_until = now + 24–72 h`; forced `due` |
| Timed section / mock | `calibration.predict_postdict`; `mastery.timed_correct`; debrief Cards |
| Session end | `effort.debt_signals_14d`; Session `phase`, `slot` mix; weekly goal progress |
| Sunday review | `brier_overall_weekly`; `yield` recompute; Plan proposal |
| Student memory edit (07.7) | `memories[]`, `prefs`, or a delete cascade (07.7) |

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 07-WRIT-001 | All writes are idempotent on `(attempt_id)` or `(event_id)` and applied in one transaction with the Attempt; a failed graph write fails the Attempt visibly ("Not saved — retry"), never silently. | Chaos test: DB failure → UI error card, no half-writes. |
| 07-WRIT-002 | Teacher overrides (§05.8.11) rewrite `mark_per_AO` on the Attempt and trigger mastery recompute; the original Mark is kept. | Audit trail. |
| 07-WRIT-003 | Nothing writes to the graph from an Ask (no Course) or from an incognito Session. | Write count 0. |

## 07.5 Driving the Plan: Mark-Yield ranking

Mark-Yield is the number that decides what the student practises next. It is the expected qualification marks gained per minute of study on one syllabus point (or one skill node such as "AO4 committed judgement"), stored as `mastery[].yield` (07.1) and consumed by the Plan (§10 screen 15), Today (screen 3) and the interleaved/new slots of every Session (04-MIX-003). It is the SYNTHESIS §7.7 formula `tariff_exposure × (1 − M) × (1 − R(t_exam)) × learnability / est_hours` written out with every variable sourced; SYNTHESIS's form is the `M_target = 1` case below.

### Formula

```
Y_s = E_s × G_s × U_s × T_s / m_s          # weighted marks per minute; shown as raw marks per hour on the nearest paper

E_s = Σ_p  w_p × P_p(s) × k_p(s)           # tariff exposure, in option-percentage points
G_s = max(0, M_target − M_s)                # gain headroom
U_s = 1 − R_s(t_paper)                      # decay urgency
T_s = clamp(learnability_s × transfer_s, 0.5, 1.5)
m_s = max(5, base_min_s × G_s × rung_factor_s + 8 × open_misconceptions_s)   # minutes
```

| Variable | Meaning | Source | Default / range |
|---|---|---|---|
| `w_p` | Value of one raw mark on paper *p* in the option grade = `papers[p].weight_pct / papers[p].max_marks` | Pack `papers[]` (§06.3) | 9609: P1 20/40 = 0.5, P2 30/60 = 0.5, P3 30/60 = 0.5, P4 20/40 = 0.5; differs on most syllabuses |
| `P_p(s)` | Probability *s* is assessed on paper *p* in the next series: Laplace-smoothed frequency over the last 8 series, `(hits + 1) / (series + 2)` | Pack `assessed_by` edges (07.6) built by the compiler from question metadata; skill nodes (AO3/AO4 techniques) have `P = 1.0` on every levels paper | 0.1–1.0 |
| `k_p(s)` | Mean raw marks tied to *s* on *p* when it appears | same edge, `marks_on_offer` | tariff-weighted |
| `M_target` | Per-point mastery target implied by the Course target grade | Course `target_grade` → {A*: 0.90, A: 0.85, B: 0.75, C: 0.65, D/E: 0.55}; floor 0.85 for skill nodes on levels papers | — |
| `M_s` | Current mastery (07-MAST-001); cohort median until 30 Attempts (07-MAST-004); projected value if the point is `projected` from another board (07.6) | Learner Graph `mastery[].M` | 0–1 |
| `R_s(t_paper)` | FSRS retrievability of the point's Items projected to the date of the paper that assesses it, tariff-weighted mean; Unseen ⇒ 0 | Learner Graph `mastery[].retrievability_at_exam`, recomputed nightly (04-FSRS-002) | 0–1 |
| `learnability_s` | Cohort mastery gain per hour on *s* ÷ Course median gain per hour, for students at the same target grade | Cohort aggregates (07.8, k ≥ 20) | 1.0 until 200 cohort Attempts on *s*; clamp 0.6–1.4 |
| `transfer_s` | `1 + 0.25 × n_dep` where `n_dep` = number of points with a confirmed `prerequisite_of` edge from *s* that are below their own target, capped at 2; skill nodes take 1.5 | 07.6 graph | 1.0–1.5 |
| `base_min_s` | Cohort minutes from Unseen to `M = 1` on *s* at this grade | Pack `est_minutes` seeded by the compiler, replaced by cohort data at 200 Attempts | 30–120 |
| `rung_factor_s` | `1 + 0.1 × (rung_mean_30d − 1)` for this student on *s*; Course mean if no Attempts | Learner Graph `rung_mean_30d` | 1.0–1.4 |
| `open_misconceptions_s` | Count of `confirmed` misconceptions on *s* | Learner Graph `misconceptions[]` | 0–3 |

Display conversion: `raw_marks_per_hour = 60 × Y_s / w_nearest_paper`, rounded to one decimal below 10 and to an integer above; the badge on the syllabus tree and the Next card reads "≈ +9 marks/h · Paper 2" (09-10 CourseTree spec).

### Worked example — 9609 AS student, Paper 2 in 42 days (Phase B), target A

`M_target = 0.85`. Four candidates after the FSRS due slot is filled; numbering illustrative.

| Point | E_s | G_s | U_s | T_s | m_s (min) | Y_s (wtd/min) | Shown |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Skill: AO4 committed judgement (`P = 1.0` on P1 §B 6 AO4 marks and P2 12 AO4 marks; `w` 0.5) | 0.5×1.0×6 + 0.5×1.0×12 = **9.0** | 0.85 − 0.30 = 0.55 | 1 − 0.50 = 0.50 | 0.8 × 1.5 = 1.2 | 60×0.55×1.2 = **39.6** | 9.0×0.55×0.50×1.2/39.6 = **0.0750** | **≈ +9 marks/h · Paper 2** |
| 5.1.2 Motivation theories — Secure, decaying (P2 0.7×12; P1 §B 0.4×20) | 4.2 + 4.0 = **8.2** | 0.85 − 0.72 = 0.13 | 1 − 0.55 = 0.45 | 1.0 | 60×0.13×1.0 = **7.8** | **0.0615** | ≈ +7.4 marks/h |
| 3.2.1 Break-even — Shaky (P2 0.6×8; P1 §A 0.3×5); 2 dependents below target; misconception `revenue_vs_profit` confirmed | 2.4 + 0.75 = **3.15** | 0.85 − 0.34 = 0.51 | 1 − 0.41 = 0.59 | min(1.1×1.5, 1.5) = 1.5 | 60×0.51×1.2 + 8 = **44.7** | **0.0318** | ≈ +3.8 marks/h |
| 4.3.3 Lean production — Unseen (P2 0.25×8; P1 §A 0.2×5) | 1.0 + 0.5 = **1.5** | 0.85 | 1.0 | 0.9 | 60×0.85×1.1 = **56.1** | **0.0205** | ≈ +2.5 marks/h |

Read it as the product intends: a 10-minute top-up on a high-exposure Secure topic outranks 45 minutes on the weakest topic, and the AO4 skill outranks both because it is assessed on every essay. The weakest-topic heuristic would have put break-even first. Why: the Layer-1 RCT `mark-yield vs weakest-topic` (13-EFF-003) is only meaningful if the ranking is a swappable strategy behind one interface — build `rank(strategy, course, user) → [(point, score, why)]`.

### Tie-breakers, overrides and consumption

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 07-YLD-001 | Ties (|ΔY| < 0.002) break in order: nearer paper date → lower `M_s` → prerequisite before dependent → longer since last Attempt → stable hash of `(user_id, point_id)`. The ranking is deterministic for identical inputs. | Property test: same graph snapshot ⇒ identical list across 100 runs. |
| 07-YLD-002 | Hard overrides filter or pin candidates; they never modify `Y_s`, so the badge always shows the honest number. Precedence: (1) wellbeing L3 (crisis, §12.5): planner paused, Today shows the safety card only; (2) wellbeing L2 (distress tag in the last 48 h, 04.9): no Unseen points, no 20-markers, Session ≤15 min; (3) locked windows: Quiet Hours, Study Hours, no block >90 min after 22:00 inside T−7 (04-MIX-004); (4) exam proximity: between-papers mode restricts candidates to the next paper's `assessed_by` set; Phase C admits no Unseen points unless overridden; (5) teacher assignment (§10.20): locked assignment Items occupy the first slots, ≤50% of a Session, until due; (6) student pin ("Study this anyway", "Not today" for 7 days). | Fixture per override; `Y_s` unchanged before/after; precedence tests. |
| 07-YLD-003 | Consumption: Plan builds the week's interleaved and new blocks from the ranked list top-down, taking the first point whose state is not Unseen for interleaved slots and the first Unseen point for new slots, skipping any point already scheduled twice that week; Today shows the top three under **Next** with badge and a one-line "why" (`"Assessed on every essay · your AO4 is at 0.30 · 40 min"`); the Session generator draws the interleaved slot from the top five so consecutive Sessions do not repeat. | Slot provenance logged per Item (04-MIX-003); Today never shows the same three points two days running unless nothing else is eligible. |
| 07-YLD-004 | Recompute: incremental (touched points + their dependents, ≤2 s) on Mark completed, Timed Paper debrief, target grade or exam date change, Pack version change, teacher assignment created or closed; full recompute nightly with `retrievability_at_exam` and at the Sunday review. A mid-day recompute changes tomorrow's Today and the current Session's *unstarted* slots only; it never reorders Items already shown. | Nightly job <30 min per 100k Courses; no in-Session reshuffle in UI tests. |
| 07-YLD-005 | Cohort priors: while `attempts_n < 30` in the Course, `M_s` and `R_s` for unattempted points come from the cohort median; the Plan carries the line "Using typical starting points until you have 30 attempts (14 so far)". | 07-MAST-004 log entry; string present. |
| 07-YLD-006 | "Why this plan" (screen 15) exposes, per block, the four factors in words — "worth 12 marks on Paper 2 · you are at 0.72 · fading by exam day · 8 minutes" — never the formula, never a decimal of `Y_s`. | Copy review; no `Y_s` decimal in DOM. |
| 07-YLD-007 | Property-based acceptance (Hypothesis/fast-check, 1,000 cases each): with other factors fixed, `Y_s` is non-decreasing in `E_s`, `G_s`, `U_s`, `T_s` and non-increasing in `m_s`; `Y_s = 0` iff `G_s = 0` or `E_s = 0`; multiplying every `E_s` by a constant preserves the ranking; a point assessed only by a paper already sat has `E_s = 0` and never appears in Next; the worked example reproduces the table above within ±0.001. | CI suite `planner/yield_properties`. |

## 07.6 The cross-board syllabus graph

The cross-board graph is the layer that lets one explanation, one misconception bank and one original Item serve 9609, Edexcel IAL Business, IB Business Management and, where content overlaps, a national exam — while keeping everything an examiner owns (schemes, grids, thresholds) strictly per board. It lives in two Postgres tables, `syllabus_nodes` and `syllabus_edges`; nothing here is a graph database (§11).

### Schema

```yaml
syllabus_node:
  node_id: "9609:2026-2028/5.1.2"        # pack_id + official numbering; skill nodes "9609:2026-2028/skill/ao4_judgement"
  pack_id, kind: content|skill|command_word|paper
  title: "Motivation theories: Taylor, Maslow, Herzberg"   # our wording
  level: IGCSE|GCSE|AS|A2|IAL_AS|IAL_A2|IB_SL|IB_HL|national
  ao_profile: {AO1: 0.3, AO2: 0.2, AO3: 0.3, AO4: 0.2}     # from assessed_by edges
  misconception_ids[], item_family_ids[], embedding_id      # voyage-4, 1024-d

syllabus_edge:
  edge_id, from_node, to_node
  type: equivalent_to|prerequisite_of|part_of|assessed_by
  # equivalent_to only:
  coverage: full|partial_from_in_to|partial_to_in_from|overlap
  depth_delta: -1|0|+1                     # +1 = to_node goes deeper (e.g. IB HL extensions)
  vocabulary_map: {"gearing": "leverage", "trade receivables": "debtors"}   # optional, per direction
  # assessed_by only:
  paper_id, weight_pct, frequency_8_series: 5, marks_on_offer_mean: 8.0    # feeds P_p(s), k_p(s) in 07.5
  confidence: 0.0–1.0
  status: proposed|confirmed|rejected
  provenance:
    method: compiler_embedding|compiler_llm|human_confirmed|human_authored
    models: ["sonnet-5@2026-08", "gemini-3.8-flash"]   # cross-family for compiler_llm
    evidence: [{pack_id, source_ref, extract≤40w}]      # both syllabus lines
    reviewer_id?, reviewed_at?, review_note?
  created_at, superseded_by?
```

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 07-XBRD-001 | `equivalent_to` is stored once and read symmetrically; `coverage` and `vocabulary_map` are direction-aware. `part_of` edges form the Pack's tree and are the only edges the compiler may auto-confirm (≥0.95, two families agree). `equivalent_to` and `prerequisite_of` are never auto-confirmed. | Schema constraint + compiler unit test. |
| 07-XBRD-002 | **Proposal pipeline** (a stage of the Curriculum Compiler, §06.4): (1) embed every node's title + our description + misconception labels; (2) candidate pairs across Packs at cosine ≥0.78 (top-5 per node); (3) Sonnet 5 batch classifies each pair `{equivalent (coverage, depth_delta), prerequisite, none}` with a one-line justification quoting both syllabus lines; (4) Gemini 3.8 Flash repeats blind; (5) `confidence` = agreement-weighted mean of the two calibrated scores; (6) write `status=proposed`. Pairs <0.60 are dropped; 0.60–0.95 go to the mapping-review queue (screen 25). Cross-family disagreement on `type` forces review regardless of score. | Golden set of 200 human-labelled 9609↔IAL pairs: precision ≥0.90, recall ≥0.80 at the review threshold. |
| 07-XBRD-003 | **Human confirmation**: a subject reviewer confirms, edits (coverage, depth, vocabulary) or rejects; the UI shows both syllabus lines, both Packs' misconceptions and a sample Item from each; ≤20 s median per decision; confirmation writes `provenance.method=human_confirmed`. Rejected pairs are not re-proposed unless a Pack version changes. | Review throughput and audit trail; re-proposal test. |
| 07-XBRD-004 | Edges are versioned with the Packs they join; a new syllabus version re-runs proposals only for changed nodes and carries confirmed edges forward when both node texts are unchanged (sha256 of our description). | Re-run touches only changed nodes. |

### What transfers, what never does

| Asset | Transfers across a confirmed `equivalent_to`? | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Concept explanations, worked examples, contrast cases (Pack `content`) | Yes | Served in the target Course with `vocabulary_map` applied and the target board's command-word table; the citation chip names the *target* syllabus line. `depth_delta = +1` withholds the deeper material's extension until the target Pack has its own node text. |
| Misconceptions and distractors | Yes | Copied as `suspected` priors at weight 0.5 in the target Course's misconception list; `confirmed` requires evidence on the target Course (04-MISC-004). Board-specific misconceptions (e.g. "evaluation inside an Analyse item" is a Cambridge command-word error) are tagged `board_specific` on the node and do not transfer. |
| Cards and FSRS state | Yes, for atomic Items with an `item_alias` (definitions, formulas, diagram rules) | The Card keeps its provenance line ("From your Mark · 9609 P2 Q3(b)") and gains the target Course; stability, difficulty and `due` carry over unchanged; the interval cap re-anchors to the target paper (04-FSRS-003). Level-based Cards ("AO4 needs a committed judgement") transfer only if the target board's grid has a matching descriptor family, else they stay on the source Course. |
| Original Items (OWN) | Conditionally | Retagged to the target node only if `command_word` exists verbatim in the target Pack and the tariff/AO split is legal for a target paper (05-GEN-001); otherwise the generator is called with the target paper's constraints. `item_stats` are kept per board, never pooled. |
| Mark schemes, levels grids, AO splits, evidence rules | **Never** | Board property; a Mark is always produced from the target Pack's `mark_scheme_items`. |
| Command-word definitions and AO ceilings | **Never** | Verbatim per syllabus version (05-PROC-012). |
| Thresholds, PUM tables, predicted grades | **Never** | Per component per series (05.8). |
| Examiner insights | **Never** as evidence | May be shown as background in the source Course only; a Mark on the target Course cites only the target board's insights. |
| Marks, Attempts, Receipts | **Never moved** | They stay on the Course that produced them; the target Course sees their effect only through projected mastery. |
| Calibration status | **Never** | Each Examiner Twin is per paper (05-SCOP-003). |
