## 09.8 The streaming contract
Every streamed surface (Turn, Mark, debrief, generated Item) obeys this contract; it is tested in CI against 20 recorded golden streams with synthetic TTFT of 0.3, 1.5, 3 and 8 s.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 09-STRM-001 | Optimistic echo: the user message appears, composer clears, scroll pins, and a three-dot indicator occupies the assistant slot within 50 ms of Send. | Performance trace: paint ≤50 ms after keydown. |
| 09-STRM-002 | At 800 ms without a first token the dots become one 13 px muted status line drawn from the route ("Reading the 9609 P2 mark scheme…", "Checking the working with SymPy…"); text, never a spinner or pulsing background. | Synthetic 1.5 s TTFT shows the line at 800±50 ms. |
| 09-STRM-003 | At 6 s: "Taking longer than usual" plus Stop; at 20 s the InlineError offers "Retry with Think" and "Copy my message". | Synthetic 8 s and 25 s traces. |
| 09-STRM-004 | Tokens are buffered and painted per frame at ≤90 characters per 16 ms; bursts are paced. | No frame paints >90 new characters. |
| 09-STRM-005 | DOM above the stream cursor is immutable: earlier paragraphs, lists and tables are never re-laid out; markdown is committed block by block. | CLS measured above the cursor = 0 on all golden streams. |
| 09-STRM-006 | Unclosed `$$…`, ``` fences, tables and AOCards hold a skeleton of the expected height until closed; inline `$…$` renders only when closed. | No visible raw LaTeX or fence markers at any frame. |
| 09-STRM-007 | Auto-scroll stops after 120 px of user scroll; a "↓ New" pill (32 h, `--bg-el`, hairline) appears bottom-centre; tapping it re-pins. | Scroll up 150 px during a stream: no yank; pill visible. |
| 09-STRM-008 | Stop replaces Send in place (same position, same 36 px); the partial Turn stays, tagged "Stopped"; no animation on the swap. | Screenshot diff of the button box before/after. |
| 09-STRM-009 | Thinking renders as a collapsed non-animated "Thought for 6 s ▸" row; expanding shows a summary, never a live token stream by default. | Story state. |
| 09-STRM-010 | The lint (§04) runs before paint; a rejected draft regenerates without any visible artefact; the template fallback paints as a normal Turn. | Golden stream with an injected "Great question!" shows no flash of the rejected text. |
| 09-STRM-011 | Mark streaming order: MarkHeader → one AOCard each within 8 s → BandTotal + CalibrationBadge → next-mark advice; spans light in the answer as their card commits. | Recorded Mark stream: header ≤2 s, each card ≤8 s, full ≤45 s p95. |
| 09-STRM-012 | Screen readers: the completed Turn is announced once via `role="log" aria-live="polite"`; never per token. Status lines are announced once each. | NVDA/VoiceOver script. |
| 09-STRM-013 | Resumable: on reconnect the client resumes the SSE stream from the last part id; the partial Turn is never duplicated. | Kill the network at 40% of a golden stream; final DOM equals the uninterrupted golden. |

## 09.9 Reading-comfort settings
**09-READ-001** One preference object, stored per user (synced) and applied by CSS custom properties on `:root`, honoured by chat, Mark view, reader, Cards, artifacts and print:

```json
{ "family": "inter|hyperlegible|opendyslexic|serif|system",
  "size_px": 17, "leading": "1.4|1.55|1.7", "tracking_em": "0|0.05|0.12",
  "measure": "narrow|medium|wide", "warm_bg": false, "capitalise_words": false,
  "theme": "system|light|dark", "contrast_plus": false, "reduce_motion": "system|on",
  "reduce_transparency": false, "read_aloud_rate": 1.0 }
```

**09-READ-002** Controls (Settings › Reading comfort, also reachable from the reader header and ⌘K "Reading comfort"): family radio with live specimen in each face; size stepper 14–24 px (chat and reader scale together; UI text does not scale below 14); leading and tracking three-segment controls; measure narrow 56 ch / medium 68 ch / wide 75 ch; **Reading-comfort preset** one tap = 18 px / 1.7 / +0.05 em / 60 ch / warm background `oklch(96% .012 85)`; "Capitalise Each Word" toggle (applies to assistant text only, never to quotes or code). Every control has a one-line consequence beneath it.

**09-READ-003** Read aloud: every Turn, Card and reader page has a Read-aloud action (system TTS; 0.8–1.5× rate); math is spoken via MathML + lazily loaded SRE ("x squared plus 3 x"); code is read with punctuation. Acceptance: read-aloud of a Turn with an inline fraction produces the SRE string, not "dollar frac".

**09-READ-004** Size and family changes apply without reload and without layout shift outside the text itself; measure is enforced by `max-width: var(--measure)` on the text column, not by the pane width. Why: dyslexic and ADHD students name busy screens and dual-column text as the reason they cover half the browser (student-voice §9); a switcher beats a single "dyslexia font" (Wallace et al. 2022).

## 09.10 Keyboard map and command-palette verbs
**09-KEYS-001** Global map (macOS ⌘ = Ctrl elsewhere). Every shortcut is listed in the `⌘/` sheet and rebindable in Settings › Shortcuts; no single-letter globals fire while a text field is focused.

| Keys | Action | Keys | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `⌘K` | Command palette | `⌘/` | Shortcut sheet |
| `⌘1 ⌘2 ⌘3` | Mode Learn · Practise · Mark | `1 2 3` (IntentRow visible) | Teach me · Check my steps · Just the answer |
| `⌘J` | Toggle right pane (rail ↔ open) | `⌘⇧J` | Cycle pane tabs |
| `⌘B` | Toggle sidebar | `⌘⇧M` | Math keypad |
| `⌘⇧P` | Photograph / upload | `⌘E` | Effort dial cycle |
| `Enter` / `⇧Enter` | Send / newline | `Esc` | Stop stream; else close topmost layer; else focus composer |
| `⇧↓` | Next help rung | `⌘↑` | Edit last user message (branches) |
| `⌘⇧C` | Copy last Turn | `⌘⇧R` | Retry last Turn |
| `⌘.` | Rewrite weakest paragraph (Mark view) | `⌘⇧L` | Another like this |
| `Space` / `1` / `3` | Flip / Again / Got it (review) | `[` `]` | Previous / next citation |
| `⌘F` | Find in reader | `⌘⇧S` | Save selection as Card |
| `⌘,` | Settings | `⌘⇧N` | New Session (same Course) |
| `Tab` (Mark view) | Move through spans | `Alt+←` | Back (route stack) |

**09-KEYS-002** Focus rules: `:focus-visible` only; ring = `0 0 0 2px var(--bg-app), 0 0 0 4px var(--border-strong)` (3:1 against both neighbours); `scroll-padding-bottom` ≥ composer height so the sticky composer never hides a focused element (WCAG 2.4.11); `Esc` always restores focus to the element that opened the layer; after a Turn completes, focus moves to the composer (the hand-back) unless the user is typing elsewhere.

**09-KEYS-003** Command palette (`⌘K`, <150 ms to first results, zero animation). Verb-first fuzzy index across Sessions, Cards, syllabus points, Papers, files, Settings and Sources. Canonical verbs and argument types:

```
Learn <syllabus point>        Practise <point|paper|"5 more like this">   Mark <clipboard|photo>
Quiz me on <point>            Open paper <code> <series> <component>        Open <source> page <n>
Explain simpler | deeper      Show me in the book                             Save as card
Start timed section <paper>   Plan this week | Move block                     Readiness review
Reading comfort               Switch Course <name>                            New Session
Memory: forget <fact>         Export <receipt|cards|session>                  Challenge this Mark
Teacher: open class <code>    Go to <screen>                                  Toggle dark mode
```

Rows show verb, argument, a 12 px context line ("3.2 Motivation · ¾ · due Thu") and a keycap. Recent verbs first; `>` prefix forces verb mode; `?` prefix searches help. Acceptance: each verb has a unit test that it resolves to the right route with the right payload.

## 09.11 Microcopy voice and the copy lint
**09-COPY-001** Voice: an examiner who is on your side. Short, specific, declarative; examiner vocabulary explained in plain words on first use; the mark scheme's own terms ("developed", "application", "judgement") used exactly. No exclamation marks, no emoji, no "Great question", no therapy-speak, no guilt, no urgency framing. Numbers carry their basis. The system never speaks about its own feelings and never apologises more than once.

**09-COPY-002** Canonical strings (do / don't). The "Do" column is the shipped string; the "Don't" column is the lint counter-example used as a regression fixture.

| # | Situation | Do | Don't |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Effort Gate | "Have a go first — a plan or the first line is enough." | "Let's try it together! What do you think the answer might be? 😊" |
| 2 | Just the answer, before attempt | "After one attempt." | "Sorry, I can't give you the answer yet!" |
| 3 | Seen-solution tag | "Seen solution · retest Thursday." | "Solution revealed — don't forget to review!" |
| 4 | Command-word check | "Evaluate — a judgement is required. None found, so AO4 is capped at Level 2." | "Great analysis! Just remember to add a conclusion for top marks!" |
| 5 | Uncredited span reason | "Assertion without a link in the chain — L1, not L2." | "This point could be developed a bit more." |
| 6 | ER quote | "Examiners' report, m25: 'simply repeating the business name will not count as application.'" | "Examiners hate it when you do this!" |
| 7 | Calibration badge | "Calibrated on 9609 P2 · agreement 0.82 · 312 scripts." | "AI-powered accurate grading." |
| 8 | Below-gate Mark | "Practice estimate — not yet calibrated for this paper. Feedback and evidence shown; no mark." | "Estimated score: 14/20 (may be inaccurate)." |
| 9 | Notification | "18 cards due · about 6 minutes." | "Don't lose your progress! Review now 🔥" |
| 10 | Exam-week grace | "Exam week: marking limits are off until Friday." | "Good news!! Unlimited marking unlocked!" |
| 11 | Quote unverifiable | "I can't confirm that quote from the set text, so I won't use it." | "Here's a quote that might be from the text." |
| 12 | Weekly card | "4 of 4 sessions. 3.2 Motivation moved to ¾. Paper 2 readiness unchanged: no timed practice this week." | "Amazing week! You're on fire! Keep the streak alive!" |
| 13 | Mastery decay | "3.4 dropped to ¼ — last unaided practice 19 days ago." | "Oh no, you're losing mastery in 3.4!" |
| 14 | Re-mark delta | "+3 · AO4 L1→L2." | "Wow, huge improvement! 🎉" |
| 15 | Quota reached | "3 of 3 levels Marks used today. Points marking and Learn continue; the next levels Mark is at 00:00, or tonight on Student." | "You've hit your limit! Upgrade now to keep going!" |
| 16 | Offline | "Offline. Cards work; Marks and new Turns will send when you're back." | "Oops! Something went wrong with your connection." |
| 17 | Distress at 1 a.m. | "That sounds like a hard night. Your last three Marks went up. Tonight: sleep. Tomorrow's first block is 25 minutes on 3.2. If it feels worse than exam stress, here is someone to talk to." | "Don't worry, you've got this! Take a deep breath and let me explain calmly." |
| 18 | Coursework request | "I can't write this for you — it would be submitted. I can mark your draft against the criteria and log what we did." | "As an AI, I'm not able to help with that request." |
| 19 | Empty Cards | "Cards appear here from your Marks and highlights." | "No cards yet! Start studying to fill this up!" |
| 20 | Teacher override | "Override saved: 6 → 8, reason 'application credited'. Both marks kept for calibration." | "Grade updated successfully!" |

**09-COPY-003** Copy lint runs on the string catalogue (CI) and on model output before paint (§04/§08). Rules, each a regex or classifier with a fixture: (a) exclamation marks: 0 allowed; (b) emoji and pictographic symbols: 0; (c) person-praise lexicon ("great", "amazing", "brilliant", "well done", "good job", "you're a natural", "genius") outside a quoted span: block; (d) guilt/loss lexicon ("don't lose", "streak", "missed", "you failed to", "falling behind", "last chance"): block; (e) urgency ("now!", "hurry", "only today"): block; (f) therapy-speak ("take a breath", "it's okay to feel", "I hear you"): block in tutor and system copy, allowed once in the distress script; (g) "Great question", "Absolutely", "Certainly", "As an AI": block; (h) hedged marks ("might be", "roughly") in BandTotal: block — the band is the hedge; (i) unlabelled estimates: any grade or mark string must carry a basis token (series, n, or "practice estimate"); (j) vendor names in headlines: block (chip only). Thresholds: praise rate on the weekly 1% Turn audit <5%; catalogue violations = 0.

**09-COPY-004** Placeholders name the action: after a Turn the composer placeholder is the hand-back ("Try the next line", "Name the stakeholder first", "Paste your rewrite"); default placeholder "Ask, paste an answer, or /practise".

**09-COPY-005** Errors state cause and remedy in ≤2 sentences with no apology theatre: "The marker timed out. Retry with Think, or copy your answer." Never "Oops".

**09-COPY-006** Localised strings follow the same lint per language; Russian and Kazakh catalogues are reviewed by a native examiner-teacher for register (formal "вы", no diminutives).

## 09.12 Accessibility gates
WCAG 2.2 AA is a set of numbers, and every number below is a CI gate (09-PRIN-013). The table is the contract; the prose after it covers the four flows that automated tools cannot judge (streaming, Mark view, math, timers). Tooling: `axe-core` runs on every Storybook story and every route in the Playwright suite; custom checks live in `@margin/a11y-checks`; Lighthouse accessibility score ≥98 on every route; a manual audit (NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver + Safari macOS and iOS, TalkBack + Chrome) runs on the 12 flows of 09-A11Y-014 before every release and monthly in between. A failing CI row blocks merge; a failing manual row blocks release.

| ID | Criterion | Requirement | Acceptance | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 09-A11Y-001 | Target size (2.5.8) | Every pointer target ≥24×24 CSS px (`--target-min`); ≥44×44 on `pointer: coarse` (`--touch-min`); citation chips (18 px visual) carry a 24 px hit area via padding, never via a transparent overlay; inline text links are the only exemption. | Custom check walks every `button, a, [role=button], input, [tabindex]` and asserts the bounding box or the 24 px spacing circle; run on every story at 1280 and on the touch profile at 390. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-002 | Focus appearance (2.4.13, treated as AA) | Ring per 09-KEYS-002; outer 2 px band must measure ≥3:1 against **both** the element surface and the page surface in light, dark and Contrast+. Where `--border-strong` fails on a given surface, the ring outer colour for that surface is `--accent` (the token matrix decides at build time; no per-component overrides). | Contrast matrix computes ring-vs-surface for every surface token; Playwright screenshots a focused control on every surface and measures the ring width ≥2 px on all four sides. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-003 | Focus not obscured (2.4.11) | `scroll-padding-bottom` ≥ composer height + 16 px on every scroll container; sticky top bar and tab strip declare `scroll-padding-top`. | Tab through 40 controls in a Session with the composer at 8 lines; every focused element's box intersects the viewport by ≥100%. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-004 | Reflow (1.4.10) | No horizontal page scroll at 320 px CSS width and at 400% zoom on a 1280 px window; only data tables, code blocks and PDF pages scroll internally, each inside its own `overflow-x: auto` container with a visible scrollbar. | Playwright at 320×568 and at 1280 with `deviceScaleFactor` 4 / zoom 400%: `document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth ≤ clientWidth` on every route. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-005 | Contrast (1.4.3, 1.4.11) | Body and UI text ≥4.5:1; text ≥24 px or ≥19 px bold ≥3:1; UI component boundaries, icons carrying meaning, focus rings and span underlines ≥3:1 against adjacent colours; placeholder text ≥4.5:1 (it is copy, 09-COPY-004). | 09-COLR-006 matrix plus a rendered-DOM pass (axe `color-contrast`) on every story in three themes. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-006 | Use of colour (1.4.1) | No state conveyed by colour alone: mastery pips by shape (09-COLR-002); span states by underline style **and** wash **and** glyph — credited = solid underline + wash, partial = dotted, uncredited = dotted + trailing 12 px × glyph (09-ICON-002); heatmap cells carry a tooltip count; band modal mark by weight; timer overtime by the "+" prefix; offline by the banner text. | Greyscale screenshot suite: every state pair remains distinguishable (perceptual diff ≥ 5 ΔE between states after desaturation). | CI |
| 09-A11Y-007 | Text spacing and resize (1.4.12, 1.4.4) | Per 09-TYPE-007; plus 200% browser zoom and iOS Dynamic Type "AX3" without clipping, overlap or loss of function; UI text never below 14 px after scaling. | Text-spacing injection + 200% zoom on every route; iOS snapshot at AX3 for composer, Cards and Mark view. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-008 | Dragging (2.5.7) | Every drag has a single-pointer alternative: PlanBlock ⋯ › Move; sheets tap-to-close and a "Expand" button; crop handles have "Full page · Top half · Bottom half" buttons; sidebar/panel resize has Settings › Layout width fields; flashcard swipe has the two buttons. | Story audit: every component with `draggable` or pointer-move handlers has a documented alternative that a keyboard script completes. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-009 | Reduced motion (2.3.3) | Per 09-MOTN-005; `prefers-reduced-transparency` removes backdrop blur and raises scrim alpha to .70. | Playwright reduced-motion run: zero bounding-box change during any transition. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-010 | Language of parts (3.1.2) | `lang` on the root follows the UI locale; every quoted passage in another language (Kazakh syllabus wording, a Russian student answer inside an English UI) carries its own `lang`; model output segments detected in another script are wrapped by the renderer. | Unit test on the renderer with mixed-script fixtures; axe `valid-lang`. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-011 | Name, role, value (4.1.2) | Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` from the string catalogue; marking glyphs carry the full phrase (09-ICON-002); the ModeChip is `role="radiogroup"`; the ConfidenceSlider is `role="radiogroup"` with three radios (never a range input); HelpLadder rungs are a `role="listbox"` with the current rung `aria-selected`; the EffortDial is a `role="radiogroup"`. | axe + a snapshot of the accessibility tree per story compared against a committed baseline. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-012 | Status messages (4.1.3) | Non-focus-moving updates use live regions: stream status lines `role="status"`; InlineError `role="alert"`; toasts `role="status"`; the "↓ New" pill `aria-live="polite"` text "New content below"; pip state changes are **not** announced (they are visible on hover/focus with a reason). | Story-level assertion that each component renders the required role. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-013 | Timing (2.2.1, 2.2.2) | Auth idle timeout ≥30 days sliding, never mid-Turn; toasts hold 4 s but every toast action is also available for 30 s via `⌘Z` or the ⋯ menu; the Effort-Gate 90 s time-box can be extended by 90 s once per Item without conditions; timed papers: extra time 0 / 25% / 50% / custom 1–100% and rest breaks are Course settings set **before** start and inherited by every Timer (§05.9), the rest-break button pauses the clock, and a paused paper survives reload; no auto-advance on timer end — the paper locks input and shows the debrief button. | Playwright: set 25% on a 90-minute paper → timer starts at 112:30; pause 3 min, reload, resume: elapsed preserved ±1 s; `⌘Z` 20 s after an Undo toast reverts. | CI |
| 09-A11Y-014 | Keyboard (2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3) | Twelve flows complete with keyboard only, visible focus at every step, no trap, logical order: (1) Landing → First Mark; (2) Setup sheets; (3) Today → Session; (4) a Learn Turn with a ladder climb and intent chip; (5) Practise Item with confidence + submit; (6) Mark view span traversal → Rewrite → re-mark; (7) Cards review 10 cards; (8) Paper runner 3 parts with the keypad; (9) Plan: move a block; (10) Settings › Reading comfort change; (11) `⌘K` verb → route; (12) Challenge a Mark. | One Playwright script per flow using only `keyboard.press`; a screenshot per step with the focus ring visible is attached to the run. | CI + manual (SR) |
| 09-A11Y-015 | Captions and transcripts (1.2.x) | Voice input (v1) shows a live transcript before send; Read-aloud never removes the text; any audio or video content in Library carries captions or a transcript, enforced at ingestion (§06). | Ingestion rejects media without `transcript_id`. | CI |

### Screen-reader flow for streaming Turns
**09-A11Y-016** The Session transcript is one `role="log"` `aria-live="polite"` `aria-relevant="additions"` region. Each Turn is a `role="article"` with `aria-label` "Tutor, turn 7" / "You, turn 6"; the article is inserted into the log **only when its `done` part arrives** (09-STRM-012), so a screen reader hears the finished Turn once, never token by token. While streaming, the pending article lives outside the live region with `aria-busy="true"`. Status lines (800 ms, 6 s) are one `role="status"` element whose text is replaced, so each is announced once. Stop is a normal button labelled "Stop response"; on Stop the partial article enters the log with the suffix "— stopped". The composer regains focus at `done` unless focus is inside another text field (09-KEYS-002); the placeholder is exposed via `aria-description`, so the hand-back is heard. Intent chips are a `role="group"` "Reply options" of three buttons with `aria-keyshortcuts="1"/"2"/"3"`; the disabled Just-the-answer chip is `aria-disabled` with its tooltip as `aria-description` ("After one attempt."). The HelpLadder announces "Help level 2 of 5, Which principle?" and "More help" carries `aria-keyshortcuts="Shift+ArrowDown"`. Acceptance: NVDA script on a golden stream produces exactly three utterances: the status line, the finished Turn, the composer placeholder.

### Screen-reader flow for Mark view and spans
**09-A11Y-017** Reading order is header → command-word line → BandTotal with CalibrationBadge → AO cards → the answer. Before the answer a visually hidden summary reads "Your answer with 3 credited, 1 partial and 2 uncredited passages. Press Tab to move between them." Each SpanHighlight is a `<mark>` with `tabindex="0"`, `role="mark"` (fallback `aria-roledescription="marked passage"`), an accessible name "Credited, AO3 Level 2, marking point 3b-2" and `aria-describedby` pointing at the reason text; Enter on a span moves focus to its AOCard, Enter on the card's "Show in answer" moves it back. Two skip links at the top: "Jump to AO cards" · "Jump to answer". The band is read as "11 to 13 out of 20, most likely 12", never as three bare numbers. ER quotes are `<blockquote>` with `cite`. Acceptance: VoiceOver rotor lists every span under Landmarks › marks; a blind tester (manual audit) can state the band, the capped AO and the first uncredited reason within 90 s on a 20-mark fixture.

### Math read-aloud
**09-A11Y-018** KaTeX renders with `output: "htmlAndMathml"`; the HTML layer is `aria-hidden`, the MathML layer is exposed. Speech Rule Engine loads lazily (first Read-aloud, first `⌘⇧M`, or when Settings › Accessibility › "Describe maths for screen readers" is on) and generates ClearSpeak strings into `aria-label` on the `<math>` element ("x squared plus 3 x over 2"); the expression explorer (step into numerator/denominator with arrow keys) is available on focused display math. Every keypad key has an `aria-label` from the catalogue ("fraction", "square root", "raise to power"). Locale: SRE English for `en`; `ru` speech rules in v1, `kk` falls back to Russian with the fallback stated in Settings. Acceptance: the 200-formula suite (09-PRIN-017) produces a non-empty, non-LaTeX label for every formula; "dollar", "frac" and "backslash" never appear in a label.

### Split of responsibility
**09-A11Y-019** CI owns 09-A11Y-001…015 as automated rows. The manual audit owns: screen-reader comprehension of Turn, Mark view and Cards; switch-access completion of flows 1, 5, 7; a five-person reading panel (two dyslexic, two ADHD, one low-vision) per quarter rating comfort on a 1–5 scale with target ≥4 and no item ≤2; and a cognitive walkthrough of every new empty/error state. Findings are filed with a severity: **blocker** (a flow cannot be completed), **major** (completed with workaround), **minor**; a release ships with zero blockers and zero majors on flows 1–7.

Why: students with extra-time entitlements say the timer and rest breaks are the difference between a usable and an unusable mock (student-voice §"Accessibility across the year"); dyslexic users cover half the browser to cope with dense layouts (student-voice §9) — reflow and reading comfort are the same requirement viewed twice.

## 09.13 Dark-mode rules
Dark mode is a second, complete palette that remaps the semantic roles of 09-COLR-001, not a filter. Every rule here is checked by the token test and the visual-regression suite in dark and Contrast+ dark.

**09-DARK-001** Mode selection. Three states in Settings › Appearance and in `⌘K` "Toggle dark mode": `system` (default; follows `prefers-color-scheme`, switches live without reload), `light`, `dark`. The choice is stored in the reading-preference object (`theme`, 09-READ-001) and mirrored to `<html data-theme>` before first paint from a cookie/localStorage read in a blocking inline script ≤300 bytes, so no flash of the wrong theme. Contrast+ is an orthogonal boolean that applies to whichever theme is active. Acceptance: reload 20 times in dark; zero frames with `--bg-app` light captured by the Playwright video.

**09-DARK-002** Ladder and no pure black. The five dark surfaces are the ladder of 09-COLR-001 (`16% → 19% → 23% → 26% → 29%` L, chroma .006–.008, hue 260). No dark token has L <14%; `#000`, `black` and `oklch(0% …)` are forbidden outside `--scrim`. Elevation is expressed by stepping up the ladder, not by shadow strength: a floating layer sits on the surface one step above its parent (popover on `--bg-el`, sheet on `--bg-subtle`+1 relative to the page), and `--shadow-2…4` keep their geometry but alpha is halved in dark (they exist to separate, not to lift). Hairline in dark is `oklch(100% 0 0 / .08)`. Acceptance: token test asserts min L and no forbidden literals; screenshot of a stacked popover-over-sheet-over-page shows three distinct surface luminances measured ≥2% L apart.

**09-DARK-003** Text and accent remaps. Text `94%` (never 100%: pure white on dark grey halos), muted `70%` (≥4.5:1 on all five surfaces — CI matrix), accent lifted and desaturated to `72% .13 250` with `16%` text on it, `--accent-subtle` `26% .04 250`. Semantic hues drop 2–3 points of chroma in dark (success `72% .12 150`, warning `80% .13 80`, danger `70% .16 25`) — bright saturated colour on grey vibrates. Credited underline stays `--accent`; the credited wash uses `--accent-subtle` at full opacity, not a light-mode alpha over dark. Acceptance: matrix passes; no dark token has chroma >.16.

**09-DARK-004** Highlight and selection alphas. `--highlight-source` `85% .14 95 / .40` (light .35), `--highlight-select` `70% .10 250 / .35` (light .30); both are applied as a **layer above** the text with `mix-blend-mode: normal`, so highlighted text keeps ≥4.5:1 (the matrix tests text-on-highlight-on-surface as a composite). Heatmap dark ramp `24% .03 250 → 72% .13 250` (09-COLR-003).

**09-DARK-005** Images, diagrams and PDF pages. PDF pages stay paper-coloured (rendered as-is) on a `--bg-subtle` surround with a 24 px gutter and a hairline — inverting a mark scheme is a defect. Product diagrams shipped as SVG use `currentColor` and semantic tokens and re-theme automatically; raster diagrams and student photos are shown unaltered with a 1 px hairline frame; user-uploaded images never receive `filter: invert()`. An optional per-document "Dim page" toggle in the reader header applies `filter: brightness(.85)` to the page canvas only (persisted per user). Charts (Progress, calibration curve) draw from tokens and are snapshot-tested in both themes. Acceptance: reader screenshot in dark shows a light page on a dark surround; no `filter: invert` in the stylesheet.

**09-DARK-006** Code blocks and math. Code uses one syntax theme per mode from tokens (background `--bg-subtle`, hairline, text `--text`, keywords `--accent`, strings `--success`, comments `--text-muted`), never a third-party theme with its own background; inline code inherits the surrounding surface +1 step. KaTeX inherits `currentColor`; fraction rules and radicals are drawn in `--text`, never in a hardcoded black. Acceptance: grep the bundle for `#282c34`, `#1e1e1e`, `#000` and other theme literals → 0.

**09-DARK-007** Print from dark. Print (09.14) always uses the light palette regardless of screen theme: `@media print` resets `data-theme` tokens to light values; highlights print as underline styles plus wash at 15% grey; the scrim, banners, rail and composer are removed. Acceptance: print preview from a dark Session is visually identical to print preview from light (pixel diff <0.5%).

**09-DARK-008** Focus, borders and states. Focus ring in dark: inner `--bg-app` 16%, outer `--border-strong` 42% or `--accent` per 09-A11Y-002; borders `27/32/42%`; disabled = `--text-muted` at .6 opacity plus a hairline, never a darker fill (it disappears); skeleton shimmer runs from `--bg-el` to `--bg-el-hover`. Selected sidebar row `--bg-el` + `--text` (not accent fill).

**09-DARK-009** Tests. (a) Token test: every light role has a dark role; L and chroma bounds; no literals. (b) Contrast matrix in dark and Contrast+ dark (09-COLR-006). (c) Visual regression of every Storybook state in dark at 320/768/1280/1600. (d) Live-switch test: toggle system theme during a stream — no reflow, no re-render of committed Turns (09-STRM-005), the stream continues. (e) A 10-person night-use panel at 30% screen brightness rates legibility ≥4/5 on the Mark view and reader.

Why: pure black with saturated accents is the most-cited dark-mode failure (ux-design §19); students study late (student-voice §"21:40 on a school night", J3), so dark mode is a primary theme, not a bonus.

## 09.14 Print and export
Print is a first-class surface: teachers file Marks, students revise from paper, and the Learning Receipt (§12) exists to be handed over. Four print templates ship at MVP; each has a Playwright print-to-PDF test on A4 and Letter in both orientations where relevant.

**09-PRNT-001** Common print stylesheet. `@media print` and the PDF export share one stylesheet: light palette forced (09-DARK-007); body `--font-serif` at 11 pt / 1.4 unless the user's reading-comfort family is Hyperlegible or OpenDyslexic, which are honoured (09-PRIN-018); 2 cm margins; measure = full column; page numbers "3 / 7" bottom-right and the document title bottom-left in 9 pt; links printed as underlined text with the URL in 8 pt after them only in the Receipt; math via KaTeX SSR with fonts embedded; images at ≤300 dpi source, never upscaled; `orphans: 3; widows: 3`; `break-inside: avoid` on AOCards, Cards, ER quotes, tables ≤12 rows and code blocks ≤40 lines; a table >12 rows repeats its `<thead>` on each page. Colours: credited = solid underline + 15% grey wash; partial = dotted; uncredited = dotted + ×; the CalibrationBadge prints in full. Acceptance: printing a 20-mark Mark to A4 yields ≤3 pages with no AOCard split across a page.

**09-PRNT-002** What is stripped. Composer, sidebar, rail, tab strip, banners, toasts, hover cards, IntentRow, HelpLadder, MessageActions, skeletons, scrim, the "↓ New" pill, usage meter, any `aria-hidden` decoration, and the celebrate ring animation frame. Citation chips print as superscript numerals with a numbered "Sources" list at the end (title · page · trust badge · deep link text). Turn branches print the active branch only. Acceptance: DOM audit in print emulation finds no element with `data-print="strip"` rendered.

**09-PRNT-003** Templates.

| Template | Trigger | Contents and layout | Page rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mark** | Mark view › ⋯ › Print / Export PDF; teacher console bulk export | Header (Course, paper, question id, tariff, command word, date, model chip, policy version); command-word line; BandTotal + badge; the student's answer with spans **first** (full width), then AO cards in a two-column grid, ER quote, next-mark advice; footer non-affiliation line (09-PRNT-006). Teacher override state prints both marks and the reason. | Portrait; answer never split mid-paragraph from its first span; AO cards `break-inside: avoid`. |
| **Learning Receipt** | Settings › Export; Receipt screen (§10.23) | Cover block: student (display name only), assignment, Course, date range, signed hash (SHA-256, first 16 hex + QR to the verification URL); timeline table (timestamp · event · rung · Mark · seen-solution flag); appendix of drafts with diff bars (added = solid left rule, removed = struck). Public-link variant strips learner state (mastery, calibration, confidence). | Portrait; timeline `<thead>` repeats; hash also in every footer. |
| **Cards** | Deck › ⋯ › Print | 3×3 grid of 63×88 mm cards per A4 (2×4 on Letter), face on odd pages and backs mirrored on even pages for duplex; provenance line 7 pt; cloze printed with a 24 mm rule; math SSR. Option: "One column list" (face · back rows) for revision sheets. | Landscape grid; cut marks 0.2 pt at grid intersections; `break-after: page` per sheet. |
| **Timed paper** | Papers › Start timed mock › "Print instead" (OWN and LICENSED Items only; `ref_only` boards print the official deep link, never text) | Board-style front page (paper code, series label "Margin practice · not a board paper", minutes, marks, extra-time note if set); questions with tariff in the right margin `[6]`, answer lines at 8 mm pitch sized to tariff (≈2 lines per mark, capped at 40), inserts on separate pages; a mark-scheme appendix only when "Include scheme" is ticked, starting on a new page. | Portrait; a question part never starts in the last 25% of a page; answer lines never split from their question stem. |

**09-PRNT-004** PDF export fidelity. Server-side rendering (headless Chromium with the same stylesheet) so the PDF equals print preview: text is selectable and searchable, MathML is embedded as tagged structure (PDF/UA tagging for headings, lists, tables, alt text on images = the accessible name used on screen), fonts embedded and subset, file ≤2 MB for a Mark and ≤10 MB for a Receipt with images. Exports carry document metadata (title, author = student display name, subject = Course, creation date, `margin:export_version`). Anki `.apkg` export of Cards keeps LaTeX and images and writes provenance into a `source` field. ICS export of the Plan (§10.15) and Markdown/DOCX of artifacts (§10.17) follow the same strip rules. Acceptance: pixel diff between browser print preview and server PDF <1% per page on the four fixture documents; `pdfinfo` shows tagged = yes; VoiceOver reads the PDF headings.

**09-PRNT-005** Watermarks. Handwritten-answer images print with a 9 pt "Original image — kept for teacher review" caption, not a diagonal watermark. Below-gate Marks (`uncalibrated`) print "Practice estimate — not yet calibrated for this paper" as the band position and print no number; `provisional` prints the badge. A Mark exported by a student for a teacher carries no watermark; a public Receipt link prints "Public copy — learner state removed". Nothing is ever watermarked "DRAFT" or "CONFIDENTIAL" in a way that fails 3:1 with body text beneath it.

**09-PRNT-006** Non-affiliation notice. Every printed or exported page footer includes, in 8 pt: "Margin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cambridge International Education or any examination board. Marks are practice estimates, not board marks. Syllabus and mark-scheme references are to the board's published documents." The board name is substituted from the Pack; the string is in the catalogue and localised. Acceptance: string present in every fixture footer; copy lint passes on it.

**09-PRNT-007** Print from mobile. Mobile routes expose "Export PDF" (server render), not `window.print()`, since mobile print dialogs drop the stylesheet; the PDF opens in the system share sheet. Acceptance: iOS Safari export of a Mark produces the same PDF hash as desktop for the same fixture.

## 09.15 Internationalisation
Margin launches with an English UI and English, Russian and Kazakh **explanation** languages; the Russian and Kazakh **UI** ship in v2 (SYNTHESIS §13). Internationalisation is built in from the first commit, so v2 is a catalogue and a font check, not a refactor.

**09-I18N-001** Locale model. Three independent settings in one object, stored per user and overridable per Course:

```json
{ "ui_locale": "en-GB",
  "explain_lang": "en|ru|kk",
  "exam_variety": "en-GB",
  "number_locale": "en-GB|ru-RU|kk-KZ",
  "decimal_comma": false,
  "timezone": "Asia/Almaty",
  "calendar": "gregory", "first_day": "monday",
  "units": "metric" }
```

`ui_locale` drives the catalogue; `explain_lang` is passed to the tutor route as a system-prompt variable (the syllabus terms stay in the exam's language and are glossed, e.g. "маржинальная прибыль (*contribution*)"); `exam_variety` fixes spelling and vocabulary in anything the student will write in an exam; `number_locale` and `decimal_comma` drive `Intl` and the keypad. Default detection: browser `navigator.languages` for `ui_locale`, Course board for `exam_variety`, `explain_lang` asked once in setup (10.2). Acceptance: a `kk-KZ` browser user on a Cambridge Course sees an English UI at MVP with Russian/Kazakh available for explanations, `exam_variety` en-GB, decimal comma on.

**09-I18N-002** Glyph coverage. CI renders the fixture "Ә Ғ Қ Ң Ө Ұ Ү Һ І — Қазақстан, Өскемен; ёж, щука, ъ; Ў ў Ғ ғ Ҳ ҳ" plus "∑ ∫ ≤ ≥ ≠ → ⇌ ° µ ½ ¾ ‰ £ ₸ ₽" in every family of 09-TYPE-001 (Inter, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, OpenDyslexic, Literata → PT Serif, Geist Mono → JetBrains Mono) at 400/500/600 and fails on any glyph drawn by a fallback font (detected by `document.fonts` + canvas glyph-bounds comparison against the fallback face). Where a family lacks a glyph (OpenDyslexic lacks parts of extended Cyrillic; Geist Mono's Cyrillic is unverified), the family declares a per-script fallback in `@font-face unicode-range` so the fallback is chosen per glyph and looks intentional: OpenDyslexic → Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for U+0400–04FF; Geist Mono → JetBrains Mono for Cyrillic. Subsets shipped: latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, math; total font payload ≤380 KB woff2 for the default UI path. Acceptance: zero fallback glyphs in the test; the Settings specimen line renders each Kazakh letter in the chosen family or its declared fallback.

**09-I18N-003** String catalogue rules. Every user-visible string lives in `catalogue/<locale>.json` keyed by a stable id (`mark.band.aria`, `gate.chip.label`); no string literals in components (ESLint `no-literal-jsx-text` + a runtime check in dev that throws on unkeyed text). ICU MessageFormat for every plural, select and number: `"{n, plural, one {# card due} other {# cards due}}"`; Russian and Kazakh use `one/few/many/other` and CLDR handles Kazakh's `one/other`. Placeholders are named, never positional; no sentence is assembled from fragments; no string is reused across contexts with different grammar (a button "Mark" and a noun "Mark" are two keys). Each key carries `description` and `max_length` for the translator; keys over their length fail the catalogue test. Copy lint (09-COPY-003) runs per locale with a per-language lexicon; formal "вы" and no diminutives (09-COPY-006). Acceptance: catalogue test finds 0 missing keys per shipped locale, 0 unused keys, 0 plurals without all CLDR categories.

**09-I18N-004** Typography per script. Serif reading face must have true Cyrillic italics (Literata does; PT Serif as fallback) — a synthesised oblique in a Russian textbook quote is a defect. Cyrillic body runs ≈8–10% wider than English: measures are in `ch` of the active family, so 68 ch holds; the UI must survive **+35% string length** (Russian and Kazakh averages) and **+50%** in buttons without truncation or overflow — labels wrap to two lines inside `--control-h-lg`, never ellipsise. Caps labels at +0.06 em tracking are permitted in Cyrillic; small caps are not (poor Cyrillic support). Acceptance: pseudo-locale run (09-I18N-008) at +35%/+50% shows no clipped text and no horizontal overflow on any route.

**09-I18N-005** Numbers, dates, units and math input. All formatting through `Intl.NumberFormat` / `Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `number_locale`; marks and bands keep the exam's convention ("11–13 / 20" with an en dash, never a hyphen); percentages follow locale ("12,5 %" in ru-RU with a narrow no-break space); currency in Business questions stays as printed in the Item ("$", "£", "₸") — never converted; dates default to "Thu 18 Sep" (short weekday + day + short month), 24-hour clock in ru/kk, 12-hour only if the OS says so; countdowns "243 days" via plural rules. Math input accepts both `.` and `,` as decimal separators and normalises to LaTeX `.` on submit while the preview line shows the locale form; thousands separators (space in ru-RU) are stripped on parse; the keypad's decimal key shows the locale glyph. SI units per the Pack's convention (Cambridge sciences: "m s⁻¹" in print, `m/s` accepted). Acceptance: 40-case formatter fixture per locale; entering `3,5` in the keypad yields `3.5` in the Attempt and "3,5" in the preview under ru-RU.

**09-I18N-006** Exam-board spelling and vocabulary. `exam_variety` selects a spelling dictionary and glossary used by the tutor, the generator and the copy lint on model output: Cambridge/AQA/OCR/Pearson/IB(UK English) → en-GB ("organisation", "programme", "labour", "maths"); College Board/AP → en-US; a future Australian board → en-AU. The tutor never "corrects" a student's spelling toward another variety. Board term maps travel with the Pack (`Pack.glossary`: "trade payables" vs "creditors", "revenue" vs "sales turnover", "mark scheme" vs "scoring guidelines"). Acceptance: the model-output lint flags en-US spellings in a 9609 Course at ≥95% recall on a 200-word fixture; 0 corrections of student spelling in the Turn eval.

**09-I18N-007** RTL readiness. Logical properties only (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`, `text-align: start`); stylelint bans physical left/right in layout properties except inside `[dir]`-scoped math and code containers. Icons with direction (chevrons, back arrow, send, "↓ New" is vertical and exempt) are mirrored via `[dir=rtl] { transform: scaleX(-1) }` on a `data-mirror` allowlist; math, code, PDFs, timers, marks ("11–13 / 20") and citation numerals are never mirrored (`dir="ltr"` + `unicode-bidi: isolate`). Tab order follows visual order in RTL. No RTL locale ships before v2, but the smoke test runs from MVP. Acceptance: `dir="rtl"` pseudo-locale screenshot suite on every route shows mirrored chrome and un-mirrored math; 0 physical-side properties reported by stylelint.

**09-I18N-008** Pseudo-locales in CI. Three built-in pseudo-locales run on every Storybook story and route: `en-XA` (accented, +35% length, brackets to expose concatenation: "[Ḿâŕķ ţĥîš âñšŵéŕ one two]"), `en-XL` (+50%, buttons and chips only), `ar-XB` (RTL mirrored, Latin text reversed). Failures: any string not wrapped in brackets (a literal), any overflow, any clipped ring or chip, any mirrored math. Acceptance: pseudo-locale job green on every PR.

**09-I18N-009** Russian and Kazakh UI (v2 scope, prepared now). Catalogue keys, plural categories, per-script fallbacks and the +35% layout tolerance are in place at MVP; v2 adds the two catalogues, native examiner-teacher review (09-COPY-006), Kazakh SRE speech (09-A11Y-018), Kazakh `Intl` data checks (Kazakh month names, `kk-KZ` decimal comma), and the Latin-script Kazakh alphabet as a display option when the state transition is stable (founder-owned; default: Cyrillic only). Every date and number surface is already locale-driven, so the v2 change is data, not code. Acceptance (v2): the 12 keyboard flows of 09-A11Y-014 pass in `ru-RU` and `kk-KZ` with no English fallback strings visible.

## 09.16 Pixel-level QA checklist (release gate)
This checklist is the release gate: every row runs on the release candidate, every row has a pass criterion and a named tool, and the release ships only when all rows are green or a founder-signed waiver names the row and the fix date. Rows marked **CI** run on every PR as well; rows marked **manual** are executed by a reviewer on the RC build and recorded in the release note. Tools: `axe` = axe-core in Playwright; `LH` = Lighthouse; `PW-diff` = Playwright screenshot diff against committed goldens (threshold 0.1% pixels unless stated); `PW-script` = Playwright assertion; `stylelint`/`eslint` = the lint rules of §09; `lint-copy` = the copy lint of 09-COPY-003; `manual` = human on the RC.

# §10 Screen-by-screen specification

## 10.0 Conventions used in this section
§10 specifies the 25 canonical screens of SYNTHESIS §6 one by one, in the order of that list, each against the tokens and components of §09. Screens are numbered 10.1–10.25; requirement IDs are `10-<SCR>-NNN` where `<SCR>` is the four-letter screen tag in the table below. Nothing in a screen spec redefines a token or a component; it names the component from 09.7 and the state it is in.

**10-CONV-001** Per-screen template. Every screen subsection contains these blocks in this order; a missing block is a spec defect.

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | One sentence: the learning outcome the screen exists to produce. |
| **Jobs served** | Row ids from §02.2 (J1–J12) and, where relevant, the exam-year moment (02-MOM-*). |
| **Route** | Path pattern, params, and what deep-linking to it requires. |
| **Layout** | Desktop (≥1280): which of the three grid columns (`280px | 1fr | 480px`) the screen occupies and the right pane's state (rail 48 px, open 480, or absent). Tablet (900–1279): `1fr 420px` with sidebar overlay. Mobile (<900): one column; which surfaces become bottom sheets (detents 50/92%). |
| **Regions and elements** | A table of regions → exact elements (component name from 09.7, size token, copy key). |
| **Wireframe** | ASCII at desktop width; a second at mobile width when the mobile layout differs structurally. |
| **States** | `empty · loading · streaming · error · offline · gated/quota`, each with the exact copy and the primary action. A state that cannot occur is listed as "n/a: reason". |
| **Interactions and shortcuts** | Pointer, keyboard (from 09.10), touch gestures, and the drag alternatives. |
| **Data** | Reads and writes by object: Learner Graph (mastery, calibration, memory), Pack (syllabus tree, Items, schemes), Attempt/Mark, Plan, Card, Session, policy object. Writes name the field. |
| **Acceptance** | Numbered criteria a reviewer verifies; performance budgets restate §11 where the screen owns them. |

**10-CONV-002** Right-pane rail behaviour (applies to 10.5, 10.6, 10.7, 10.16, 10.17). Default state on every fresh Session is the 48 px rail: a vertical strip with the four tab icons (Source · Scratchpad · Artifact · Cards, 20 px optical) and a citation-count badge (`--text-xs` tabular) under Source. It opens to `--panel-w` on: the first citation-chip click, the first artifact card, any Mark (Mark view opens it to the cited scheme line), the Reader, `⌘J`, or a tab-icon click. It collapses on `⌘J`, the rail toggle, or `Esc` when focus is inside it and no layer is open. Opening does not change the centre measure (the centre column is fixed at 68 ch and centred in `1fr`); the transition is `--dur-drawer` on `transform` only. On tablet portrait the same content is a bottom sheet at the 50% detent; on mobile it is a full-height sheet at 92%. The open/closed state persists per Course. Acceptance: fresh Session screenshot shows exactly two panes and a 48 px rail; a chip click opens the pane within one `--dur-drawer` with the centre paragraph width unchanged.

**10-CONV-003** Routes. All routes are under one SPA shell; the browser back button walks the route stack and, on mobile, the top-bar back arrow does the same. Course-scoped routes carry the Course id so a shared link opens the right Pack version.

| Screen | Route | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Landing / First Mark | `/` | anonymous; `?q=<sample_id>` pre-fills a sample |
| Course setup | `/start` · `/start/:step` | steps `board · syllabus · papers · date · target · level · consent · import` |
| Home / Today | `/home` | default route for a signed-in user |
| Course home | `/c/:courseId` | tabs `/learn /papers /cards /plan /progress` |
| Session | `/c/:courseId/learn/:sessionId` | `?turn=<turnId>` scrolls to a Turn |
| Practise runner | `/c/:courseId/practise/:runId` | `?item=<n>` |
| Mark view | `/c/:courseId/marks/:markId` | anonymous first Mark: `/m/:markToken` (24 h) |
| Handwriting capture | `/capture/:token` | phone hand-off; token bound to a Session or run |
| Papers · Paper runner · Debrief | `/c/:courseId/papers` · `/paper/:runId` · `/paper/:runId/debrief` | |
| Cards · Wrong-question bank | `/c/:courseId/cards` · `/c/:courseId/cards/wrong` | review: `/review/:deckId` full-screen |
| Progress · Plan | `/c/:courseId/progress` (`/paper/:paperId`) · `/c/:courseId/plan` | |
| Library / Reader | `/library` · `/read/:docId?page=n&span=id` | |
| Settings | `/settings/:section` | `appearance · reading · language · memory · notifications · usage · shortcuts · data` |
| Teacher · Parent · Challenge · Receipt · Admin | `/t/:classId` · `/p/:digestId` · `/c/:courseId/marks/:markId/challenge` · `/receipt/:receiptId` · `/admin/*` | |

**10-CONV-004** Breakpoints and grid, restated from 09-SPCE-005 for use in every layout block: `mobile <900` (one column, 16 px gutters, top bar 44), `tablet 900–1279` (`1fr 420px`, sidebar overlay with 40% scrim, portrait <1024 turns the right pane into a sheet), `desktop ≥1280` (`280px 1fr 480px`, top bar 48), `wide ≥1600` (surplus to centre margins). Container queries (`@container`) drive component variants, not viewport queries, so a Mark view inside the teacher console at 900 px behaves like its tablet layout.

**10-CONV-005** Wireframe legend. Wireframes are drawn at 96 columns for desktop (≈1280 px, 1 col ≈ 13 px) and 40 columns for mobile (≈390 px).

## 10.1 Landing / First Mark
**Purpose.** Give an anonymous visitor an examiner-grade Mark on their own answer inside 90 seconds, before any account exists, so the first thing Margin does is the thing nobody else does (SYNTHESIS §3.3, §5 bet 2).

**Jobs served.** J1 (know what an examiner would give it and why); 02-MOM-001 (September start). Secondary: J4 for the "just mark it" visitor.

**Route.** `/` (anonymous). A sample chip appends `?q=<sample_id>`. Once a Mark starts streaming the URL becomes `/m/:markToken` (24-hour token, shareable read-only) without a page load.

**Layout.** Desktop: no sidebar, no rail; one centred column, composer 640 px wide with its top edge at 40% viewport height; below it the four sample chips; footer with the non-affiliation line (09-PRNT-006). When the Mark streams, the page becomes the Mark view layout (10.7) in place: answer left, Mark right, right pane open at the cited scheme line. Tablet: same, composer 560 px. Mobile: composer full width above the keyboard-safe area, chips wrap to two rows, Mark view stacks (answer on top).

**Regions and elements.**

| Region | Elements |
|---|---|
| Top bar (48) | wordmark (text, 14 px 600) · "Sign in" text button · theme toggle. No nav, no pricing link above the fold. |
| Line | `--text-h2` 24/1.25 · 500: "Paste an answer, or photograph one. We'll mark it like an examiner." (key `landing.line`) |
| Composer | Composer in `text` state, placeholder "Paste your answer here — question text first if you have it" · **+** (file: PDF/DOCX/image) · ModeChip locked to **Mark** with Learn/Practise present but `disabled` (tooltip "After your first Mark") · camera (→ 10.8 anonymous path) · **Send**. |
| Sample chips | four outline chips 32 h: "9609 12-mark evaluation" · "0580 vectors" · "9701 mechanism" · "Photograph your own". A sample chip fills the composer with a real OWN Item question and a stored exemplar answer (Tier 0, mid-band) and skips the board/subject sheet. |
| Two-field sheet | Sheet (desktop: 480 px centred panel, `--shadow-3`; mobile: 50% detent) with **Board** typeahead (MVP: Cambridge International live; AQA/OCR/Pearson/IB listed as "coming" and disabled) and **Subject** typeahead by code or name ("9609 Business"). Two fields, one primary button "Mark it". |
| Footer | non-affiliation line · Privacy · Terms · "For teachers" text link. |

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 Margin                                                                     Sign in   ☾
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════



                 Paste an answer, or photograph one. We'll mark it like an examiner.

        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Paste your answer here — question text first if you have it                  │
        │                                                                              │
        │ [+] (Learn|Practise|●Mark)                            Quick▾  [Camera] [■Send]│
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          (9609 12-mark evaluation) (0580 vectors) (9701 mechanism) (Photograph your own)



 Margin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cambridge International Education…   Privacy · Terms
```

**States.** `empty` is the default; there is no other landing content. `loading`: after "Mark it" the composer collapses upward over `--dur-base` and the Mark view skeleton (MarkHeader, three AOCard skeletons, BandTotal skeleton) appears; status line at 800 ms. `streaming`: per 09-STRM-011. `error`: InlineError in the Mark column ("The marker timed out. Retry, or copy your answer."); the pasted text is preserved in the composer. `offline`: composer stays editable; Send shows "Marks need a connection"; nothing is queued anonymously. `gated`: anonymous quota is 2 Marks per device per 24 h (cookie + IP heuristic); the third attempt shows a one-line card above the composer "Two free Marks used today. Save a Course to keep marking — it takes a minute." with **Save this Course**; Learn/Practise stay disabled anonymously. No paywall copy appears before the first Mark.

**Interactions and shortcuts.** Paste (`⌘V`) into the composer; Enter sends; a paste longer than 4,000 words shows "Paste one question's answer at a time" inline and marks the first 4,000 words. Drag-and-drop of an image or PDF onto the composer opens the capture/confirm flow. The sample chip swaps the composer content and shows a 13 px muted line "Sample answer — edit it or paste your own". After the first Mark and the first re-mark, an inline card below the delta (not a modal) reads "Save this Course to keep this Mark, your rewrite and your Cards." with Email · Apple · Google; dismissing it leaves a text link in the Mark header. On token expiry (24 h) the `/m/:markToken` route shows the Mark read-only with the same card. `?` in the empty composer opens the palette help.

**Data.** Writes an anonymous Attempt `{anon_device_id, item_id | user_question_text, response, transcript_confirmed, timestamp}` and its Mark; no Learner Graph, no memory, no Cards until Save (Cards are generated but held on the Attempt). On Save the Attempts migrate to the account and the Course setup (10.2) starts pre-filled with the board and subject. Reads the Pack for the chosen syllabus (scheme items for the sample Items; command-word table for user questions). Telemetry: `landing_view`, `paste`, `sheet_complete`, `mark_done` (with `ttfm_ms`), `remark_done`, `save_click`.

**Acceptance.**
1. Time from Send to MarkHeader ≤2 s p95 and to `done` ≤45 s p95 on the four sample Items (staging soak).
2. No account, cookie banner, email field or pricing appears before `mark_done`; the only blocking UI before the Mark is the two-field sheet (skipped for samples).
3. LCP ≤1.5 s, initial JS ≤220 KB gz, fonts ≤380 KB; Lighthouse performance ≥90 on the mid-tier Android profile.
4. `/m/:markToken` renders the full Mark with spans and band for 24 h to anyone with the link, then the expiry card; no learner state is exposed (there is none).
5. Funnel targets instrumented: paste→full Mark ≥55%, Mark→rewrite ≥70%, Mark→Save ≥35% within the session (SYNTHESIS §5 bet 2).
6. Keyboard flow 1 of 09-A11Y-014 completes; the sample chips are reachable by Tab and announce their subject.

## 10.2 Course setup sheets (onboarding as a flow)
**Purpose.** Turn the anonymous visitor's first Mark into a Course — the home object every Attempt hangs on — with the fewest fields that let the scheduler, the Examiner Twin and the Plan work on day one.

**Jobs served.** J3 (highest-value 20 minutes needs a Plan, which needs a date), J8 (an honest estimate needs papers and target), J6 (mock import), 02-MOM-001.

**Route.** `/start` → `/start/:step`, steps in order: `save · course · papers · date · level · consent · import`. Each step is a route so the back arrow and browser Back work and a refresh resumes; progress is held in the session store (server-side once `save` completes, local before). Entry points: the "Save this Course" card (10.1), a class code (`/join/:code`, which pre-fills board, syllabus, papers and exam series from the Class and skips to `level`), the app-store first launch (which runs `course → papers → date` first and then routes to a marked Item before `save`, per SYNTHESIS §3.3 last sentence), and "Add a Course" from Home.

**Layout.** Not modals: a flow of sheets. Desktop: a 480 px panel centred in the viewport on `--bg-app`, `--shadow-3`, with a 12 px caps step line ("Step 2 of 5") and a hairline progress track (2 px, `--accent`) at the top; the previous sheet slides out left and the next in from the right over `--dur-page` on `transform` (reduced motion: crossfade). Mobile: each sheet is a full-screen route with the 44 pt top bar (back · step · skip when allowed). Every sheet has ≤2 fields, one primary button 44 h, and a text-button secondary ("Back" or "Skip"). The account step is one sheet; three Course sheets are required; consent is required by policy; import is optional. Anonymous pre-account onboarding (the two-field sheet of 10.1) is the only sheet shown before the Mark — SYNTHESIS §6's "≤3 sheets" bound applies to that pre-Mark path.

**Sheets.**

| Step | Fields (≤2) | Rules and copy |
|---|---|---|
| `save` | Email · or Apple / Google buttons | Magic link; no password at MVP. Line: "Save this Course to keep this Mark, your rewrite and your Cards." Under-13 detection deferred to `consent`. |
| `course` | **Board** (pre-filled) · **Syllabus** typeahead "9609 Business (2026–28)" with the version chosen by exam series | Version is shown, never hidden: "Pack 9609 · 2026–28 · v14". Level (AS / A Level / IGCSE) is a property of the syllabus row, not a field. |
| `papers` | **Components** multi-select chips from the Pack (P1 · P2 · P3 · P4; AS-only preset) · **Exam series** segmented (June 2027 · Nov 2026 · March 2027 where the Pack has it) | Per-paper dates fill from the Pack timetable when published; else the series' last day with "date to confirm" and a Plan that re-flows when the timetable lands. |
| `date` | **Target grade** segmented (A* A B C D E; AS a–e) · **Study days** 7-day toggle row with two rest days pre-selected | Target drives nothing punitive: it sets the marks-to-next-grade line and the phase mix, and can be changed in Course memory. Rest days are shown as neutral. |
| `level` | **Current level** segmented ("Just started" · "Mid-course" · "Revising, mock done") · **Explanation language** (English · Русский · Қазақша) | Below: "Or let a 3-question probe decide" → a ProbeCard with ConfidenceSlider seeds mastery (SYNTHESIS §3.3 5:00); the self-report becomes a cohort prior only. |
| `consent` | **Age band** (Under 13 · 13–15 · 16–17 · 18+) · **Parent or guardian email** (required <16; optional 16–17) | Under-13 routes to a school-only path ("Margin for under-13s is available through a school"); 13–15 requires a verified parent email before memory and notifications turn on; teen defaults: Quiet Hours 22:00–07:00 on, notifications off, memory on but visible. One-line consequence under each option; links to the policy in 9 pt. |
| `import` (optional) | one picker: **Mock paper photos** (→ 10.8 batch, then §10.11 post-mortem) · **Anki / Quizlet deck** (.apkg, .txt, .csv) · **Notes PDF** (PMT/SME → Library, trust rank 5) · **Timetable** (ICS or photo → Plan busy blocks) · **Class code** | "Skip for now" is always visible; imports run in the background with a Toast on completion; nothing blocks the first Today. |

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │ STEP 3 OF 5 ────────────────────────────      │
                    │                                              │
                    │ Which papers are you sitting?                │
                    │ (●P1) (●P2) (●P3) (●P4)   AS only ▸          │
                    │                                              │
                    │ Exam series                                  │
                    │ (●June 2027 | Nov 2026 | March 2027)         │
                    │ P2 · Thu 27 May 2027 (timetable published)   │
                    │                                              │
                    │ Back                          [■ Continue ]  │
                    └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**States.** `empty`: each sheet's primary button is disabled until its required field is valid; no red until blur. `loading`: Pack fetch for the syllabus shows a 32 px row skeleton in the typeahead; the primary button shows a 16 px spinner ≤1 s. `error`: inline under the field ("That code isn't a class we know. Check with your teacher."), never a modal; magic-link send failure offers "Try Google instead". `offline`: the flow cannot start; a Banner explains and the pending anonymous Mark stays cached for 24 h. `gated`: a Class whose teacher locked syllabus/papers renders those sheets read-only with "Set by your teacher"; a board without a live Pack shows "Coming — we'll email you when 9700 Biology is ready" and still creates the Course in `waiting` state with Cards and Library working.

**Interactions and shortcuts.** Enter = Continue when valid; `Esc` = Back; `⌘.` = Skip where allowed; segmented controls are radiogroups with arrow keys; typeahead accepts code or name and shows the Pack version on the row; the 7-day row toggles with Space. Changing board on `course` after `papers` resets `papers` and says so in one line. The whole flow completes in ≤90 s at the median (telemetry `setup_ms`).

**Data.** Writes the Course `{board, syllabus_code, syllabus_version, level, exam_session, papers[] with dates, target_grade, study_days[], explain_lang, age_band, consent{parent_email, verified_at}, class_id?}`; the anonymous Attempt(s) re-parent to `course_id`; probe answers create Attempts with `confidence` and seed the Learner Graph; imports create Library Sources (with provenance USER), Cards (with `imported_from`), Plan busy blocks or a mock run. Reads Pack metadata (papers, series, timetable), Class (for codes), policy object (age gates).

**Acceptance.**
1. Required path is exactly five sheets (`save · course · papers · date · level`) plus `consent`; no sheet has more than two fields; a reviewer counts them in Storybook.
2. Refresh on any step resumes at that step with entered values; browser Back moves one step, never exits the flow silently.
3. A class-code entry pre-fills and locks teacher-set fields and lands on `level` in one step.
4. Under-16 without a verified parent email reaches Today with memory visible and notifications off; the state is shown in Settings › Memory.
5. Import of a 200-card `.apkg` with LaTeX and images completes in the background and produces Cards with provenance lines; the flow never waits on it.
6. Keyboard flow 2 of 09-A11Y-014 completes; every segmented control announces its options and current value.

## 10.3 Home / Today
**Purpose.** Answer "what is the highest-value thing to do right now" in one glance and start it in one tap: the scheduler's session mix rendered as three cards, with the week visible and nothing that shames.

**Jobs served.** J3 (21:40 on a school night), J12 (review what is due), J8 indirectly (the exam chip), 02-MOM-002…004 (calendar-position behaviour).

**Route.** `/home`. Default after sign-in. Multi-Course users see one Today merged across Courses by mark-yield, each card tagged with its Course; the Course switcher is in the top bar.

**Layout.** Desktop: sidebar shows Courses (not a syllabus tree — Home is above Courses) with Recent and Due groups beneath; centre column 68 ch; no right pane (no rail either — nothing here cites). Tablet: same without sidebar (overlay). Mobile: single column; the 7-day strip is horizontally scrollable with today centred; the three cards stack; the composer is absent (Home is not a chat — a conversation without a Course is an Ask and is reached from `⌘K` or the sidebar).

**Regions and elements.**

| Region | Elements |
|---|---|
| Top bar | Course switcher (text button with ▾) · usage dot (plain, opens Settings › Usage) · `⌘K` |
| Date line | `--text-ui` muted: "Thursday 18 September · 243 days to P2". No greeting, no name, no emoji, nothing above 20 px except card titles. |
| Week strip | 7 × 44 pt day cells (Mon-first per locale), today with a 2 px `--accent` ring, planned blocks as 4 px marks under the date, exam chips (`--text-xs` tabular "P2 · 27 May") on exam days when within 14 days; rest days rendered in `--text-muted` with a 12 px "rest" label, never crossed out. Tapping a day opens Plan (10.15) at that day. |
| Today cards | three TodayCards in a row (stack <900): **Continue** (the open Session or Item: "3.2 Motivation · your rewrite is waiting"), **Due** ("18 cards · about 6 minutes" · Review), **Next** (the scheduler's next block: "Practise · 9609 P2 · one 8-mark Analyse · 12 min" · Start). Each card: 14 px 500 title, one 13 px line, one action. |
| Session mix line | `--text-sm` muted under the cards: "Today's mix: 60% due retrieval · 25% interleaved practice · 15% new — Phase A, 34 weeks out" with a "Why" text link to the phase rules (§04.7/§07). |
| Weekly goal | one row: "This week: 3 of 4 sessions · 2 rest days" as four 10 px discs (filled/empty) plus two muted "rest" discs; no streak, no flame, no counter of consecutive days anywhere. Hidden in exam weeks. |
| Quiet Hours | Banner (32 px) when inside Quiet Hours: "Quiet Hours until 07:00 — Cards are here if you want them; nothing is due." Not dismissible; no notifications fire. |
| Exam-week collapse | Inside T−7 of a paper, Home collapses to one card: "Paper 2 · Thursday 09:00 · 3 days" with Continue/Due/Next stacked under it, rings hidden, no deltas, no predicted grade (SYNTHESIS §3.4). |


**States.** `empty` (new Course, nothing due, no Session): the three cards still show work — Continue: "Start with a probe on 3.2 Motivation" · Due: "No cards yet — they come from your Marks" · Next: "Practise one 4-mark Explain · 8 min"; never a greeting or an illustration. `loading`: three card skeletons with final geometry; the week strip renders from cache immediately. `error` (scheduler unavailable): cards fall back to the last computed queue with a 13 px line "Showing yesterday's plan — refreshing"; never blank. `offline`: Due card is live (local FSRS); Continue/Next show "Needs a connection" as their line with the action disabled; the Banner shows the offline string (09-COPY-002 #16). `gated/quota`: if today's levels-Mark quota is exhausted, Next never proposes a levels Mark; it proposes points Items or Cards and says why in the mix line ("levels Marks resume at 00:00"). Between-papers mode: Next is restricted to the next paper only.

**Interactions and shortcuts.** Enter/Space on a card runs its action; `1/2/3` are **not** bound here (no text field, but the numbers belong to IntentRow — avoid overload); `⌘⇧N` new Session; `⌘K`. Tapping "Why" opens a popover with the phase rule and the mark-yield list behind Next (top 3 syllabus points with `yield_s`). Long-press/⋯ on Next offers "Something else" → the next two candidates; a decline is logged, not argued. The widget (iOS/Android) mirrors Due and Next with the same strings and deep links.

**Data.** Reads: Learner Graph (due queue with counts and minutes, phase, mark-yield ranking, last open Session/Item), Plan (blocks for the strip, rest days, Quiet Hours, weekly goal), Course (exam dates, papers, between-papers flag), policy object (quotas, teen defaults). Writes: `session_started {source: continue|due|next}`, `next_declined {item_id, reason?}`, `home_view` telemetry. Nothing on Home mutates mastery.

**Acceptance.**
1. Copy corpus test on Home: zero matches for the streak/shame lexicon; no `%` in any mastery string; the mix line's percentages are the only percentages.
2. Every state shows three actionable cards; the empty state has been reviewed in Storybook for a Course with 0 Attempts.
3. TTI ≤1.5 s from cache; cards paint from the last queue before the network responds (stale-while-revalidate).
4. Quiet Hours banner appears exactly inside the configured window across DST changes (unit test with `Asia/Almaty` and `Europe/London`).
5. Exam-week collapse triggers at T−7 days 00:00 local for the nearest paper and reverts after the paper's end time.
6. A moderated test of five students: each names what to do next within 3 s and starts it in one tap.

## 10.4 Course home / Syllabus tree
**Purpose.** Orient the student in the exam's own structure — the official syllabus tree with honest mastery on every point — and make the Course's facts (Pack version, dates, memory, files, class) visible and editable in one place.

**Jobs served.** J8 (where do I stand), J5 (enter Learn at the right point), J2 (find the point behind a wrong answer), J9 (class link).

**Route.** `/c/:courseId` (the tree is the Learn tab's default state without a Session). Tabs `/learn · /papers · /cards · /plan · /progress` share the Course header.

**Layout.** Desktop: the sidebar **is** the CourseTree (280 px) and the centre column shows the Course header and the selected node's detail; right pane is a rail (opens on a citation from a node's description). Tablet: tree in the overlay sidebar, detail in centre. Mobile: the tree is the screen (route stack: Course → Unit → Point → detail), the header collapses to two rows.

**Regions and elements.**

| Region | Elements |
|---|---|
| Course header | `--text-h1` "Cambridge International A Level Business 9609" · line: "June 2027 · target A · Pack 9609/2026–28 v14 · updated 2 Sep" (Pack chip opens the changelog) · ReadinessRing per paper (64 px) with reason text ("P2 · 41% · no timed section yet") — hidden inside T−7 · "Next exam in 243 days" tabular. |
| Tabs | Learn · Papers · Cards · Plan · Progress (40 px strip, `--text-ui` 500). |
| Tree filters | chip row: All · Shaky · Due today · High yield · Unseen · per-paper (P1…P4); a 36 px filter input (`⌘K` scoped "in this Course"); sort: Syllabus order (default) · Mark-yield. |
| CourseTree | official numbering and wording from the Pack ("3.2 Motivation" → "3.2.1 Motivation theories: Taylor, Maslow, Herzberg, McClelland, Vroom"); rows 32 px, indent 16, MasteryPip 10 px at row start, mark-yield badge right (`--text-xs` tabular "▲ 4.1 marks" = expected marks recoverable), due-count badge, a small `ecf`-style "seen" tag on points with an unexpired seen-solution. Units collapsible; state persisted. |
| Node detail (centre) | title and Pack wording; pip with its reason sentence; Items summary ("14 Items · 6 questions from 4 series · 3 misconceptions"); row of actions **Learn** (primary) · Practise · Cards · Show in book¹ (citation chip → right pane at the syllabus page); the three misconceptions as one-line rows; last three Attempts with date, tariff and Mark band. |
| Course facts | collapsible groups under the header on mobile / a right-aligned card on desktop: **Memory** (editable rows: "Target A", "Prefers worked examples in maths", "Extra time 25%"; each row with edit/forget), **Files** (uploads with trust badge), **Class** (join/leave, teacher name, locked settings), **Extra time and rest breaks** (inherited by every Timer). |


**States.** `empty` (Course just created): every pip is Unseen (empty ring); the centre shows "Start with a 3-question probe on what school is teaching now" with **Start probe** and a "Pick a point" hint; rings show "—" with "No timed practice yet". `loading`: tree rows skeleton at final row height; header from cache. `error`: tree from cache with a 13 px line "Mastery may be out of date"; if the Pack fails to load, "Syllabus unavailable — retry" inline. `offline`: tree and pips from the local Learner Graph snapshot; Learn/Practise actions disabled with the reason; Cards enabled. `gated`: a Pack in `waiting` state (board not live) shows the official tree with pips disabled and the line "Marking for 9700 arrives when its Pack is live; Cards and Library work now"; a Class-locked Course shows a lock glyph on teacher-set facts.

**Interactions and shortcuts.** Click/Enter on a row selects (no animation, 09-MOTN-003); `→/←` expand/collapse; typing filters; `⌘K` "Learn <point>" jumps here then into a Session; hovering/focusing a pip shows the reason tooltip; the Pack chip opens a changelog sheet ("v14: 3.2 wording updated to the 2026 syllabus; 2 Items withdrawn"); "Show in book" opens the right pane at the syllabus page (≤400 ms p95); memory rows edit inline with Enter/Esc and "Forget" removes with an Undo toast; the decay reason names the date and the fix ("practise unaided before 20 Sep").

**Data.** Reads: Pack (tree, wording, Items per node, misconceptions, version, changelog), Learner Graph (mastery state and M_s, retrievability, decay date, mark-yield `yield_s`, seen-solution expiry, last Attempts), Course (dates, target, papers, extra time), memory rows, Library files, Class. Writes: memory edits (`memory_update`), filter/sort/collapse state (per user), `tree_node_selected`, extra-time and rest-break settings (`Course.extra_time_pct`, `Course.rest_breaks`).

**Acceptance.**
1. Pips are distinguishable in a greyscale screenshot and every pip's tooltip contains a count, a last-seen date and a decay date (or "—" with the reason).
2. Node numbering and wording match the Pack byte-for-byte; the Pack version chip matches `Course.pack_version`; a changed Pack shows the new chip within one session start.
3. No percentage appears anywhere in the tree or node detail; rings show a whole number with a reason line, hidden inside T−7.
4. Filter "High yield" sorts by `yield_s` descending and the badge value equals the scheduler's number for the same node (same query).
5. Memory rows are editable and forgettable with Undo; a forgotten row never re-appears from inference (unit test on the memory writer).
6. Tree of 220 nodes renders in ≤120 ms after data and scrolls at 60 fps (virtualised).

## 10.5 Session (Course › Learn workspace)
**Purpose.** The Session is the workspace where tutoring happens: one Course-scoped thread of Turns and Attempts in which the Effort Gate, the Help Ladder, intent chips, citation chips and the source pane are all one gesture apart, and the hand-back returns the work to the student after every Turn.

**Jobs served.** J2 (I got it wrong and don't know why), J4 (explain this so it sticks), J5 (teach me the point school is on), J11 ("just the answer" without losing the learning); 02-MOM-002 (mid-course), 02-MOM-005 (the 21:40 school night).

**Route.** `/c/:courseId/learn/:sessionId`. `?turn=<turnId>` scrolls to and focuses a Turn; `?item=<itemId>` opens a Session with that Item already posed. `⌘⇧N` mints a new `sessionId` in the same Course. A Session is a container, not a memory boundary: the Learner Graph (§07.3) is read on every Turn regardless of which Session it is in.

**Layout.** Desktop ≥1280: sidebar = CourseTree (280) with Recent and Due beneath; centre = Turn stream at 68 ch centred in `1fr` with the Composer sticky at the bottom edge (56 px rest, grows to 8 lines); right pane = 48 px rail by default, opening to 480 per 10-CONV-002. Tablet 900–1279: `1fr 420px`, sidebar as overlay, right pane a 50 % bottom sheet in portrait. Mobile <900: single column; the tree, the source pane, the math keypad and the mode menu are sheets; the composer sits above the keyboard-safe area and the HelpLadder moves from the message margin to a single "More help" button under the Turn.

**Regions and elements.**

| Region | Elements |
|---|---|
| Top bar (48) | Course switcher · Session title (auto: the first Item's syllabus point, editable) · ⋯ (Rename · Export Receipt · Delete) · usage dot · `⌘K` |
| Turn stream | alternating **UserMessage** and **Turn (assistant)**; Item cards (question text, tariff, command word, mapped point, **EffortGateChip**); **IntentRow** under the tutor Turn while a gradable Item is open; **HelpLadder** (5 rungs, 8×8) in the left message margin of the Turn that owns the Item; **CitationChip**s after the sentences they support; Mark cards rendered inline (compact 10.7 in the centre column, "Open Mark ↗" to the full view); **ThinkingRow** collapsed |
| Composer | ModeChip **Learn · Practise · Mark** (`⌘1/2/3`, remembered per Course) · `+` (file, photo, from Library) · EffortDial · camera · **Send/Stop**; placeholder = the hand-back string of the last Turn (09-COPY-004) |
| Right pane | tabs ⟨Source⟩ ⟨Scratchpad⟩ ⟨Artifact⟩ ⟨Cards⟩; Source shows the cited page with the span highlighted and `[` `]` citation arrows; Scratchpad and Artifact per 10.17 |
| Session end card | after 20 min idle or `Esc Esc`: three lines — what moved, what is scheduled, one next action; no praise, no score |

```
┌ 9609 ▾ · 3.2 Motivation ─────────────────────────────────────────────── ● ⌘K ─┐|rail|
│ TREE           │                                                              │  ⟨S⟩3
│ ◔ 3.2 Motivat. │  ┌ Item · 9609 P2 · 8 marks · Analyse · 3.2.1 ────────────┐  │  ⟨Sc⟩
│ ○ 3.3 Managem. │  │ Analyse two ways Herzberg's motivators could raise…    │  │  ⟨A⟩
│ ◕ 3.4 Comms    │  │ (Your go first)  90 s ▸                                │  │  ⟨C⟩
│ ─────────────  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│ RECENT         │                          Pay is a hygiene factor so it… ┐    │
│ DUE 18         │                                                              │
│                │ ▪ Right: you separated hygiene from motivators.              │
│ ▪              │ ▪ The chain stops at "staff are happier" — Analyse wants the  │
│ ▪              │   effect on *this* firm's output.¹                            │
│ ▫              │ ▪ Name one thing at Zara that would change. ¹ syllabus p.41   │
│ ▫              │ (Teach me) (Check my steps) (Just the answer ·disabled)       │
│ ────────── ⇧↓  │ ↓New                                                          │
│ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ Name the stakeholder first                                                │ │
```
