| `orchestrator` | Task classification, route table (§08.2), prompt registry, cache-layout enforcement, Turn lint and effort-gate vetting (§04), failover, provider adapters | Providers, `retrieval`, `sandbox`, Redis | TTFT p50 <800 ms |
| `retrieval` | Hybrid search, graph expansion, rerank, citation resolution, grounding score | Postgres (pgvector), Voyage | p95 <120 ms |
| `ingest` (workers) | Two-pass parse, typing, segmentation, scheme structuring, mapping, ER mining, embedding, provenance ledger; the curriculum compiler DAG (§06) | Object storage, Postgres, batch APIs | Pages/hour; per-page confidence |
| `marking` (workers + streaming path) | Points and Levels engines (§05), pre-solve, second-family mark, seeding/auto-pause, CalibrationRecord writes | `orchestrator`, `sandbox`, Postgres | First AO card <8 s |
| `scheduler` | FSRS-6 optimiser, Plan generation, Today queue, between-papers mode, notifications (≤1/day), Quiet Hours | Postgres, push providers | Today ready before 05:00 local |
| `sandbox` broker | SymPy/Python execution, unit checks, diagram/graph renderers; no network | E2B self-hosted or Anthropic code-execution tool | p95 verify <2 s |
| `evals` + `analytics` | Langfuse (self-hosted), eval datasets and runs, QWK dashboards, cost attribution, experiment assignment | ClickHouse (via Langfuse), Postgres read replica | Eval run <30 min on PR |
| `billing` | Stripe webhooks → entitlement service; regional PSP adapters; meter | Stripe, Postgres, Redis | Entitlement lag <5 s |

**11-ARCH-002 — Stack (FINAL unless marked).** Use the following and record any substitution in the ADR log with a benchmark.

| Layer | Choice | Why (one line) |
|---|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript end to end; Python only in `ingest`, `sandbox`, FSRS optimiser and evals | One language across web, mobile, gateway; AI coding agents produce fewer cross-language seams |
| Web | Next.js 16.3, React 19.2, RSC + route handlers, PWA | Mature streaming; Chromebook/PWA for schools |
| Mobile | Expo SDK 57, Expo Router, EAS Update; native modules only for camera maths capture if Expo camera proves insufficient | Shared domain packages; OTA fixes in exam week without store review |
| UI primitives | shadcn/Radix under a fully custom token skin (§09) — PROVISIONAL on [E15] | Accessible primitives; every pixel still ours |
| AI transport | Vercel AI SDK 7 for UI message streams and `useChat` only; provider-native SDKs (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@google/genai`, `openai`, DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible) behind our adapter interface (§08.11) | Differentiators (cache_control, citations, structured outputs, effort) are exactly what abstractions lag on |
| Primary store | Postgres 16 + pgvector 0.8.x (HNSW, `halfvec(1024)`), `tsvector` FTS, RLS; managed (Neon/Supabase/Cloud SQL) per region | One store for relational + vector + FTS + graph adjacency to tens of millions of chunks; add a dedicated vector DB only when retrieval p95 >100 ms at target QPS |
| Cache/queues | Redis 7 (quotas, stream buffers, prompt cache, rate limits); Inngest 4 or Trigger.dev 4 for durable jobs (ingest DAG, batch polling, nightly FSRS, evals) | Durable steps and retries without running Temporal |
| Object storage | S3/GCS per region: raw PDFs, page images, figure crops, handwriting originals, Receipt PDFs; SSE-KMS | Region-pinned by tenant policy |
| Observability | Langfuse 4 self-hosted (traces, prompts, datasets, LLM-judge), OpenTelemetry, Sentry; Braintrust optional for hosted experiments | Prompt versioning and eval datasets in one place |
| Auth | Better Auth 1.7 (or Clerk) with passkeys, magic link, Google/Microsoft/Apple; SAML/OIDC for schools | Must support guardian consent and SSO in one identity model |
| Payments | Stripe (Checkout, Billing, Tax) behind a `PaymentProvider` interface; Kaspi Pay (KZ), Razorpay (IN) adapters in v1 | Regional tiers need local PSPs; entitlements must not depend on any one PSP's webhook shape |
| Parsing | Docling (structural) + VLM page audit (Gemini 3.8 Flash batch → 3.1 Pro/Opus 5 on flagged pages); Mathpix for handwritten maths | Old-scan maths is the weakest parser category; two passes with confidence is the only route to scheme-grade accuracy |
| Math | KaTeX 0.18 render, MathLive 0.110 input, MathML + lazy SRE for a11y (§09) | Synchronous SSR-safe rendering; screen-reader speech |
| Embeddings | Voyage voyage-4 family int8 1024-d; rerank-2.5-lite (50→8), rerank-2.5 on marking flows | <120 ms p95 with pgvector |

**11-ARCH-003 — Topology per region.** Deploy the full data plane (Postgres, Redis, object storage, `api`, `orchestrator`, `retrieval`, `marking`) in each residency region (`eu`, `uk`, `us`; `global` maps to `us` at launch). The control plane (Pack authoring, evals, billing ledger) is single-region with no pupil PII. *Acceptance:* a tenant with `residency=eu` produces zero rows in non-EU Postgres and zero provider calls to non-EU endpoints in the audit log for a 24-hour synthetic soak.

**11-ARCH-004 — Packs are data.** No board-, syllabus- or paper-specific logic in code paths; behaviour differences come from Pack rows (`boards.level_procedure`, `command_words`, `ao_weights`). *Acceptance:* `grep -rE "9609|0450|9708|9709|0580"` in `apps/` and `services/` returns only test fixtures and sample-chip strings. Why: SYNTHESIS §3.1 — a new board is a new Pack, never new code.

**11-ARCH-005 — One stack for teachers, parents and Admin.** The teacher console, parent digest and Compiler reuse `api`, `retrieval` and `marking`; they differ by role and policy object only. *Acceptance:* no second deployable or duplicated marking code path exists.

## 11.2 Data model

The data model has three planes: **Pack** (curriculum data, global, `org_id NULL`), **Learner** (everything derived from Attempts, tenant-scoped), **Tenancy/Trust** (orgs, consent, ledger, audit). Every learner-plane row carries `org_id`, `user_id`, `policy_version`, `created_at`; every Pack row carries `pack_id`, `pack_version`, `provenance`.

**11-DATA-001 — Canonical entities and key fields.** Implement these tables (Pack tables per §06; only the fields the platform depends on are listed here).

| Entity | Key fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tenants` (orgs) | `id, type ∈ {individual, family, school, tutor_centre}, region, residency ∈ {eu, uk, us, global}, plan, policy jsonb, dpa_signed_at, sso_config_id` | `policy` is the per-tenant policy object (§08.8) |
| `users` | `id, org_ids[], role ∈ {student, parent, teacher, admin, tutor}, age_band ∈ {u13, 13_15, 16_17, 18plus}, age_assurance {method, confidence, checked_at}, consent_status, locale, timezone, quiet_hours, study_hours, deleted_at` | No `date_of_birth` after assurance; store band only |
| `guardian_links` | `parent_user_id, student_user_id, consent_evidence_id, scope jsonb {digest, predicted_grade:false, controls}, verified_at, expires_at` | The consent graph edge (11.8) |
| `courses` | `id, user_id, org_id, pack_id, pack_version, board, syllabus_code, level, exam_session, target_grade, papers jsonb, exam_dates jsonb, settings {extra_time_pct, rest_breaks, reading_comfort}` | Home object (SYNTHESIS §3.1) |
| `packs` | `id, board_id, syllabus_code, version_years, readiness ∈ {draft, ingested, mapped, gold_seeded, gated, live}, gate_report jsonb, published_at` | Pinned per Course |
| `items` | `id, pack_id, kind ∈ {definition, formula, skill, evaluation_point, diagram_rule, question_part}, syllabus_node_ids[], tariff, command_word, ao_split jsonb, provenance ∈ {OWN, LICENSED, USER}, text_status ∈ {own, licensed, ref_only}, stats {n, p_correct, discrimination, mean_latency}` | Atomic gradable/retrievable unit |
| `mark_schemes` | per §05 schema: `id, item_id, scheme_type, marking_points jsonb, levels jsonb, best_fit, ecf_policy, indicative_content[], wording_status, provenance` | Never displayed verbatim without `LICENSED` |
| `sessions` | `id, course_id, user_id, topic_node_id, mode ∈ {learn, practise, mark}, policy_version, incognito bool, started_at, ended_at` | Incognito writes no learner state |
| `turns` | `id, session_id, role, parts jsonb, rung, lint_result jsonb, model, route, cache_hit bool, usage jsonb, cost_usd, trace_id, stream_id` | Per-call field list in §08.12 |
| `attempts` | `id, user_id, course_id, item_id, session_id, syllabus_points[], response jsonb, transcript_confirmed bool, image_key, gate_state ∈ {pending, attempted, planned, dont_know}, rung_reached, intent ∈ {teach, check, answer}, confidence ∈ {sure, think_so, guessing}, latency_ms, seen_solution bool, retest_due_at, policy_version, teacher_override jsonb, mark_id, created_at` | The atomic record; every metric is a projection of this table |
| `marks` | `id, attempt_id, contract jsonb (§05 output contract), total_band {low, modal, high}, per_ao jsonb, calibration_status ∈ {gated, provisional, uncalibrated}, model_family, second_family, disagreement, policy_version, challenge_state, visible_to_student bool` | `visible_to_student=false` below gate |
| `learner_state` | `user_id, course_id, node_id, mastery_state ∈ {unseen, shaky, secure, exam_ready}, m_value, retrievability, misconception_prior jsonb, brier_7d, last_unaided_at, why text` | Materialised nightly and on Attempt write |
| `cards` | `id, user_id, source {attempt_id \| item_id}, front, back, fsrs_state jsonb, due_at, exam_cap_at` | FSRS-6 per §04 |
| `plans` | `id, course_id, week_start, blocks jsonb, phase ∈ {A, B, C, between_papers}, proposed_at, accepted_at, sleep_rule_applied bool` | Proposed, never silently applied |
| `assignments` | `id, class_id, teacher_id, item_ids[], allowed_help ∈ {none, ladder_max_rung:n, full}, due_at, locked bool, receipt_required bool` | Teacher-locked practice |
| `classes` / `class_members` | `id, org_id, teacher_id, course_id, code`; `class_id, student_id, joined_at` | Class bound to one Course |
| `calibration_records` | `id, pack_id, paper_id, question_family, tier ∈ {0, 1, 2}, script_key, human_marks jsonb[], model_marks jsonb[], qwk, level_agreement, signed_error, run_variance, fairness_buckets jsonb, series, measured_at` | Source of the calibration page and gates (§05, §13) |
| `provenance_ledger` | `doc_id, provenance, licence_id, licence_basis, source_url, sha256, ingested_at, expiry, kill_switch bool, takedown {requested_at, removed_at, requester}` | Append-only; kill switch honoured at retrieval |
| `receipts` | `id, assignment_id \| course_id, user_id, events jsonb[], hash, signature, key_id, issued_at, public_token` | §12.2 |
| `audit_log` | `id, actor_id, actor_role, action, object_type, object_id, org_id, ip_hash, ua_hash, before jsonb, after jsonb, at` | Append-only, 7-year retention for school tenants |
| `memories` | `user_id, course_id, fact, source_turn_id, sensitive bool, excluded bool, created_at` | Every fact deletable (§07) |
| `uploads` | `id, user_id, org_id, storage_key, kind, sha256, scan_status, retention_until, provenance='USER'` | Never embedded into global partitions |
| `entitlements` / `usage_meters` | `user_id, plan, quotas jsonb, grace_until`; `user_id, window, counters jsonb` | 11.10 |

**11-DATA-002 — Attempt is write-once, append-corrections.** `attempts` rows are never updated except `teacher_override`, `mark_id`, `retest_due_at`; corrections create new rows linked by `supersedes_id`. *Acceptance:* a DB trigger rejects any other `UPDATE`.

**11-DATA-003 — Row-level security.** Enable RLS on every learner-plane table with policies `org_id = current_setting('app.org_id')` and role-scoped views: students read their own rows; teachers read `attempts` (fields: item, rung_reached, mark, gate_state, timestamps — never `response` text unless the assignment is `receipt_required` or the student shared) for their class only; parents read only the materialised `parent_digest` view. Pack tables are `org_id NULL`, read-only to tenants. *Acceptance:* the RLS test suite (≥200 cases across roles) passes in CI; a teacher token cannot `SELECT response FROM attempts` for a student outside their class (query returns zero rows, not an error).

**11-DATA-004 — Vector partitioning.** `chunks` is partitioned by `partition_key = coalesce(org_id::text, 'global')`; per-tenant USER uploads live in the tenant partition; a retrieval query names its partitions explicitly. *Acceptance:* the injection/isolation suite (§12.10) shows 0 cross-tenant chunk returns over 10,000 randomised queries.

**11-DATA-005 — Versioning.** `pack_version` and `policy_version` are pinned on `courses` and `sessions`; a Pack revision creates a new version and a migration note shown in the Course ("Pack updated to 2026–28 v3 — 2 syllabus points renumbered"); it never mutates history. *Acceptance:* re-running a Mark from a year-old Attempt with its pinned versions reproduces the same contract fields except `calibration_status`.

**11-DATA-006 — Learner state is a projection.** `learner_state`, mastery pips, readiness rings, Progress and the parent digest are computed only from `attempts`, `cards` reviews and `marks`; no surface reads chat text to infer mastery. *Acceptance:* deleting all `turns` for a user leaves every Progress number unchanged.

**11-DATA-007 — Retention fields are first-class.** Every table with pupil data has `retention_until` derived from the tenant policy object; a nightly job hard-deletes expired rows and writes a count to `audit_log`. *Acceptance:* the deletion-SLA test (11.13) passes.

## 11.3 API surface

The API is REST + SSE, versioned under `/v1`, JSON everywhere, typed with a shared OpenAPI document generated from Zod schemas; the mobile and web clients consume the same generated client.

**11-API-001 — Endpoint sketch.** Implement at minimum:

| Endpoint | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns` → SSE | One Turn in Learn/Practise/Mark; server picks route, applies gate/lint | Body `{message_parts[], intent?, effort?, client_msg_id}`; headers `x-route, x-model, x-cache-read-tokens, x-policy-version, x-stream-id` |
| `GET /v1/streams/{stream_id}?from={offset}` → SSE | Resume a stream after disconnect | Buffered in Redis for 15 min |
| `POST /v1/attempts` | Create Attempt (response, confidence, gate state) | Idempotent on `client_attempt_id` |
| `POST /v1/attempts/{id}/mark` → SSE | Stream the Mark contract: `header → ao_card × n → advice → calibration → sources → provenance` | Scheme must be resolvable or returns `feedback_only=true` |
| `POST /v1/marks/{id}/challenge` | Challenge-a-mark: second family re-mark, escalation | Rate-limited 1 per Mark |
| `POST /v1/uploads` (multipart) → `{upload_id, scan_status}` | Files and photos; DLP scan; transient by default | Max 20/message; 25 MB each |
| `POST /v1/uploads/{id}/transcribe` → SSE | Handwriting → editable transcript with low-confidence tokens | Confirm step writes `transcript_confirmed` |
| `GET /v1/retrieve?q&course_id&filters` (internal + teacher console) | Chunks with scores, citations, link expansion | Never exposed to anonymous callers |
| `GET /v1/courses/{id}/today` | Scheduler queue: Continue · Due · Next | Precomputed; ETag |
| `POST /v1/cards/{id}/review` | FSRS update `{rating ∈ {again, good}, elapsed_ms}` | Idempotent on `(card_id, client_review_id)`; batchable for offline sync |
| `GET/POST /v1/courses/{id}/plan` | Read proposed Plan; accept/modify | Accept is explicit |
| `POST /v1/receipts` / `GET /v1/receipts/{id}.pdf` / `GET /r/{public_token}` | Learning Receipt issue, export, public view | §12.2 |
| `POST /v1/classes/{code}/join`, `POST /v1/assignments`, `POST /v1/marks/{id}/override` | Teacher-as-calibrator scope | Override ≤2 clicks: `{new_marks, reason_code}` |
| `GET /v1/me/export` → job → signed URL; `DELETE /v1/me` | Data portability and erasure | 11.13 SLAs |
| `GET /v1/usage` | Meter: session, day, week counters and published limits; grace state | Drives the usage banner |
| `POST /v1/admin/ingest` → `{run_id}`; `GET /v1/admin/ingest/{run_id}` | Compiler DAG; `parse_report` per document | Admin role only |
| `POST /v1/webhooks/stripe`, `/kaspi`, `/razorpay` | Entitlement updates | Signature-verified; idempotent on event id |
| `GET /calibration/{syllabus}/{paper}` (public) | Published calibration page JSON | [founder default: published externally] |

**11-API-002 — Idempotency.** Every mutating endpoint accepts `Idempotency-Key` (UUID, 24 h window, keyed by user); replays return the original response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Turn creation additionally dedupes on `client_msg_id` per session so a retried Send never creates two Turns or double-bills a Mark. *Acceptance:* a chaos test that retries every mutating call 3× under injected 502s produces exactly one row per logical action and one quota decrement.

**11-API-003 — Streaming parts.** SSE events are typed message parts: `text, thinking_summary, status, citation, math, diagram, tool_call, tool_result, mark_header, ao_card, command_word_check, advice, calibration, sources, provenance, card_suggestion, gate_prompt, intent_row, error, done`. Each carries `seq`, `part_id`, and for text `delta`. Clients render by part type; unknown types are ignored, never fatal. *Acceptance:* schema-validated in CI against the shared Zod definitions; a client built against v1 renders a v1.1 stream with new part types without error.

**11-API-004 — Errors are cards, not modals.** Errors return RFC 9457 problem details with a `user_message` suitable to render inline and an `retryable` flag. Never expose provider error text to the client. *Acceptance:* error snapshot test covers 429, 503, quota, policy-blocked, scheme-missing.

**11-API-005 — Rate limits by route class.** Enforce in `api` before any provider call: anonymous landing Mark 3/day/IP-hash and 1 concurrent; authenticated Turn 60/min burst 10; Mark per plan quota (11.10); upload 30/hour; export 2/day. Return `Retry-After`. *Acceptance:* k6 suite confirms limits and that a limited Turn returns a soft slow-down message, never a hard mid-session stop (SYNTHESIS §12 free-tier rules).

**11-API-006 — Policy object on every request.** `api` resolves `{residency, allowed_providers, retention_days, age_band, consent_mode, training_opt_in=false, school_safe}` from tenant + user and attaches it to the internal request context; `orchestrator`, `retrieval` and storage refuse a request without one. Where a user belongs to two tenants (family + school) the stricter value per field wins. *Acceptance:* unit tests for the merge; a request without policy fails closed with a logged 500, not a permissive default.

## 11.4 Retrieval (RAG) pipeline

Retrieval exists to put the right syllabus line, scheme point, examiner sentence or textbook paragraph in front of the model and the student, with a page-and-span address. Ingestion mechanics and the compiler stages are §06; this subsection fixes the retrieval-side contract.

**11-RAG-001 — Chunk by structure, never by fixed window alone.** Segment by document type before chunking: textbook `chapter → section → subsection → paragraph | figure | table | worked_example`; question paper `paper → section → question → part → marks`; mark scheme `question part → marking point | level band → guidance`; examiner report `question → commentary sentence group`; syllabus `unit → topic → learning objective`. Then apply HybridChunker at 256–512 tokens aligned to the embedding tokenizer, keeping tables, marking points and level grids whole and carrying `heading_path`. *Acceptance:* 0 chunks split a marking point, table row or level descriptor (structural lint on ingest).

**11-RAG-002 — Required metadata per chunk.** `doc_id, doc_type, board, syllabus_code, syllabus_version_years[], subject, level, paper, variant, series, question_id, marks, command_word, ao[], topic_path[], page_start, page_end, bbox[], figure_ids[], language, trust_rank, provenance, licence_id, source_hash, ingest_version, parse_confidence, partition_key`. Ingest rejects a chunk missing any non-nullable field. Why: a 2021 scheme line can be wrong for the 2026–28 syllabus; filters must run before similarity.

**11-RAG-003 — Query pipeline.** (1) Query understanding on the cheap route (§08.2): `{intent, syllabus_code, topic_guess, question_ref?, language}` as structured output; (2) SQL prefilter on `syllabus_code`, `syllabus_version`, `partition_key ∈ {global, tenant}`, `kill_switch=false`, `expiry > now()`; (3) hybrid: pgvector HNSW cosine on `halfvec(1024)` top-50 ∪ FTS `ts_rank_cd` top-50 → Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), `hnsw.iterative_scan=relaxed_order` when filters are selective; (4) graph expansion via `links`: question → its scheme items and ER commentary; textbook hit → its syllabus objective + ≤2 linked questions; (5) rerank 50→8 (`rerank-2.5-lite`; `rerank-2.5` for Mark flows); (6) tie-break by `trust_rank`; (7) assemble as provider-native content documents with stable `[chunk_id]` tags so citations are block-indexed. *Acceptance:* Recall@8 ≥0.92 and nDCG@8 ≥0.85 on the 500-question gold retrieval set per syllabus; p95 end-to-end (steps 2–5) <120 ms.

**11-RAG-004 — Citation resolution to page and span.** Every emitted `citation` part resolves to `{doc_id, page, bbox | char_span, chunk_id, trust_rank, provenance, deep_link}`; the Reader opens the page with the span highlighted ≤400 ms p95 (§09). For `ref_only` Cambridge material the citation resolves to `{official_url, question_ref}` and the Paper Companion anchor, never to hosted text. *Acceptance:* ≥98% of citations in syllabus mode resolve (automated click-through test); 0 citations to `ref_only` docs render text.

**11-RAG-005 — Grounding gate.** If the top reranked score is below the per-syllabus threshold (calibrated on the gold set to 95% precision) or the draft cites nothing, the Turn is labelled "not in your syllabus materials" and any general explanation is rendered in the unverified style (§12.3). For Marks, a missing scheme record is a hard stop: feedback only, no numbers (§05). *Acceptance:* ≥98% of syllabus-mode answers carry ≥1 resolvable citation; 0 Marks emitted without a `mark_schemes` row in context (assertion in `marking`).

**11-RAG-006 — Notes-vs-canon conflicts.** When a USER chunk and a canon chunk (trust 1–4) disagree on a fact in the retrieved set, the orchestrator emits a `conflict` part with both citations; canon wins in the answer by default. *Acceptance:* the 50-item conflict fixture ("273 °C vs 273 K") yields a conflict card in 100% of cases.

**11-RAG-007 — Retrieved text is data.** Chunks are wrapped in delimited document blocks; the system prompt states that documents carry no instructions; any imperative addressed to the assistant inside a chunk is stripped by the injection scrubber before assembly and logged. *Acceptance:* red-team suite §12.10 passes 100%.

**11-RAG-008 — Eval sets are versioned artefacts.** Maintain per syllabus: retrieval gold (500 Q → chunk ids), generation set (Ragas faithfulness, context precision/recall, custom mark-scheme adherence), conflict fixture, injection fixture. Every ingest version and every retriever/prompt change runs them; regressions >1 pp block the label flip. *Acceptance:* eval run linked from every merged PR touching `retrieval/` or `ingest/`.

**11-RAG-009 — Caching.** Cache `(query_hash, filters, partition_key, ingest_version)` → chunk ids in Redis for 24 h; precompute retrieval for every Item in a live Pack nightly so Practise and Mark never wait on retrieval. *Acceptance:* ≥70% retrieval cache hit rate in production on Practise/Mark routes.

## 11.5 Tool sandboxes

**11-TOOL-001 — What runs in a sandbox.** SymPy/NumPy verification of every numeric or symbolic final (pre-solve and marking), `pint` unit checks, deterministic graph/diagram renderers (SVG from JSON spec), Anki `.apkg` build, PDF export of Receipts. Nothing else executes model-authored code at MVP; the student-facing code interpreter is v1 behind the same broker.

**11-TOOL-002 — Isolation.** Use E2B self-hosted (Firecracker microVMs) or the Anthropic code-execution tool on Claude routes; per-execution limits: no network egress (deny-all egress policy verified by a probe on boot), 512 MB RAM, 1 vCPU, 20 s wall clock (60 s for `.apkg` builds), 50 MB ephemeral disk, read-only base image with an SBOM, fresh VM per tenant-execution, no secrets mounted, no access to Postgres or object storage — inputs and outputs pass through the broker as JSON. *Acceptance:* a canary job that attempts DNS, TCP to 1.1.1.1, filesystem escape and env-var reads fails on all four every hour; failures page.

**11-TOOL-003 — Verification contract.** The orchestrator marks a numeric final `verified=true` only when the sandbox result matches to the tolerance in the Item (`abs_tol`, `rel_tol`, `sig_figs`); a mismatch renders both values with "check this" and never a confident single answer. *Acceptance:* 0 unverified numeric finals on STEM routes (assertion in the Turn lint).

**11-TOOL-004 — Client-side Pyodide.** Load Pyodide lazily (never in the chat route's initial bundle) for instant answer checking in Practise and offline Card maths; results are advisory and re-verified server-side before they touch an Attempt. *Acceptance:* Pyodide absent from the initial JS payload (bundle analysis in CI).

**11-TOOL-005 — Per-route tool allow-lists.** Each route in the route table declares its tools; a tutoring Turn may call `retrieve`, `verify_math`, `render_diagram`, `suggest_card`; it cannot call `delete_card`, `update_plan`, `send_notification`, `issue_receipt`. Tool calls outside the allow-list are dropped and logged as security events. *Acceptance:* unit test per route; injection suite confirms no privilege escalation via document content.

## 11.6 Realtime streaming

**11-RT-001 — Transport.** SSE over HTTP/2 from `api` (which proxies `orchestrator`); WebSocket only for the v1 voice pilot broker. Each assistant Turn has a `stream_id`; `orchestrator` writes parts to a Redis stream every ≤250 ms or every part boundary; `api` fans out. Buffers live 15 minutes after `done`.

**11-RT-002 — Resumability.** A client reconnecting with `from=offset` receives every part it missed, in order, exactly once; a Turn whose stream died server-side is finished by a worker, not restarted. *Acceptance:* the network-flap test (kill the connection at 10 random offsets per Turn, 200 Turns) loses zero parts and duplicates none.

**11-RT-003 — Streaming contract to the UI.** Optimistic user message <50 ms; `status` part at 800 ms if no text yet ("Reading the 9609 P2 mark scheme…"); "Taking longer than usual" + Stop at 6 s; Stop aborts the provider call within 300 ms and bills only consumed tokens; paint ≤90 characters per 16 ms frame; previous DOM immutable; unclosed math/code held as a skeleton until the part closes; CLS above the cursor = 0. *Acceptance:* Playwright trace on golden conversations measures each budget; CLS assertion in CI (11.16).

**11-RT-004 — Mark streaming order.** `mark_header` first, then `ao_card` parts in AO order, each within 8 s of the previous, `command_word_check`, `advice`, `calibration`, `sources`, `provenance`, `done`; the credited spans in a card are emitted with the card so highlights light up as it lands. *Acceptance:* synthetic 20-mark Mark shows first `ao_card` <8 s p95 and `done` <45 s p95 in the staging soak.

**11-RT-005 — Backpressure and failover.** Quotas and policy checks run before the provider call; provider 429/503/529 or TTFT >4 s triggers the failover path from the route table with `x-failover=1` in telemetry; the client sees the same stream id. *Acceptance:* chaos test with a blackholed primary provider completes ≥99% of Turns via fallback with no client-visible error.

## 11.7 Offline, PWA and sync

**11-OFF-001 — What works offline.** Cards review (due queue, two-button grading, interval hints), the Today list as last fetched, downloaded Course notes and syllabus tree with pips, the Reader for OWN/LICENSED-offline-permitted documents already opened, Receipt viewing, the Plan. Nothing that needs a model call pretends to work: Learn, Practise marking and Mark show the offline banner and queue nothing except Card reviews and draft text. *Acceptance:* airplane-mode E2E test on web (service worker + IndexedDB) and Expo (SQLite) completes 20 Card reviews and shows a correct due count after reconnect.

**11-OFF-002 — Sync model.** Client-generated UUIDs; an outbox of `card_review`, `draft_response`, `plan_accept` events with monotonic `client_seq`; server applies idempotently (11-API-002) and returns the authoritative FSRS state; conflicts resolve by "server FSRS state wins, client reviews are replayed in order". *Acceptance:* two devices reviewing the same deck offline then syncing produce a deterministic state equal to the ordered replay.

**11-OFF-003 — Offline storage limits and privacy.** Cache ≤200 MB per Course on mobile; encrypted at rest with the OS keystore; cleared on logout and on tenant policy `retention_days` expiry; no transcripts cached for under-18 school tenants beyond the current Session. *Acceptance:* logout leaves no readable Course data in app storage (forensic check in the release checklist).

**11-OFF-004 — PWA.** Installable on Chromebook/desktop; app shell cached; background sync for the outbox; offline banner is a system state (§10 screen 24), never a modal.

## 11.8 Multi-tenancy and the consent graph

**11-TEN-001 — Tenant types and membership.** `individual` (one consumer), `family` (parent-owned, ≤3 students on the Family plan), `school` (admin, teachers, classes, students), `tutor_centre` (school-like, 1:20–50 seats). A user may belong to several tenants; the stricter policy object per field applies (11-API-006).

**11-TEN-002 — Visibility matrix (FINAL).**

| Data | Student | Teacher (own class) | Parent (linked) | School admin | Margin staff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Turn transcripts | Own, full | Never (aggregate hint depth only) | Never | Never | Only with a logged support ticket the student opened, or a safety escalation |
| Attempts (item, rung, gate, mark, timestamps) | Own | Yes | Aggregates only | Aggregates | Evals in pseudonymised form |
| Answer text on Attempts | Own | Only for assignments marked `receipt_required` or student-shared | Never | Never | Calibration with consent |
| Marks and overrides | Own (when visible) | Yes, plus override | Trend only | Aggregates | Yes (pseudonymised) |
| Predicted grade | Own (Progress › Paper) | Gated papers only | Only if student enables | No | No |
| Memories | Own, editable | Never | Never | Never | Never |
| Receipt | Own; shares by link | When shared | When shared | No | No |

*Acceptance:* the RLS suite encodes this matrix cell by cell.

**11-TEN-003 — Consent graph for under-18s.** Model consent as edges, not flags: `guardian_links` (parent → student, with `consent_evidence`), `school_consents` (school → student cohort, with the DPA and the FERPA/COPPA school-official basis), each with `scope` (what processing it authorises: `study_data`, `digest`, `predicted_grade_share`, `voice`, `research_pseudonymised`) and `expires_at`. A processing action checks the union of valid edges for the required scope; missing scope fails closed. Age band `16_17` and `18plus` consumers self-consent under GDPR where the member-state age allows; `13_15` requires a school edge at launch [founder default: 16+ consumer at launch; 13+ consumer opens after the external consent audit, target month 9]; `u13` is never onboarded. *Acceptance:* consent coverage report shows 100% of `13_15` and `16_17` (where required by member state) accounts with a valid edge; an account whose last edge expires is frozen (read-only, export available) within 24 h.

**11-TEN-004 — Parent controls change nothing the student owns.** Parents set Study Hours, Quiet Hours, digest cadence and payment; they cannot read transcripts, edit memories, or unlock predicted grades. Controls may be adjusted by asking the assistant in the parent surface with an explicit Allow/Deny confirmation. Auto-removal of guardian scope on the student's 18th birthday (age band change), with notice to both.

## 11.9 Authentication, age assurance and school SSO

**11-AUTH-001 — Methods.** Passkeys first; magic link; Google, Microsoft, Apple sign-in; class code + school SSO. No passwords stored for new accounts; sessions are httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 30-day sliding with device list and remote revoke in Settings.

**11-AUTH-002 — Age assurance path.** At "Save this Course": (1) self-declared age band (never full DOB retained after assurance); (2) signal checks: school-tenant membership, SSO directory attribute, payment-holder age for family plans, and an age-estimation classifier on usage signals in the style of the labs' age prediction (PROVISIONAL: vendor or in-house, decided by the DPIA); (3) for `13_15` and `16_17` where consent is required, the guardian or school edge (11-TEN-003). Uncertain bands default to the more protective band. Store `{method, confidence, checked_at}` only. *Acceptance:* a declared 19-year-old exhibiting strong under-16 signals is moved to teen defaults and asked to verify; DPIA documents the false-positive/negative trade-off.

**11-AUTH-003 — School SSO in v1.** SAML 2.0 and OIDC (Google Workspace for Education, Microsoft Entra), roster via Wonde and Clever/ClassLink connectors; MVP ships class codes only. Just-in-time provisioning maps directory roles to `teacher`/`student`; an SSO-provisioned under-16 inherits the school consent edge. *Acceptance:* a pilot school onboards in <1 day with no manual account creation.

**11-AUTH-004 — Anonymous first Mark.** The landing Mark runs under a device-bound anonymous principal (signed cookie, 24 h) with the strictest policy object (`residency` by geo-IP, `age_band=unknown` → teen defaults, no memory writes, transient upload). Converting to an account migrates the Mark and Attempt.

## 11.10 Billing, quotas and the meter

**11-BILL-001 — SKUs (PROVISIONAL on [E9]; numbers are [founder default]).** Student Monthly $8; Student "Until exams" $59 (entitlement `expires_at = last_paper_date + 7 days`, max 10 months, computed from the Course's exam dates); Parent/Family $19/month (≤3 students); School seat $10/student/year (invoice, not card); Tutor per seat; regional tiers −40% (KZ, IN, PK, NG, EG, TR) by billing country with Stripe Tax and local PSPs. Teacher role is free forever and needs no card.

**11-BILL-002 — Entitlement service.** Entitlements are derived server-side from `subscriptions` + `grants` (school seats, trials, grace) and cached in Redis; PSP webhooks only update `subscriptions`. Feature checks call `entitled(user, capability)`; the client never decides. *Acceptance:* revoking a subscription propagates to the meter in <5 s; a replayed webhook is a no-op.

**11-BILL-003 — Quotas and meter (FINAL free-tier rules from SYNTHESIS §12).** Counters per user per `session / day / week / month`: `levels_marks` (free 3/day; 6/day in exam-week grace from T−14 to the last paper; paid 40 Opus-class per month then soft slow-down to Sonnet-draft marking with a factual line), `points_marks` (uncapped, slow-down), `cheap_turns` (uncapped, slow-down), `uploads` (≥20/day free), `voice_minutes` (v1). Limits are published as plain numbers on `/v1/usage` and the Settings meter; grace and slow-down states are explicit fields. Slow-down means longer queue and cheaper route, never a hard stop mid-Session. *Acceptance:* zero silent limit changes — any change to a published limit requires a versioned `limits.json` change with a changelog entry visible in-app.

**11-BILL-004 — Until-exams SKU mechanics.** Purchase requires ≥1 Course with an exam date; expiry recomputes if the student edits dates (max 10 months from purchase); renewal offers the next series only after results day.

## 11.11 Observability, tracing and evals infrastructure

**11-OBS-001 — Traces.** Every request carries a W3C `traceparent`; every model call is a Langfuse span with the per-call fields defined in §08.12 (`policy_version, route, model, effort, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, ttft_ms, total_ms, cost_usd, failover, rung, lint_result, gate_state, intent, calibration_status`) plus platform fields `tenant_id, residency, age_band, experiment_arms[], stream_id, ingest_version`. Prompts are referenced by `(name, version)` and never copied into logs. PII: user ids are pseudonymous; message text is stored in traces only for tenants whose policy allows (`trace_content ∈ {none, redacted, full}`; school tenants default `redacted`).

**11-OBS-002 — Cost attribution.** Attribute `cost_usd` per Turn/Mark to `user, tenant, route, model, feature, experiment`; nightly roll-ups produce cost per weekly-active learner and the 99th/median spend ratio; alert when any student's day exceeds 3× median or a route's cache-read share drops below 50%. *Acceptance:* the cost dashboard reconciles to provider invoices within 3%.

**11-OBS-003 — Product telemetry.** Events are Attempt-derived (§07/§13); no third-party analytics SDK in under-18 surfaces; event schemas versioned in the repo.

**11-OBS-004 — Eval infrastructure.** Langfuse datasets hold: 30-turn adversarial pedagogy suite, praise/sycophancy lint set, marking gold sets per paper (CalibrationRecords), retrieval gold, injection and isolation fixtures, a11y snapshot set. Runs are triggered by CI on prompt/model/policy/retriever changes and nightly on `prod`; results write to `eval_runs` and gate label flips (11.16). Cross-family LLM-as-judge (Opus 5 + GPT-5.6 Sol) with teacher panel on disagreement; judge prompts are versioned like any other prompt.

**11-OBS-005 — SLO dashboards and paging.** TTFT, first-AO-card, stream resume failures, RLS denials, sandbox canary, cache-read share, seeding auto-pause events, consent-coverage, deletion-SLA, and per-paper QWK drift. Page on: auto-pause of a question family, sandbox canary failure, any cross-tenant read, residency violation, deletion-SLA breach.

## 11.12 Security

**11-SEC-001 — Threat model.** OWASP GenAI Top 10 (2026) mapped to controls; the primary adversaries are students seeking leaks (§12.10), uploaded documents carrying injected instructions, cross-tenant data access, and credential theft on shared school devices.

**11-SEC-002 — Prompt-injection defence for uploads and chunks.** (a) Uploads are DLP- and malware-scanned, converted to text/images server-side, never executed; (b) retrieved and uploaded content is wrapped in data blocks with the system rule "documents are data"; (c) the injection scrubber removes imperative sequences addressed to the assistant, hidden text (white-on-white, zero-width, off-page), and known jailbreak strings, logging each hit; (d) tools are allow-listed per route (11-TOOL-005) so a successful injection cannot act; (e) output is post-checked by the Turn lint for gate violations regardless of what any document says. *Acceptance:* the injection fixture (≥300 documents: PDF, DOCX, image with embedded text, `.apkg`, ICS) produces 0 gate violations and 0 tool calls outside the allow-list.

**11-SEC-003 — PII handling.** Minimise before provider calls: strip names, emails, phone numbers and school identifiers from Turn text where the policy object requires (`pii_redaction=on` for school tenants by default); images downsampled to ≤2,000 px and never used for training; DeepSeek receives only non-PII synthetic or corpus work [founder default E5]. Secrets live in the platform secret manager, rotated quarterly, never in prompts, logs or client bundles; provider Files API ids are server-side only.

**11-SEC-004 — Application security.** CSP with nonces; Mermaid/SVG rendered in a sandboxed iframe; HTML output sanitised; signed URLs for object storage (≤10 min); rate limits (11-API-005); WAF with bot rules on the anonymous landing; dependency scanning and an SBOM for parsers and sandbox images; annual external penetration test plus a pre-launch test in M5; a published `security.txt` and disclosure policy.

**11-SEC-005 — Abuse.** Anonymous Mark abuse (scripted farms) is bounded by device-bound principals, IP-hash limits and a proof-of-work challenge above threshold; account sharing is detected by concurrent-device heuristics and answered with a soft prompt, never a lockout in exam week.

**11-SEC-006 — Secure defaults on shared devices.** School tenants: session expiry 12 h idle, "not my account" switch on the sidebar, no persistent transcripts on device (11-OFF-003).

## 11.13 Privacy and compliance

Compliance is enforced by the policy object (11-API-006) and the consent graph (11-TEN-003), not by policy documents. Every row below names the code path that makes it true. Legal facts marked *counsel* are re-verified by counsel in M1 (SYNTHESIS §9); the build does not wait for that verification because every control works under the adverse reading.

**11-PRIV-001 — Regime table.** Implement the controls column; the owner column names who signs the evidence at each release.

| Regime | Applies to | What Margin does (code path) | Evidence artefact | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDPR (EU) / UK GDPR | All EU/UK users; Margin is **controller** for consumers, **processor** for school tenants | Lawful basis per tenant type stored on `tenants.policy.lawful_basis ∈ {consent, contract, school_public_task}`; DPIA before launch and re-run on any new processing purpose; data-subject tooling `GET /v1/me/export`, `DELETE /v1/me` (11-API-001); 72-hour breach clock (11-PRIV-009) | DPIA v1 signed before M5 beta; RoPA (11-PRIV-008) | DPO (contracted at MVP) |
| Children's consent age (GDPR Art. 8, member-state derogations) | `13_15` and `16_17` consumers | `consent_age_by_country.json` in config: 13 (UK, IE, BE, DK, EE, FI, LV, MT, PT, SE, NO), 14 (AT, BG, CY, IT, LT, ES), 15 (CZ, FR, GR, SI), 16 (DE, NL, HU, HR, LU, PL, RO, SK), default 16 when unlisted; `age_band` + billing/geo country → `self_consent_ok bool`; below the line a guardian or school edge is required (11-TEN-003). At launch consumers are 16+ [founder default E4], so the table gates only school tenants until month 9 | Consent-coverage report (11-TEN-003) | DPO |
| UK ICO Age Appropriate Design Code (AADC) | Any UK user likely to be under 18 | Defaults for `age_band ≠ 18plus`: `trace_content=none`, geolocation off, memory scoped to Course only, no third-party SDKs (11-OBS-003), no nudges toward more usage (no streaks, ≤1 notification/day), high-privacy by default with no "turn everything on" toggle; parental controls transparent to the child (a banner "Your parent set Quiet Hours 22:00–07:00") | AADC 15-standard mapping doc; DPIA §children | DPO + Head of Product |
| COPPA (US) | Under-13 — **never onboarded** (`u13` band refused at 11-AUTH-002); 13–17 in US school tenants | For school tenants the **school-consent exception** is the basis: the school's DPA authorises collection for educational use only; `school_consents.scope` excludes `marketing`, `research_pseudonymised` unless the school opts in separately; written retention policy attached to the DPA; separate consent for any third-party disclosure beyond sub-processors | DPA §COPPA; sub-processor list | DPO + Sales lead |
| FERPA (US schools) | US school tenants | Margin acts as a **school official** under the school's direct control: `tenants.policy.ferpa_school_official=true` restricts all use of education records to the tenant's purposes; no re-use for product research without de-identification; parent access served through the school (Margin exports on the school's request) | DPA §FERPA; audit_log export | DPO |
| US state student-privacy (SOPIPA, SOPPA, NDPA) | US school tenants | Sign the SDPC NDPA on request; no targeted advertising ever (there is no ad surface); no student profile for non-educational purposes | Signed NDPA per district | Sales lead |
| EU AI Act Annex III (high-risk: evaluating learning outcomes / steering learning) — *counsel* | School deployments in the EU; build as if in scope for all marking and Plan features | Technical file (11-PRIV-005) complete **before 2 Dec 2027** (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 deferral); human oversight = teacher confirmation before any Mark enters a school-recorded grade (SYNTHESIS §8.11); logging = `audit_log` + Langfuse traces retained per 11-PRIV-006; accuracy = the per-paper calibration page (§05, §13.3) | Technical file repo `compliance/annex-iii/` | CTO (owner), DPO (co-signer) |
| EU AI Act Article 50 (transparency, applies since 2 Aug 2026) | Every user | Persistent disclosure (12.9): "Margin is an AI. Marks are practice estimates." in the sidebar footer, the first Turn of every Session, every Mark's provenance chip and every export; generated Items and model paragraphs carry `ai_generated=true` and a visible "AI-written" tag | Screenshot set in the release checklist (§09.16) | Head of Product |
| UK Online Safety Act / DfE product-safety expectations | UK under-18 users | Content filters and escalation (12.4, 12.8); safeguarding contact per school tenant; age assurance (11-AUTH-002) | Safety case doc | Trust & Safety lead |
| Provider data-use terms | All | `training_opt_in=false` is a constant, not a setting; provider adapters assert the zero-retention / no-training flag per call where the API offers one; Fable 5.1 excluded for tenants with `zdr_required=true` (30-day provider retention); DeepSeek only for `pii=false` synthetic work and never for `residency ∈ {eu, uk}` [founder default E5] | Adapter unit tests; audit_log `provider` column | CTO |

**11-PRIV-002 — Residency via regional endpoints.** `residency ∈ {eu, uk, us, global}` on the tenant selects the data plane (11-ARCH-003) and the provider endpoint map in config:

```yaml
endpoints:
  eu:   { anthropic: vertex/europe-west4, google: vertex/europe-west4, openai: eu.api.openai.com, deepseek: null }
  uk:   { anthropic: vertex/europe-west2, google: vertex/europe-west2, openai: eu.api.openai.com, deepseek: null }
  us:   { anthropic: first-party, google: first-party, openai: api.openai.com, deepseek: batch-only-non-pii }
  global: alias us
cost_uplift: { vertex_regional: 0.10 }
```

A `null` endpoint means the route falls to the next fallback in the route table (§08.2), never to a non-regional host. *Acceptance:* the 24-hour synthetic soak in 11-ARCH-003 plus a nightly query `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE residency IN ('eu','uk') AND provider_region NOT LIKE 'europe-%'` returning 0; a non-zero result pages (11-OBS-005).

**11-PRIV-003 — Data minimisation before providers.** Apply 11-SEC-003 redaction when `pii_redaction=on`; never send `users.email`, `guardian_links`, or `age_assurance` fields to any provider; images ≤2,000 px; the Turn payload contains the pseudonymous `user_id` hash only in metadata fields the provider does not train on. *Acceptance:* a provider-payload lint in CI fails on any field name from the `pii_fields` list.

**11-PRIV-004 — Retention and deletion SLAs per entity.** Defaults below; the tenant policy object may shorten any value, never lengthen it beyond the ceiling. Detailed defaults for learner-visible controls are in §07.8; this table is the platform ceiling.

| Entity | Default retention | Ceiling (school tenant) | Deletion trigger → hard-delete SLA | Backups purged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `turns` (chat text) | 12 months rolling; incognito 0 | 90 days | User delete / account deletion → 24 h (soft) · 7 days (hard) | ≤30 days |
| `uploads` (files, photos) | Transient: 30 days unless saved to a Course; saved = Course lifetime | 30 days transient · Course lifetime saved | Same as owner row | ≤30 days |
| `attempts`, `marks` | Course lifetime + 24 months (drives Progress, calibration) | Course lifetime + 12 months | Account deletion → 7 days; pseudonymised calibration copies retain only `response`-less fields unless `research_pseudonymised` scope exists | ≤30 days |
| `learner_state`, `cards` | Course lifetime + 12 months | Same | Account deletion → 7 days | ≤30 days |
| `memories` | Until user deletes or account deletion | Same | Single memory → immediate; account → 7 days | ≤30 days |
| `receipts` | 7 years (evidential) | 7 years | Student may revoke the public token immediately; the record persists for the teacher who received it | n/a (encrypted archive) |
| `audit_log` | 7 years (school), 2 years (consumer) | 7 years | Never by user action; legal hold only | n/a |
| Langfuse traces (`trace_content`) | `none`: metadata 90 days · `redacted`: 30 days · `full`: 14 days | `redacted` max | Account deletion → traces for that `user_id` purged ≤7 days | 30 days |
| `age_assurance` evidence | Only `{method, confidence, checked_at}`; raw signals discarded at write | Same | With account | n/a |
| Anonymous landing principal (11-AUTH-004) | 24 h | — | Automatic | n/a |
| Frozen account (consent lapsed, 11-TEN-003) | Read-only 90 days, then deletion notice + 30 days | Same | Automatic | ≤30 days |

`DELETE /v1/me` returns `{job_id, expected_by}`; a confirmation email lists what is retained (Receipts already shared, audit rows, invoices) and why. *Acceptance:* the deletion-SLA test creates a user with rows in every table above, deletes, and asserts 0 rows keyed by that user in primary and replica by hour 168, with an `audit_log` entry `{action:'erasure_complete', counts}`; the export job returns a machine-readable ZIP (JSON per table + original uploads) ≤24 h.

**11-PRIV-005 — Annex III technical file (contents and owner).** Maintain `compliance/annex-iii/` in the monorepo, regenerated by CI from source-of-truth artefacts; the CTO owns it, the DPO co-signs each quarterly snapshot, and the file must be complete and dated before **2 Dec 2027**.

| Section | Source of truth | Regenerated by |
|---|---|---|
| 1. System description, intended purpose, versions, deployers | `README`, route table, Pack registry | Release job |
| 2. Risk management system: hazards (wrong Mark enters a grade, leak, bias by L1/handwriting), controls, residual risk | 11.17, §13.3 fairness buckets, 12.10 | Quarterly review |
| 3. Data governance: Pack provenance (three classes), gold-set composition and stratification, fairness buckets | `provenance_ledger`, `calibration_records` | Nightly export |
| 4. Technical documentation: architecture (11.1), model cards per route with dates, prompts by `(name, version)` | ADR log, Langfuse prompt registry | Release job |
| 5. Logging: what `audit_log` and traces capture, retention (11-PRIV-004), access controls | This section | Static + tests |
| 6. Human oversight: teacher confirmation gate, override flow, challenge-a-mark, calibrator role | §05, §10.20, §10.22 | Static + tests |
| 7. Accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity: calibration page history, seeding/auto-pause events, pen-test summaries, red-team results (12.10) | `eval_runs`, security reports | Monthly |
| 8. Post-market monitoring plan and incident log | 12.8 | Continuous |
| 9. Instructions for deployers (schools): configuration, limits, "not a board mark" | School admin guide | Release job |
| 10. EU declaration of conformity and registration record (when required) — *counsel* | Legal | Manual |

*Acceptance:* `pnpm compliance:build` produces the file with no section stamped "TODO"; the M18 definition of done (§13.7) checks the date.

**11-PRIV-006 — DPA template terms (school and tutor tenants).** Ship a signable DPA at `/legal/dpa` with fixed terms: Margin as processor; processing purposes limited to the tenant's educational use; sub-processors per 11-PRIV-007 with 30-day notice of changes and a right to object; residency per tenant choice; no training on pupil data (constant); retention per 11-PRIV-004 with the tenant's shorter values; deletion within 30 days of contract end with certificate; breach notice per 11-PRIV-009; audit right once per year plus on incident; SCCs / UK IDTA for any transfer; FERPA school-official and COPPA school-consent clauses for US tenants; security measures annex referencing 11.12. Tenants may attach the SDPC NDPA; conflicts resolve in the tenant's favour on protection, never on scope. *Acceptance:* `tenants.dpa_signed_at` must be set before any student joins a school tenant (API refuses `POST /v1/classes/{code}/join` otherwise).

**11-PRIV-007 — Sub-processor list policy.** Publish `/legal/subprocessors` generated from config: provider, purpose, region, data categories, ZDR status. Adding a provider or region requires a config PR that (a) updates the page, (b) emails tenant admins with `dpa_signed_at` (30-day objection window), (c) is blocked from production until the window closes unless the tenant list is empty. *Acceptance:* CI compares the endpoint map (11-PRIV-002) with the published list and fails on any provider missing from it.

**11-PRIV-008 — Records of processing (RoPA).** Maintain `compliance/ropa.yaml`: one entry per processing activity `{purpose, lawful_basis, data_categories, data_subjects, recipients, transfers, retention_ref, security_ref}`; the DPO reviews quarterly; a new table with pupil data requires a RoPA entry in the same PR (migration lint checks the table name against RoPA). *Acceptance:* migration lint blocks a learner-plane table absent from RoPA.

**11-PRIV-009 — Breach notification clock.** T0 = the moment any staff member or system flags a suspected personal-data breach (Sentry security event, RLS denial spike, cross-tenant read, lost device report). T0+1 h: incident channel opened and DPO paged; T0+24 h: scope assessment (tenants, data categories, record counts) written; **T0+72 h: notification to the ICO / lead EU supervisory authority** where required, and to affected school tenants regardless (DPA term); affected users notified without undue delay when risk is high; T0+14 d: post-mortem in the incident log (12.8). *Acceptance:* a tabletop exercise each quarter runs the clock end to end and records timestamps; the runbook is `runbooks/breach.md`.

**11-PRIV-010 — Rights tooling for schools.** School admins can trigger export or deletion for a student in their tenant (audit-logged, student notified); teachers cannot. A student in two tenants (family + school) has each tenant's data deleted independently; the consumer account survives a school deletion. *Acceptance:* RLS suite cases `admin_export_own_tenant_ok`, `admin_export_other_tenant_denied`, `teacher_delete_denied`.

## 11.14 Performance budgets

§13.6 owns the release-gate numbers (13-PERF-001…014, 13-PERF-020…024); this subsection allocates them to routes and services, adds the budgets §13.6 does not name (per-route bundles, cold start, offline cache, API latency), and fixes how each is measured in CI and in production. A budget breached in CI blocks the merge; a budget breached in production for 15 minutes pages the owning service (11-OBS-005).

**11-PERF-001 — Model-call latency per route.** Measured as TTFT (first `text` or `mark_header` part on the wire at `api`) and end-to-end (`done` part).

| Route (§08.2) | TTFT p50 | TTFT p95 | End-to-end p95 | CI measurement | Production measurement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tutoring Turn (Sonnet 5, cached) | <800 ms | <1.5 s | <12 s for ≤120-word Turn | 20 golden conversations per PR touching `orchestrator/`, `prompts/`; assert p95 over 3 runs | Synthetic every 10 min per region + real-traffic histogram by `route` |
| Trivial/nav (Haiku 4.5) | <500 ms | <1.0 s | <3 s | Same | Same |
| Levels Mark 8–30 marks (Opus 5 high) | `mark_header` <3 s | <5 s | first `ao_card` <8 s · each subsequent card ≤8 s after the previous · `done` <45 s | Synthetic 20-marker per paper per PR touching `marking/` | Hourly synthetic per paper; real-traffic percentile per `paper_id` |
| Points Mark (Sonnet draft → Opus confirm) | <2 s | <4 s | <15 s | Synthetic 6-part maths script | Same |
| Handwriting transcribe (Gemini 3.1 Pro / Mathpix) | first token <3 s | — | confirmed transcript ready <20 s | 4 fixtures: typed, neat, messy, maths | Same |
| Retrieval (steps 2–5 of 11-RAG-003) | — | <120 ms | — | Bench harness against the staging index per PR touching `retrieval/` | Server timing header, p95 per syllabus |
| Sandbox verify | — | <2 s | 20 s hard wall | Fixture set of 50 finals | Broker metric |
| Failover path (11-RT-005) | adds ≤1.5 s to TTFT | — | — | Chaos test with blackholed primary | `x-failover=1` histogram |

Why: TTFT on thinking models regresses silently when someone raises `effort` or drops the cache prefix; the PR-level golden set catches both (architecture research risk 10).

**11-PERF-002 — Non-AI API latency.** `api` p95 <250 ms for every endpoint in 11-API-001 except SSE and exports; `GET /v1/courses/{id}/today` p95 <120 ms (precomputed, ETag); `POST /v1/cards/{id}/review` p95 <100 ms; RLS overhead ≤10 ms per query (measured with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` in the RLS suite). *Acceptance:* k6 run per release at 1× peak (13-PERF-020) reports every endpoint under budget.

**11-PERF-003 — Core Web Vitals per route (p75, mobile and desktop).** Targets are the CWV "good" thresholds; the per-route table exists because the routes differ in what dominates.

| Route | LCP | INP | CLS | Dominant element / interaction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` Landing / First Mark | ≤2.0 s | ≤200 ms | ≤0.05 | Composer visible and focusable | No hero image; fonts `font-display: swap` with metric-matched fallback |
| `/course/[id]` Session | ≤2.5 s | ≤200 ms | ≤0.1 total; **0 above the streaming cursor** (11-RT-003) | Send → optimistic paint <50 ms | Measured with a custom `cls-above-cursor` observer that ignores shifts below the viewport line of the cursor |
| `/course/[id]/mark/[markId]` | ≤2.5 s | ≤200 ms | ≤0.1 | Answer pane with highlights | Span highlights arrive with `ao_card` parts; reserve card heights with skeletons |
| `/course/[id]/cards` | ≤2.0 s | ≤100 ms | ≤0.05 | Again / Got it tap → next card | Offline-first; must hold when the network is absent |
| `/course/[id]/paper/[id]` runner | ≤2.5 s | ≤200 ms | 0 during a timed paper | Timer tick, answer input | Any layout shift during a timed paper is a P1 bug |
| Teacher console | ≤3.0 s | ≤200 ms | ≤0.1 | Class table | Data-heavy; virtualised rows |

*Measured in CI:* Lighthouse CI on every PR for the six routes above against a seeded staging tenant (mobile emulation, 4× CPU throttle, "Fast 3G"); fails on LCP >budget +10% or CLS >budget. *Measured in production:* web-vitals RUM (first-party, no third-party SDK per 11-OBS-003) sampled 100% for under-18 tenants' aggregate only, joined with CrUX monthly. *Acceptance:* dashboard per route; 13-PERF-010 gate.

**11-PERF-004 — Bundle size budgets per route (gzipped, initial JS + CSS, excluding lazily loaded chunks).**

| Route | JS | CSS | Lazy chunks allowed on first interaction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Landing | ≤120 KB | ≤20 KB | none before first paint; KaTeX loads on first `math` part |
| Session (chat) | ≤180 KB | ≤25 KB | KaTeX 0.18 (≤90 KB), MathLive (≤250 KB, on maths input focus), Mermaid (on `diagram` part), Pyodide (≤10 MB, never before an explicit Practise check or offline Card maths, 11-TOOL-004), PDF viewer (on first citation open) |
| Mark view | ≤160 KB | ≤25 KB | KaTeX, PDF viewer |
| Cards | ≤100 KB | ≤15 KB | Pyodide for maths Cards only |
| Paper runner | ≤150 KB | ≤20 KB | MathLive, camera module |
| Teacher console | ≤220 KB | ≤30 KB | Charts on the calibration tab |
| Shared vendor (React 19 + Next runtime + Radix used) | counted inside the route numbers | — | — |

*Measured in CI:* `size-limit` with per-route entries; a PR that raises any route by >5% needs a `perf-approved` label from the web owner; a PR that exceeds the budget fails. *Production:* build artefact sizes recorded per release in `release_notes` (11.16). *Acceptance:* 13-PERF-011 plus the per-route table above; `grep pyodide` in the Session initial chunk returns nothing.

**11-PERF-005 — Cold start and server rendering.** `api` container cold start ≤1.5 s to first healthy response; `orchestrator` ≤2 s including prompt registry load; serverless route handlers (if used for `web`) p95 cold start ≤400 ms with a minimum of 2 warm instances per region during 06:00–24:00 local in exam season; RSC HTML for Home/Course p95 ≤600 ms server time. *Measured:* deploy-time probe records cold start per service; alarm at 2× budget. *Acceptance:* cold-start metric on the release dashboard.

**11-PERF-006 — Mobile app budgets (Expo).** Cold launch to interactive Home ≤2.0 s on a 2023 mid-range Android (Pixel 7a class); ≤1.2 s on iPhone 14; JS bundle ≤4 MB; camera → captured photo preview ≤500 ms; crash-free sessions ≥99.5% (11-ARCH-001). *Measured:* Maestro flows on device farm per release; Sentry performance in production.

**11-PERF-007 — Offline cache size and freshness (with 11-OFF-003).** Per Course: ≤200 MB total on mobile, ≤100 MB on web (IndexedDB); composed of Cards (≤5 MB), syllabus tree + notes (≤20 MB), Reader documents (≤150 MB, LRU by last opened, OWN/LICENSED-offline-permitted only), Today snapshot (≤1 MB), Plan (≤1 MB). Sync outbox flushes ≤10 s after reconnect; Today refreshes within 30 s of foreground. *Measured:* the airplane-mode E2E in 11-OFF-001 asserts sizes with `navigator.storage.estimate()` and the Expo SQLite file size. *Acceptance:* a Course that exceeds the ceiling evicts Reader documents first, never Cards or the outbox.

**11-PERF-008 — Streaming render budget.** ≤90 characters per 16 ms frame; long-task (>50 ms) count during a streaming Turn ≤2; main-thread blocked time during a Mark stream ≤300 ms total; KaTeX render of a held math block ≤30 ms per block. *Measured:* Playwright trace on 10 golden conversations per PR touching `web/` streaming components; production Long Animation Frames API sampled. *Acceptance:* 11-RT-003 plus this row.

**11-PERF-009 — Database budgets.** Attempt write path (insert + learner_state projection + Card creation) p95 ≤80 ms; nightly FSRS optimiser ≤30 min for 100k users; Today precompute for all active Courses finished before 05:00 local per region (11-ARCH-001); pgvector index build for a 10M-chunk partition ≤4 h off-peak. *Measured:* `pg_stat_statements` top-20 dashboard; job durations in Inngest. *Acceptance:* alarm on any job overrunning 150% of its budget.

**11-PERF-010 — Perf regressions are release blockers, not tickets.** Any budget in 11-PERF-001…009 exceeded on staging for 24 h holds the release (13-GATE-002); in production, a budget breached for two consecutive weekly reviews opens a P2 with an owner and a due date inside 14 days. *Acceptance:* the weekly perf review note lists each budget with current p50/p95/p75, delta vs last week, and owner.

## 11.15 Cost controls

Cost is controlled at four levels: the route table (§08.2, §08.10) fixes the price of one call; quotas (11-BILL-003) fix how many calls a user may make; this subsection fixes the alarms, budgets, caches and downgrade rules between the two; and the monthly review changes the config. The envelope to defend: blended chat Turn ≈$0.0095, median student ≈$1.6–2.6/month, heavy student $8–13, free tier ≤$0.5–1/MAU in season (SYNTHESIS §11–12).

**11-COST-001 — Quotas per plan (authoritative copy is `config/limits.json`, versioned; 11-BILL-003 governs the free tier).**

| Counter | Free | Student Monthly / Until-exams | Family (per student) | School seat | Teacher | Window | Over-limit behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `levels_marks` (Opus-class) | 3/day (6/day exam-week grace T−14 → last paper) | 40/month, then Sonnet-draft marking with the factual line "Draft marking until {reset_date} — same scheme, single marker" | 40/month | 40/month pooled per class, teacher can reallocate | 10/day for calibration tasks | day / month | Soft: cheaper route + queue; never a mid-Session stop |
| `points_marks` | uncapped, slow-down after 30/day | uncapped, slow-down after 80/day | same as Student | same | uncapped | day | Slow-down: Sonnet only, +queue |
| `cheap_turns` (tutoring + trivial) | uncapped, slow-down after 150/day | uncapped, slow-down after 400/day | same | same | uncapped | day | Slow-down: `effort=low`, Gemini Flash fallback first |
| `uploads` | 20/day | 60/day | 60/day | 60/day | 100/day | day | Hard at 3× (abuse) |
| `transcriptions` | 10/day | 40/day | 40/day | 40/day | 200/day | day | Soft |
| `generated_items` ("5 more like this") | 15/day | 60/day | 60/day | 60/day | 200/day | day | Soft: serve from the pre-generated bank |
| `voice_minutes` (v1) | 0 | 60/month | 60/month | 30/month | 0 | month | Hard, with meter |
| `exports` | 2/day | 5/day | 5/day | 5/day | 20/day | day | Hard |
| `challenges` | 1 per Mark | 1 per Mark | same | same | n/a | per Mark | Hard |

*Acceptance:* `GET /v1/usage` returns every counter with `{used, limit, window_resets_at, state ∈ {ok, slow, grace, capped}}`; a limit change without a `limits.json` version bump and changelog entry fails CI (zero silent limit changes, 11-BILL-003).

**11-COST-002 — Per-student spend alarms.** Compute `spend_usd` per user per day from `turns.cost_usd` + Mark costs. Alarms: (a) **>3× the rolling 7-day median** of active users in the same plan → flag `spend_outlier`, route the user's remaining cheap Turns at `effort=low`, no user-visible change; (b) **>6× median** → cap Opus-class routes for the rest of the day (marking continues on Sonnet-draft with the factual line), and open a review item; (c) 99th-percentile daily spend **≤6× median** is a guard-rail KPI (SYNTHESIS §12) — breach for 3 consecutive days pages the cost owner. Whitelist: teacher calibration tasks and the seeding traffic (§05) are excluded from the median. *Acceptance:* a synthetic user replaying 200 Marks in a day triggers (a) then (b) with the right route changes visible in traces; the dashboard shows the ratio daily.

**11-COST-003 — Tenant budgets.** Every school and tutor tenant has `policy.budget = {monthly_usd_cap, alert_at_pct: [50, 80, 100], on_cap ∈ {slow_down, notify_only}}` defaulting to `seats × $1.20/month` [founder default], `on_cap=slow_down`. Family tenants have a cap of `students × $6`. Consumer individuals have no tenant cap (per-user alarms apply). At `alert_at_pct` the tenant admin gets an email with the top routes; at 100% with `slow_down`, Opus-class routes degrade to the next rung of §08.7 for that tenant until month end — never a lockout, never during a timed paper already started. *Acceptance:* tenant cost roll-up by day and by class visible in the Admin console; the cap test drives a staging tenant past 100% and asserts the downgrade applies within 5 minutes and the meter shows `state=slow`.

**11-COST-004 — Cache policies (with §08.3 and 11-RAG-009).**

| Cache | Key | TTL | Target | Alarm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Provider prompt cache (persona + Pack prefix ≥1,024 tokens, byte-stable) | `(model, prompt_version, pack_version, policy_class)` | 1 h provider TTL; refreshed by traffic | `cache_read_input_tokens` share ≥60% of input tokens per route | Share <50% for 30 min on any route (11-OBS-002) |
| Mark context cache (scheme + anchors + generic principles per question part) | `(item_id, scheme_version, model)` | 1 h; pre-warmed for assignments due in <24 h and for Items in tomorrow's Today queues | ≥80% cache hit on Marks of assigned Items | <60% |
| Retrieval result cache | `(query_hash, filters, partition_key, ingest_version)` | 24 h | ≥70% on Practise/Mark | <50% |
| Pre-solve cache (key + SymPy verification per Item) | `(item_id, pack_version)` | Pack lifetime | 100% of live-Pack Items pre-solved nightly | Any live Item missing a key |
| Generated-Item bank | `(item_id, variant_seed)` | Pack lifetime | "5 more like this" served from bank ≥70% | <50% |
| Transcription cache | `sha256(image)` | 30 days | Duplicate photo never re-transcribed | — |
| Today / Plan precompute | `(course_id, date)` | 24 h | 100% precomputed before 05:00 local | Job overrun (11-PERF-009) |

Rules: dynamic content (student text, retrieved chunks, timestamps) comes **after** the cached prefix; no timestamp, random id or per-user string inside the prefix; changing `effort` or an image flag invalidates the provider cache, so the orchestrator holds those constant within a Session. *Acceptance:* CI asserts `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` on every golden conversation (13-PERF-012) and a prefix-stability test hashes the prefix across 100 Turns of one Session and finds one hash.

**11-COST-005 — Batch windows.** All unattended work runs on Batch APIs (50% discount) in named windows, UTC: `02:00–06:00` nightly (ER mining, tagging, Card generation from yesterday's lost marks, eval nightly runs, embedding of new ingests), `Sat 00:00–Sun 12:00` weekly (full re-embeds, pre-generated Item bank top-up, judge runs). Batch jobs carry `priority ∈ {p0_exam_week, p1, p2}`; p0 may run outside the window (e.g. seeding). DeepSeek off-peak pricing is used only for `pii=false` synthetic generation in the `us` plane [founder default E5]. Interactive routes never wait on a batch. *Acceptance:* ≥90% of bulk tokens per week are billed at batch rates (cost dashboard split `interactive / batch`).

**11-COST-006 — Model downgrade rules (the cost triggers for the §08.7 degradation ladder).** §08.7 defines the rungs (primary → same-family cheaper → cross-family fallback → template); this table says when cost, not availability, moves a route down one rung, and what the student sees.

| Trigger | Scope | Downgrade | User-visible |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free user past `levels_marks` daily limit | User, rest of day | Levels Mark → feedback-only with spans, no number ("3 examiner Marks used today · resets 00:00 · feedback continues") | Limit banner (§10.24) |
| Paid user past 40 Opus-class Marks/month | User, rest of month | Opus 5 → Sonnet 5 single marker, same scheme, `second_family=false`, badge "draft marking" | Factual line on the Mark |
| Cheap Turn slow-down threshold | User, rest of day | Sonnet 5 medium → Sonnet 5 low → Gemini 3.8 Flash; queue +2–5 s | Nothing (never a hard stop) |
| Spend outlier (a)/(b) in 11-COST-002 | User, day | As above, plus Opus cap at (b) | Nothing / factual line |
| Tenant cap at 100% (11-COST-003) | Tenant, month | One rung down on every route | Admin email; meter `state=slow` |
| Global daily spend >120% of forecast | Platform | `effort` medium → low on tutoring; second-family marking from 100% to 20% on gated papers only (never on ungated papers, §08.6) | Nothing; noted in release notes if >24 h |
| Provider price change detected by the re-pricing job (11-COST-008) | Route | Route table re-ranked by `quality_per_usd`; a swap needs the §08.9 eval gate first | Nothing |

Never downgraded by cost: the effort gate, the Help Ladder, Cards, probes, the distress and crisis flows, teacher calibration Marks, and any Mark on a timed paper already started. *Acceptance:* route-decision unit tests for every row; `x-downgrade-reason` recorded on the Turn; no downgrade row produces a modal.

**11-COST-007 — Token discipline.** `max_tokens` per route from config (tutoring 400; trivial 300; Mark per-AO JSON 1,200; advice 300); `thinking` display `summarized` and `effort` from the route table; images downsampled to ≤2,000 px; retrieved context capped at 8 chunks (11-RAG-003) and ≤6,000 tokens; conversation window trimmed to the last 12 Turns plus the Session summary; web-search results excluded from echo. Token budgets are expressed **per model** and re-baselined with `count_tokens` in CI when a model changes (the 4.7+ tokeniser is ≈30% denser). *Acceptance:* per-route input/output token histograms; a Turn exceeding 2× the route's p95 input tokens logs `context_bloat`.

**11-COST-008 — Dated price hazards live in config, with a re-pricing job.** `config/pricing.yaml` holds per-model input/output/cache prices with `valid_from`/`valid_to`; a monthly job (1st, 03:00 UTC) re-reads provider price pages, diffs against config, and opens a PR; hazards already known are pre-loaded:

```yaml
hazards:
  - model: gemini-3.8-flash      # and 3.7/3.6 Flash
    event: price_doubles
    effective: 2027-01-01
    action: re-rank fallback order; consider Flash-Lite for trivial route
  - model: claude-haiku-4-5
    event: retirement_possible
    effective: 2026-10-15        # earliest date; replacement model to be evaluated
    action: eval Haiku-5-class candidate against the trivial/classifier gold set before this date
  - model: deepseek-v4-*
    event: peak_offpeak_pricing
    effective: 2026-08-16
    action: batch windows only; never budget on unverified numbers
  - model: claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-5 / claude-fable-5-1
    event: commitment_floor
    effective: 2027-06-30 / 2027-07-24 / 2027-09-01
    action: plan successor evals one quarter before each date
```

*Acceptance:* CI fails if any route references a model whose `valid_to` is in the past or whose hazard `effective` date is <30 days away without an `ack_by` field naming the reviewer.

**11-COST-009 — Monthly cost review.** First working week of each month, 45 minutes, owners: CTO (chair), finance, content lead. Inputs (auto-generated from 11-OBS-002): cost per weekly-active learner by plan and region; median vs heavy vs 99th spend; cache-read share per route; batch share; second-family marking share per paper; top 20 users by spend with anonymised route mix; provider invoice reconciliation (≤3% variance); forecast for the next exam-season peak at 3× (13-PERF-020); hazards due in 90 days. Outputs: a PR to `limits.json`/`pricing.yaml`/route table if anything changes, each with a changelog line; a one-paragraph note in the release notes if any student-visible limit moved. *Acceptance:* review notes exist for every month since M3; every config change links to a review note or an incident.

**11-COST-010 — Exam-season grace is budgeted, not absorbed.** Before each Cambridge series (March, June, November) finance signs the grace budget: expected extra Marks from the 6/day free grace × blended Mark cost × 14 days × forecast active free users; the platform alarm at 120% of forecast (11-COST-006) refers to this signed number. *Acceptance:* 13-PERF-024 sign-off record per series.

## 11.16 CI/CD gates, environments and release process

§13.7 defines what must pass per environment (13-GATE-001…005); this subsection defines the pipeline that runs those checks, the environments themselves, flags, migrations, rollback and how a release becomes visible to users. AI coding agents and humans go through the same pipeline; there is no bypass label.

**11-CICD-001 — Pipeline stages (GitHub Actions or equivalent; every stage is a required check on `main`).**

| # | Stage | Runs on | Required checks (fail = block) | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Static | every push | `pnpm lint` (ESLint + Biome), `tsc --noEmit` across the monorepo, Prettier, secret scan (gitleaks), dependency audit (no critical CVE), licence check (no GPL in client bundles), copy lint (§09.11) on changed strings, RoPA/migration lint (11-PRIV-008) | ≤4 min |
| 2 | Unit + contract | every push | Vitest ≥80% line coverage on `packages/domain` and `services/*`; Zod ⇄ OpenAPI contract snapshot (11-API-003); route-table and policy-object merge tests (11-API-006); RLS suite ≥200 cases against a disposable Postgres (11-DATA-003); token-count baselines (`count_tokens`) per route | ≤8 min |
| 3 | Build + budgets | every push | Next.js and Expo builds; `size-limit` per route (11-PERF-004); Pyodide/KaTeX absent from initial chunks; Pack validation (`pnpm packs:validate` — schema, AO weights sum to 100, every command word in the board table, every `question_part` has a `mark_schemes` row or `feedback_only=true`, no `ref_only` text, provenance non-null) | ≤6 min |
| 4 | Browser | every PR | Playwright flows: First Mark end-to-end on specimen material, Save Course + consent sheet, effort gate → ladder → Just the answer → retest tag, handwriting confirm, Card review offline/online, Receipt export, teacher override, challenge-a-mark; axe-core on the 25 canonical screens (0 serious/critical); contrast check of every token pair in light and dark (§09.4); reduced-motion snapshot (no animation frames with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`); CLS-above-cursor assertion on 10 golden streams (11-RT-003); visual diff (Chromatic/Argos) needing approval | ≤15 min |
| 5 | Eval subset | PR touching `prompts/`, `orchestrator/`, `marking/`, `retrieval/`, `ingest/`, `config/routes*` | Pedagogy subset ≥50 dialogues, leak <5%, praise <5% (§13.2); marking gate subset ≥40 gold scripts per touched paper within the §13.3 tolerances; retrieval gold Recall@8 ≥0.92; injection fixture 0 violations; cache-read assertion on golden conversations; cost per golden conversation within ±15% of the route budget | ≤30 min (11-ARCH-001) |
| 6 | Staging deploy | merge to `main` | Migrations applied (11-CICD-005); smoke suite; synthetic TTFT/CWV started | ≤10 min |
| 7 | Nightly on staging | 02:00 UTC | 13-GATE-002 full suites; 3× load test freshness (≤35 days); DPIA/policy tests (0 EU-tenant calls to non-EU endpoints, incognito writes no learner state); deletion-SLA test (11-PRIV-004); sandbox canary; a11y full crawl | ≤3 h |
| 8 | Canary → prod | manual promote by the release owner | 13-GATE-003 (5% ≥2 h; ≥6 h in exam weeks) with auto-rollback; then 100% | — |

*Acceptance:* branch protection requires stages 1–5 green and one human review; `CODEOWNERS` routes prompts, gate thresholds, gold sets and `limits.json` to the owning role (13-GATE-005); the median PR-to-staging time is ≤45 minutes.

**11-CICD-002 — Environments.**

| Env | Data | Providers | Who | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` (local + ephemeral preview per PR) | Seeded synthetic tenants (one per type), 9609 sample Pack, no real pupil data ever | Record/replay fixtures by default; live providers behind `LIVE_PROVIDERS=1` with a $20/day cap per developer | Engineers, agents | Fast loop |
| `staging` (one per residency: `eu`, `us`) | Synthetic + pseudonymised gold scripts (consented); production Packs | Live, own keys, batch windows mirrored | Team, partner-school pilots on invitation | Gates, load, soak |
| `canary` (production infrastructure, tagged) | Production | Live | 5% of traffic by sticky `user_id` hash, excluding school tenants that opted out of canaries and excluding any tenant in a live timed paper | Progressive delivery |
| `prod` (per residency) | Production | Live | Everyone | — |

Rules: no production pupil data leaves `prod` (pseudonymised eval extracts go through the §13.1 consent path); every environment has its own secrets, provider keys and Langfuse project; `staging` is destroyed and recreated from migrations monthly to prove reproducibility. *Acceptance:* an engineer can stand up `dev` with one command in ≤10 minutes; the monthly staging rebuild is logged.

**11-CICD-003 — Feature flags.** Flags live in Postgres (`flags` table) with a 5-second cache, evaluated server-side and passed to clients in the policy context; three kinds: `release` (dark-launch, removed within 30 days of 100%), `experiment` (user-level randomised, registered in the §13 experiment registry with primary outcome and kill criterion, e.g. the debt guard 04-DEBT-003), `ops` (kill switches: `marks_visible_{paper}`, `second_family_on`, `voice_pilot`, `provider_{name}_enabled`, `anon_landing_mark`). Every flag has an owner, an expiry, and a default that is safe when the flag service is unreachable (fail closed for anything that shows numbers or unlocks help). Flags never change pedagogy rules that §00 lists as non-negotiable. *Acceptance:* a flag past expiry fails CI; the flag audit lists every flag with owner, age, exposure; killing `provider_anthropic_enabled` in staging reroutes 100% of Turns within 10 s.
